Dress the salad with lemon juice, the remaining olive oil, salt and pepper and fold in the rocket.
Let the chicken rest for 3 minutes, slice it and serve next to the salad.

title: Chicken lentil soup with leaf spinach, carrot and lemon
instructions: Chop the onion, dice the carrot and cut the chicken into small cubes.
Sweat the onion and carrot in the rapeseed oil in a pot for 3 minutes and stir in the turmeric.
Add the stock and lentils and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the chicken cubes and let them cook gently for 8 minutes, then stir in the spinach.
Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper and serve sprinkled with parsley.

title: Chicken edamame stir-fry with pak choi, carrot and brown rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice according to the packet for about 25 minutes.
Cut the chicken into strips, the carrot into thin sticks and the pak choi into pieces, and grate the ginger.
Stir-fry the chicken in the sesame oil over high heat for 5 minutes.
Add the carrot, edamame and ginger for 3 minutes, then add the pak choi and fry for 2 more minutes.
Deglaze with soy sauce and serve with the rice.

title: Chicken bulgur salad with chickpeas, tomato and parsley
instructions: Pour boiling water over the bulgur and leave it covered to soak for 10 minutes.
Season the chicken and fry it in a non-stick pan with half of the oil for 5 minutes per side.
Dice the cucumber and tomato and finely chop the parsley.
Mix the bulgur with the vegetables, chickpeas, parsley, lemon juice and the remaining oil.
Slice the chicken and arrange it on the salad.

title: Oven-baked chicken with Brussels sprouts, sweet potato and mustard yoghurt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, halve the Brussels sprouts and cut the sweet potato into cubes.
Toss the vegetables with the olive oil, salt and pepper and spread them on a tray.
Season the chicken with paprika and salt, add it to the tray and bake everything for 25 minutes.
Stir the yoghurt with the mustard and a pinch of salt.
Slice the chicken and serve with the roasted vegetables and the mustard yoghurt.

title: Chicken wrap with black beans, red cabbage and avocado
instructions: Cut the chicken into strips, season with cumin, salt and pepper and fry in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes.
Rinse the beans and lightly mash them with a fork, finely shred the red cabbage.
Mash the avocado with lime juice and a little salt.
Warm the wrap briefly in the pan, fill with yoghurt, beans, cabbage, chicken, avocado and coriander, roll up and cut in half.

title: Chicken chickpea curry with leaf spinach
instructions: Dice the chicken, finely chop the onion and grate the ginger.
Brown the chicken in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes, fry the onion and ginger with it for 2 minutes and dust with curry powder.
Add the coconut milk, tomatoes and chickpeas and simmer for 12 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts and season with salt.
Serve the curry in a bowl sprinkled with coriander.

title: Chicken buckwheat salad with green beans, cherry tomatoes and light feta
instructions: Simmer the buckwheat in twice the amount of salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Trim the green beans, halve them and cook in salted water for 8 minutes, then rinse in cold water.
Season the chicken, fry it in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes per side and slice it.
Mix the buckwheat, beans and halved cherry tomatoes with lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Top with the chicken, crumble the feta over it and sprinkle with basil.

title: Air fryer chicken strips in oat crust with pea mint mash
instructions: Cut the chicken into 6 strips and season with salt, pepper and paprika.
Dip the strips first in the whisked egg white, then coat them in the oats and spray with the rapeseed oil.
Cook in the air fryer at 190 °C for about 12 minutes until crisp, turning halfway.
Boil the peas in salted water for 4 minutes, drain and roughly blend with mint, yoghurt, salt and pepper.
Serve the chicken strips with the pea mash.

title: Turkey sweet potato pan with pinto beans and baby spinach
instructions: Cut the sweet potato into small cubes, the turkey into strips and the onion into wedges.
Fry the sweet potato in half of the rapeseed oil covered for 8 minutes until almost soft.
Add the turkey and onion with the remaining oil and fry for 5 minutes, seasoning with paprika, cumin and salt.
Add the pinto beans, warm for 2 minutes and fold in the baby spinach.
Season with lime juice and pepper and serve.

title: Sliced turkey with kidney beans, pepper and courgette
instructions: Cut the turkey into thin strips and the pepper, courgette and onion into pieces.
Sear the turkey in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes and remove it.
Fry the onion, pepper and courgette in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add the passata, kidney beans, paprika and turkey and simmer for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.

title: Air fryer turkey patties with chickpea radish salad and dill yoghurt
instructions: Knead the minced turkey with oats, finely chopped onion, salt and pepper and shape 3 flat patties.
Cook in the air fryer at 190 °C for about 12 minutes, turning halfway.
Slice the cucumber and radishes and mix them with the chickpeas and lemon juice.
Stir the yoghurt with chopped dill and a pinch of salt.
Serve the patties with the salad and dill yoghurt.

title: Turkey breast with white bean tomato ragout and leaf spinach
instructions: Season the turkey breast and fry it in half of the olive oil for 5 minutes per side, then keep warm.
Chop the garlic and briefly sweat it in the remaining oil.
Add the tomatoes and beans and simmer for 8 minutes.
Fold in the spinach until wilted and season the ragout.
Slice the turkey, lay it on the ragout and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Air fryer turkey skewers with chickpea couscous and cucumber yoghurt
instructions: Cut the turkey, pepper and courgette into cubes, thread them alternately onto 3 skewers and brush with olive oil, paprika and salt.
Cook the skewers in the air fryer at 190 °C for about 12 minutes, turning halfway.
Pour the same amount of boiling water over the couscous, leave to swell for 5 minutes and mix in the chickpeas.
Grate the cucumber, squeeze it out and stir it into the yoghurt with salt and pepper.
Arrange the skewers on the couscous and serve the cucumber yoghurt alongside.

title: Turkey leek pan with peas and wholemeal penne
instructions: Cook the penne in salted water until al dente according to the packet.
Cut the turkey into strips, fry it in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes, then remove it.
Halve the leek lengthways, wash it, slice into rings and sweat in the same pan for 4 minutes.
Stir in the stock, peas and cream cheese, return the turkey and simmer for 3 minutes.
Toss with the penne, season and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Turkey chickpea tagine with carrot, courgette and parsley
instructions: Cut the turkey into large cubes, the carrot into slices and the courgette into thick pieces, and chop the onion.
Brown the turkey in the olive oil in a casserole for 4 minutes, then fry the onion and ras el hanout with it for 2 minutes.
Add the carrot, tomatoes and 150 ml water and braise covered for 15 minutes.
Add the courgette and chickpeas and braise for another 8 minutes.
Season with lemon juice and salt and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Beef chilli with black beans and Hokkaido pumpkin
instructions: Cut the pumpkin with its skin into small cubes and chop the onion.
Fry the minced beef in the rapeseed oil until crumbly, then fry the onion with it for 2 minutes.
Briefly toast the cumin and chilli flakes, then add the pumpkin, tomatoes and 100 ml water.
Simmer covered for 15 minutes, then let the beans heat through for 5 minutes.
Season and serve sprinkled with coriander.

title: Ginger beef strips with broccoli, edamame and quinoa
instructions: Rinse the quinoa and cook it in twice the amount of water for 15 minutes.
Cut the steak across the grain into thin strips, divide the broccoli into small florets and chop the ginger and garlic.
Sear the beef strips in the sesame oil for 2 minutes and remove them.
Fry the broccoli, edamame, ginger and garlic with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes.
Add the beef and soy sauce, toss briefly and serve with the quinoa.

title: Air fryer beef kofta with bulgur chickpea salad and yoghurt
instructions: Knead the minced beef with finely grated onion, cumin, half of the parsley, salt and pepper and shape 4 long koftas.
Cook the koftas in the air fryer at 200 °C for about 10 minutes, turning halfway.
Pour boiling water over the bulgur and leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Mix the bulgur with the chickpeas, diced tomato, remaining parsley, lemon juice, olive oil and salt.
Serve the koftas with the salad and the yoghurt.

title: Beef rump steak with white bean rocket salad and cherry tomatoes
instructions: Take the steak out of the fridge 20 minutes before frying and pat it dry.
Fry the steak in a very hot pan with half of the oil for 3 minutes per side, season and let it rest for 4 minutes.
Rinse the beans, halve the cherry tomatoes and cut the onion into thin rings.
Mix the beans, tomatoes, onion and rocket with lemon juice, the remaining oil, salt and pepper.
Slice the steak and serve it on the salad.

title: Beef strips with Brussels sprouts, mushrooms and chickpeas
instructions: Trim and halve the Brussels sprouts and precook them in salted water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Cut the steak into thin strips, the mushrooms into slices and the onion into strips.
Sear the beef strips in half of the oil for 2 minutes, salt them and remove.
Fry the Brussels sprouts, mushrooms and onion in the remaining oil for 6 minutes, then fry the chickpeas and thyme with them for 2 minutes.
Return the beef, season with salt and pepper and serve.

title: Minced beef pointed cabbage pan with chickpeas and tomato
instructions: Quarter the pointed cabbage, remove the core and cut it into thin strips, then dice the onion.
Fry the minced beef in the rapeseed oil until crumbly, then fry the onion, paprika and cumin with it for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and fry for 6 minutes, turning, until soft.
Stir in the tomatoes and chickpeas and simmer for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.

title: Salmon with beluga lentil salad, baby spinach and radishes
instructions: Cook the beluga lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until al dente and drain.
Slice the radishes, halve the cherry tomatoes and finely dice the onion.
Mix the lentils with the vegetables, baby spinach, lemon juice, olive oil, dill, salt and pepper.
Salt the salmon and fry it skin side down in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes, turn and finish cooking for 2 minutes.
Serve the salmon on the lentil salad.

title: Air fryer redfish with peas, green beans and dill potatoes
instructions: Cut the potatoes into wedges and boil them in salted water for 15 minutes.
Brush the redfish with half of the olive oil, paprika and salt and cook in the air fryer at 180 °C for about 9 minutes.
Cook the green beans for 8 minutes and the peas for 3 minutes in salted water and drain.
Toss the potatoes with the remaining oil and chopped dill.
Arrange the fish with the vegetables and potatoes and drizzle with lemon juice.

title: Pollock with mustard lentils, carrot and leek
instructions: Cook the lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until al dente and drain.
Finely dice the carrot, slice the leek into rings and sweat them in half of the oil for 4 minutes.
Add the lentils and stock, simmer for 3 minutes and stir in the mustard and yoghurt.
Salt the pollock and fry it in the remaining oil for 3 minutes per side.
Spread the mustard lentils on a plate, lay the fish on top and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Tuna borlotti salad with egg, cucumber, pepper and tomato
instructions: Hard-boil the egg for 9 minutes, cool it in cold water, peel and quarter it.
Rinse the beans, dice the cucumber, pepper and tomato and cut the onion into thin rings.
Whisk the lemon juice with olive oil, salt and pepper and toss with the beans, vegetables and chopped parsley.
Flake the tuna and arrange it with the egg quarters on the salad.

title: Prawn quinoa bowl with edamame, mango and red cabbage
instructions: Rinse the quinoa and cook it in twice the amount of water for 15 minutes.
Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain.
Fry the prawns in half of the sesame oil for 3 minutes until pink.
Dice the mango and cucumber and finely shred the red cabbage.
Arrange everything side by side in a bowl and drizzle with lime juice, soy sauce and the remaining sesame oil.

title: Trout fillet on pea barley with dill yoghurt
instructions: Finely dice the onion and briefly toast it with the barley in a dry pot.
Pour in the stock and simmer the barley covered for 25 minutes, adding the peas for the last 4 minutes.
Salt the trout and fry it skin side down in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes, turn and finish for 1 minute.
Stir the yoghurt with chopped dill, lemon juice and salt.
Spread the pea barley on a plate, lay the trout on top and add the dill yoghurt.

title: Air fryer salmon with Hokkaido pumpkin, chickpeas and kale
instructions: Cut the pumpkin with its skin into wedges and toss with the chickpeas, half of the olive oil, paprika and salt.
Cook in the air fryer at 190 °C for 12 minutes.
Salt the salmon, place it on the vegetables and cook for another 9 minutes.
Strip the kale from its stalks and wilt it in the remaining oil in a pan for 3 minutes.
Arrange everything and drizzle with lemon juice.

title: Cod in tomato chickpea sauce with leaf spinach
instructions: Chop the garlic, sweat it briefly in the olive oil in a wide pan and stir in the paprika.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas and simmer for 8 minutes.
Salt the cod, place it in the sauce and let it cook covered for 8 minutes.
Add the spinach to the sauce next to the fish and let it wilt.
Season with pepper and serve in a deep plate.

title: Prawn wholemeal spaghetti with broccoli, peas and cherry tomatoes
instructions: Cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente according to the packet, adding the broccoli florets and peas 4 minutes before the end.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and chop the garlic.
Fry the prawns in the olive oil for 2 minutes, add the garlic, tomatoes and chilli flakes and fry for 2 more minutes.
Drain the pasta and vegetables, toss them in the pan with lemon juice and season with salt and pepper.

title: Red lentil dal with carrot, leaf spinach and skyr
instructions: Chop the onion, grate the ginger and finely dice the carrot.
Sweat the onion, ginger and carrot in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes and briefly toast the curry powder.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and 300 ml water and simmer for 15 minutes until the lentils break down.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts and season with salt.
Serve the dal in a bowl with a dollop of skyr.

title: Oven frittata with broccoli, peas and cottage cheese
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C, divide the broccoli into small florets and blanch with the peas in salted water for 3 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with cottage cheese, salt and pepper and slice the spring onions into rings.
Brush a small ovenproof pan with the olive oil, spread the vegetables in it and pour over the egg mixture.
Bake in the oven for 18 minutes until the frittata is set and lightly browned.
Serve with halved cherry tomatoes.

title: Air fryer lentil cottage cheese patties with cucumber dill salad
instructions: Cook the lentils in water for 10 minutes until soft, drain well and let them cool.
Mix the lentils with cottage cheese, egg, oats, salt and pepper and shape 4 patties.
Cook the patties in the air fryer at 190 °C for about 14 minutes until golden, carefully turning halfway.
Thinly slice the cucumber and mix with the baby spinach, yoghurt, chopped dill, lemon juice and salt.
Serve the patties with the salad.

title: Black bean quinoa bowl with cottage cheese and tomato salsa
instructions: Rinse the quinoa and cook it in twice the amount of water for 15 minutes.
Rinse the beans and sweetcorn and warm them with the cumin in a small pot for 3 minutes.
Finely dice the tomato and pepper and mix with lime juice, chopped coriander and salt into a salsa.
Arrange the quinoa, beans with sweetcorn, salsa and cottage cheese side by side in a bowl.

title: Wholemeal fusilli with edamame basil cream and cherry tomatoes
instructions: Cook the fusilli in salted water until al dente according to the packet, adding the edamame for the last 4 minutes.
Blend a third of the edamame with basil, quark, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, salt and 3 tbsp pasta water until smooth.
Halve the cherry tomatoes.
Toss the pasta and remaining edamame with the cream, fold in the tomatoes and season with pepper.

title: Baked sweet potato with lentil spinach filling and lime skyr
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, wash the sweet potato, prick it several times and bake for 40 minutes until soft.
Cook the lentils in water for 20 minutes until tender, drain and mix with cumin, salt and the baby spinach until it wilts.
Stir the skyr with lime juice and a pinch of salt and cut the spring onions into rings.
Cut the sweet potato open lengthways, fill with the lentil spinach mixture, top with the lime skyr and sprinkle with feta and spring onions.

title: Beluga lentil salad with light feta, cucumber, pepper and mint skyr
instructions: Cook the beluga lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until al dente, drain and let them cool.
Dice the cucumber and pepper and finely chop the onion.
Mix the lentils with the vegetables, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Stir the skyr with half of the chopped mint.
Serve the salad with crumbled feta, the remaining mint and the mint skyr.

title: Broccoli chickpea bowl with egg and tahini yoghurt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, divide the broccoli into florets and roast with the chickpeas, paprika and salt on a tray for 20 minutes.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve them.
Finely shred the red cabbage.
Stir the yoghurt with tahini, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Arrange the broccoli, chickpeas, red cabbage and eggs in a bowl and spoon the tahini yoghurt over.

title: Air fryer ginger tofu with pointed cabbage carrot salad and brown rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice according to the packet for about 25 minutes.
Pat the tofu dry, dice it and toss with half of the soy sauce and the grated ginger.
Cook in the air fryer at 200 °C for about 15 minutes until crisp, shaking now and then.
Finely shred the pointed cabbage, grate the carrot and mix with lime juice, sesame oil, the remaining soy sauce and spring onions.
Arrange the rice, salad and tofu together in a bowl.

title: Tempeh chickpea pan with pepper and leaf spinach
instructions: Cut the tempeh into thin slices, the pepper into strips and the onion into wedges.
Fry the tempeh in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes per side until golden and deglaze with half of the soy sauce.
Add the onion and pepper and fry for 4 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, paprika and remaining soy sauce and fry for 2 minutes.
Fold in the spinach until wilted and season with pepper.

title: Green tofu pea curry with courgette and brown rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice according to the packet for about 25 minutes.
Dice the tofu, cut the courgette into half moons and grate the ginger.
Toast the curry paste and ginger in a pot with 3 tbsp coconut milk for 1 minute.
Add the remaining coconut milk, 100 ml water, courgette and tofu and simmer for 8 minutes, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Season with salt, sprinkle with coriander and serve with the rice.

title: Stuffed courgettes with soy mince, white beans and tomato
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, pour 120 ml hot water over the soy mince and leave to soak for 10 minutes.
Halve the courgettes lengthways, scoop out the flesh with a spoon and chop it.
Fry the onion and courgette flesh in the olive oil for 3 minutes, add the squeezed soy mince, lightly mashed white beans, half of the tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 5 minutes.
Fill the courgette halves, place them in a dish with the remaining tomatoes and bake for 25 minutes.
Serve sprinkled with basil.

title: Cumin tofu on bulgur pilaf with chickpeas and cucumber soy yoghurt
instructions: Finely dice the onion and sweat it in half of the oil for 2 minutes, then add the diced tomato and bulgur.
Bring to the boil with 90 ml water and a little salt, add the chickpeas and leave covered on low heat for 12 minutes.
Dice the tofu, season with cumin, paprika and salt and fry in the remaining oil for 8 minutes until crisp all over.
Grate the cucumber and stir it into the soy yoghurt with chopped mint and salt.
Arrange the pilaf on a plate, top with the tofu and add the cucumber soy yoghurt.

title: Air fryer tempeh with millet tabbouleh, chickpeas and pomegranate
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water, simmer it in twice the amount of salted water for 10 minutes, then leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Cut the tempeh into cubes, toss with soy sauce and cook in the air fryer at 190 °C for about 10 minutes until crisp.
Finely dice the cucumber and tomato and chop the parsley.
Mix the millet with the vegetables, chickpeas, parsley, lemon juice, olive oil and salt.
Serve the tabbouleh with the tempeh and sprinkle with pomegranate seeds.

title: Edamame chickpea salad with smoked tofu, carrot and sesame
instructions: Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, rinse in cold water and drain.
Dice the smoked tofu and cucumber, grate the carrot and cut the spring onions into rings.
Whisk the soy sauce, lime juice and sesame oil into a dressing.
Toss all the ingredients with the dressing and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Tofu kidney bean stew with Swiss chard and sweet potato
instructions: Chop the onion and garlic, dice the sweet potato and cut the chard into strips, keeping stalks and leaves apart.
Sweat the onion, garlic and chard stalks in the olive oil for 3 minutes and stir in the paprika.
Add the sweet potato, tomatoes and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the tofu cubes, kidney beans and chard leaves and simmer for another 6 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.

title: Tofu Brussels sprouts pan with Hokkaido pumpkin and white beans
instructions: Halve the Brussels sprouts, cut the pumpkin with its skin into small cubes and precook both in salted water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Dice the tofu and fry it in half of the olive oil for 6 minutes until golden, deglaze with soy sauce and remove.
Fry the onion, Brussels sprouts and pumpkin in the remaining oil for 6 minutes until lightly browned.
Add the beans, thyme and tofu, fry for 2 minutes and season with salt and pepper.

title: Cauliflower chickpea soup with smoked tofu cubes
instructions: Chop the onion, sweat it in half of the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes and briefly toast the turmeric and cumin.
Add the cauliflower florets, chickpeas and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend the soup until smooth and season with salt and pepper.
Dice the smoked tofu and fry it in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until crisp.
Serve the soup with a dollop of soy yoghurt and the tofu cubes.

title: Parippu – Sri Lankan red lentil coconut dal with kale and brown rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice in twice the amount of water for 30 minutes.
Chop the onion and garlic and sweat them in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes, then stir in the turmeric and cumin.
Add the lentils, coconut milk and 200 ml water and simmer for 15 minutes until creamy.
Finely shred the kale and cook it along for the last 4 minutes.
Season the dal with lime juice, salt and pepper and serve with the rice.

title: Thenthuk – Tibetan vegetable noodle soup with tofu and spinach
instructions: Knead the flour with 40 ml water and a pinch of salt into a smooth dough and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the rapeseed oil for 2 minutes, then add the diced carrot and tomato.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce, bring to the boil and add the diced tofu.
Pull the dough flat, tear it into small pieces straight into the soup and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach, season and serve sprinkled with spring onions.

title: Laghman – Uyghur noodle stir-fry with tofu, pepper and green beans
instructions: Cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente according to the packet and drain.
Dice the tofu, fry it in the rapeseed oil for 5 minutes until golden and set aside.
Fry the onion, garlic, pepper strips and halved beans for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, cumin and chilli.
Dice the tomato, add it with the soy sauce and 50 ml water and braise for 4 minutes.
Fold in the noodles and tofu, season and serve hot.

title: Matar tofu – pea and tofu curry with tomato and basmati rice
instructions: Cook the basmati rice in twice the amount of salted water for 12 minutes.
Dice the tofu, fry it in half of the rapeseed oil for 5 minutes and set aside.
Sweat the onion, garlic and ginger in the remaining oil for 3 minutes and briefly toast the garam masala and turmeric with them.
Add the tomatoes and peas, simmer for 8 minutes and fold in the tofu.
Season, sprinkle with coriander and serve with the rice.

title: Lobia masala – black-eyed bean curry with leaf spinach and wholemeal chapati
instructions: Finely chop the onion and garlic and fry them in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garam masala and cumin, add the tomatoes and reduce for 5 minutes.
Add the black-eyed beans, simmer for 5 minutes and stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Warm the chapati in a dry pan for 1 minute per side.
Season the curry, sprinkle with coriander and serve with the chapati.

title: Kootu – South Indian mung dal and pumpkin stew with coconut and millet
ingredients: Mung dal (split yellow mung beans, dry)
instructions: Rinse the mung dal and cook it with 300 ml water and the turmeric for 15 minutes until soft.
Rinse the millet with hot water and let it simmer in 100 ml salted water for 15 minutes.
Dice the pumpkin, cut the beans into pieces, add them to the dal and cook for 10 minutes.
Toast the mustard seeds and cumin in the rapeseed oil until they pop and stir them in with the coconut milk.
Season, sprinkle with coriander and serve with the millet.

title: Misal – spicy Maharashtrian mung bean curry with wholemeal roll
instructions: Soak the mung beans overnight and cook them in fresh water for 25 minutes until soft.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes and stir in the curry powder and chilli.
Dice the tomato, add it and simmer with the mung beans and 150 ml water for 10 minutes.
Season with lime juice and salt and sprinkle with chopped red onion and coriander.
Serve with the halved, briefly toasted roll.

title: Kala chana salad – Indian chickpea salad with cucumber, tomato and peanuts
instructions: Rinse the black chickpeas and drain them well.
Finely dice the cucumber, tomato and red onion and chop the mint and coriander.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, chaat masala and a little salt.
Mix everything, roughly chop the peanuts and scatter them over the top.

title: Mulligatawny – vegan lentil and apple curry soup with coconut milk
instructions: Dice the onion, carrot, celery and apple and grate the ginger.
Sweat the vegetables and ginger in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes and briefly toast the curry powder with them.
Add the lentils, rice and stock and simmer for 18 minutes.
Purée half of the soup, stir in the coconut milk and heat through.
Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Pho chay – Vietnamese vegetable rice noodle soup with tofu and herbs
instructions: Halve the onion and toast it with the ginger in a dry pan for 5 minutes.
Simmer the stock with the onion, ginger, star anise, cinnamon and soy sauce for 15 minutes, then strain.
Soak the rice noodles according to the packet and slice the tofu and shiitake.
Cook the tofu, mushrooms and pak choi in the broth for 4 minutes.
Place the noodles in a bowl, pour the soup over them and serve with the sprouts, herbs and lime juice.

title: Mala tofu cucumber salad with peanuts, coriander and jasmine rice
instructions: Cook the jasmine rice in twice the amount of water for 12 minutes.
Cut the tofu into cubes and fry it in a non-stick pan without fat for 6 minutes on all sides.
Smash the cucumber with the back of a knife, cut it into pieces and salt it lightly.
Whisk the sesame oil, soy sauce, chopped garlic, Sichuan pepper, chilli and lime juice and toss with the cucumber and tofu.
Sprinkle with peanuts, coriander and spring onions and serve with the rice.

title: Yasai kare – Japanese vegetable curry with tofu, pumpkin and brown rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice in twice the amount of water for 30 minutes.
Cut the onion into wedges and the carrot and pumpkin into chunks and fry them in the rapeseed oil for 5 minutes.
Dust the flour and curry powder over the top, sweat briefly and deglaze with the stock.
Add the apple, soy sauce and diced tofu and simmer for 12 minutes until thick, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Serve the curry next to the rice.

title: Khao pad sapparot – Thai pineapple fried rice with tofu and cashews
instructions: Cook the jasmine rice and let it cool completely, ideally using rice from the day before.
Dice the tofu and fry it in the rapeseed oil in a wok for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, diced pepper and peas and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the rice, diced pineapple, curry powder and soy sauce and fry for 4 minutes, stirring.
Serve with toasted cashews, spring onions and lime juice.

title: Musabbaha – warm chickpeas with tahini, lemon and wholemeal pitta
instructions: Warm the chickpeas with a little water for 5 minutes, drain and reserve 3 tbsp of the cooking water.
Stir the tahini with the lemon juice, crushed garlic, cooking water and salt until smooth.
Roughly mash a third of the chickpeas and mix everything with the tahini sauce.
Garnish with olive oil, cumin, parsley and diced tomato and serve with the warm pitta.

title: Timman bagilla – Iraqi dill rice with broad beans and yoghurt
instructions: Wash the basmati rice and soak it for 20 minutes.
Finely dice the onion, sweat it in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes until translucent and stir in the turmeric.
Add the rice, beans, chopped dill and 120 ml water, salt and cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the yoghurt with grated garlic and a little salt and serve with the rice.

title: Vospapur – Armenian red lentil soup with apricots and bulgur
instructions: Dice the onion and sweat it in the olive oil for 4 minutes, then briefly toast the tomato paste, paprika and cumin with it.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer for 12 minutes.
Chop the apricots, add them with the bulgur and cook for a further 10 minutes.
Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper and sprinkle with mint.

title: Yeşil mercimek salatası – Turkish lentil salad with pepper paste and walnuts
instructions: Cook the lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until al dente, drain and let them cool.
Stir the pepper paste with the olive oil, lemon juice, chilli flakes and salt.
Finely dice the tomato, pepper and red onion and chop the parsley.
Mix the lentils with the vegetables, parsley and dressing and sprinkle with chopped walnuts.

title: Vegetarian molokhia – Egyptian jute leaf stew with chickpeas and rice
instructions: Cook the basmati rice in twice the amount of salted water for 12 minutes.
Bring the stock to the boil, add the chickpeas and let the frozen molokhia thaw in it while stirring.
Chop the garlic and toast it with the ground coriander in the olive oil for 1 minute until golden.
Stir the garlic oil into the stew and let it steep for 3 minutes without boiling.
Season with lemon juice and salt and serve with the rice.

title: Tabbouleh with beluga lentils and plenty of parsley
instructions: Cook the beluga lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until al dente, drain and let them cool.
Pour 50 ml hot water over the bulgur and let it soak for 10 minutes.
Chop the parsley and mint very finely and finely dice the tomato and spring onions.
Mix everything with lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper and leave to infuse for 10 minutes.

title: Muhammara bulgur bowl with chickpeas, cucumber and walnuts
instructions: Pour 100 ml boiling salted water over the bulgur and let it soak covered for 15 minutes.
Roast the pepper in the oven at 220 °C for 20 minutes, peel it and roughly chop two thirds of it.
Purée the remaining pepper with most of the walnuts, the pepper paste, pomegranate molasses, olive oil and cumin into muhammara.
Arrange the bulgur, chickpeas, pepper pieces and diced cucumber in a bowl, add the muhammara and sprinkle with the remaining walnuts and parsley.

title: Vegetarian khoresh karafs – Persian celery herb stew with yellow split peas and rice
instructions: Pre-cook the yellow split peas in 400 ml water for 25 minutes.
Dice the onion and fry it in the rapeseed oil with the turmeric for 4 minutes, then cut the celery into pieces and fry for 5 minutes.
Chop the parsley and mint, sweat them briefly and braise with the split peas and their cooking water for 15 minutes.
Cook the basmati rice in twice the amount of salted water for 12 minutes.
Season the stew with lemon juice and salt and serve with the rice.

title: Calabacitas – Mexican courgette and corn vegetables with black beans and light feta
instructions: Chop the onion and garlic and sweat them in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes.
Dice the courgette, add it with the corn and cumin and fry for 6 minutes.
Add the diced tomato and beans, braise for 4 minutes and season with salt and pepper.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan, sprinkle the vegetables with crumbled feta and coriander and serve together.

title: Sopa de tortilla – Mexican tomato soup with pinto beans, avocado and tortilla strips
instructions: Cut the tortilla into thin strips and bake in the oven at 200 °C for 8 minutes until crisp.
Sweat the onion and garlic in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes and briefly toast the chipotle and cumin with them.
Add the tomatoes and stock, simmer for 10 minutes and purée until smooth.
Add the pinto beans and warm for 3 minutes, then season with lime juice and salt.
Serve the soup with diced avocado, tortilla strips and coriander.

title: Solterito – Peruvian bean and corn salad with light feta and olives
instructions: Blanch the broad beans and edamame for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Dice the tomato, finely slice the red onion and halve the olives.
Whisk the lime juice with the olive oil, chilli, salt and pepper.
Mix everything with the corn and dressing, dice the feta and scatter it over the top with the parsley.

title: Quibebe – Brazilian pumpkin chickpea stew with spring onions and rice
instructions: Cook the basmati rice in twice the amount of salted water for 12 minutes.
Sweat the onion and garlic in the olive oil for 3 minutes and stir in the paprika.
Dice the pumpkin and tomato, add them and braise with 150 ml water for 15 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, simmer for 5 minutes and lightly mash the pumpkin.
Season, sprinkle with spring onions and parsley and serve with the rice.

title: Aguadito – Peruvian coriander rice soup with peas, corn and white beans
instructions: Purée the coriander and spinach with 100 ml of the stock until smooth.
Sweat the onion, garlic and diced pepper in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes.
Add the rice and the remaining stock and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the peas, corn, beans and herb purée and leave to steep for 5 minutes.
Season with lime juice, salt and pepper.

title: Tostadas de lentejas – crispy corn tortillas with lentils, red cabbage and avocado
instructions: Cook the lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until tender, drain and season with chipotle, cumin and salt.
Bake the tortillas in the oven at 200 °C for 6 minutes until crisp.
Finely shred the red cabbage and knead it with half of the lime juice and salt, then dice the tomato and onion.
Mash the avocado with the remaining lime juice.
Top the tostadas with avocado, lentils, red cabbage, tomato, onion, soy yoghurt and coriander.

title: Habichuelas guisadas – Dominican red bean stew with pumpkin and rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice in twice the amount of water for 30 minutes.
Finely dice the onion, pepper and garlic and sweat them in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and oregano, add the pumpkin in small cubes and 200 ml water and simmer for 12 minutes.
Add the beans, reduce for 8 minutes until thick and partly mash the pumpkin.
Sprinkle with coriander and serve next to the rice.

title: Revithada – baked chickpeas from Sifnos with onions, lemon and rosemary
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and slice the onions into thin rings.
Mix the chickpeas, onions, rosemary, bay leaf, olive oil and stock in a small baking dish and season with salt.
Braise covered in the oven for 45 minutes until the onions are completely soft.
Finish with lemon juice, pepper and parsley and serve with the bread.

title: Horiatiki with chickpeas – Greek village salad with light feta and olives
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into wedges, the cucumber into thick half moons and the pepper into rings.
Slice the red onion into thin rings and add it to the vegetables with the chickpeas and olives.
Dress with salt, pepper and olive oil.
Place the feta on top in one piece and sprinkle with oregano.

title: Potaje de garbanzos – Spanish chickpea stew with chard, potato and paprika
instructions: Dice the onion, garlic and carrot and sweat them in the olive oil for 4 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, add the diced potato, bay leaf and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and the chard cut into strips and cook for 8 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, mash a few chickpeas and season.

title: Insalata di ceci – Sicilian chickpea salad with orange, fennel and olives
instructions: Peel the orange, cut it into segments and catch the juice.
Slice the fennel and red onion very thinly.
Whisk the orange juice with the lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Toss the chickpeas, fennel, onion, olives and rocket with the dressing and top with the orange segments and toasted pine nuts.

title: Maneštra – Istrian bean, corn and vegetable stew with potatoes
instructions: Dice the onion, garlic, carrot and celery and sweat them in the olive oil for 5 minutes.
Briefly toast the tomato paste, add the diced potato, bay leaf and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the borlotti beans and corn and simmer for a further 10 minutes.
Mash some of the beans, season and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Louvi – Cypriot black-eyed beans with chard, lemon and olive oil
instructions: Wash the chard and cut the stems into pieces and the leaves into wide strips.
Cook the chard stems in salted water for 3 minutes, add the leaves and cook for a further 2 minutes, then drain.
Warm the black-eyed beans and mix them with the chard, diced tomato and chopped garlic.
Dress with lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper and serve with the bread.

title: Kusksu – Maltese bean and pasta soup with broad beans, peas and ricotta
instructions: Finely dice the onion and sweat it in the olive oil for 4 minutes, then briefly toast the tomato paste.
Pour in the stock, bring to the boil and cook the orzo in it for 8 minutes.
Add the broad beans and peas and cook for 4 minutes.
Season, add the ricotta as a dollop and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Puy lentil salad with goat cheese, rocket and walnuts
instructions: Cook the lentils with the thyme in plenty of water for 22 minutes until al dente and drain.
Very finely dice the carrot and red onion and chop the parsley.
Mix the lukewarm lentils with the vegetables, parsley, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Arrange on the rocket, crumble the goat cheese over the top and sprinkle with toasted walnuts.

title: Fregola with chickpeas, cherry tomatoes and rocket
instructions: Chop the onion and garlic and sweat them in the olive oil for 3 minutes.
Add the fregola, toast for 2 minutes and cook risotto-style for 12 minutes, adding the stock gradually.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes and chickpeas and cook for 3 minutes.
Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper and fold in the rocket.

title: Vegan maafe – Senegalese peanut stew with chickpeas, sweet potato and millet
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and let it simmer in 70 ml salted water for 15 minutes.
Chop the onion, garlic and ginger and sweat them with 3 tbsp of the stock in a pot for 4 minutes.
Dice the sweet potato, add it with the tomatoes, the remaining stock and the chilli and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the peanut butter until smooth, add the chickpeas and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Season and serve with the millet.

title: Ewa agoyin – Nigerian black-eyed beans with pepper tomato sauce and wholemeal bread
instructions: Warm the black-eyed beans with a little water and salt and roughly mash them with a fork.
Coarsely purée the pepper, tomato and half of the onion.
Slice the remaining onion into rings and fry it in the rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until dark, then add the chilli.
Add the purée and reduce for 12 minutes until the sauce is thick, then season with salt.
Spoon the sauce over the beans and serve with the bread.

title: Mchuzi wa maharage – Kenyan kidney bean coconut curry with brown rice
instructions: Cook the brown rice in twice the amount of water for 30 minutes.
Fry the onion and garlic in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes until golden and stir in the curry powder and turmeric.
Dice the tomato, add it and reduce to a sauce for 5 minutes.
Add the beans and coconut milk and simmer for 10 minutes until creamy.
Season, sprinkle with coriander and serve with the rice.

title: Moin moin – Nigerian steamed bean cake with tomato cucumber salad
instructions: Soak the black-eyed beans for 2 hours, rub off the skins and rinse.
Purée the beans very finely with the pepper, onion, stock, rapeseed oil, chilli, turmeric and salt.
Pour the mixture into 2 greased heatproof ramekins, cover and steam for 45 minutes.
Dice the tomato and cucumber and mix with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Let the bean cakes rest briefly, turn them out and serve with the salad.

title: Loubia – Moroccan white beans in tomato with cumin and wholemeal bread
instructions: Finely chop the onion and garlic and sweat them in the olive oil for 4 minutes.
Briefly toast the cumin and paprika, add the tomatoes and reduce for 8 minutes.
Add the beans and 50 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Season, sprinkle with the herbs and serve with the bread.

title: Matapa – Mozambican spinach peanut coconut stew with chickpeas and rice
instructions: Cook the basmati rice in twice the amount of salted water for 12 minutes.
Finely grind the peanuts and chop the onion and garlic.
Wilt the onion, garlic and spinach with 50 ml water for 5 minutes and chop finely.
Add the ground peanuts, coconut milk and chickpeas and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with the rice.

title: Katogo – Ugandan plantains with borlotti beans in tomato sauce
instructions: Peel the plantain and cut it into thick slices.
Sweat the onion in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes, add the diced tomato and curry powder and reduce for 4 minutes.
Add the plantain and 150 ml water and braise covered for 15 minutes until soft.
Add the beans and spinach, cook for 4 minutes and season.

title: Adess – Moroccan lentil stew with carrot, cumin and wholemeal couscous
instructions: Chop the onion and garlic, sweat them in the olive oil for 3 minutes and stir in the cumin, paprika and turmeric.
Add the lentils, diced carrot, tomatoes and 350 ml water and simmer for 25 minutes.
Pour 70 ml boiling salted water over the couscous, let it soak for 5 minutes and fluff it up.
Season the stew, sprinkle with coriander and serve with the couscous.

title: Bob chorba – Bulgarian bean soup with mint and paprika
instructions: Dice the onion, carrot, pepper and celery and sweat them in the rapeseed oil for 5 minutes.
Stir in the paprika, add the diced tomato and stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the beans and simmer for a further 10 minutes.
Stir in the dried mint and season with salt and pepper.

title: Shchi – Russian white cabbage soup with white beans and dill
instructions: Dice the onion and carrot and sweat them in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes, then briefly toast the tomato paste.
Cut the white cabbage into thin strips, add it with the diced potato, bay leaf and stock and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the beans, cook for 5 minutes and season.
Serve with a dollop of soy yoghurt and chopped dill.

title: Lencsefőzelék – Hungarian lentil stew with paprika and egg
instructions: Cook the lentils with the bay leaf in the stock for 25 minutes until soft.
Finely dice the onion and sweat it in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes until translucent, then briefly sweat the garlic and flour with it.
Stir in the paprika, stir the roux into the lentils and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper and remove the bay leaf.
Serve with the halved egg and the bread.

title: Krupnik – Polish barley soup with mushrooms and white beans
instructions: Slice the mushrooms and fry them in the rapeseed oil for 5 minutes.
Dice the carrot, celeriac and leek, add them and sweat for 3 minutes.
Add the barley and stock and simmer for 25 minutes, adding the diced potato after 10 minutes.
Add the beans, warm for 5 minutes, season and sprinkle with dill.

title: Ajapsandali – Georgian aubergine vegetable stew with kidney beans and coriander
instructions: Cut the aubergine, pepper, potato and tomato into large cubes and the onion into wedges.
Fry the aubergine and onion in the olive oil for 6 minutes.
Add the pepper, potato, tomato and 100 ml water and braise covered for 20 minutes.
Add the beans, chopped garlic and chilli and braise for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and sprinkle with plenty of coriander and basil.

title: Apple strudel overnight oats with skyr and flaked almonds
instructions: Stir the oats, skyr, milk and cinnamon together in a screw-top jar until smooth.
Finely grate half of the apple and fold it in.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Dice the remaining apple and scatter it over the oats with the raisins and flaked almonds.

title: Vegan mango coconut overnight oats with soy yoghurt and lime
instructions: Stir the oats, soy yoghurt, oat drink and chia seeds together in the jar.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Peel and dice the mango and toss it with the lime juice.
Spoon the mango over the oats and sprinkle with desiccated coconut.

title: Blueberry cheesecake overnight oats with quark and lemon
instructions: Stir the oats with the milk in the jar.
Beat the quark with the maple syrup and lemon zest until smooth and spoon it on top as a second layer.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
In the morning top with the blueberries, lightly crushing a few of them.

title: Gingerbread overnight oats with pear, cocoa and hazelnuts
instructions: Stir the oats, skyr, milk, cocoa and gingerbread spice together in the jar until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Wash the pear and cut it into thin wedges, roughly chop the hazelnuts.
Arrange the pear wedges and hazelnuts on top of the oats.

title: Peanut banana overnight oats with pea protein and oat drink
instructions: Mix the oats, pea protein and chia seeds in the jar.
Stir in the oat drink and half of the peanut butter until there are no lumps left.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Slice the banana, lay it on the oats and drizzle the remaining peanut butter over the top.

title: Kefir cherry overnight oats with almonds and vanilla
instructions: Mix the oats, chia seeds and vanilla in the jar and stir in the kefir.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Halve the cherries and put them on top of the oats.
Toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes and scatter them over the top.

title: Piña colada overnight oats with pineapple, coconut and skyr
instructions: Stir the oats, skyr and coconut milk together in the jar until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Cut the pineapple into small cubes and toss with the lime juice.
Top the oats with the pineapple and sprinkle with desiccated coconut.

title: Matcha chia pudding with almond drink, mango and coconut
instructions: Whisk the matcha with 2 tbsp of the almond drink until smooth, then stir in the rest of the almond drink and the maple syrup.
Stir in the chia seeds, leave to swell for 10 minutes and stir well again.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Spoon the soy yoghurt on top, dice the mango and scatter it over with the desiccated coconut.

title: Apple cinnamon chia pudding with skyr and pecans
instructions: Stir the chia seeds, milk and cinnamon together, leave to swell for 10 minutes and stir again.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Dice the apple and soften it in a non-stick pan with 2 tbsp water for 4 minutes.
Spoon the skyr onto the chia pudding, spread the apple cubes over it and sprinkle with chopped pecans.

title: Pumpkin spice porridge with Hokkaido pumpkin, milk and pecans
instructions: Wash and deseed the pumpkin, dice it with the skin on and cook in a little water for 10 minutes until soft, then purée finely.
Bring the oats to the boil with the milk and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Stir in the pumpkin purée, spices and maple syrup and simmer for 1 more minute.
Pour into a bowl and sprinkle with chopped pecans.

title: Savoury oat porridge with spinach, poached egg and feta
instructions: Bring the oats to the boil with the stock and simmer for 5 minutes until creamy.
Stir in the baby spinach until it wilts and season with pepper.
Slide the egg into simmering water and poach for 4 minutes.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the egg and serve with crumbled feta, halved cherry tomatoes and chilli flakes.

title: Millet porridge with orange, dates and hemp seeds
instructions: Rinse the millet in a sieve under hot water.
Bring the millet to the boil with the almond drink, cinnamon and finely chopped dates, cover and leave to swell over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Peel the orange and cut out the segments.
Pour the porridge into a bowl and top with the orange segments, almond butter and hemp seeds.

title: Buckwheat porridge with blueberries, skyr and almond butter
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat and bring it to the boil with the milk and vanilla.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes until soft, stirring occasionally.
Stir in half of the blueberries until they start to burst.
Pour into a bowl and top with the skyr, the remaining blueberries and the almond butter.

title: Quinoa breakfast porridge with coconut milk, mango and cashews
instructions: Rinse the quinoa thoroughly in a sieve under hot water.
Bring the quinoa to the boil with the coconut milk, soy milk and cardamom, cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes until creamy.
Peel and dice the mango, roughly chop the cashews and toast them briefly in a dry pan.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the mango and cashews.

title: Amaranth porridge with plums, yoghurt and walnuts
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with the milk and 50 ml water, cover and leave to swell over low heat for 25 minutes.
Stone and quarter the plums and stew them with cinnamon and 2 tbsp water for 5 minutes until soft.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and add the yoghurt on top.
Serve with the plums and chopped walnuts.

title: Protein semolina pudding with berry compote and vanilla
instructions: Simmer the berries in a small pan with 2 tbsp water for 5 minutes to a compote.
Bring the milk to the boil with the vanilla, sprinkle in the semolina and simmer for 3 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Take the pan off the heat, let cool for 1 minute and stir in the protein powder until smooth.
Spoon the semolina into a bowl, top with the compote and dust with cinnamon.

title: Vegetarian congee with shiitake, egg and spring onions
instructions: Wash the rice and bring it to the boil with the stock and the ginger cut into strips.
Simmer over low heat for 40 minutes until thick, stirring often.
Slice the shiitake and add after 25 minutes, boil the egg for 7 minutes and peel it.
Season the congee with soy sauce, pour into a bowl and serve with the halved egg, spring onions and sesame oil.

title: Mocha protein porridge with espresso, cocoa and banana
instructions: Bring the oats to the boil with the milk and espresso and simmer for 4 minutes until creamy.
Take off the heat, let cool for 1 minute, then stir in the protein powder and cocoa until smooth.
Slice the banana.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the banana slices and cocoa nibs.

title: Overnight spelt flakes with kiwi, skyr and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Stir the spelt flakes, skyr, milk and maple syrup together in the jar until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Peel the kiwis and cut them into slices or cubes.
Top the flakes with the kiwi and sprinkle with pumpkin seeds.

title: Rhubarb strawberry overnight oats with vanilla skyr
instructions: Cut the rhubarb into pieces and simmer with the maple syrup and 2 tbsp water for 6 minutes to a compote, then let cool.
Stir the oats, milk, half of the skyr and the vanilla together in the jar and spoon the compote on top.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Top with the remaining skyr and quartered strawberries.

title: Vegan peach chia pudding with soy yoghurt and hemp seeds
instructions: Stir the chia seeds with the soy milk and maple syrup, leave to swell for 10 minutes and stir again.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Wash and stone the peach and cut it into wedges.
Spoon the soy yoghurt onto the pudding, lay the peach wedges on top and sprinkle with hemp seeds.

title: Toasted oat porridge with figs, tahini and cinnamon
instructions: Toast the oats in a dry pan for 3 minutes, stirring, until golden brown.
Pour in the milk and cinnamon and simmer for 4 minutes until creamy.
Wash and quarter the figs.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the skyr and figs and drizzle with tahini.

title: Vegan caramelised banana porridge with walnuts and oat drink
instructions: Bring the oats to the boil with the oat drink, linseed and cinnamon and simmer for 4 minutes until creamy.
Halve the banana lengthways and caramelise it in a non-stick pan with the maple syrup for 2 minutes per side.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and add the soy yoghurt.
Lay the caramelised banana on top and sprinkle with chopped walnuts.

title: Red berry compote overnight oats with redcurrants, cherries and skyr
instructions: Bring the redcurrants and cherries to the boil with the maple syrup and 3 tbsp water, thicken for 1 minute with the starch mixed in a little water and let cool.
Stir the oats, milk and skyr together in the jar.
Spoon the red berry compote on top as a layer.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.

title: Vegan chai overnight oats with soy milk, apricots and pistachios
instructions: Stir the oats, soy milk, soy yoghurt, maple syrup and chai spice together in the jar.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Wash and stone the apricots and cut them into wedges, roughly chop the pistachios.
Top the oats with the apricots and pistachios.

title: Asparagus frittata with peas, ricotta and mint
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C and cut the asparagus into 3 cm pieces.
Fry the asparagus and peas in the olive oil in an ovenproof pan for 4 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper, pour over the vegetables and dot the ricotta on top.
Bake in the oven for 10 to 12 minutes until set, sprinkle with mint and serve with the bread.

title: Light loco moco – Hawaiian rice bowl with beef patty, fried egg and mushroom gravy
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions and shape the mince with salt and pepper into a flat patty.
Fry the patty in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes per side until cooked through, remove and fry the egg sunny side up in the pan juices.
Fry the sliced mushrooms for 3 minutes, add the stock and soy sauce and thicken with the cornflour mixed with a little water.
Put the rice in a bowl, top with the patty, mushroom gravy and fried egg and sprinkle with spring onion.

title: Egg white omelette with broccoli, tomatoes and chives
instructions: Divide the broccoli into small florets and blanch in salted water for 3 minutes.
Whisk the egg whites and the egg with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan, pour in the egg mixture, scatter over the broccoli and halved tomatoes and let set covered for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with chives and serve with the wholemeal bread.

title: Changua – Colombian milk and egg soup with spring onions, coriander and wholemeal bread
instructions: Bring the milk to the boil with 100 ml water, salt and the white parts of the spring onions and simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Slide the eggs one at a time into the simmering milk and poach for 4 minutes.
Cut the bread into cubes and put them in a soup bowl.
Ladle the soup with the eggs over the top and sprinkle with spring onion greens, coriander and pepper.

title: Poached eggs on pea and mint smash with sourdough
instructions: Cook the peas for 3 minutes, drain and roughly mash with the olive oil, lemon juice, mint, salt and pepper.
Slide the eggs one at a time into simmering water and poach for 4 minutes.
Toast the sourdough and spread the pea smash on it.
Place the eggs on top and sprinkle with crumbled feta and pepper.

title: Migas – Tex-Mex scrambled eggs with corn tortilla strips, pepper and salsa
instructions: Cut the tortilla into thin strips and fry them in the rapeseed oil for 2 minutes until crisp.
Dice the pepper and half of the onion, add and fry for 3 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with salt and chilli, pour in and let set while stirring, fold in the cheddar.
Finely dice the tomato and remaining onion, mix with the coriander into a salsa and serve on top of the migas.

title: Baleadas – Honduran tortilla with bean purée, scrambled egg, avocado and feta
instructions: Heat the beans with the cumin, salt and 2 tbsp water in a small pan and mash to a purée.
Whisk the egg and cook it in the rapeseed oil into scrambled egg.
Warm the tortilla in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side.
Spread the bean purée over the tortilla, top with the scrambled egg, avocado slices and crumbled feta and fold in half.

title: Pumpkin shakshuka with Hokkaido pumpkin, pepper and yoghurt
instructions: Wash and deseed the pumpkin and cut it into small cubes with the skin on, dice the pepper and onion.
Fry the vegetables in the olive oil for 6 minutes and briefly toast the spices with them.
Add the tomatoes, season with salt and simmer for 10 minutes until the pumpkin is soft.
Make two wells, slide the eggs in and let them set covered for 6 minutes.
Serve with dollops of yoghurt and coriander.

title: Eggs Kejriwal – Indian chilli cheese toast with fried egg and cucumber
instructions: Lightly toast the bread slices and spread them thinly with mustard.
Finely chop the chilli, scatter it over the toasts with the cheddar and melt under the grill for 2 minutes.
Fry the eggs in the rapeseed oil until the whites are set.
Place one fried egg on each toast, sprinkle with coriander, salt and pepper and serve with cucumber slices.

title: Eggah – Egyptian herb omelette with parsley, onion and wholemeal pita
instructions: Finely dice the onion and chop the parsley.
Whisk the eggs with the parsley, onion, spices, salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a small pan, pour in the mixture and let it set covered over low heat for 8 minutes, then turn and fry for 2 more minutes.
Cut into pieces and serve with tomato slices and the pita.

title: Oeufs cocotte with spinach, leek and wholemeal bread
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and grease an ovenproof ramekin with the butter.
Slice the leek into fine rings and sweat with the spinach in a pan for 3 minutes, season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Put the vegetables into the ramekin, make a hollow, crack in the eggs and spoon the soured cream around them.
Bake in a water bath in the oven for 12 to 14 minutes until the whites are set and serve with the bread.

title: Kai jeow – Thai omelette with jasmine rice, cucumber and sriracha
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Beat the eggs vigorously with the fish sauce and 1 tbsp water until frothy.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a small wok until very hot, pour in the eggs and cook for 2 minutes per side until golden and puffy.
Place the omelette on the rice, sprinkle with spring onion and serve with cucumber slices and sriracha.

title: Akuri – Parsi scrambled eggs with tomato, chilli and wholemeal chapati
instructions: Finely chop the onion, tomato, chilli and ginger.
Sweat the onion in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes until translucent, then fry the ginger, chilli, turmeric and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the tomato and cook for 2 minutes until soft.
Pour in the whisked eggs and let them set softly over low heat while stirring, then serve with coriander and the warmed chapati.

title: Broccoli cheddar egg muffins with pepper to go
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and line 4 holes of a muffin tin with paper cases.
Divide the broccoli into very small florets, finely dice the pepper and divide between the cases.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, chives, salt and pepper, pour over and sprinkle with the cheddar.
Bake for 20 minutes, let cool briefly and eat warm or cold, they keep chilled for 3 days.

title: Breakfast burrito with scrambled eggs, sweet potato and spinach in a wholemeal wrap
instructions: Peel the sweet potato, cut into small cubes and fry covered in the rapeseed oil with paprika and cumin for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the spinach and let it wilt.
Whisk the eggs, add them to the pan and let them set for 2 minutes while stirring, then season with salt and pepper.
Warm the wrap, add the filling and feta, roll up tightly and cut in half.

title: Baked eggs in portobello mushrooms with spinach and wholemeal toast
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, twist the stalks out of the mushrooms and brush the caps with olive oil.
Wilt the spinach with chopped garlic in a pan and fill the mushrooms with it.
Crack one egg into each mushroom, sprinkle with cheese and bake for 12 to 14 minutes.
Season with pepper and serve with the wholemeal toast.

title: Tigrillo – Ecuadorian plantain and egg scramble with cheese and coriander
instructions: Peel the plantain, cut into pieces and boil in salted water for 15 minutes until soft.
Drain and roughly mash, finely dice the onion and fry in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes.
Add the plantain, whisk the eggs over it and let them set while stirring.
Fold in the cheese in small pieces until it melts and serve sprinkled with coriander.

title: Egg in a hole with tomato avocado salad
instructions: Cut a 6 cm circle out of the centre of each bread slice.
Toast the bread slices and circles in the rapeseed oil for 1 minute, turn them and crack one egg into each hole.
Cover and fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set and season with salt and pepper.
Halve the tomatoes, dice the avocado, mix with the rocket, lime juice and salt and serve alongside.

title: Sweet potato frittata with spinach and goat cheese
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, peel the sweet potato and cut it into thin slices.
Fry the sweet potato in the olive oil in an ovenproof pan covered for 8 minutes until soft, add the spinach and let it wilt.
Whisk the eggs with thyme, salt and pepper, pour over and dot with pieces of goat cheese.
Bake in the oven for 10 minutes until set and serve cut into pieces.

title: Light croque madame with turkey breast, fried egg and lamb’s lettuce
instructions: Bring the milk to the boil with the cornflour, nutmeg and pepper while stirring until thickened and stir in half of the cheese.
Spread one toast slice with mustard, top with the turkey, place the second slice on top and spread with the sauce and remaining cheese.
Bake in the oven at 220 °C for 8 minutes until golden, frying the egg sunny side up in the meantime.
Place the fried egg on the toast and serve with lamb’s lettuce.

title: Stuffed sweet potato with baked egg, kale and feta
instructions: Halve the sweet potato lengthways and bake at 200 °C for 30 minutes until soft.
Finely shred the kale, sweat it in the olive oil for 3 minutes and season with salt.
Press the flesh of each half down a little, add the kale and crack one egg into each half.
Bake for another 10 to 12 minutes until the whites are set and sprinkle with feta and chilli flakes.

title: Tortang talong – Filipino aubergine omelette with tomato salad and brown rice
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions and roast the aubergine in the oven at 220 °C or over a gas flame for 15 minutes until soft.
Peel the aubergine, leaving the stem on, and press the flesh flat with a fork.
Whisk the eggs with crushed garlic, salt and pepper, dip the aubergine in it and fry in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes per side, pouring the remaining egg over it.
Dice the tomato and onion, season with salt and serve with the rice alongside the omelette.

title: Vegan tofu scramble with kale, sweet potato and black beans
instructions: Peel the sweet potato, dice it small and fry covered in the rapeseed oil for 8 minutes until soft.
Crumble the tofu roughly with a fork, add it to the pan with the turmeric and paprika and fry for 4 minutes.
Finely shred the kale and fry it with the beans for 3 minutes.
Season with nutritional yeast, salt and pepper and serve.

title: Egg crêpe wrap with turkey breast, spinach and cream cheese
instructions: Whisk the eggs with 2 tbsp water, salt and pepper.
Spread thinly in a large non-stick pan with the rapeseed oil and cook for 2 minutes per side to an egg crêpe.
Spread the crêpe with cream cheese, top with spinach, turkey breast and pepper strips and roll up tightly.
Cut in half diagonally and serve with the wholemeal bread.

title: Jianbing – Chinese breakfast crêpe with egg, herbs and cucumber
instructions: Mix both flours with 90 ml water and a pinch of salt to a thin batter.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a large pan, spread the batter thinly and cook for 1 minute.
Crack the egg straight onto the crêpe, whisk and spread it, scatter over the spring onions, coriander and sesame and turn once the egg has set.
Brush with hoisin sauce, lay cucumber sticks on top, fold into a parcel and cut in half.

title: Protein pancakes with skyr, banana and strawberries
instructions: Grind the oats finely and blend with the egg, 80 g skyr, half of the banana and the baking powder to a smooth batter.
Brush a non-stick pan thinly with rapeseed oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes per side.
Slice the remaining banana and the strawberries.
Stack the pancakes and serve with the remaining skyr, banana and strawberries.

title: Gluten-free buckwheat pancakes with apple and cinnamon quark
instructions: Mix the buckwheat flour, egg, milk and baking powder to a thick batter and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
Cut the apple into thin slices and fry in the pan with 1 tsp rapeseed oil for 3 minutes.
Cook 3 pancakes from the batter, 2 minutes per side each.
Stir the quark with cinnamon and maple syrup until smooth and serve with the apple slices alongside the pancakes.

title: Cong you bing – Chinese spring onion pancake with egg and cucumber
instructions: Knead the flour with a pinch of salt and 40 ml hot water until smooth and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Roll the dough out thinly, brush with sesame oil, sprinkle with finely sliced spring onions, roll up, coil into a spiral and roll flat again.
Fry the pancake in the rapeseed oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Whisk the egg, pour it into the pan, press the pancake on top and fry for 1 minute, then cut into pieces and serve with cucumber and soy sauce.

title: Vegan oat banana pancakes with linseed and berries
instructions: Stir the linseed with 3 tbsp water and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
Blend the oats, banana, soy milk, baking powder and linseed to a thick batter.
Cook 4 small pancakes in a non-stick pan with the rapeseed oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Briefly warm the berries in a small pan and serve them with the soy yoghurt alongside the pancakes.

title: Chocolate protein waffles with quark and cherries
instructions: Grind the oats finely and mix with the egg, 80 g quark, cocoa, maple syrup and baking powder until smooth.
Preheat the waffle iron and brush it with rapeseed oil.
Bake 2 waffles from the batter for 4 minutes each.
Serve with the remaining quark and the halved cherries.

title: Savoury courgette feta waffles with yoghurt dip
instructions: Coarsely grate the courgette, salt it, leave for 5 minutes and squeeze out firmly.
Mix the courgette with the eggs, flour, crumbled feta and pepper.
Brush the waffle iron with rapeseed oil and bake 2 waffles from the batter for 5 minutes each until golden.
Stir the yoghurt with dill and salt and serve with the waffles.

title: Light Kaiserschmarrn with quark and warm blueberries
instructions: Separate the eggs, mix the yolks with the quark, flour, milk and vanilla, whisk the whites until stiff and fold them in.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan, add the batter and cook over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Turn it over, tear it into pieces with two spatulas and fry for 3 more minutes until golden.
Warm the blueberries in a small pan for 2 minutes, dust the pancake pieces with cinnamon and serve with the berries.

title: Spelt crêpes with ricotta and berries
instructions: Whisk the flour, egg and milk to a smooth, thin batter and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Brush a non-stick pan thinly with rapeseed oil and cook 2 thin crêpes for 1 minute per side each.
Stir the ricotta with the maple syrup until smooth and spread it over the crêpes.
Scatter the berries on top, fold the crêpes into triangles and serve.

title: Uttapam – South Indian rice and lentil pancake with tomato and onion
instructions: Soak the urad lentils overnight, drain and blend with the rice flour, soy yoghurt, 80 ml water and salt to a thick batter.
Finely chop the tomato, onion, chilli and coriander.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a pan, spread the batter into a thick round, scatter the vegetables on top and press down, cook for 4 minutes, turn and cook for 3 more minutes.
Stir the coconut with 2 tbsp water and a pinch of salt into a quick chutney and serve alongside.

title: Light tapsilog – Filipino beef with garlic rice and fried egg
instructions: Cut the steak into thin strips and marinate with the soy sauce, lime juice, half of the garlic and pepper for 10 minutes.
Cook the rice, toast the remaining garlic in a little rapeseed oil until golden and fry the rice in it for 2 minutes.
Fry the beef in the remaining oil over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until cooked through and fry the egg sunny side up.
Arrange on a plate with the garlic rice, fried egg, tomato and cucumber.

title: Swiss chard scrambled eggs with feta and pine nuts on wholemeal bread
instructions: Wash the chard, finely dice the stalks and slice the leaves into strips, toast the pine nuts in a dry pan.
Fry the stalks with the garlic in the olive oil for 3 minutes, add the leaves and let them wilt for 1 minute.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper, pour in and let them set until creamy.
Serve on the toasted bread and sprinkle with the feta, pine nuts and lemon zest.

title: Bubble and squeak with Brussels sprouts, potatoes and poached eggs
instructions: Trim the Brussels sprouts, cook in salted water for 6 minutes and roughly chop.
Roughly crush the potatoes, mix with the sprouts, finely diced onion, salt and pepper and shape into a flat cake.
Fry in the rapeseed oil over medium heat for 5 minutes per side until crisp and brown.
Poach the eggs in simmering water for 4 minutes, place them on the cake and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Light Dutch baby with berries and skyr
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220 °C with a small cast-iron pan inside.
Blend the eggs, flour, milk and vanilla to a smooth batter.
Melt the butter in the hot pan, pour in the batter and bake for 15 minutes until well puffed and golden.
Briefly warm the berries, spoon them into the centre with the skyr and drizzle with maple syrup.

title: Koko – Ghanaian millet porridge with ginger, peanuts and yoghurt
instructions: Grind the millet finely and stir it with 100 ml cold water until smooth.
Bring 200 ml water to the boil with the grated ginger, clove and chilli, stir in the millet mixture and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Sweeten with the maple syrup and pour into a bowl.
Top with the yoghurt and serve with chopped peanuts and banana slices.

title: Pumpkin waffles with skyr, pear and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Dice the pumpkin, steam for 10 minutes until soft and purée finely.
Mix the pumpkin purée with the flour, egg, milk, cinnamon and baking powder to a thick batter.
Brush the waffle iron with rapeseed oil and cook 2 waffles for 4 minutes each until golden.
Cut the pear into wedges and serve on the waffles with the skyr and pumpkin seeds.

title: Mote pillo – Ecuadorian corn scrambled eggs with spring onions and avocado
instructions: Slice the spring onions and sweat the white parts in the rapeseed oil with the paprika and cumin for 2 minutes.
Add the corn and fry for 3 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper, pour in and let set until creamy while stirring.
Serve with the spring onion greens, coriander and avocado slices.

title: Kaşarlı tost – Turkish cheese toast with egg, tomato, cucumber and olives
instructions: Hard-boil the egg for 9 minutes, cool and peel.
Grate the kaşar, put it between the toast slices and toast in a sandwich maker or a covered pan for 4 minutes until golden.
Slice the tomato and cucumber and quarter the egg.
Halve the toast diagonally and serve with the vegetables, egg, olives and pul biber.

title: Spinach crêpes with cottage cheese, cherry tomatoes and herbs
instructions: Blend the spinach with the milk, egg, flour and a pinch of salt until smooth and let rest for 5 minutes.
Brush a non-stick pan thinly with rapeseed oil and cook 2 thin crêpes from the batter for 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Mix the cottage cheese with the chopped herbs, salt and pepper and halve the tomatoes.
Fill the crêpes with the cottage cheese and tomatoes and fold them over.

title: Mushroom thyme toast with poached eggs and rocket
instructions: Slice the mushrooms and fry them in the olive oil with garlic and thyme for 5 minutes until golden, season with salt and pepper.
Poach the eggs in simmering water for 4 minutes.
Toast the bread and spread it thinly with the cream cheese.
Top the bread slices with rocket, the mushrooms and one egg each and sprinkle with pepper.

title: Cottage cheese pancakes with apple and cinnamon
instructions: Mix the cottage cheese, egg, flour, baking powder and a pinch of cinnamon to a thick batter.
Brush a non-stick pan thinly with rapeseed oil and cook 3 pancakes for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.
Cut the apple into thin wedges and fry in the pan with cinnamon for 2 minutes.
Serve the pancakes with the apples and drizzle with maple syrup.

title: Egg bánh mì with pickled carrots, cucumber and coriander
instructions: Cut the carrot into fine strips and leave to marinate with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the soy sauce and fry in the rapeseed oil to a thin omelette, then roll up and slice into strips.
Split the baguette, toast briefly and spread with the mayonnaise.
Fill with the omelette, carrots, cucumber strips, coriander and chilli.

title: Savoury oat porridge with fried egg, leek and mountain cheese
instructions: Slice the leek into fine rings and sweat in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes.
Add the oats and stock and simmer for 5 minutes while stirring until creamy, stir in the spinach.
Fry the egg sunny side up in a small pan.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, sprinkle with the cheese, place the fried egg on top and season with pepper.

title: Breakfast smørrebrød with egg, beetroot and horseradish skyr
instructions: Hard-boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool, peel and slice.
Mix the skyr with the horseradish and a pinch of salt and spread on the rye bread.
Slice the beetroot thinly and lay it on the bread with the egg slices.
Sprinkle with cress and pepper.

title: Potato rösti waffles with smoked salmon and herb skyr
instructions: Peel the potatoes, grate them coarsely and squeeze them out firmly in a cloth.
Mix with the egg, salt and pepper.
Brush the waffle iron with rapeseed oil and cook 2 waffles from the mixture for 6 to 8 minutes each until crisp.
Mix the skyr with the chopped herbs and serve on the waffles with the smoked salmon.

title: Kimchijeon – Korean kimchi pancake with tofu and radish
instructions: Roughly chop the kimchi, finely crumble the tofu and slice the spring onion.
Mix the rice flour with the egg and 50 ml cold water until smooth and fold in the kimchi, tofu and spring onion.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a pan, spread the batter flat and fry for 4 minutes per side until crisp.
Cut the radish into fine matchsticks and serve with the pancake cut into pieces and soy sauce for dipping.

title: Açaí bowl with berries, banana and hemp seeds
instructions: Let the açaí purée soften for 5 minutes.
Blend with half of the banana, the soy yoghurt and half of the berries to a thick cream.
Spoon into a bowl and slice the remaining banana.
Top with rows of banana slices, the remaining berries, the oats and hemp seeds.

title: Skyr bowl with roasted apricots, pistachios and honey
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, halve and stone the apricots.
Roast the apricots cut side up with half of the honey and the cardamom for 12 minutes.
Toast the oats in a dry pan for 2 minutes and chop the pistachios.
Put the skyr into a bowl, top with the apricots, oats and pistachios and drizzle with the remaining honey.

title: Sweet quinoa breakfast bowl with yoghurt, berries and almonds
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water, cook in 100 ml water for 15 minutes and let cool.
Mix the quinoa with the maple syrup, cinnamon and vanilla.
Put the yoghurt into a bowl and pile the quinoa on top.
Scatter with the berries and chopped almonds.

title: Savoury breakfast bowl with sweet potato, egg, avocado and spinach
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210 °C, dice the sweet potato, toss with the olive oil and paprika and roast for 20 minutes.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes until jammy, cool and peel.
Put the spinach into a bowl and arrange the sweet potato, halved tomatoes and avocado slices on top.
Halve the eggs, place them on top and sprinkle with pumpkin seeds, salt and pepper.

title: Japanese salmon rice breakfast bowl with egg, cucumber and nori
instructions: Wash the rice and cook it with 75 ml water for 15 minutes.
Fry the salmon in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes per side and flake it.
Boil the egg for 7 minutes, peel and halve it and thinly slice the cucumber.
Put the rice into a bowl, top with the salmon, egg and cucumber, drizzle with soy sauce and sprinkle with nori strips, sesame and spring onions.

title: Mediterranean bulgur breakfast bowl with egg, tomato, cucumber and za'atar
