Mix with 10 g of the desiccated coconut, the cream cheese, coconut milk and matcha into a mouldable mixture.
Chill for 30 minutes, shape 4 balls and roll them in the remaining desiccated coconut.
Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days and enjoy cold.

title: Chaffles – cheese waffles with avocado and fried egg
instructions: Preheat the waffle iron and whisk 2 eggs with the mozzarella, almond flour and a pinch of salt.
Grease the waffle iron with a little butter and bake 2 waffles from the batter for 4 minutes each until golden.
Fry the remaining egg in the rest of the butter until the white is set.
Top the waffles with avocado slices, rocket and the fried egg and sprinkle with chilli flakes.

title: Salmon in coconut curry sauce with spinach
instructions: Chop the ginger and garlic and sweat in the coconut oil with the curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk, bring to the boil, add the salmon in pieces and cook gently covered for 8 minutes until cooked through.
Fold in the spinach, let it wilt and season with the lime juice and salt.
Serve sprinkled with coriander.

title: Cauliflower mac and cheese with chicken thigh
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, cut the cauliflower into small florets, parboil in salted water for 5 minutes and drain well.
Dice the chicken and fry in the butter for 6 to 8 minutes until cooked through.
Heat the cream with the cream cheese, mustard, nutmeg and three quarters of the cheddar until smooth and mix with the cauliflower and chicken.
Fill into a small dish, sprinkle with the remaining cheddar and paprika and bake for 15 minutes until golden.

title: Buffalo chicken wings with blue cheese dip and celery sticks
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220 °C, pat the wings dry, season with paprika, garlic powder and salt and bake on a rack for 40 minutes until crisp and cooked through.
Melt the butter, stir with the chilli sauce and toss the hot wings in it.
Mash the blue cheese and stir with the sour cream and mayonnaise into a dip.
Cut the celery into sticks and serve with the wings and dip.

title: Cod with mustard dill sauce, broccoli and almonds
instructions: Divide the broccoli into florets and steam for 5 minutes, then toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan.
Salt the cod and fry in the oil and half of the butter for 3 to 4 minutes per side until cooked through.
Briefly bring the crème fraîche to the boil with the mustard and remaining butter and stir in the chopped dill.
Serve the fish with the broccoli and sauce and sprinkle with the almonds.

title: Baked sardines with parsley garlic oil and fennel salad
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220 °C, rub the sardines with 1 tsp oil and salt and bake for 12 minutes until cooked through.
Finely chop the parsley and garlic and stir with half of the remaining oil.
Shave the fennel very thinly and mix with the olives, toasted pine nuts, lemon juice and remaining oil.
Drizzle the sardines with the herb oil and serve with the fennel salad.

title: Tuna patties with herb remoulade and cucumber salad
instructions: Squeeze the tuna well and knead with the egg, almond flour, parsley, salt and pepper.
Shape 4 patties and fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Finely chop the gherkin and capers and stir with the mayonnaise, yoghurt and dill into the remoulade.
Shave the cucumber into thin slices, salt them and serve with the patties and the remoulade.

title: Goat cheese salad with walnuts, raspberries and lamb’s lettuce
instructions: Roughly chop the walnuts and toast in a dry pan for 3 minutes.
Cut the goat cheese into 4 slices, sprinkle with thyme and sear in a non-stick pan for 1 minute per side.
Whisk the oil with the lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper and dress the lamb’s lettuce with it.
Top the salad with the goat cheese, raspberries and walnuts.

title: Peanut butter chocolate cups with cream cheese filling and 85 % dark chocolate
instructions: Melt the chocolate over a water bath and stir the peanut butter with the cream cheese until smooth.
Divide half of it between 2 mini muffin cases and chill for 10 minutes.
Add the peanut cream on top, cover with the remaining chocolate and sprinkle with sea salt.
Leave to set in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.

title: Eggs in Dijon cream sauce with leaf spinach
instructions: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until firm, refresh in cold water and peel.
Finely dice the shallot, sweat in half of the butter until translucent, add the cream and 3 tbsp water, simmer for 2 minutes and stir in the mustard.
Wilt the spinach in the remaining butter and season with nutmeg and salt.
Halve the eggs, warm them in the mustard sauce and serve with the spinach and chives.

title: Crispy tofu cubes with avocado lime dip, radishes and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210 °C, press the tofu well, dice it, toss with the rapeseed oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt and bake for 25 minutes until crisp.
Mash the avocado with the olive oil, lime juice, coriander and salt into a creamy dip.
Quarter the radishes, toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan and serve everything with the tofu and dip.

title: Pulled chicken in lettuce cups with avocado and chipotle mayo
instructions: Rub the chicken with the oil, cumin, half of the chipotle powder and salt and braise covered in a small pot with 100 ml water for 35 minutes until cooked through and tender.
Shred the meat with two forks and mix with the braising liquid.
Stir the mayonnaise with the sour cream, remaining chipotle and lime juice and slice the avocado.
Fill the chicken into 4 lettuce leaves and top with the avocado, onion rings, chipotle mayo and coriander.

title: Aubergine rolls with goat cheese, walnut and rocket
instructions: Cut the aubergine lengthwise into 6 thin slices, salt them, leave for 10 minutes and pat dry.
Brush the slices with three quarters of the oil and grill in a grill pan for 3 minutes per side until soft.
Stir the goat cheese with the chopped walnuts and thyme, spread over the slices and roll up.
Arrange the rolls on the rocket and drizzle with the remaining oil, lemon juice and chilli flakes.

title: Beef mince mushroom skewers with chimichurri and leaf salad
instructions: Knead the beef mince with the finely chopped onion, salt and pepper and shape into 6 balls.
Thread the balls alternately with the mushrooms onto 3 skewers, brush with 1 tsp oil and cook in a grill pan for 10 to 12 minutes until the meat is cooked through.
Finely chop the parsley, oregano and garlic and stir with the remaining oil, lemon juice, chilli and salt into chimichurri.
Serve the skewers with the salad and drizzle with the chimichurri.

title: Florentine tofu scramble with baby spinach, cherry tomatoes and nutritional yeast
instructions: Roughly crumble the tofu with a fork and mix it with the turmeric and nutritional yeast.
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan and fry the tofu for 5 minutes, turning it often.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, add them with the spinach and cook for 2 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Season with salt and pepper and serve straight away.

title: Tofu scramble with peppers, mushrooms and chives
instructions: Dice the pepper, slice the mushrooms and roughly crumble the tofu.
Heat the rapeseed oil and fry the mushrooms and pepper briskly for 4 minutes.
Add the tofu, turmeric and nutritional yeast and fry for another 4 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with chopped chives.

title: Mexican tofu scramble with black beans and tomato salsa
instructions: Finely dice the tomatoes and onion and mix with the lime juice, coriander and a little salt to make the salsa.
Dice the pepper and toast it in a dry non-stick pan for 3 minutes.
Crumble in the tofu, season with the cumin, paprika and nutritional yeast and fry for 4 minutes.
Fold in the beans, warm for 2 minutes and serve with the salsa.

title: Smoky tempeh strips with roasted tomatoes, mushrooms and spinach
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, halve the tomatoes and roast them on a tray for 15 minutes.
Cut the tempeh into thin strips and marinate with the tamari and smoked paprika.
Fry the tempeh in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes per side until crisp, then remove.
Fry the mushrooms in the pan for 4 minutes, wilt the spinach for 1 minute and serve everything with the tomatoes.

title: Tofu shakshuka with edamame, peppers and cumin
instructions: Dice the onion, garlic and pepper and steam them in a small pan with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, cumin and paprika and simmer for 8 minutes until thick.
Cut the tofu into 4 thick slices, nestle them into the sauce with the edamame and leave covered for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with salt, pepper and parsley and serve in the pan.

title: Chickpea flour omelette with silken tofu, courgette and herbs
instructions: Blend the chickpea flour, silken tofu, pea protein, turmeric and 60 ml water until smooth.
Finely grate the courgette, slice the spring onion into rings and fold both into the batter with the herbs.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan, pour in the batter and cook covered over medium heat for 6 minutes until set.
Flip, cook for another 3 minutes and serve with kala namak, salt and pepper.

title: Savoury lupin skillet with crispy courgette, spinach and smoked tofu
instructions: Coarsely grate the courgette, squeeze it out well and finely dice the onion.
Dice the smoked tofu and fry in the olive oil for 3 minutes, then fry the onion and courgette with it for 4 minutes.
Add the lupins, paprika and thyme and heat for 3 minutes.
Fold in the spinach until it wilts and season with salt and pepper.

title: Green tofu breakfast pan with broccoli, peas and mint
instructions: Cut the broccoli into small florets and blanch them with the peas in boiling water for 3 minutes.
Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in the olive oil for 6 minutes until golden all over.
Drain the vegetables, add to the tofu and toss with the nutritional yeast and lemon juice for 2 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper and chopped mint.

title: Tofu menemen with pointed peppers, tomatoes and pul biber
instructions: Slice the pointed pepper into rings and fry it in the olive oil in a small pan for 4 minutes until soft.
Dice the tomatoes, add them and cook down for 5 minutes.
Crumble in the tofu roughly, stir in the nutritional yeast and pul biber and cook for 4 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve in the pan sprinkled with parsley.

title: Tempeh hash with Brussels sprouts, red onions and mustard herbs
instructions: Trim and halve the Brussels sprouts, parboil them in salted water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Cut the tempeh into small cubes and the onion into wedges.
Toast the tempeh in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes, then fry the sprouts, onion and edamame with it for 5 minutes.
Stir the mustard with 2 tbsp water, toss it through with the thyme and marjoram and season.

title: Silken tofu frittata with asparagus, peas and chervil
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C and cut the asparagus into 3 cm pieces.
Blend the silken tofu, pea protein, chickpea flour, nutritional yeast and turmeric until smooth.
Put the asparagus and peas into a small baking dish lined with baking paper and pour the mixture over them.
Bake for 25 minutes until set, rest briefly and serve with kala namak and chervil.

title: Tofu bhurji with cauliflower, tomatoes and curry leaves
instructions: Chop the cauliflower very finely, dice the onion and tomatoes and grate the ginger.
Heat the rapeseed oil, toast the mustard seeds and curry leaves for 30 seconds, then fry the onion and ginger for 3 minutes.
Add the cauliflower and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Crumble in the tofu, season with turmeric, nutritional yeast and salt, fry for 4 minutes and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Baked mushrooms filled with herby tofu cream and spinach
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, twist out the mushroom stalks and chop them finely.
Blend the tofu with the nutritional yeast, garlic, lemon juice and herbs until creamy, then fold in the stalks and chopped spinach.
Fill the mushroom caps with the cream and bake on a lined tray for 18 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve warm.

title: Korean-style rolled tofu omelette with carrot and spring onion
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, pea protein, chickpea flour, turmeric and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Finely grate the carrot, finely chop the spring onion and spinach and stir them into the mixture.
Spread the sesame oil in a square or small pan, pour in the mixture thinly and cook over low heat for 6 minutes until set.
Carefully roll up from one side, cook for 2 more minutes and cut into 6 slices.

title: Lupin tofu burrito bowl with peppers, corn and avocado lime
instructions: Crumble the tofu and fry it with the cumin and chilli in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes.
Dice the pepper, add it with the lupins and corn and fry for 3 minutes.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice and salt and shred the iceberg lettuce.
Put the lettuce into a bowl, top with the pan mixture and finish with the avocado cream.

title: Soy chunk breakfast patties with baked beans in tomato sauce
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes, squeeze it out well and knead with the mashed tofu, chickpea flour, sage, fennel seed and salt.
Shape into 4 small patties and brown them in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes per side.
Finely dice the onion and simmer with the passata, smoked paprika and beans for 10 minutes until thick.
Wilt the spinach in the hot pan and serve everything together.

title: Tempeh broccoli breakfast rice with cauliflower rice and ginger
instructions: Cut the tempeh into small cubes, divide the broccoli into small florets and grate the ginger.
Toast the tempeh in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until crisp and remove.
Steam the broccoli, edamame and ginger with 3 tbsp water for 3 minutes, add the cauliflower rice and fry for 4 minutes.
Toss in the tempeh and tamari and sprinkle with spring onion greens.

title: Savoury tofu muffins with peppers, spinach and spring onion
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C and line 4 cups of a muffin tin with paper cases.
Blend the tofu, pea protein, chickpea flour, nutritional yeast, baking powder, turmeric and 50 ml water until smooth.
Finely chop the pepper, spinach and spring onion, fold them in and spoon the mixture into the cases.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden and leave to cool for 5 minutes.

title: Pan-fried smoked tofu with sautéed mushrooms, tomatoes and rocket
instructions: Cut the smoked tofu into 4 slices and fry them in a dry non-stick pan for 3 minutes per side.
Tear the oyster mushrooms into strips and fry them briskly with the thyme for 5 minutes.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, fry them for 2 minutes and sprinkle over the nutritional yeast.
Put the rocket on a plate, arrange the tofu and mushrooms on top and season.

title: Tofu chilaquiles verdes with crushed corn tostada and salsa verde
instructions: Break the corn tortilla into pieces and toast them in a dry pan for 4 minutes until crisp, then remove.
Blend the tomatillos with the chilli, coriander, pea protein, salt and 3 tbsp water to a salsa verde.
Crumble the tofu into the pan, fry for 4 minutes, pour in the salsa and simmer for 3 minutes.
Fold in the tortilla pieces and serve topped with onion rings, shredded lettuce and coriander.

title: Pea and tofu fritters with cucumber soy yoghurt and dill
instructions: Thaw the peas and roughly blend them with the tofu, pea protein, chickpea flour, half of the herbs and salt.
Shape the mixture into 4 flat fritters.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan and fry the fritters for 4 minutes per side until golden.
Grate the cucumber, mix with the soy yoghurt, remaining herbs and salt and serve with the fritters.

title: Mediterranean tofu scramble with olives, capers and roasted pepper
instructions: Dice the courgette and steam it in a non-stick pan with 2 tbsp water for 3 minutes.
Crumble in the tofu, season with nutritional yeast and oregano and fry for 4 minutes.
Cut the roasted pepper into strips, halve the olives and warm them with the capers for 2 minutes.
Season with pepper, salt carefully and sprinkle with basil.

title: Edamame tofu breakfast salad with cucumber, radish and sesame
instructions: Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Cut the tofu into cubes and brown it all over in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes.
Thinly slice the cucumber and radishes and stir together the tamari and rice vinegar.
Toss everything with the dressing and sprinkle with sesame and spring onion greens.

title: Tofu huevos rancheros with beans, tomato sauce and corn tortilla
instructions: Simmer the passata with the diced pepper, cumin, chilli and oregano for 8 minutes to a ranchero sauce.
Stir the pea protein with 3 tbsp water and add it to the sauce with the beans.
Cut the tofu into 2 thick round slices and fry without oil for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Briefly warm the tortilla in the pan, spoon over the sauce, top with the tofu slices and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Tofu kimchi pan with pak choi, shiitake and spring onions
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes, quarter the pak choi lengthways and slice the shiitake.
Fry the tofu in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden all over.
Add the shiitake and pak choi and fry for 3 minutes, then fry the kimchi and tamari with them for 2 minutes.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with spring onion greens.

title: Berry cheesecake bowl with soy skyr, lemon and buckwheat crunch
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein, lemon zest and vanilla until smooth.
Toast the buckwheat in a dry pan for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Spoon the cream into a bowl, top with the berries and sprinkle with the buckwheat crunch.

title: Mango lassi overnight oats with soy yoghurt, cardamom and pea protein
instructions: Mix the oats, pea protein and cardamom in the jar and stir in the soy yoghurt and soy drink until lump-free.
Purée half of the mango finely and spoon it on top as a layer.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Dice the remaining mango and put it on top of the oats.

title: Apple cinnamon protein pancakes made with buckwheat and soy skyr
instructions: Mix the buckwheat flour, pea protein, baking powder and half of the cinnamon, then stir in the soy drink to a thick batter.
Finely grate half of the apple and fold it in.
Cook 4 small pancakes in a dry non-stick pan for 2 minutes per side.
Cut the remaining apple into thin wedges and serve with the soy skyr and cinnamon on the pancakes.

title: Blueberry protein buckwheat waffles with soy skyr topping
instructions: Preheat the waffle iron and blend the silken tofu with the soy drink and vanilla until smooth.
Stir in the buckwheat flour, soy protein and baking powder and fold in a third of the blueberries.
Bake 2 waffles from the batter for 4 minutes each until golden.
Serve with the soy skyr and the remaining blueberries.

title: Chocolate silken tofu mousse bowl with raspberries and cacao nibs
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, soy protein, cocoa and banana in a blender for 1 minute until very creamy.
Spoon the mousse into a bowl and chill for 10 minutes.
Top with the raspberries and cacao nibs.

title: Cherry chocolate chia pudding with soy drink and soy protein
instructions: Whisk the soy drink, soy protein and cocoa in the jar until lump-free, then stir in the chia seeds.
Leave to swell for 10 minutes, stir again and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Thaw the cherries, crush half of them and layer them with the soy skyr on top of the pudding.

title: Strawberry rhubarb soy skyr bowl with hemp seeds and vanilla
instructions: Cut the rhubarb into small pieces and simmer with the maple syrup and 2 tbsp water for 6 minutes to a compote, then cool.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein and vanilla until smooth and spoon into a bowl.
Quarter the strawberries, add them with the compote on top of the skyr and sprinkle with hemp seeds.

title: Buckwheat porridge with pear, cinnamon and pea protein
instructions: Bring the buckwheat flakes to the boil with the soy drink and cinnamon and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring.
Remove from the heat, stir the pea protein smooth with 3 tbsp water and fold it in.
Cut the pear into wedges, arrange them on the porridge and sprinkle with hemp seeds.

title: Green smoothie bowl with spinach, kiwi, soy skyr and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Blend the soy skyr, pea protein, spinach, frozen banana and half a kiwi in a blender until thick and creamy.
Pour into a bowl and smooth the surface.
Peel and slice the remaining kiwi and arrange it on the bowl with the pumpkin seeds.

title: Baked blueberry oats with gluten-free oats and silken tofu
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Blend the oats, silken tofu, pea protein, soy drink, baking powder and lemon zest until smooth.
Pour into a small ovenproof dish, press in the blueberries and bake for 22 minutes.
Leave to cool for 5 minutes and eat warm from the dish.

title: Gingerbread silken tofu cream with orange and chopped almonds
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, soy protein, maple syrup and gingerbread spice in a blender until creamy.
Peel and segment the orange and roughly chop the almonds.
Spoon the cream into a bowl, lay the orange segments on top and sprinkle with almonds.

title: Tropical pineapple coconut bowl with soy skyr and lime
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein, lime juice and lime zest until smooth.
Cut the pineapple into small cubes.
Put the skyr into a bowl, spread the pineapple on top and sprinkle with desiccated coconut.

title: Peach melba chia pudding with raspberry purée and soy protein
instructions: Whisk the soy drink, soy protein and vanilla, stir in the chia seeds and leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Stir again and chill overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Crush the raspberries with a fork to a purée and cut the peach into wedges.
Layer the pudding with the soy skyr, raspberry purée and peach wedges.

title: Matcha quinoa porridge with pea protein and blueberries
instructions: Rinse the quinoa in hot water and simmer it with 150 ml soy drink for 15 minutes until soft.
Whisk the remaining soy drink with the matcha and pea protein until lump-free.
Remove from the heat, stir in the matcha mixture and serve with the blueberries.

title: Carrot cake overnight oats with soy skyr, walnuts and cinnamon
instructions: Finely grate the carrot and mix it with the oats, pea protein, cinnamon and nutmeg in the jar.
Stir in the soy drink until there are no lumps left.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Top with the soy skyr and sprinkle with chopped walnuts and a little cinnamon.

title: Buckwheat crêpes with vanilla soy skyr and strawberries
instructions: Whisk the buckwheat flour, pea protein and soy drink to a thin batter and rest for 5 minutes.
Cook 2 thin crêpes in a dry non-stick pan for 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein and vanilla until smooth and slice the strawberries.
Fill the crêpes with the cream and strawberries and fold them into triangles.

title: Millet protein porridge with warm plum compote and cinnamon
instructions: Rinse the millet in hot water and let it swell with the soy drink over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stone and quarter the plums and simmer with the cinnamon, clove and 2 tbsp water for 5 minutes to a compote.
Stir the soy protein smooth with 3 tbsp water and fold it into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the warm compote.

title: Tiramisu breakfast cream with espresso, silken tofu and cocoa
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, soy skyr, soy protein and maple syrup until creamy.
Soak the oats with the espresso and put them into a glass.
Layer the cream on top and dust generously with cocoa.

title: Baked apple soy skyr bowl with cinnamon and toasted walnuts
instructions: Cut the apple into wedges and braise with the cinnamon and 2 tbsp water in a pan for 6 minutes until soft.
Toast the walnuts in the dry pan for 2 minutes and chop them.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein and vanilla until smooth, spoon into a bowl and top with the baked apple and walnuts.

title: Blackberry vanilla breakfast shake with soy drink and pea protein
instructions: Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Chocolate banana breakfast shake with cocoa, soy drink and flaxseed
instructions: Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and blend in a few ice cubes if you like.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Pumpkin spice protein porridge with Hokkaido squash and pecans
instructions: Finely grate the squash and simmer with the oats, soy drink and spices for 6 minutes until creamy.
Remove from the heat, stir the pea protein smooth with 3 tbsp water and fold it in.
Spoon into a bowl and sprinkle with chopped pecans and a little cinnamon.

title: Poppy seed lemon soy skyr with blueberries and flaxseed
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein, lemon juice, lemon zest and poppy seeds until smooth.
Spoon into a bowl and leave for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with the blueberries and flaxseed.

title: Autumn fig soy skyr bowl with hazelnuts and cinnamon
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein and cinnamon until smooth and spoon into a bowl.
Quarter the figs and roughly chop the hazelnuts.
Arrange the figs on the skyr and sprinkle with the hazelnuts.

title: Apricot overnight buckwheat with soy yoghurt and almond butter
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat thoroughly and stir it with the soy yoghurt, soy drink, soy protein and vanilla in the jar.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Stone the apricots and cut them into wedges.
Put the apricots on the buckwheat and drizzle with almond butter.

title: Larb lettuce wraps with soy mince, tofu, mint and lime
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze it out well, then finely crumble the tofu.
Toast the rice flour in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden and remove, then fry the soy mince and tofu for 6 minutes until crumbly.
Remove from the heat and mix in the onion strips, tamari, lime juice, chilli, herbs and toasted rice flour.
Spoon into the lettuce leaves and serve with cucumber slices.

title: Tofu miso soup with shiitake, pak choi, wakame and edamame
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, dice the tofu, slice the shiitake and cut the pak choi into strips.
Bring the water to the boil, simmer the shiitake and edamame for 4 minutes, then add the pak choi and tofu for 2 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat, dissolve the miso in a little of the broth and stir it in without boiling again.
Drain the wakame, add it and serve with spring onion rings.

title: Edamame spaghetti with sesame ginger vegetables and spring onions
instructions: Cook the edamame spaghetti according to the packet for about 6 minutes and drain.
Cut the pepper and carrot into thin strips and grate the ginger.
Cook the vegetables and sugar snap peas with the ginger and 3 tbsp water in a pan for 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Toss in the spaghetti, tamari and sesame oil and sprinkle with sesame, spring onion greens and chilli.

title: Gado-gado with tofu, tempeh, vegetables and light peanut lime sauce
instructions: Cut the tofu and tempeh into cubes and fry them in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden.
Blanch the beans for 4 minutes and the cabbage strips and sprouts for 1 minute in boiling water, then drain.
Stir the peanut butter with the tamari, lime juice, fresh chilli, garlic and 3 tbsp warm water until smooth.
Arrange the vegetables, cucumber slices, tofu and tempeh and drizzle the sauce over the top.

title: Tofu poke with edamame, red cabbage, cucumber and nori strips
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and marinate with the tamari, rice vinegar and grated ginger for 10 minutes.
Cook the edamame for 3 minutes and refresh, finely shred the red cabbage, dice the cucumber and grate the carrot.
Arrange everything side by side in a bowl and put the marinated tofu in the middle.
Cut the nori into thin strips and scatter over with the sesame.

title: Bibimbap bowl with tofu, cauliflower rice, spinach namul and gochugaru
instructions: Slice the tofu, drizzle with half of the tamari and fry without oil for 3 minutes per side.
Cook the cauliflower rice in the pan for 4 minutes and put it into a bowl.
Blanch the spinach for 1 minute, squeeze it out and mix with the sesame oil and garlic, then briefly fry the sprouts, shiitake and edamame one after another.
Arrange the vegetables, grated carrot and tofu on the cauliflower rice and season with the remaining tamari and gochugaru.

title: Tofu shirataki pho with star anise, sprouts and Thai basil
ingredients: Star anise, cinnamon, Thai basil, chilli
instructions: Halve the onion and char it with the ginger in a dry pan for 4 minutes.
Simmer with the stock, star anise and cinnamon for 15 minutes, then remove the spices, onion and ginger and season with tamari.
Rinse the shirataki thoroughly, slice the tofu and cut the pak choi into strips, then let them steep in the broth for 3 minutes.
Ladle into a bowl and serve with the sprouts, Thai basil, chilli and lime wedges.

title: Mapo tofu with soy mince, Sichuan pepper and cauliflower rice
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out, then cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes.
Toast the soy mince with the ginger, garlic, chilli and tomato purée in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes.
Add 150 ml water, the tamari and the tofu, simmer gently for 5 minutes and thicken with the starch mixed in water.
Steam the cauliflower rice for 4 minutes, serve with the mapo tofu and sprinkle with leek rings and Sichuan pepper.

title: Summer rolls with tofu, mango, herbs and tamari peanut dip
instructions: Cut the tofu into sticks and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 5 minutes until golden.
Cut the cucumber, carrot and mango into thin strips.
Dip the rice paper sheets one at a time briefly in warm water, fill with lettuce, tofu, vegetables, mango and herbs and roll up tightly.
Stir the peanut butter, pea protein, tamari, lime juice and 4 tbsp water into a dip and serve alongside.

title: Yam woon sen – Thai glass noodle salad with tofu, edamame and celery
instructions: Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 5 minutes, drain and cut shorter, then cook the edamame for 3 minutes.
Dice the tofu and brown it in a dry non-stick pan for 5 minutes.
Thinly slice the celery, halve the tomatoes and cut the onion into strips.
Stir together the tamari, lime juice, garlic and chilli and toss everything with the dressing and coriander.

title: Tofu teriyaki with broccoli, shirataki rice and sesame
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 7 minutes until crisp all over.
Divide the broccoli into florets and steam with the edamame for 4 minutes.
Stir together the tamari, maple syrup, grated ginger, starch and 4 tbsp water, pour into the pan and glaze the tofu in it.
Rinse the shirataki rice, heat it in a dry pan for 3 minutes and serve with the tofu, broccoli and sesame.

title: Garlic pak choi stir-fry with tofu, shiitake and cashews
instructions: Dice the tofu and fry it in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes, then remove.
Toast the cashews for 2 minutes, then fry the sliced garlic and shiitake strips with them for 3 minutes.
Quarter the pak choi and cook it with them for 3 minutes.
Stir together the tamari, pea protein, starch, chilli and 5 tbsp water, add with the tofu and bring briefly to the boil.

title: Sichuan tempeh with green beans and chilli garlic
instructions: Trim the beans and fry them in a hot non-stick pan with 3 tbsp water for 6 minutes until blistered.
Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out, finely dice the tempeh, chop the mushrooms and fry everything for 6 minutes until crumbly.
Toast the garlic, chilli and Sichuan pepper with it for 1 minute.
Add the beans, deglaze with the tamari and rice vinegar and toss well.

title: Tempeh sambal with spinach, tomatoes and cauliflower rice
instructions: Cut the tempeh into thin slices and fry them in a dry non-stick pan for 3 minutes per side until crisp.
Dice the tomatoes and shallot and cook down with the sambal for 5 minutes to a thick sauce.
Add the tempeh and edamame to the sauce and season with the tamari and lime juice.
Steam the cauliflower rice and spinach for 4 minutes and serve with the tempeh sambal.

title: Japanese kabocha tofu bowl with edamame and sesame dressing
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, cut the squash into wedges and roast on baking paper for 20 minutes.
Dice the tofu and add it to the tray for the last 12 minutes, then steam the broccoli and edamame for 4 minutes.
Stir the tahini, tamari, rice vinegar and 2 tbsp water into a dressing.
Arrange everything with cucumber slices in a bowl, pour over the dressing and sprinkle with shichimi.

title: Korean soy chunk bulgogi salad with cucumber and kimchi
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in hot water for 15 minutes, squeeze them out well and tear into strips.
Finely grate the pear and stir with the tamari, garlic and gochugaru, then marinate the soy chunks and tofu strips in it for 10 minutes.
Fry in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until the edges caramelise, adding the sesame oil at the end.
Arrange the lettuce and cucumber, top with the bulgogi and kimchi and sprinkle with sesame.

title: Laksa soup with tofu, soy drink, shirataki and sprouts
instructions: Toast the curry paste in a pot for 1 minute, pour in the stock, soy drink and coconut milk and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Cut the tofu into cubes and let it steep in the soup with the edamame for 4 minutes.
Rinse the shirataki thoroughly, put it into a bowl and ladle the soup over it.
Serve with the sprouts, cucumber strips, herbs and lime.

title: Suan la tang – hot and sour soup with tofu, shiitake and bamboo
ingredients: White pepper, chilli oil, spring onion greens
instructions: Cut the tofu, bamboo shoots and carrot into thin strips and slice the shiitake.
Bring the stock to the boil, simmer the vegetables and mushrooms for 4 minutes, then let the tofu steep for 2 minutes.
Stir the starch and pea protein smooth with 4 tbsp cold water and use it to thicken the soup slightly.
Season hot and sour with the tamari, rice vinegar and white pepper and serve with spring onion greens and chilli oil.

title: Tofu satay skewers with cucumber acar and peanut tamari sauce
instructions: Cut the tofu into 12 cubes, marinate with half of the tamari, turmeric, cumin and coriander seed and thread onto 3 skewers.
Finely slice the cucumber, carrot and onion and mix with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt to make acar.
Grill the skewers in a dry griddle pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Stir the peanut butter, pea protein, remaining tamari and 4 tbsp warm water together and serve with the skewers and acar.

title: Okonomiyaki with white cabbage, tofu, chickpea flour and nori
instructions: Shred the cabbage very finely and slice the spring onion into rings.
Blend the tofu with the pea protein, chickpea flour and 60 ml water until smooth, then fold in the cabbage and spring onion.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan, add the batter as one thick pancake and fry covered for 6 minutes per side.
Stir the tamari with the tomato purée into a sauce, brush it over and sprinkle with nori strips, ginger and sesame.

title: Lupin tabbouleh with lots of parsley, tomatoes, mint and lemon
instructions: Rinse the quinoa, cook it in 30 ml water for 12 minutes and leave to cool.
Roughly chop the lupins, finely dice the tofu and chop the parsley and mint very finely.
Finely dice the tomatoes, cucumber and spring onion.
Mix everything with the lemon juice, olive oil, allspice, salt and pepper and leave to infuse for 10 minutes.

title: Edamame spaghetti alla Norma with roasted aubergine and basil
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220 °C, dice the aubergine, toss with the olive oil and salt and roast for 20 minutes until golden.
Chop the garlic and simmer with the passata and chilli for 10 minutes, then stir the pea protein smooth with 3 tbsp water and stir it in.
Cook the edamame spaghetti for about 6 minutes and drain.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce and aubergine and serve with basil.

title: Red lentil pasta with soy mince bolognese and celery
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out well.
Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery and toast them with the soy mince and crumbled tofu in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes.
Add the passata, oregano and bay leaf and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Cook the lentil pasta for about 7 minutes, drain and serve with the sauce.

title: Greek village salad with oregano tofu, olives and red onions
instructions: Cut the tofu into large cubes and marinate with the lemon juice, nutritional yeast, oregano and salt for 10 minutes.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges, the cucumber into thick slices and the pepper and onion into rings.
Arrange the vegetables with the lupins and olives in a bowl.
Put the tofu with its marinade on top, season with pepper and sprinkle with oregano.

title: Red lentil soup with mint, paprika and pan-fried tofu cubes
instructions: Dice the onion and carrot and sweat with the tomato purée and cumin in a pot for 3 minutes.
Rinse the lentils, add them with the stock and simmer for 18 minutes until soft, then blend finely.
Stir the pea protein smooth with 4 tbsp of the soup, fold it in and season with lemon juice and salt.
Dice the tofu, fry without oil for 6 minutes until crisp and put it on the soup with the mint and pul biber.

title: Baked falafel with pea protein, leaf salad and tahini lemon sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C and coarsely blend the chickpeas, pea protein, chickpea flour, onion, herbs, cumin, baking powder and salt.
Shape the mixture into 6 small balls, flatten slightly and bake on baking paper for 20 minutes, turning halfway.
Stir the tahini with the soy yoghurt, lemon juice, salt and 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Arrange the lettuce, tomatoes and cucumber, place the falafel on top and drizzle with the sauce.

title: Bread-free fattoush with roasted chickpeas, tofu and sumac
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, pat the chickpeas dry, season with sumac and salt and roast for 18 minutes until crisp.
Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes.
Tear the lettuce and roughly chop the tomatoes, cucumber and radishes.
Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, pea protein and sumac, toss everything with it and sprinkle with the herbs.

title: Cauliflower paella with smoked tofu, peppers, peas and saffron
instructions: Dice the smoked tofu and fry it in a large non-stick pan without oil for 4 minutes.
Dice the onion, pepper and tomatoes and fry them for 5 minutes.
Add the cauliflower, edamame, peas, saffron, smoked paprika and stock and cook for 8 minutes until the liquid has evaporated.
Season with salt and serve in the pan with the lemon wedge.

title: Provençal ratatouille with lupins, tofu and herbes de Provence
instructions: Cut the courgette, aubergine, pepper, tomatoes and onion into even cubes.
Heat the olive oil and fry the onion, aubergine and pepper for 6 minutes, then add the courgette, garlic and tomatoes.
Dice the tofu, add it with the lupins and herbs and braise covered for 20 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve in a deep bowl.

title: Lentil pasta with broccoli hemp pesto and pan-fried tofu
instructions: Divide the broccoli into florets and cook them with the lentil pasta in the same pot for about 7 minutes.
Blend a third of the broccoli with the hemp seeds, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, garlic, basil and 4 tbsp cooking water to a pesto.
Dice the tofu and fry it in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden.
Toss the pasta and broccoli with the pesto and serve with the tofu.

title: Vegan karnıyarık – aubergines with soy mince and tomato filling
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, halve the aubergine lengthways, score the cut sides and bake cut side down for 20 minutes.
Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes, squeeze out, crumble the tofu and fry both with the onion, pepper and olive oil for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, cumin and pul biber and cook down for 5 minutes.
Turn the aubergines over, press open in the middle, fill and bake for another 15 minutes, then serve with parsley.

title: Stuffed peppers with soy mince, quinoa and tomato sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C, soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out, and cook the quinoa for 12 minutes.
Mix the soy mince, quinoa, mashed tofu, finely diced onion, herbs, paprika and salt.
Cut open the peppers, deseed and fill them, then set them in a small dish with the passata.
Bake covered for 30 minutes and serve with the sauce.

title: Harira soup with chickpeas, lentils, soy chunks and coriander
instructions: Dice the onion and celery and steam them with the ginger, turmeric and cinnamon in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes.
Dice the tomatoes and add them with the lentils, soy chunks and stock, then simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and diced tofu and cook for 5 minutes.
Season with lemon juice and salt and sprinkle with coriander and parsley.

title: Ful medames with tofu, tomatoes, cumin and lemon
instructions: Simmer the broad beans with 50 ml water, the garlic and cumin for 8 minutes and roughly mash.
Stir the pea protein with the lemon juice and 2 tbsp water and fold it in.
Dice the tofu and fry without oil for 5 minutes, then finely dice the tomatoes and cucumber.
Spoon the beans into a bowl, top with the tofu, tomatoes, cucumber, parsley and chilli and drizzle with olive oil.

title: Lemony edamame linguine with courgette, peas and mint
instructions: Cut the courgette into long ribbons with a peeler.
Cook the edamame linguine for about 6 minutes, adding the peas for the last minute, then drain.
Warm the olive oil with the garlic and chilli and toss the courgette ribbons in it for 2 minutes.
Mix in the pasta, peas, lemon juice, lemon zest, nutritional yeast and mint and season.

title: Antipasti salad with lupins, artichokes, smoked tofu and rocket
instructions: Cut the smoked tofu into strips and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 4 minutes.
Quarter the artichokes, cut the pepper into strips and halve the tomatoes.
Mix the rocket with the lupins, artichokes, pepper and tomatoes in a bowl.
Lay the smoked tofu on top, season with balsamic, oregano, salt and pepper and sprinkle with basil.

title: Sicilian caponata with pan-fried tofu, edamame, capers and celery
instructions: Dice the aubergine and fry it in a large non-stick pan with 4 tbsp water for 8 minutes until soft and browned.
Dice the onion, celery and tofu and fry them for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, edamame, capers and vinegar and cook down for 10 minutes until sweet and sour.
Serve lukewarm or cold with basil.

title: Tofu souvlaki skewers with soy tzatziki and tomato cucumber salad
instructions: Cut the tofu into 12 cubes, marinate with the lemon juice, oregano and salt and thread onto 3 skewers.
Grill the skewers in a dry griddle pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Grate a third of the cucumber, squeeze it out and stir with the soy skyr, garlic, dill and salt to make tzatziki.
Dice the remaining cucumber, the tomatoes and onion, season with salt and serve with the skewers and tzatziki.

title: Tofu and chickpea flour kuku sabzi with herbs and barberries
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C and chop the herbs and spring onion very finely.
Blend the tofu, pea protein, chickpea flour, turmeric, baking powder, salt and 50 ml water until smooth and fold in the herbs and barberries.
Spread into a small dish lined with baking paper and bake for 25 minutes.
Cut into 4 pieces and serve with the soy yoghurt and cucumber slices.

title: Mercimek köfte plate with soy mince, quinoa, lettuce leaves and lemon
instructions: Simmer the lentils and quinoa with 150 ml water for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed, and soak the soy mince in hot water and squeeze it out.
Finely dice the onion and toast it without oil with the tomato purée, pul biber and cumin for 3 minutes.
Knead everything vigorously with the soy mince, pea protein, spring onion and parsley and season with salt.
Shape 8 oblong köfte by hand and serve with the lettuce leaves and lemon wedges.

title: Chili sin carne with soy mince, kidney beans, peppers and cocoa
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes, squeeze out well and finely crumble the tofu.
Dice the onion and pepper and toast them with the soy mince, tofu and spices in a pot for 5 minutes.
Add the passata, beans, corn and cocoa and simmer for 20 minutes until thick.
Season with salt and serve sprinkled with coriander.

title: Taco salad bowl with soy chunk mince, salsa and avocado
instructions: Soak and squeeze out the soy mince, crumble the tofu and fry both with the tomato purée and spices for 6 minutes until crumbly.
Finely dice the tomatoes and onion and mix with half of the lime juice and salt to make the salsa.
Dice the avocado and drizzle with the remaining lime juice and shred the lettuce.
Put the lettuce into a bowl and top with the mince, beans, salsa and avocado.

title: Ceviche de chochos – lupin ceviche with tomatoes, corn, tofu and lime
instructions: Cut the red onion into thin strips, salt and soak in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Dice the tomatoes and pepper and cut the tofu into small cubes.
Stir the lime and orange juice with the ají paste and salt.
Toss the lupins, tofu, vegetables, corn and onion with the marinade, leave for 10 minutes and serve with coriander.

title: Feijoada bowl with smoked tofu, black beans, kale and orange
ingredients: Bay leaf, cumin, garlic, smoked paprika
instructions: Dice the smoked tofu and fry it in a pot without oil for 4 minutes, then toast the onion and garlic with it for 2 minutes.
Add the beans, diced tomatoes, stock, bay leaf and spices and simmer for 15 minutes, then stir the pea protein smooth with a little stock and stir it in.
Cut the kale into thin strips and steam it in a pan with 2 tbsp water for 3 minutes.
Serve the feijoada with the kale and orange slices.

title: Tofu saltado with tomatoes, red onions and coriander
instructions: Cut the tofu into strips and sear it in a hot non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes.
Cut the onion into wedges and fry it with the edamame for 3 minutes.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and toss them in for 1 minute.
Deglaze with the tamari, vinegar, ají and cumin and serve with coriander.

title: Misir wot with red lentils, tofu, berbere and gomen
instructions: Chop the onion very finely and toast it in a pot without fat for 6 minutes, stirring, then toast the ginger, garlic, tomato purée and berbere for 1 minute.
Add the lentils and 250 ml water and simmer for 18 minutes until thick, then stir the pea protein smooth with 3 tbsp water and fold it in.
Dice the tofu and let it steep in the sauce for 5 minutes.
Cut the kale into strips, steam with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes, season with salt and serve beside the wot.

title: Light maafe stew with tofu, spinach, tomatoes and peanut butter
instructions: Dice the onion, carrot and tomatoes and steam them with the ginger, garlic and chilli in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes.
Stir the peanut butter and pea protein smooth with the stock, pour in and simmer for 10 minutes.
Dice the tofu and let it steep for 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts and season with salt.

title: Moroccan tofu tagine with courgette, preserved lemon and olives
instructions: Cut the onion into strips and the carrot and courgette into thick pieces.
Dice the tofu and fry it in a casserole without oil for 5 minutes, then toast the onion and spices for 2 minutes.
Add the vegetables, edamame, stock and chopped preserved lemon and braise covered for 15 minutes.
Add the olives, leave for 2 minutes and serve with coriander.

title: Palak tofu with spinach sauce, ginger and garam masala
instructions: Blanch the spinach for 2 minutes, refresh in cold water, squeeze out and blend finely with the soy yoghurt.
Dice the tofu and fry it in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden, then remove.
Finely chop the onion, ginger and garlic and sweat with the cumin and chilli for 5 minutes.
Stir in the spinach purée and garam masala, add the tofu, heat for 3 minutes and season with salt.

title: Chickpea tofu masala with tomatoes, spinach and coriander
instructions: Finely chop the onion and ginger and steam them with the spices in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas and simmer for 10 minutes, then stir the pea protein smooth with a little sauce and stir it in.
Dice the tofu and cook it with the spinach for 4 minutes.
Season with salt and serve sprinkled with coriander.

title: Tofu tikka salad with mint soy yoghurt, cucumber and red onions
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and marinate with half of the soy skyr, the tandoori spice and salt for 10 minutes.
Roast under the oven grill at 230 °C for 12 minutes until the edges darken.
Stir the remaining soy skyr with the mint, lemon juice and salt.
Arrange the lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes and onion rings, add the tofu tikka and drizzle with the mint sauce.

title: Sambar with tofu, toor dal, aubergine and okra
ingredients: Sambar powder, mustard seeds, curry leaves, turmeric
instructions: Rinse the toor dal and cook with the stock and turmeric for 25 minutes until soft.
Dice the aubergine, cut the okra into pieces and cook them with the tomatoes, tamarind and sambar powder for 10 minutes.
Dice the tofu, add it with the pea protein stirred smooth and let it steep for 5 minutes.
Toast the mustard seeds and curry leaves in a dry pan for 1 minute, scatter over the sambar and season with salt.

title: Styrian runner bean salad with smoked tofu, pumpkin seed oil and onions
instructions: Cut the smoked tofu into small cubes and the onion into thin rings.
Whisk the cider vinegar, pea protein, salt, pepper and 2 tbsp water.
Mix the beans, tofu and onion with the dressing and leave to infuse for 10 minutes.
Serve on lamb’s lettuce, drizzle with pumpkin seed oil and sprinkle with chives.

title: Soy chunk paprika goulash with cauliflower mash
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in the hot stock for 15 minutes, squeeze out and keep the stock.
Dice the onion and pepper and toast them in the oil with the soy chunks, tofu cubes and tomato purée for 6 minutes, then add the spices.
Deglaze with the reserved stock and braise for 20 minutes until thick.
Cook the cauliflower florets for 12 minutes until soft, blend with a little cooking water, salt and nutmeg and serve with the goulash.

title: Swabian lentil stew with smoked tofu, carrots and leek
instructions: Dice the carrot, leek and celeriac and simmer with the lentils, bay leaf and stock for 25 minutes.
Dice the smoked tofu and fry it in a pan without oil for 4 minutes.
Stir the pea protein smooth with a little stock and add it to the stew with the tofu.
Season tangily with the cider vinegar, marjoram, salt and pepper.

title: Beetroot tofu salad with apple, horseradish and dill
instructions: Dice the tofu and fry it in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden.
Cut the beetroot and apple into cubes.
Stir the soy skyr with the horseradish, cider vinegar, dill and salt.
Arrange the lamb’s lettuce, add the beetroot, apple and tofu, spoon over the dressing and sprinkle with dill.

title: Kohlrabi tofu pan with peas, dill and mustard
instructions: Peel the kohlrabi and cut it into sticks, and dice the tofu.
Fry the tofu in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes, add the kohlrabi with 4 tbsp water and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the peas, stir the soy drink with the mustard and starch, pour it in and simmer for 2 minutes until creamy.
Season with salt, pepper and plenty of dill.

title: Tofu tinga salad bowl with chipotle tomatoes, cabbage and lime
instructions: Roughly tear the tofu and fry it in a dry non-stick pan for 5 minutes.
Slice the onion, dice the tomatoes and add them with the chipotle, oregano and garlic, then cook down for 8 minutes.
Finely shred the cabbage and slice the radishes, then mix with the lime juice and salt.
Warm the beans and edamame for 3 minutes, put the cabbage into a bowl and top with the tinga, beans and edamame.

title: Jerk tofu with black beans, mango salsa and cauliflower rice
instructions: Cut the tofu into thick slices, rub with the tamari and jerk spice and leave for 10 minutes.
Grill in a dry griddle pan for 4 minutes per side.
Finely dice the mango, pepper and onion and mix with the lime juice and coriander to make a salsa.
Steam the cauliflower rice with the beans for 5 minutes, season with salt and serve with the tofu and salsa.

title: Moqueca stew with tofu, peppers, tomatoes and lime
instructions: Cut the tofu into thick cubes and marinate with the lime juice, garlic and salt for 10 minutes.
Slice the onion, peppers and tomatoes into rings and slices and layer them in a shallow pot.
Add the tofu and edamame, stir the coconut milk with the pea protein and paprika, pour it over and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Serve in the pot sprinkled with coriander.

title: Mushroom tofu stroganoff with mustard, paprika and cauliflower rice
instructions: Cut the tofu into strips, slice the mushrooms and finely dice the onion.
Fry the tofu in the oil for 5 minutes until golden and remove, then fry the onion and mushrooms for 6 minutes.
Finely grate the cauliflower, steam it in a second pan for 5 minutes and season with salt.
Add the paprika, mustard, soy yoghurt and tofu to the mushrooms, just warm through and serve on the cauliflower rice with parsley.

title: Zurich-style tofu strips with mushrooms and broccoli
instructions: Cut the tofu into thin strips and fry in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the sliced onion and mushrooms and fry for 5 more minutes.
Stir the soy drink with the cornflour, pour it in and simmer for 2 minutes until creamy, then season with nutmeg.
Steam the broccoli for 5 minutes and serve with the tofu strips and parsley.

title: Courgette lasagne with soy mince bolognese and nutritional yeast tofu cream
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes, squeeze out and fry it with the onion in the oil for 4 minutes.
Add the passata, oregano and garlic and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend the tofu with the soy drink, nutritional yeast, nutmeg and salt until smooth and slice the courgette lengthwise into thin strips.
Layer the courgette, bolognese and cream in a small dish and bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.

title: Shepherd's pie with lentils, soy mince and cauliflower topping
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out, then finely dice the carrot, onion and mushrooms.
Fry the vegetables and soy mince in the oil for 5 minutes, add the tomato purée, lentils, stock and thyme and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Cook the cauliflower for 12 minutes until soft and blend with the soy drink, nutritional yeast, nutmeg and salt.
Put the filling into a small dish, spread the mash over it and bake at 220 °C for 15 minutes until golden.

title: Stuffed courgettes with lupin tofu filling and tomato sauce
instructions: Roughly chop the lupins, then halve the courgettes lengthwise and hollow them out.
Chop the courgette flesh and fry it with the onion, lupins and crumbled tofu in the oil for 6 minutes, then season.
Pour the passata into a dish, fill the courgette halves and set them on top.
Bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Roast pumpkin with lupins, smoked tofu, red onions and sage
instructions: Deseed the pumpkin and cut it into wedges, cut the onion into wedges and dice the smoked tofu.
Toss the pumpkin and onion with the oil, rosemary and salt and roast at 210 °C for 20 minutes.
Add the lupins, smoked tofu and sage leaves and roast for another 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with chilli flakes and serve warm.

title: Brussels sprout tempeh pan with mushrooms and mustard
instructions: Trim and halve the Brussels sprouts and precook them in salted water for 6 minutes.
Dice the tempeh and fry it in the oil for 5 minutes until crisp.
Add the mushrooms, onion and Brussels sprouts and fry for 6 more minutes.
Stir the mustard with 2 tbsp water and the thyme, toss through and serve.

title: Cabbage rolls with soy mince and tofu filling in tomato sauce
instructions: Blanch the cabbage leaves in salted water for 4 minutes and shave down the thick centre rib.
Soak the soy mince for 10 minutes, squeeze out and mix with the crumbled tofu, onion, marjoram and paprika.
Divide the filling over the 4 leaves, roll them up and brown them all over in the oil for 4 minutes.
Pour in the passata with the caraway and braise covered for 30 minutes.

title: Edamame spaghetti aglio e olio with broccoli and cherry tomatoes
instructions: Cook the edamame spaghetti for about 6 minutes as per the packet, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes.
Gently sweat the sliced garlic in the olive oil with the chilli flakes for 1 minute.
Toss in the halved cherry tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Drain the pasta and broccoli, toss them in the pan and serve with the nutritional yeast and parsley.

title: Chickpea pasta with spinach and lemon tofu ricotta
instructions: Cook the chickpea pasta for about 8 minutes as per the packet.
Mash the tofu with the lemon juice, lemon zest, nutritional yeast, nutmeg and salt into a crumbly ricotta.
Sweat the garlic in the oil and wilt the spinach for 2 minutes.
Toss the pasta with the spinach and a little cooking water, top with the tofu ricotta and serve with basil.

title: Roast vegetable tray with smoked tofu and herb soy skyr
instructions: Cut the peppers, courgette and onion into large pieces and the smoked tofu into cubes.
Spread everything on a lined baking tray with the rosemary, paprika and salt.
Roast at 220 °C for 25 minutes, turning halfway.
Stir the soy skyr with the herbs and salt and serve with the roast vegetables.

title: Savoy cabbage stew with white beans, smoked tofu and carrots
instructions: Dice the smoked tofu and fry in a pot without oil for 4 minutes, then toast the onion with it for 2 minutes.
Cut the savoy cabbage into strips and the carrot into slices, add them with the stock and caraway and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir the pea protein smooth with a little cold stock and stir it in with the beans, then leave for 5 minutes.
Season with marjoram and parsley and serve.

title: Stuffed portobello mushrooms with tofu spinach filling and tomato salad
instructions: Twist out the mushroom stalks and chop finely, then set the caps open side up on a baking tray.
Fry the onion, garlic and mushroom stalks in the oil for 3 minutes, wilt the spinach and mix with the crumbled tofu, nutritional yeast and thyme.
Fill the 3 mushroom caps and bake at 200 °C for 18 minutes.
Arrange the sliced tomatoes with the balsamic, chives and salt and serve alongside.

title: Soy mince patties with cucumber salad and mustard dip
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out very well.
Knead with the mashed tofu, finely diced onion, chickpea flour, marjoram, paprika and salt and shape 4 patties.
Fry the patties in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes on each side.
Slice the cucumber thinly and mix with the dill, salt and half the soy yoghurt, stir the rest with the mustard and serve alongside.

title: Green asparagus tofu pan with peas and lemon
instructions: Cut off the woody asparagus ends and slice the spears diagonally into 4 cm pieces.
Dice the tofu and fry it in the oil for 6 minutes until golden all over.
Add the asparagus and fry for 5 minutes, then cook the peas with it for 2 minutes.
Season with the lemon juice, lemon zest, salt and herbs.

title: Fennel tofu pan with orange, edamame and black olives
ingredients: Fennel seeds, chilli flakes, fennel fronds
instructions: Cut the fennel into thin wedges, dice the tofu and segment the orange, keeping the juice.
Fry the tofu in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the fennel, edamame and fennel seeds and fry for 6 minutes, then stir the pea protein into the orange juice and pour it in.
Fold in the orange segments and olives and serve with chilli flakes and fennel fronds.

title: Porcini ragout with tempeh and creamy polenta
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out, then dice the tempeh.
Fry the tempeh and soy chunks in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes, then fry the onion, garlic and mushrooms with them for 6 minutes.
Braise with 50 ml water and the thyme for 5 minutes.
Bring the soy drink to the boil, stir in the polenta and leave to thicken for 5 minutes until creamy, season with salt and serve with the ragout and parsley.

title: Sauerkraut pan with smoked tofu, apple, edamame and caraway
instructions: Dice the smoked tofu and fry it in a non-stick pan without oil for 5 minutes.
Add the onion strips and apple wedges and fry for 3 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut, edamame, caraway, bay leaf, juniper and 50 ml water and braise for 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, season and serve hot.

title: Broccoli tofu bake with cashew nutritional yeast sauce
instructions: Divide the broccoli into florets and blanch for 3 minutes, then cut the tofu into cubes.
Blend the cashews, nutritional yeast, soy drink, cornflour, spices and salt until smooth.
Put the broccoli and tofu into a small baking dish and pour the sauce over.
Bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes until the top is golden.

title: Lupin patties with radish cucumber salad and herb dip
instructions: Coarsely blend the lupins and knead with the chickpea flour, finely diced onion, cumin, parsley and salt.
Shape 4 flat patties and chill for 10 minutes.
Fry the patties in the oil for 4 minutes on each side until golden.
Slice the cucumber and radishes and season with salt, stir the soy yoghurt with the chives and dill and serve everything together.

title: Red Thai curry with tofu, bamboo shoots, peppers and edamame
instructions: Dice the tofu and fry it in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Toast the curry paste in a pot for 1 minute, then add the coconut milk, 100 ml water and the kaffir lime leaves.
Simmer the pepper strips, bamboo shoots and edamame in it for 6 minutes.
Add the tofu, season with the tamari and lime juice and serve with Thai basil.

title: Green Thai curry with tofu, courgette and snow peas
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes.
Toast the curry paste for 1 minute, pour in the coconut milk and 100 ml water and bring to the boil.
Cut the courgette into half-moons and simmer with the snow peas and edamame for 5 minutes.
Fold in the tofu, season with the tamari and serve with basil, coriander and lime zest.

title: Massaman-style Thai pumpkin curry with tofu, edamame, cinnamon and tamarind
instructions: Cut the pumpkin and tofu into cubes and the onion into wedges.
Toast the curry paste with the cinnamon, cardamom and star anise in a pot for 1 minute, then add the coconut milk and 150 ml water.
Simmer the pumpkin, onion and tamarind for 12 minutes, then let the tofu and edamame steep in it for 4 minutes.
Stir the pea protein smooth with 3 tbsp water and stir it in, then serve sprinkled with chopped peanuts.

title: Nasu dengaku – miso aubergine with glazed tofu and edamame
instructions: Halve the aubergine lengthwise, score the flesh in a diamond pattern and bake cut side up at 220 °C for 20 minutes.
Cut the tofu into 4 thick slices and fry in a non-stick pan without oil for 3 minutes on each side.
Stir the miso with the ginger and 2 tbsp water, spread it over the aubergine and tofu and caramelise under the grill for 4 minutes.
Cook the edamame for 4 minutes and serve everything with sesame and spring onion greens.

title: Kung pao tofu with peanuts, peppers and edamame
ingredients: Sichuan pepper, dried chillies, ginger, garlic
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes until crisp.
Stir the tamari, rice vinegar, cornflour and 4 tbsp water into a sauce.
Toast the chillies, Sichuan pepper, ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, then stir-fry the peppers, edamame and spring onions for 3 minutes.
Add the tofu and sauce, glaze for 1 minute and sprinkle with the peanuts.

title: Sweet and sour tofu with soy chunks, pineapple, peppers and cauliflower rice
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out, dice the tofu and fry both without oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Stir together the rice vinegar, tomato purée, tamari, cornflour and 80 ml water.
Cut the peppers, onion and pineapple into pieces and stir-fry with the ginger and garlic for 4 minutes, then add the sauce and tofu and glaze for 1 minute.
Finely grate the cauliflower, steam for 4 minutes and serve with the sweet and sour tofu.

title: Sundubu jjigae – Korean silken tofu stew with kimchi and shiitake
instructions: Chop the kimchi and toast it with the garlic, sambal oelek and gochugaru in a small pot for 2 minutes.
Add the stock, sliced shiitake and courgette half-moons and simmer for 6 minutes.
Dice the firm tofu and add it, then spoon in the silken tofu in large pieces.
Leave to steep gently for 3 minutes without stirring and serve with spring onion greens.

title: Lemongrass tofu with chilli, pak choi and edamame
instructions: Chop the lemongrass, garlic and chilli very finely, dice the tofu and marinate it with them for 10 minutes.
Fry the tofu in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then fry the onion wedges with it for 2 minutes.
Quarter the pak choi lengthwise and cook it with the edamame for 3 minutes.
Deglaze with the tamari and serve with coriander.

title: Miso ramen with shirataki noodles, tofu, shiitake and corn
instructions: Rinse the shirataki noodles thoroughly and heat them dry in a pan for 2 minutes.
Simmer the stock with the ginger, garlic and shiitake for 5 minutes, then cook the pak choi and edamame in it for 3 minutes.
Take the pot off the heat, stir the miso smooth in a little stock and stir it in.
Put the noodles into a bowl, pour over the stock with the vegetables and top with the tofu cubes, corn, nori and spring onions.

title: Sri Lankan style tempeh bean curry with tofu and curry leaves
ingredients: Curry leaves, mustard seeds, turmeric, cinnamon, chilli
instructions: Soak the soy chunks for 10 minutes and squeeze out, then dice the tempeh and tofu.
Toast the mustard seeds and curry leaves in a dry pot for 1 minute, then toast the onion, turmeric, cinnamon and chilli with them for 3 minutes.
Add the beans in pieces, tomatoes, tempeh, tofu, soy chunks, coconut milk and 100 ml water.
Simmer covered for 12 minutes until the beans are tender and season with salt.

title: Tofu jalfrezi with peppers, onions and broccoli
ingredients: Cumin, garam masala, turmeric, green chilli, coriander
instructions: Cut the tofu into large cubes and fry all over in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes.
Toast the cumin for 30 seconds, then sear the onion and peppers in large pieces with the ginger and chilli for 4 minutes.
Add the broccoli florets, tomatoes, turmeric and garam masala and braise covered for 5 minutes.
Fold in the tofu, season with salt and serve with coriander.

title: Light dal makhani with urad lentils, kidney beans and tofu
ingredients: Garam masala, cumin, fenugreek leaves, chilli
instructions: Soak the urad lentils overnight and cook them in fresh water for 35 minutes until soft.
Toast the onion, ginger and cumin without fat for 5 minutes, then simmer the passata and spices for 5 minutes.
Add the lentils, kidney beans and diced tofu and simmer for 10 minutes until creamy.
Stir the pea protein smooth with the soy yoghurt, fold it in off the heat and sprinkle with fenugreek leaves.

title: Aloo gobi with tofu, peas and turmeric
instructions: Divide the cauliflower into small florets, cut the potato into small cubes and dice the tofu.
Toast the cumin in a dry non-stick pot for 30 seconds, then toast the onion, ginger and turmeric for 3 minutes.
Add the cauliflower, potato and 100 ml water and cook covered for 12 minutes.
Cook the tofu and peas with it for 4 minutes, season with salt and serve with coriander.

title: Tofu vindaloo with potatoes, spinach and tomatoes
instructions: Dice the tofu and marinate it with the vinegar, garlic, ginger and vindaloo spice for 15 minutes.
Brown the onion in a non-stick pot without fat for 5 minutes, add the potato cubes, passata, chilli and 100 ml water and simmer for 12 minutes.
Add the tofu with the marinade and simmer for 6 minutes, then wilt the spinach for 1 minute.
Stir the pea protein smooth with 2 tbsp water, stir it in and season with salt.

title: Keema matar with soy mince, tofu, peas and cucumber raita
ingredients: Garam masala, cumin, turmeric, chilli, coriander
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out well, then finely crumble the tofu.
Toast the cumin in the oil for 30 seconds, fry the onion and ginger for 4 minutes, then fry the soy mince and tofu with them for 4 minutes.
Add the passata, spices, peas and 80 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes.
Finely grate the cucumber, stir with the soy yoghurt, salt and a little cumin and serve as raita with the keema and coriander.

title: Pad krapow with soy mince, tofu, green beans and Thai basil
ingredients: Thai basil, garlic, bird's eye chilli
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out, then crumble the tofu.
Fry the garlic and chilli in the oil for 30 seconds, then fry the soy mince and tofu hard for 5 minutes.
Fry the beans in pieces and the pepper with it for 4 minutes, deglaze with the tamari and fold in the basil.
Finely grate the cauliflower, steam for 4 minutes and serve with the krapow.

title: Steamed tofu with ginger spring onion sauce and pak choi
instructions: Cut the tofu into 2 thick blocks and steam on a deep plate over boiling water for 10 minutes.
Halve the pak choi and steam it for the last 4 minutes.
Cut the ginger and spring onions into fine strips and lay them on the tofu.
Briefly heat the sesame oil, pour it over and drizzle with the tamari.

title: Tofu rendang with green beans and lemongrass
ingredients: Galangal, ginger, turmeric, chilli, kaffir lime leaves
instructions: Pound or blend the shallots, galangal, ginger, chilli and lemongrass into a paste.
Toast the paste in a non-stick pot for 4 minutes, then add the coconut milk, tamarind, turmeric, lime leaves and 100 ml water.
Dice the tofu and reduce with the beans and edamame uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce clings thickly to the tofu.
Stir the pea protein with 2 tbsp water, fold it in and season with salt.

title: Tofu adobo with vinegar, garlic, pak choi and edamame
instructions: Cut the tofu into thick slices and fry in a non-stick pan without oil for 3 minutes on each side.
Fry the garlic and onion with it for 2 minutes, then add the vinegar, tamari, bay leaves, peppercorns and 80 ml water.
Braise gently for 10 minutes until the sauce has reduced slightly.
Cook the pak choi and edamame with it for 4 minutes and remove the bay leaves.

title: Kimchi tofu stir-fry with soy chunks, Chinese cabbage and spring onions
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out, then slice the tofu.
Fry the soy chunks and onion in the sesame oil for 4 minutes, then fry the kimchi, sambal oelek and gochugaru with them for 3 minutes.
Add the Chinese cabbage in strips and let it wilt for 2 minutes.
Briefly fry the tofu slices in a second pan without oil, arrange them on the stir-fry and sprinkle with spring onions and sesame.

title: Shawarma tofu plate with tahini soy skyr, radishes, tomatoes and red cabbage
instructions: Cut the tofu into thin slices and marinate with the shawarma spice, garlic, 1 tbsp water and salt for 15 minutes.
Fry the tofu in a non-stick pan without oil for 3 minutes on each side until crisp.
Stir the soy skyr smooth with the tahini, 1 tbsp water and salt.
Cut the radishes, tomatoes, red cabbage and onion, arrange with the tofu, add the sauce and sprinkle with sumac and parsley.

title: Lentil lemon soup with chard, tofu and cumin
instructions: Sweat the onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes and briefly toast the cumin with them.
Add the lentils and stock and simmer for 25 minutes until tender.
Add the chard in strips and the tofu in cubes and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir the pea protein smooth with the lemon juice, stir it in and serve with coriander.

title: Vegan ghormeh sabzi – Persian herb stew with kidney beans and tofu
instructions: Chop the herbs and spinach very finely and sweat them in a non-stick pot without fat for 8 minutes until dark.
Fry the onion in the oil for 5 minutes until golden, then add the turmeric and fenugreek leaves.
Add the herbs, beans, dried lime and 200 ml water and braise for 25 minutes.
Let the tofu cubes steep in it for 5 minutes, stir the pea protein smooth with the lime juice, stir it in and season with salt.

title: Tofu kofta with soy mince in tomato cinnamon sauce
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out very well.
Knead with the mashed tofu, grated onion, chickpea flour, parsley and spices and shape 6 long koftas.
Fry the koftas in the oil all over for 6 minutes, pour in the passata with 1 pinch of cinnamon and simmer gently for 10 minutes.
Serve with a dollop of soy yoghurt and parsley.

title: Tofu fajita pan with peppers, soy chunks, avocado and lettuce leaves
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out, then cut the tofu into strips.
Sear the tofu and soy chunks with the fajita spice in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes.
Fry the peppers and onion in strips with it for 5 minutes and deglaze with the lime juice.
Serve with avocado slices, coriander and the 4 lettuce leaves for wrapping.

title: Black bean patties with soy mince, coleslaw and mustard
instructions: Soak the soy mince for 10 minutes and squeeze out, then roughly mash the beans.
Knead the beans, soy mince, tofu, chickpea flour and spices and shape 2 patties.
Fry the patties in the oil for 4 minutes on each side.
Finely shred the cabbage and carrot, mix with the soy yoghurt, mustard and salt and serve with the patties.

title: BBQ tempeh with roast broccoli and cider vinegar slaw
instructions: Soak the soy chunks for 10 minutes and squeeze out, then slice the tempeh.
Stir the tomato purée, maple syrup, mustard, paprika, garlic powder and 2 tbsp water into a BBQ sauce and brush it over the tempeh and soy chunks.
Roast with the broccoli florets on a tray at 220 °C for 18 minutes.
Finely shred the cabbage, mix with the soy yoghurt, cider vinegar and salt and serve alongside.

title: Cajun tofu with okra, tomatoes, peppers and celery
instructions: Dice the tofu, toss with half the Cajun spice and fry in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes.
Sweat the onion, pepper and celery in the oil in a pot for 5 minutes.
Add the sliced okra, tomatoes, remaining spice, thyme, bay leaf and 80 ml water and braise for 15 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, fold in the tofu and serve.

title: Argentinian chimichurri tofu with lupins, grilled peppers and courgette
instructions: Finely chop the parsley and stir with the oil, vinegar, oregano, garlic, chilli flakes, 2 tbsp water and salt into chimichurri.
Cut the tofu into 4 thick slices and marinate with 1 tbsp chimichurri.
Grill the tofu, pepper strips and courgette slices in a griddle pan without oil for 8 minutes, warming the lupins for 2 minutes.
Arrange everything and drizzle with the remaining chimichurri.

title: Tofu steaks with oyster mushroom mustard cream and green beans
instructions: Cut the tofu into 2 thick steaks, season with salt and fry in a non-stick pan without oil for 4 minutes on each side.
Cook the beans in salted water for 7 minutes.
Fry the shallot and torn oyster mushrooms in the same pan for 5 minutes and add the thyme.
Take the pan off the heat, stir in the soy yoghurt and mustard and serve with the tofu, beans and parsley.

title: Ribollita without bread with cavolo nero, white beans and smoked tofu
instructions: Dice the smoked tofu and fry in a pot without oil for 4 minutes, then sweat the onion, celery and garlic with it for 4 minutes.
Add the passata, stock, rosemary and thyme and bring to the boil.
Strip the cavolo nero from its stalks, cut into ribbons and simmer for 15 minutes.
Mash half the beans, stir in all the beans, simmer for 5 minutes until thick and serve with chilli flakes.

title: Tom kha – Thai coconut soup with tofu, mushrooms and lemongrass
ingredients: Galangal, kaffir lime leaves, chilli, coriander
instructions: Steep the stock with the bruised lemongrass, galangal slices and kaffir lime leaves for 8 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, sliced mushrooms, tomato wedges and edamame and simmer for 5 minutes.
Dice the tofu and warm it in the soup for 3 minutes.
Season with the lime juice, salt and chilli and serve with coriander.

title: Courgette noodles with lentil tofu bolognese and nutritional yeast
instructions: Cook the lentils in water for 20 minutes until al dente and drain.
Finely crumble the tofu and brown it with the onion and garlic in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes.
Add the passata, lentils and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Spiralise the courgettes into noodles, warm them in a pan for 2 minutes and serve with the bolognese, nutritional yeast and basil.

title: Harissa tofu skewers with courgette, peppers and mint soy skyr
instructions: Cut the tofu into 12 cubes and marinate with the harissa, cumin and salt for 15 minutes.
Cut the courgette, pepper and onion into pieces and thread them alternately with the tofu onto 4 skewers.
Grill all over in a griddle pan without oil for 10 minutes.
Stir the soy skyr with the mint, lemon zest and salt and serve with the skewers.

title: Pea and mint soup with smoked tofu croutons
instructions: Sweat the onion in a pot with 2 tbsp water for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the peas and stock and simmer for 6 minutes, then blend finely with the mint and pea protein.
Cut the smoked tofu into small cubes and toast in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes until crisp.
Serve the soup with the soy yoghurt, tofu croutons and lemon zest.

title: Roast cauliflower steak with lupins, tofu, tahini and pomegranate
instructions: Cut the cauliflower into 2 thick slices, brush with the oil, cumin and salt and roast at 220 °C for 25 minutes.
Dice the tofu and roast it with the lupins for the last 10 minutes.
Stir the tahini smooth with the lemon juice, 2 tbsp water and salt.
Arrange the cauliflower steaks with the lupins and tofu, drizzle with the tahini and sprinkle with pomegranate, sumac and parsley.

title: Tofu cacciatore with peppers, mushrooms, olives and tomatoes
instructions: Cut the tofu into large pieces and fry all over in a non-stick pan without oil for 6 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic, peppers and mushrooms and fry for 5 minutes.
Add the passata, rosemary, oregano and olives and braise for 15 minutes.
Season and serve sprinkled with parsley.

title: Gigantes plaki with baked tofu, dill and tomatoes
instructions: Sweat the onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes, then add the passata and oregano.
Stir the pea protein smooth with 3 tbsp water and stir it into the sauce.
