Add the tofu and pea protein and simmer for another 5 minutes until cooked through.

title: Gigantes baked beans with tofu feta and dill
instructions: Dice the onion and carrots and dice the tofu.
Toss the tofu with the lemon juice and miso paste and leave to marinate for 15 minutes.
Sweat the onion and carrots in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the beans, tomatoes, pea protein and oregano, transfer to a small baking dish, top with the tofu and bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
Sprinkle with the dill and serve straight away.

title: Briam with courgette, potatoes, lupins and tofu feta
instructions: Slice the courgette, potatoes and tomatoes, thinly slice the onion and dice the tofu.
Toss the tofu with the lemon juice and oregano and leave to marinate for 10 minutes.
Mix the vegetable slices and lupins with the oregano, garlic and 4 tbsp water in a baking dish and bake covered at 200 °C for 30 minutes.
Scatter the tofu feta on top and bake uncovered for 10 minutes until golden.
Sprinkle with the dill and serve straight away.

title: Lentil bolognese with edamame spaghetti
instructions: Finely chop the carrots, celery and onion.
Sweat the onion, carrots and celery in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the red lentils, chopped tomatoes, tomato purée and oregano to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Cook the edamame spaghetti in plenty of salted water for 7 minutes until al dente and drain.
Toss the spaghetti with the bolognese and serve with basil.

title: Courgette lasagne with soy mince and silken tofu béchamel
instructions: Thinly slice the courgette and finely chop the garlic.
Pour the vegetable stock over the soy mince, leave to soak for 10 minutes and squeeze out well.
Dry-fry the soy mince, garlic, passata and oregano in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until crumbly.
For the cream, blend the silken tofu, nutritional yeast, pea protein and nutmeg until smooth.
Layer the courgette slices, soy mince sauce and béchamel alternately in a small baking dish and bake at 190 °C for 30 minutes.

title: Caponata with lupins, capers and celery
instructions: Dice the aubergine, celery, tomatoes and onion.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C conventional, spread the aubergine on a lined baking tray and roast for 20 minutes.
Sweat the onion and celery in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the tomatoes, aubergine, capers, balsamic vinegar, lupins and pea protein to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with the basil and serve straight away.

title: Tofu cacciatore with peppers, mushrooms and rosemary
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 1 cm thick slices, cut the red pepper into strips, slice the mushrooms and dice the onion.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the onion, red pepper, mushrooms and rosemary and fry for another 5 minutes until well browned.
Add the passata, black olives, pea protein and tofu to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 12 minutes.

title: Vegetable paella with tofu, peas and saffron
instructions: Dice the tofu, red pepper and onion.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Sweat the onion and red pepper in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the short-grain rice, chopped tomatoes, vegetable stock and saffron to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 18 minutes.
Add the peas, tofu and pea protein and cook for another 4 minutes until cooked through.

title: Pisto manchego with smoked tofu
instructions: Dice the courgette, red pepper, green pepper, aubergine, tomatoes, onion and smoked tofu.
Dry-fry the smoked tofu in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until well browned.
Sweat the onion, red pepper and green pepper in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the courgette, aubergine, tomatoes and pea protein to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes until soft.
Stir in the smoked tofu.

title: Oven ratatouille with herbes de Provence tofu
instructions: Slice the aubergine, courgette and tomatoes, dice the red pepper and onion and pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes.
Toss the tofu with the herbes de Provence and leave to marinate for 10 minutes.
Put the passata with the nutritional yeast, onion and pepper into a baking dish and arrange the vegetable slices on top, overlapping.
Scatter the tofu in between and bake at 190 °C for 35 minutes.

title: French cassoulet-style bean pot with smoked tofu and carrots
instructions: Dice the smoked tofu, carrots, onion and celery.
Dry-fry the smoked tofu in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until well browned.
Sweat the onion, carrots and celery in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the white beans, chopped tomatoes, vegetable stock, pea protein and thyme to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Stir in the smoked tofu and parsley.

title: Tofu paprikash with soy skyr and onions
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes and dice the red pepper, onion and tomatoes.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Sweat the onion and red pepper in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the tomatoes, vegetable stock, tofu and paprika to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Take off the heat, stir in the soy skyr and serve with steamed cauliflower rice.

title: Golabki cabbage rolls with soy mince tofu filling in tomato sauce
instructions: Blanch the white cabbage in boiling water for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Pour the vegetable stock over the soy mince, leave to soak for 10 minutes and squeeze out well.
Knead the soy mince, crumbled tofu, raw rice, chopped onion and marjoram, divide between the cabbage leaves and roll into 4 parcels.
Place the rolls in a pot, pour over the passata and braise gently, covered, for 35 minutes.
Sprinkle with the dill and serve straight away.

title: Lobio Georgian bean stew with lupins, walnuts and coriander
instructions: Finely chop the onion and finely chop the coriander and walnuts.
Sweat the onion and fenugreek in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the kidney beans, lupins, chopped tomatoes and pea protein to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Roughly mash a third of the beans, season with apple cider vinegar and sprinkle with walnuts and coriander.

title: Khoresh bademjan with tofu and dried lime
instructions: Cut the aubergine into sticks, thinly slice the onion and pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C conventional, spread the aubergine on a lined baking tray and roast for 20 minutes.
Dry-fry the tofu and onion in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the chopped tomatoes, tomato purée, vegetable stock, pea protein, dried lime and turmeric to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Add the aubergine and simmer for another 5 minutes until soft.

title: Sabich plate with roasted aubergine, tofu and tahini yoghurt
instructions: Slice the aubergine, pat the tofu dry and cut into 1 cm thick slices and dice the cucumber and tomatoes.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C conventional, spread the aubergine, tofu and turmeric on a lined baking tray and roast for 20 minutes.
For the dip, stir together the soy yoghurt, tahini and pea protein with 1 tbsp water until smooth.
Arrange the aubergine, tofu, cucumber and tomatoes in a plate, drizzle with the dip and sprinkle with the parsley.

title: Tofu choila with fenugreek and onion chili salad
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, thinly slice the red onion, finely chop the garlic, ginger and green chilli and dice the cucumber.
Dry-fry the tofu and cumin in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until well browned.
Toast the fenugreek in a dry pan for 30 seconds.
Put the tofu, red onion, garlic, ginger, green chilli, lemon juice, pea protein and fenugreek in a bowl and mix well.
Arrange the tofu and cucumber in a plate and sprinkle with the coriander.

title: Sri Lankan squash curry with tofu and curry leaves
ingredients: Curry leaves, mustard seeds, turmeric, cinnamon
instructions: Cut the Hokkaido squash and tofu into 2 cm cubes, dice the onion and cut the green beans into rough pieces.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Sweat the onion, curry leaves and mustard seeds in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the Hokkaido squash, coconut milk and vegetable stock to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Add the tofu, green beans and pea protein and simmer for another 6 minutes until cooked through.

title: Tofu adobo with garlic, bay leaf and green beans
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, slice the garlic and cut the green beans into rough pieces.
Dry-fry the tofu and garlic in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the apple cider vinegar, tamari, bay leaves, peppercorns, pea protein and 80 ml water and reduce for 8 minutes.
Steam the green beans for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Arrange the tofu and green beans in a plate.

title: Huli huli tofu with grilled pineapple and pepper
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 1 cm thick slices, cut the pineapple and red pepper into rough pieces, finely grate the ginger and slice the spring onions into thin rings.
Toss the tofu with the tamari, ginger, tomato purée and pea protein and leave to marinate for 15 minutes.
Dry-fry the tofu, pineapple and pepper in a griddle pan for 8 minutes until charred lines appear.
Dry-fry the cauliflower rice in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes until soft.
Arrange the cauliflower rice, tofu, pineapple and red pepper in a plate and sprinkle with the spring onions.

title: Cajun tofu with okra and tomatoes gumbo style
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, slice the okra and dice the red pepper, celery and onion.
Dry-fry the tofu and Cajun spice in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until well browned.
Sweat the onion, red pepper and celery in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the okra, chopped tomatoes, vegetable stock, pea protein and thyme to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Add the tofu and simmer for another 3 minutes until cooked through.

title: BBQ pulled jackfruit with lupins and coleslaw
ingredients: Smoked paprika, mustard powder, garlic powder
instructions: Tear the jackfruit into bite-sized pieces, cut the onion into thin strips and cut the white cabbage into thin strips.
Dry-fry the jackfruit, onion, soy mince and paprika in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until well browned.
Add the tomato paste, apple cider vinegar, lupins and 100 ml water and reduce for 10 minutes, pulling the jackfruit apart with two forks.
For the dressing, stir together the soy skyr and cider vinegar until smooth.
Toss the white cabbage with the dressing.

title: Yasai itame Japanese stir-fried vegetables with tofu and soybean sprouts
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, cut the Chinese cabbage into rough pieces, cut the carrots into thin strips, slice the onion and finely grate the ginger.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the onion, carrots, Chinese cabbage, soybean sprouts and ginger and fry for another 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Stir the tamari with the pea protein and 2 tbsp water, add and toss briefly.

title: Chinese tomato tofu with spring onions
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and crumble roughly with your fingers, cut the tomatoes into wedges and slice the spring onions into thin rings.
Dry-fry the tofu and turmeric in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until crumbly.
Add the tomatoes and cook for another 4 minutes until soft.
For the sauce, stir together the tamari, cornflour and pea protein with 3 tbsp water until smooth.
Stir in the sauce, simmer for 1 minute until thickened, sprinkle with spring onions and serve with shirataki rice.

title: Rajma with tofu and garam masala
instructions: Finely chop the onion and green chilli, finely grate the ginger and pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes.
Sweat the onion, ginger, green chilli and cumin in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the kidney beans, chopped tomatoes and garam masala to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Add the tofu and pea protein and simmer for another 5 minutes until cooked through.
Serve in a deep plate topped with the soy yoghurt and sprinkled with coriander.

title: Baingan bharta with lupins and coriander
instructions: Preheat the oven to 230 °C conventional, spread the aubergine on a lined baking tray and roast until soft for 30 minutes.
Peel the aubergines and mash the flesh with a fork.
Dice the tomatoes and onion and finely chop the ginger and green chilli.
Heat the oil in a pot and sweat the onion, ginger, green chilli and cumin for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the tomatoes, aubergine, lupins and pea protein to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 8 minutes.
Sprinkle with the coriander and serve straight away.

title: Suya tofu skewers with peanut spice and tomato onion salad
ingredients: Chilli flakes, ground ginger, smoked paprika, garlic powder
instructions: Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes, slice the tomatoes and cucumber and slice the red onion into thin rings.
Grind the peanuts finely and mix with the pea protein, chili, ginger, paprika and garlic to make suya spice.
Coat the tofu all over in the peanuts and pea protein.
Thread the tofu alternately onto 3 skewers.
Cook the tofu in the air fryer at 200 °C for 12 minutes until crisp, shaking halfway through.
Put the tomatoes, red onion, cucumber and lime juice in a plate and mix well.

title: Pozole stew with corn, lupins and green salsa
instructions: Dice the green pepper and onion, finely chop the green chilli and thinly slice the radishes.
Sweat the onion and green pepper in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the sweetcorn, lupins, vegetable stock, pea protein and oregano to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
For the sauce, blend the coriander, green chilli and lime juice until smooth.
Arrange everything in a soup bowl, drizzle with the sauce and sprinkle with the radishes.

title: Tofu amok with coconut milk, kaffir lime and pak choi
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, halve the pak choi and slice the red chilli into thin rings.
For the sauce, whisk the coconut milk, curry paste, pea protein and turmeric with 2 tbsp water vigorously.
Mix the tofu with the sauce and finely shredded kaffir lime leaves, transfer to a heatproof dish and steam for 15 minutes until set.
Steam the pak choi for 3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Serve the amok with the pak choi, drizzle with lime juice and sprinkle with chili rings.

title: Poke bowl with marinated tofu, edamame, mango and shirataki rice
instructions: Dice the tofu and mango, slice the cucumber, cut the red cabbage into thin strips and let the edamame thaw.
Toss the tofu with the tamari and lime juice and leave to marinate for 15 minutes.
Rinse the shirataki rice thoroughly and dry-fry in a pan for 3 minutes.
Layer the shirataki rice, tofu, edamame, mango, cucumber and red cabbage in a bowl one after the other.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and nori and serve straight away.

title: Buddha bowl with roasted sweet potato, lupins, kale and tahini
instructions: Wash the vegetables, dice the sweet potato, tear the kale into bite-sized pieces and cut the red cabbage into thin strips.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C conventional, spread the sweet potato, lupins and paprika on a lined baking tray and roast for 22 minutes.
For the dressing, stir together the tahini, lemon juice and nutritional yeast with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Layer the kale, red cabbage, sweet potato and lupins in a bowl one after the other.
Drizzle with the tahini dressing and serve straight away.

title: Burrito bowl with soy mince, black beans, corn and cauliflower rice
instructions: Pour the vegetable stock over the soy mince, leave to soak for 10 minutes and squeeze out well.
Dry-fry the soy mince, cumin and chipotle powder in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until crumbly.
Dry-fry the cauliflower rice in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until soft.
Dice the red pepper and finely chop the coriander.
Layer the cauliflower rice, soy mince, black beans, sweetcorn and red pepper in a bowl one after the other.
Serve with the soy yoghurt, coriander and lime juice.

title: Bibimbap bowl with tofu, spinach, carrots and soybean sprouts
instructions: Rinse the shirataki rice thoroughly and dry-fry in a pan for 3 minutes.
Pat the tofu dry and cut into 1 cm thick slices and cut the carrots into thin strips.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Blanch the baby spinach, carrots and soybean sprouts in boiling water for 1 minutes and refresh in cold water.
For the sauce, stir together the miso paste, tamari and gochugaru with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Arrange the shirataki rice, tofu, baby spinach, carrots and soybean sprouts in a bowl, drizzle with the sauce and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.

title: Mezze bowl with beetroot hummus, smoked tofu, cucumber and tomato
instructions: Dice the smoked tofu, dice the cucumber, halve the cherry tomatoes and finely chop the parsley.
For the dip, blend the chickpeas, beetroot, lemon juice and cumin with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Dry-fry the smoked tofu in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until crisp.
Layer the cucumber, cherry tomatoes, lupins, smoked tofu and parsley in a bowl one after the other.
Add the beetroot hummus to one side and sprinkle with sumac.

title: Teriyaki tempeh bowl with broccoli and quinoa
instructions: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 15 minutes.
Slice the tempeh, cut the broccoli into small florets, finely grate the ginger and slice the spring onions into thin rings.
Steam the broccoli for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Dry-fry the tempeh in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until well browned.
Stir the tamari, ginger, cornflour, pea protein and 4 tbsp water together, add and reduce for 1 minute until glossy.
Arrange the quinoa, broccoli and tempeh in a bowl and sprinkle with the spring onions.

title: Thai pumpkin curry bowl with tofu and quinoa
instructions: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 15 minutes.
Dice the Hokkaido squash and tofu.
Add the red curry paste, coconut milk and Hokkaido squash to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 12 minutes.
Add the tofu, baby spinach and pea protein and simmer for another 4 minutes until cooked through.
Put the quinoa in a bowl, top with the curry, drizzle with lime juice and sprinkle with Thai basil.

title: Mediterranean beluga lentil bowl with roasted vegetables and tofu feta
instructions: Boil the beluga lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until tender and drain.
Cut the courgette, red pepper and red onion into rough pieces and dice the tofu.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C conventional, spread the courgette, red pepper, red onion and thyme on a lined baking tray and roast for 20 minutes.
Toss the tofu with the lemon juice, pea protein and oregano and leave to marinate for 10 minutes.
Arrange the rocket, beluga lentils, courgette, red pepper, red onion, tofu and black olives in a bowl.

title: Green goddess bowl with edamame, broccoli, peas and herb dressing
instructions: Cut the broccoli into small florets and let the edamame thaw.
Blanch the broccoli, edamame and peas in boiling water for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
For the dressing, blend the avocado, soy skyr, parsley and lemon juice until smooth.
Arrange the baby spinach, broccoli, edamame and peas in a bowl, drizzle with the dressing and sprinkle with the hemp seeds.

title: Sushi bowl with smoked tofu, cucumber, nori and edamame
instructions: Rinse the short-grain rice in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 15 minutes.
Stir in the rice vinegar.
Cut the smoked tofu into sticks, cut the cucumber and carrots into sticks, cut the nori into thin strips and let the edamame thaw.
Dry-fry the smoked tofu in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes until crisp.
For the dressing, stir together the tamari, ginger and pea protein with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Arrange the short-grain rice, smoked tofu, edamame, cucumber and carrots in a bowl, drizzle with the dressing and sprinkle with the nori.

title: Shawarma bowl with soy chunks, red cabbage and tahini yoghurt
instructions: Pour boiling water over the soy chunks, leave for 10 minutes and drain.
Cut the tofu into strips, cut the red cabbage into thin strips and dice the tomatoes and cucumber.
Toss the soy chunks and tofu with the shawarma spice and leave to marinate for 5 minutes.
Dry-fry the soy chunks and tofu in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until well browned.
For the dip, stir together the soy yoghurt and tahini until smooth.
Arrange the cauliflower rice, red cabbage, tomatoes, cucumber, soy chunks and tofu in a bowl, drizzle with the dip and sprinkle with the parsley.

title: Tandoori tofu bowl with roasted cauliflower and cucumber raita
instructions: Boil the beluga lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until tender and drain.
Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes, cut the cauliflower into small florets and finely grate the cucumber.
Toss the tofu with the soy yoghurt, lime juice and tandoori spice and leave to marinate for 15 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C conventional, spread the tofu and cauliflower on a lined baking tray and roast for 20 minutes.
Stir the cucumber with the remaining soy yoghurt and coriander into a raita and arrange in a bowl with the spinach, lentils, cauliflower and tofu.

title: Kimchi tofu bowl with shirataki rice, spinach and sesame
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, slice the cucumber and slice the spring onions into thin rings.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Rinse the shirataki rice and fry in the pan with the kimchi, pea protein and tamari for 3 minutes.
Blanch the baby spinach in boiling water for 1 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Arrange the shirataki rice, tofu, baby spinach and cucumber in a bowl and sprinkle with the sesame seeds and spring onions.

title: Millet bowl with roasted Brussels sprouts, smoked tofu and cranberries
instructions: Rinse the millet in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 15 minutes.
Wash the vegetables, halve the Brussels sprouts and dice the smoked tofu.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C conventional, spread the Brussels sprouts and smoked tofu on a lined baking tray and roast for 20 minutes.
For the dressing, stir together the mustard, cider vinegar and pea protein with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Arrange the millet, Brussels sprouts, smoked tofu and cranberries in a bowl, drizzle with the dressing.

title: Courgette noodle bowl with pea basil pesto, lupins and cherry tomatoes
instructions: Spiralize the courgettes into noodles.
For the sauce, blend the peas, basil, nutritional yeast, lemon juice and garlic with 3 tbsp water until smooth.
Dry-fry the courgette in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes until tender-crisp.
Toss the courgette and lupins with the sauce.
Put into a bowl and top with the halved cherry tomatoes.

title: Autumn bowl with Hokkaido squash, kale, tempeh and maple mustard
instructions: Wash the vegetables, dice the Hokkaido squash and tempeh and tear the kale into bite-sized pieces.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C conventional, spread the Hokkaido squash and tempeh on a lined baking tray and roast for 22 minutes.
For the dressing, stir together the mustard, maple syrup and cider vinegar with 1 tbsp water until smooth.
Toss the kale and lupins with the dressing.
Arrange the kale, lupins, Hokkaido squash and tempeh in a bowl and sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds.

title: Peri peri tofu bowl with corn, pepper and cauliflower rice
ingredients: Smoked paprika, chilli flakes, oregano, garlic powder
instructions: Cut the tofu and red pepper into 2 cm cubes.
Toss the tofu with the lemon juice, paprika and chilli flakes and leave to marinate for 15 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C conventional, spread the tofu, red pepper and sweetcorn on a lined baking tray and roast for 18 minutes.
Dry-fry the cauliflower rice in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until soft.
For the dip, stir together the soy skyr, pea protein and parsley until smooth.
Arrange the cauliflower rice, tofu, red pepper and sweetcorn in a bowl, drizzle with the dip.

title: Miso tofu bowl with glazed carrots, edamame and sesame
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, slice the carrots, slice the spring onions into thin rings and let the edamame thaw.
For the sauce, stir together the miso paste and pea protein with 3 tbsp water until smooth.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C conventional, spread the carrots and tofu on a lined baking tray and roast for 20 minutes.
Glaze the carrots and tofu with the miso sauce and arrange in a bowl with the edamame.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and spring onions and serve straight away.

title: Harissa lupin bowl with roasted carrots, mint and soy yoghurt
instructions: Cut the carrots into wedges.
Toss the lupins and carrots with the harissa and lemon juice and leave to marinate for 5 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C conventional, spread the lupins and carrots on a lined baking tray and roast for 22 minutes.
For the dip, stir together the soy yoghurt, pea protein and mint until smooth.
Arrange the baby spinach, carrots and lupins in a bowl, drizzle with the dip and sprinkle with the mint.

title: Cold edamame spaghetti bowl with broccoli, cucumber and sesame ginger
instructions: Cut the broccoli into small florets, cut the cucumber and carrots into sticks and finely grate the ginger.
Cook the edamame spaghetti in plenty of salted water for 6 minutes until al dente and drain.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
For the dressing, stir together the tamari, rice vinegar, ginger and sesame oil until smooth.
Toss the edamame spaghetti, broccoli, cucumber and carrots with the dressing.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and coriander and serve straight away.

title: Meal prep pumpkin chili with soy chunks and chickpeas
instructions: Pour boiling water over the soy chunks, leave for 10 minutes and drain.
Dice the Hokkaido squash, red pepper and onion.
Dry-fry the soy chunks, onion and cumin in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until well browned.
Add the Hokkaido squash, red pepper, chickpeas, chopped tomatoes and vegetable stock to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep tofu vegetable curry with cauliflower rice
instructions: Dice the tofu and red pepper and cut the broccoli into small florets.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the curry paste, coconut milk, vegetable stock, broccoli and red pepper to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 8 minutes.
Add the tofu and pea protein and simmer for another 3 minutes until cooked through.
Dry-fry the cauliflower rice in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until soft.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep lupin bolognese with courgette noodles
instructions: Finely chop the carrots, onion and celery.
Sweat the onion, carrots and celery in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the lupins, soy mince, passata and oregano to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Spiralize the courgette, put the raw noodles into the container, add the bolognese beside them and sprinkle with nutritional yeast.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Meal prep tempeh broccoli box with lupins and peanut lime sauce
instructions: Dice the tempeh, cut the broccoli into small florets and rinse and drain the lupins.
Dry-fry the tempeh in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until well browned.
Steam the broccoli for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
For the sauce, stir together the peanut butter, lime juice and tamari with 3 tbsp water until smooth.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep crumbled tofu pan with peppers and brown rice
instructions: Rinse the brown rice in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 30 minutes.
Pat the tofu dry and crumble roughly with your fingers and dice the red pepper and onion.
Dry-fry the tofu, soy mince, onion and paprika in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until crumbly.
Add the red pepper, tomato purée and tamari and fry for another 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep oven tofu with Brussels sprouts, potatoes and mustard
instructions: Wash the vegetables, cut the tofu and potatoes into 2 cm cubes and halve the Brussels sprouts.
Toss the tofu with the mustard, tamari and pea protein and leave to marinate for 10 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C conventional, spread the tofu, Brussels sprouts, potatoes and thyme on a lined baking tray and roast for 28 minutes.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep edamame quinoa salad jar
instructions: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 15 minutes.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, dice the cucumber, finely chop the red onion and let the edamame thaw.
For the dressing, stir together the soy yoghurt, lemon juice and parsley until smooth.
Put the dressing into a screw-top jar first, then layer in the edamame, lupins, quinoa, tomatoes, cucumber and onion.
Keep sealed in the fridge for up to 3 days and shake before eating.

title: Meal prep lentil vegetable stew with smoked tofu
instructions: Wash the vegetables, dice the smoked tofu, carrots and potatoes and slice the leek into thin rings.
Dry-fry the smoked tofu in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until well browned.
Add the beluga lentils, carrots, leek, potatoes, vegetable stock and marjoram to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Add the smoked tofu and pea protein and simmer for another 2 minutes until cooked through.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep soy chunk and tofu stroganoff with mushrooms
instructions: Pour boiling water over the soy chunks, leave for 10 minutes and drain.
Slice the mushrooms, cut the leek into thin strips and cut the tofu into strips.
Dry-fry the soy chunks, tofu, leek and paprika in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until well browned.
Add the mushrooms and fry for another 5 minutes until well browned.
Add the vegetable stock and mustard to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Take off the heat, stir in the soy yoghurt, pack with the cauliflower rice into a container and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Meal prep lupin patties with cucumber dill salad
instructions: Finely chop the onion and thinly slice the cucumber.
Soak the lupin grits in 60 ml hot water for 10 minutes and knead with the crumbled tofu, onion, mustard, chickpea flour and spices.
With damp hands shape the mixture into 4 patties.
Bake the patties on a tray at 200 °C for 20 minutes, turning once.
For the dressing, stir together the soy yoghurt, cider vinegar and dill until smooth.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Meal prep sesame ginger tofu with sugar snaps and buckwheat
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 12 minutes.
Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, halve the sugar snap peas, cut the carrots into thin strips and finely grate the ginger.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the sugar snap peas, carrots, ginger, tamari and pea protein and fry for another 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep sheet pan fajitas with tofu, peppers and black beans
instructions: Cut the tofu, red pepper, yellow pepper and red onion into strips.
Toss the tofu, red pepper, yellow pepper and red onion with the cider vinegar and fajita spice and leave to marinate for 5 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C conventional, spread the tofu, red pepper, yellow pepper and red onion on a lined baking tray and roast for 22 minutes.
Rinse the beans and mix them with the pea protein into the hot tray vegetables.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep pumpkin tofu ragout with sage
instructions: Dice the Hokkaido squash and tofu and dice the onion.
Dry-fry the tofu and sage in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the onion, Hokkaido squash, chopped tomatoes and vegetable stock to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Add the tofu, kale and pea protein and simmer for another 3 minutes until cooked through.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep vegetable frittata with chickpea flour and tofu
instructions: Dice the red pepper and onion.
Blend the tofu, chickpea flour, nutritional yeast, pea protein and turmeric in a blender for 30 seconds until creamy.
Stir in the baby spinach, red pepper and onion.
Put everything into a small baking dish and bake in the preheated oven at 190 °C for 30 minutes.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep Mediterranean lupin box with roasted vegetables and lemon tahini
instructions: Cut the aubergine, courgette and red pepper into 2 cm cubes.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C conventional, spread the aubergine, courgette, red pepper, lupins and oregano on a lined baking tray and roast for 25 minutes.
For the dressing, stir together the tahini, lemon juice and pea protein with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep Asian noodle box with edamame spaghetti, tofu and pak choi
instructions: Cook the edamame spaghetti in plenty of salted water for 6 minutes until al dente and drain.
Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, cut the pak choi into rough pieces, cut the carrots into thin strips, finely grate the ginger and slice the spring onions into thin rings.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the pak choi, carrots, ginger, tamari and rice vinegar and fry for another 3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Meal prep soy mince cabbage pan with carrots and caraway
instructions: Pour the vegetable stock over the soy mince, leave to soak for 10 minutes and squeeze out well.
Cut the white cabbage into thin strips, coarsely grate the carrots, dice the onion and pat the tofu dry and crumble roughly with your fingers.
Dry-fry the soy mince, tofu, onion and caraway in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until crumbly.
Add the white cabbage, carrots and tomato purée and cook for another 8 minutes until soft.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

title: Meal prep smoked tofu bean salad with mustard vinaigrette
instructions: Blanch the green beans in boiling water for 5 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Dice the smoked tofu, finely chop the red onion and slice the radishes.
For the dressing, stir together the mustard, cider vinegar and pea protein with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Toss the green beans, white beans, red onion, radishes, smoked tofu and dill with the dressing.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Beluga lentil Brussels sprout pan with tofu and walnuts
instructions: Boil the beluga lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until tender and drain.
Wash the vegetables, halve the Brussels sprouts, pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes and dice the onion.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the Brussels sprouts and onion and fry for another 6 minutes until well browned.
Stir in the beluga lentils, balsamic vinegar and pea protein.
Sprinkle with the walnuts and serve straight away.

title: Artichoke lupin pan with lemon and parsley
instructions: Quarter the artichoke hearts, halve the cherry tomatoes and finely chop the onion and parsley.
Dry-fry the artichoke hearts, lupins, onion and garlic in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden all over.
Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for another 2 minutes until soft.
Stir the pea protein with the lemon juice and 2 tbsp water, toss through and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Savoy cabbage lentil pan with tempeh and mustard
instructions: Boil the beluga lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until tender and drain.
Cut the savoy cabbage into thin strips, dice the tempeh and dice the onion.
Dry-fry the tempeh in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until well browned.
Add the savoy cabbage, onion and caraway and cook for another 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the beluga lentils, mustard and vegetable stock.

title: Pea mint patties from lupin grits with beetroot dip
instructions: Soak the lupin grits in 50 ml hot water for 10 minutes.
Roughly mash the peas with a fork.
Knead the peas, lupin grits, mint, onion, chickpea flour and pea protein, shape 4 patties and dry-fry for 4 minutes per side.
For the dip, blend the beetroot and soy skyr until smooth.
Arrange the rocket in a plate, drizzle with the dip.

title: Roasted romanesco with lupin herb crust and tahini
instructions: Cut the romanesco into small florets and finely chop the parsley.
Put the lupin grits, nutritional yeast, parsley and garlic powder in a bowl and mix well.
Toss the romanesco and lupins with 2 tbsp water, sprinkle with the herb mixture and roast at 210 °C for 22 minutes.
For the dressing, stir together the tahini and lemon juice with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Arrange everything in a plate, drizzle with the dressing.

title: Mushroom lentil ragout with cauliflower mash and tofu
instructions: Boil the beluga lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until tender and drain.
Slice the portobello mushrooms, dice the onion, pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes and cut the cauliflower into small florets.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and fry the portobello mushrooms, tofu, onion and thyme for 8 minutes until well browned.
Add the chopped tomatoes, vegetable stock, beluga lentils and pea protein to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Boil the cauliflower for 12 minutes until soft, blend with the nutritional yeast and nutmeg until smooth and serve with the ragout.

title: White bean spinach pan with tofu and lemon
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, finely chop the garlic and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the garlic, cherry tomatoes and white beans and cook for another 3 minutes until soft.
Add the baby spinach and cook for another 2 minutes until soft.
Season with the lemon juice and pea protein, salt and pepper.

title: Aubergine lentil moussaka with silken tofu topping
instructions: Slice the aubergine, dice the onion and pat the tofu dry and crumble roughly with your fingers.
Brush the aubergine slices thinly with olive oil and roast on a tray at 220 °C for 15 minutes.
Add the beluga lentils, tofu, chopped tomatoes, onion and cinnamon to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
For the cream, blend the silken tofu, nutritional yeast, pea protein and nutmeg until smooth.
Layer the aubergines and lentil sauce in a small baking dish, finish with the cream and bake at 190 °C for 25 minutes.

title: Kohlrabi pea vegetables with smoked tofu and chervil
instructions: Dice the kohlrabi and smoked tofu.
Dry-fry the smoked tofu in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until well browned.
Add the kohlrabi and vegetable stock to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 8 minutes.
Add the peas and simmer for another 3 minutes until cooked through.
Stir the silken tofu with the pea protein until smooth, stir it in, season with nutmeg and top with the smoked tofu and chervil.

title: Edamame pea fritters with soy skyr herb dip
instructions: Let the edamame thaw, slice the spring onions into thin rings and finely chop the parsley.
Blend the edamame, peas and chickpea flour in a blender for 20 seconds until creamy.
Stir in the spring onions.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 3 minutes per side until golden.
For the dip, stir together the soy skyr, parsley and lemon juice until smooth.
Arrange the lamb's lettuce in a plate, drizzle with the dip.

title: Fennel bean ragout with tofu and orange
ingredients: Fennel seeds, orange zest, chilli flakes
instructions: Cut the fennel into wedges, pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, dice the onion and peel and slice the orange.
Dry-fry the tofu in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Sweat the onion, fennel and fennel seeds in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the chopped tomatoes, white beans and pea protein to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Fold in the tofu and serve with the orange pieces and orange zest.

title: Red cabbage lentil pan with apple and tempeh
instructions: Boil the beluga lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until tender and drain.
Cut the red cabbage into thin strips and dice the apple, tempeh, tofu and onion.
Dry-fry the tempeh and tofu in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until well browned.
Add the red cabbage, onion, apple and cloves and cook for another 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the beluga lentils, cider vinegar and pea protein.

title: Chard lupin pan with garlic and chili
instructions: Wash the vegetables, cut the chard into strips and slice the garlic and red chilli.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and fry the garlic and red chilli for 1 minutes until golden all over.
Add the chard and lupins and cook for another 5 minutes until soft.
Season with the lemon juice and nutritional yeast, salt and pepper.

title: Black bean courgette pan with tofu, coriander and lime
instructions: Dice the courgette, tofu and red onion.
Dry-fry the tofu and cumin in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden all over.
Add the courgette and red onion and fry for another 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add the black beans and cook for another 2 minutes until cooked through.
Season with the lime juice and pea protein, salt and pepper.
Sprinkle with the coriander and serve straight away.

title: Green bean mushroom pan with lupins and savory
instructions: Blanch the green beans in boiling water for 4 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Tear the oyster mushrooms into bite-sized pieces and dice the onion.
Dry-fry the oyster mushrooms, onion and savory in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until well browned.
Add the green beans, lupins and tamari and fry for another 4 minutes until cooked through.
Season with the pea protein, salt and pepper.

title: Egg white omelette with spinach, mushrooms and chives
instructions: Slice the mushrooms, halve the cherry tomatoes and slice the chives into thin rings.
Dry-fry the mushrooms in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes until well browned.
Add the baby spinach and cook for another 1 minutes until soft.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites and chives with salt and pepper.
Heat a non-stick pan, pour in the egg mixture and cook covered over medium heat for 4 minutes until set.

title: Broccoli pepper egg muffins with nutritional yeast
instructions: Wash the vegetables, finely chop the broccoli, dice the red pepper and slice the spring onions into thin rings.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites and nutritional yeast with salt and pepper.
Stir in the broccoli, red pepper and spring onions.
Spoon the mixture into 6 muffin cases and bake in the preheated oven at 180 °C for 20 minutes until set.

title: Scrambled eggs with smoked tofu, spring onions and cherry tomatoes
instructions: Dice the smoked tofu, slice the spring onions into thin rings and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Dry-fry the smoked tofu in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes until well browned.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with salt and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture into the pan and cook over low heat for 3 minutes until creamy, stirring slowly.
Sprinkle with the spring onions and serve straight away.

title: Buckwheat egg white pancakes with roasted tomatoes and basil
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220 °C conventional, spread the cherry tomatoes on a lined baking tray and roast for 12 minutes.
Whisk the buckwheat flour, egg whites and eggs into a smooth batter and leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil and cook 3 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Serve the pancakes with the roasted tomatoes and basil.

title: Egg white banana waffles with gluten-free oats and berries
instructions: Blend the gluten-free oats, egg whites, banana, pea protein and cinnamon in a blender for 30 seconds until creamy.
Preheat a waffle iron and cook 2 waffles from the batter for 4 minutes each until golden.
Sprinkle with the mixed berries and serve straight away.

title: Fluffy egg white porridge with blueberries and cinnamon
instructions: Bring the gluten-free oats and soy drink to the boil in a pan and simmer for 3 minutes.
Quickly stir in the egg whites and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until creamy and fluffy.
Stir in the cinnamon.
Sprinkle with the blueberries and flaked almonds and serve straight away.

title: Egg salad in romaine leaves with soy skyr and mustard
instructions: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, refresh in cold water and peel.
Cook the egg whites in a dry non-stick pan for 2 minutes until set and dice.
Chop the eggs and finely chop the radishes and chives.
Put the eggs, egg whites, soy skyr, mustard, chives and radishes in a bowl and mix well.
Spoon the egg salad into the romaine leaves.

title: Courgette egg white fritters with herb soy yoghurt
instructions: Coarsely grate the courgette.
Salt the courgette, leave for 10 minutes and squeeze out firmly.
Whisk the courgette, egg whites, eggs, chickpea flour and pea protein into a smooth batter and leave to rest for 2 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 3 minutes per side until golden.
For the dip, stir together the soy yoghurt and dill until smooth.

title: Chia egg white pancakes with raspberries
instructions: Blend the gluten-free oats, egg whites, pea protein, apple purée and vanilla in a blender for 30 seconds until creamy.
Stir in the chia seeds and leave for 5 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Sprinkle with the raspberries and serve straight away.

title: Breakfast bowl with scrambled eggs, black beans and tomato salsa
instructions: Finely chop the tomatoes, red onion and coriander.
Put the tomatoes, red onion, coriander and lime juice in a bowl and mix well.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with salt and pepper.
Cook the egg mixture in a non-stick pan over low heat for 3 minutes until creamy.
Arrange the spinach, scrambled eggs and warmed beans in a bowl and top with the salsa.

title: Baked peppers with egg and spinach
instructions: Halve the red pepper.
Fill the pepper halves with the spinach and lupins and add 1 egg and some egg white to each.
Bake in the preheated oven at 190 °C for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with the chilli flakes and serve straight away.

title: Gluten-free avocado egg toast with cress
instructions: Toast the gluten-free bread until golden and spread with the mashed avocado.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with salt and pepper.
Cook the egg mixture in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes until set and place on the toast.
Sprinkle with cress and chili flakes and serve with the cherry tomatoes.

title: Tamagoyaki with spinach and nori
instructions: Blanch the baby spinach in boiling water for 1 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites and tamari with salt and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture into a non-stick pan in three batches, top each with spinach and nori and roll up.
Cut the roll into 6 slices and serve with cucumber slices.

title: Savoury quinoa egg breakfast pot with mushrooms
instructions: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 15 minutes.
Slice the mushrooms.
Dry-fry the mushrooms in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until well browned.
Add the quinoa and baby spinach and cook for another 2 minutes until soft.
Whisk the egg and egg whites with the nutritional yeast, pour over and cook covered for 4 minutes until set.

title: Red shakshuka with eggs, pointed peppers and coriander
instructions: Cut the red pepper and onion into strips.
Sweat the onion, red pepper and cumin in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the chopped tomatoes to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 8 minutes.
Pour the egg whites into the sauce, make two hollows, crack in the eggs and cook covered for 6 minutes until set.
Sprinkle with the coriander and serve straight away.

title: Green shakshuka with spinach, leek and eggs
instructions: Wash the vegetables, slice the leek into thin rings and dice the peas.
Sweat the leek, peas and cumin in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the baby spinach and cook for another 2 minutes until soft.
Stir in the egg whites, make two hollows, crack in the eggs and cook covered for 6 minutes until set.
Serve with the soy yoghurt and dill.

title: Potato courgette frittata with leek and basil
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes until tender and drain.
Slice the potatoes, thinly slice the courgette, slice the leek into thin rings and finely chop the basil.
Dry-fry the courgette, leek and potatoes in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until golden all over.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites and basil with salt and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables and bake at 190 °C for 15 minutes until set.

title: Egg spinach curry with lupins and tomatoes
instructions: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, refresh in cold water and peel.
Finely chop the onion and finely grate the ginger.
Sweat the onion, ginger and garam masala in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the chopped tomatoes, baby spinach and lupins to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 8 minutes.
Pour the egg whites into the curry while stirring, add the halved eggs and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Egg fried cauliflower rice with edamame and carrots
instructions: Dice the carrots, slice the spring onions into thin rings, finely grate the ginger and let the edamame thaw.
Dry-fry the cauliflower rice, carrots and ginger in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Whisk the egg and egg whites, add to the pan and scramble for 2 minutes until set.
Add the edamame and tamari and fry for another 2 minutes until cooked through.
Sprinkle with the spring onions and serve straight away.

title: Baked spinach egg nests with beluga lentils
instructions: Boil the beluga lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until tender and drain.
Finely chop the garlic and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Add the baby spinach and garlic and cook for another 2 minutes until soft.
Put the lentils and spinach in a small baking dish, make two hollows, add the egg whites and eggs and bake at 190 °C for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle with the cherry tomatoes and serve straight away.

title: Green asparagus with poached eggs, lupins and herb soy dip
instructions: Blanch the green asparagus in boiling water for 4 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Slide the eggs one at a time into gently simmering water and poach for 3 minutes.
For the dip, stir together the soy skyr, parsley and lemon juice until smooth.
Arrange the green asparagus, lupins and eggs in a plate, drizzle with the dip.

title: Miso rice noodle soup with soft egg, tofu and pak choi
instructions: Boil the egg for 7 minutes, refresh in cold water, peel and halve.
Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, halve the pak choi and slice the spring onions into thin rings.
Add the vegetable stock, pak choi and tofu to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 4 minutes.
Stir the egg whites into the hot broth, stir in the miso and pour over the soaked rice noodles.
Serve with the halved egg and spring onions.

title: White cabbage okonomiyaki with egg and soy skyr sauce
instructions: Cut the white cabbage into thin strips and slice the spring onions into thin rings.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites, chickpea flour, white cabbage and spring onions into a smooth batter and leave to rest for 2 minutes.
Shape the mixture into a pancake in a non-stick pan and fry for 5 minutes per side until golden.
For the sauce, stir together the tomato purée and tamari with 1 tbsp water until smooth.
Drizzle with the sauce and soy skyr in stripes.

title: Kuku sabzi Persian herb omelette with walnuts
instructions: Finely chop the parsley, dill and coriander, slice the spring onions into thin rings and roughly chop the walnuts.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites and turmeric with salt and pepper.
Stir in the parsley, dill, coriander, spring onions and walnuts.
Put everything into a small baking dish and bake in the preheated oven at 180 °C for 22 minutes.
Cut into pieces and serve with the soy yoghurt.

title: Spanish tortilla with egg whites, pepper and onions
instructions: Thinly slice the potatoes and cut the onion and red pepper into thin strips.
Steam the potatoes, onions and pepper with 4 tbsp water, covered, in a non-stick pan for 12 minutes until soft.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with salt and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over, cook covered for 6 minutes, flip and cook for 2 more minutes.
Sprinkle with the black olives and serve straight away.

title: Egg white wraps with smoked tofu, rocket and tomato
instructions: Whisk the egg whites and eggs with salt and pepper.
Cook 2 thin wraps one after the other in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes each until set.
Cut the smoked tofu and tomatoes into sticks.
For the cream, stir together the soy skyr and mustard until smooth.
Spread the wraps with the cream, fill with smoked tofu, rocket and tomato and roll up.

title: Menemen with eggs, green pepper and tomatoes
instructions: Slice the green pepper into thin rings and dice the tomatoes.
Sweat the green pepper in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the tomatoes and pul biber and simmer for another 5 minutes until soft.
Add the eggs and egg whites and cook for 3 minutes, stirring gently, until creamy.

title: Curried egg salad with lupins and apple on romaine
instructions: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, refresh in cold water and peel.
Chop the eggs, dice the apple and celery and tear the romaine lettuce into bite-sized pieces.
Put the eggs, lupins, apple, celery, soy skyr and curry powder in a bowl and mix well.
Serve on the romaine leaves.

title: Stuffed courgette with egg and soy mince
instructions: Pour the vegetable stock over the soy mince, leave to soak for 10 minutes and squeeze out well.
Halve the courgette and dice the tomatoes and onion.
Dry-fry the soy mince, onion, tomatoes and oregano in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes until crumbly.
Hollow out the courgette halves, fill with the filling, pour over the whisked egg and egg whites and bake at 190 °C for 25 minutes.

title: Oven ratatouille with baked eggs
instructions: Dice the aubergine, courgette, red pepper, tomatoes and onion.
Preheat the oven to 210 °C conventional, spread the aubergine, courgette, red pepper, tomatoes, onion and herbes de Provence on a lined baking tray and roast for 25 minutes.
Pour the egg whites over the vegetables, crack the eggs into two hollows and bake for 10 more minutes.
Sprinkle with the basil and serve straight away.

title: Egg millet pan with leek and turmeric
instructions: Rinse the millet in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 15 minutes.
Wash the vegetables, slice the leek into thin rings and dice the carrots.
Sweat the leek and carrots in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the millet and cook for another 2 minutes until cooked through.
Whisk the egg and egg whites with the turmeric, pour over and scramble for 3 minutes until set.
Sprinkle with the chives and serve straight away.

title: Lentil salad with soft-boiled eggs, rocket and mustard
instructions: Boil the beluga lentils in salted water for 20 minutes until tender and drain.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, refresh in cold water and peel.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and finely chop the red onion.
For the dressing, stir together the mustard and cider vinegar with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Toss the beluga lentils, lupins, rocket, cherry tomatoes and red onion with the dressing.
Halve the eggs and arrange on the salad.

title: Air fryer egg white broccoli bites with tomato dip
instructions: Finely chop the broccoli.
Put the broccoli, egg whites, chickpea flour, nutritional yeast and garlic powder in a bowl and mix well.
Spoon the mixture into 8 silicone moulds and cook in the air fryer at 170 °C for 14 minutes until golden.
Simmer the passata with oregano for 3 minutes and serve as a dip.

title: Egg pancake rolls with smoked tofu and cucumber
instructions: Whisk the eggs and egg whites with salt and pepper.
Cook 2 thin pancakes from the egg mixture in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes each.
Cut the smoked tofu and cucumber into sticks.
Spread the pancakes with soy skyr and dill, top with smoked tofu and cucumber, roll up and cut into 8 pieces.

title: Egg drop soup with tofu, spinach and corn
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes and slice the chives into thin rings.
Add the vegetable stock, sweetcorn, tamari and tofu to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 4 minutes.
Stir the cornflour with 2 tbsp water and stir in, whisk the egg and egg whites and pour into the soup in a thin stream while stirring.
Add the baby spinach and cook for another 1 minutes until soft.
Sprinkle with the chives and serve straight away.

title: Avgolemono soup with egg, lemon, rice and tofu
instructions: Dice the tofu and carrots.
Add the vegetable stock, short-grain rice and carrots to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Whisk the egg, egg whites and lemon juice, gradually whisk in 4 tbsp hot stock and stir the mixture into the soup off the boil.
Add the tofu and cook for another 3 minutes until cooked through.
Sprinkle with the dill and serve straight away.

title: Clear vegetable broth with egg custard, carrots and peas
instructions: Whisk the eggs, egg whites, soy drink and nutmeg, pour into a small dish and bake in a water bath at 160 °C for 25 minutes until set.
Wash the vegetables, slice the carrots and slice the leek into thin rings.
Add the vegetable stock, carrots, leek and peas to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 10 minutes.
Cut the egg custard into diamonds, add to the soup and sprinkle with chives.

title: Chickpea flour egg flatbread with spinach and tomato salad
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour, eggs, egg whites and cumin into a smooth batter and leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Stir in the baby spinach.
Cook the batter as one large flatbread in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes per side.
Dice the tomatoes and finely chop the red onion.
Season with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.

title: Protein egg edamame snack box with cucumber sticks
instructions: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, refresh in cold water and peel.
Cut the cucumber into sticks and let the edamame thaw.
Blanch the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
For the dip, stir together the soy skyr and mustard until smooth.
Halve the eggs and pack into a container with the edamame, cucumber sticks and dip.

title: Meal prep egg vegetable box with quinoa and broccoli
instructions: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 15 minutes.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, refresh in cold water and peel.
Cut the broccoli into small florets and cut the red pepper into strips.
Steam the broccoli and red pepper for 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Cook the egg whites in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes until set and cut into strips.
Let cool, pack into an airtight container and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.

title: Spinach egg gratin with silken tofu and nutmeg
instructions: Blanch the leaf spinach in boiling water for 1 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Finely chop the onion.
For the cream, blend the silken tofu, egg whites, nutritional yeast and nutmeg until smooth.
Put the spinach and onion in a small baking dish, pour over the cream, add two eggs on top and bake at 190 °C for 18 minutes.

title: Egyptian egg spinach pan with lupins and dukkah spice
instructions: Dice the tomatoes.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Dry-fry the baby spinach, lupins and tomatoes in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes until soft.
Stir in the egg whites, crack the eggs on top and cook covered for 5 minutes until set.
Mix the sesame with cumin and coriander seeds and sprinkle over.

title: Japanese oyakodon-style tofu egg pot with onions
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, thinly slice the onion and slice the spring onions into thin rings.
Add the vegetable stock, tamari, onion and tofu to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Lightly whisk the eggs and egg whites, pour over the tofu and onions and cook covered for 2 minutes until just set.
Rinse and warm the shirataki rice and slide the tofu egg mixture on top, sprinkle with spring onions.

title: Skyr bowl with persimmon, pomegranate and puffed quinoa
instructions: Dice the persimmon.
Stir the skyr with cinnamon until smooth and spoon into a bowl.
Sprinkle with the persimmon, pomegranate seeds and puffed quinoa and serve straight away.

title: Cottage cheese buckwheat pancakes with blueberries
instructions: Blend the cottage cheese, egg whites, buckwheat flour and cinnamon in a blender for 30 seconds until creamy.
Heat a non-stick pan with a little oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Sprinkle with the blueberries and serve straight away.

title: Quark Kaiserschmarrn made with rice flour and apple purée
instructions: Stir the low-fat quark, egg, rice flour and vanilla until smooth, whisk the egg whites until stiff and fold in.
Pour the batter into a non-stick pan, cook covered for 4 minutes, flip and tear into pieces with two spatulas.
Fry for another 2 minutes until golden and serve with the apple purée and cinnamon.

title: Savoury cottage cheese bowl with cucumber, radishes and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Dice the cucumber, slice the radishes and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Arrange the cottage cheese, cucumber, radishes and cherry tomatoes in a bowl.
Sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds and cress and serve straight away.

title: Baked skyr oat bake with rhubarb and strawberries
instructions: Wash the fruit, chop the rhubarb and quarter the strawberries.
Stir together the skyr, gluten-free oats, egg whites, pea protein and vanilla.
Stir in the rhubarb and strawberries.
Put everything into a small baking dish and bake in the preheated oven at 180 °C for 25 minutes.

title: Overnight quark with chia, mango and lime
instructions: Put the low-fat quark, chia seeds, lime juice and lime zest in a screw-top jar and mix well.
Cover and leave to set in the fridge for at least 6 hours.
Thaw the mango, dice it and spread over the quark.

title: Filled egg white omelette with spinach, light feta and cherry tomatoes
instructions: Halve the cherry tomatoes and pat the light feta dry and crumble roughly with your fingers.
Dry-fry the baby spinach in a non-stick pan for 1 minutes until soft.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with salt and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over the spinach, crumble the feta over and cook covered for 4 minutes until set.
Arrange the cherry tomatoes in a plate.

title: Greek yoghurt with figs, walnuts and cinnamon
instructions: Quarter the figs and roughly chop the walnuts.
Arrange the Greek yoghurt in a bowl.
Sprinkle with the figs, walnuts and cinnamon and serve straight away.

title: Scrambled eggs with cottage cheese, chives and roasted pepper
instructions: Cut the red pepper into strips and slice the chives into thin rings.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C conventional, spread the red pepper on a lined baking tray and roast for 12 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with salt and pepper.
Cook the egg mixture over low heat for 3 minutes, stirring slowly, until creamy, then fold in the cottage cheese.
Arrange the red pepper in a plate and sprinkle with the chives.

title: Matcha skyr with kiwi and desiccated coconut
instructions: Peel and slice the kiwi.
Stir the skyr with the matcha until smooth and spoon into a bowl.
Sprinkle with the kiwi and desiccated coconut and serve straight away.

title: Cheesecake cream in a glass with raspberries
instructions: Put the low-fat quark, maple syrup and lemon zest in a bowl and mix well.
Layer the low-fat quark and raspberries in a glass one after the other.
Cover and chill in the fridge for at least 30 minutes.

title: Air fryer quark coconut balls
instructions: Put the low-fat quark, egg whites, pea protein, rice flour and vanilla in a bowl and mix well.
With damp hands shape the mixture into 8 balls.
Roll the balls in the desiccated coconut and air-fry at 170 °C for 10 minutes until golden.

title: Mozzarella tomato skewers with basil and skyr dip
instructions: Dice the light mozzarella.
Thread the cherry tomatoes, light mozzarella and basil alternately onto 6 skewers.
For the dip, stir together the skyr and lemon juice until smooth.

title: Chocolate quark mousse with cherries
instructions: Stone and chop the cherries.
Whip the low-fat quark with the cocoa and maple syrup until airy.
Layer the low-fat quark and cherries in a dessert glass one after the other.
Cover and chill in the fridge for at least 20 minutes.

title: Baked cinnamon apple skyr crumble
instructions: Dice the apple and roughly chop the almonds.
Preheat the oven to 190 °C conventional, spread the apple and cinnamon on a lined baking tray and roast until soft for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle the oats and almonds over and bake for 8 more minutes until crisp.
Arrange the skyr in a bowl and sprinkle with the apple and gluten-free oats.

title: Frozen yoghurt bark with berries and pistachios
instructions: Put the Greek yoghurt and maple syrup in a bowl and mix well.
Spread the yoghurt 1 cm thick on a board lined with baking paper and scatter over the berries and chopped pistachios.
Freeze for at least 3 hours and break into pieces.

title: Peach quark gratin with flaked almonds
instructions: Cut the peach into wedges.
Put the low-fat quark, egg whites and vanilla in a bowl and mix well.
Lay the peach wedges in a small baking dish and spread the quark mixture over.
Sprinkle with the flaked almonds and bake at 200 °C for 15 minutes until golden.

title: Caprese salad with light mozzarella, egg and rocket
instructions: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, refresh in cold water and peel.
Slice the tomatoes and light mozzarella and quarter the eggs.
Spread the rocket on a plate, layer the tomato and mozzarella slices alternately on top and add the egg quarters.
Drizzle with lemon juice, season with salt and pepper and top with basil.

title: Beluga lentil salad with light feta and skyr herb dressing
instructions: Rinse the beluga lentils in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 20 minutes.
Dice the cucumber, finely chop the red onion, finely chop the parsley and pat the light feta dry and crumble roughly with your fingers.
For the dressing, stir together the skyr, parsley and lemon juice until smooth.
Toss the beluga lentils, cucumber and red onion with the dressing.
Sprinkle with the light feta and serve straight away.

title: Broccoli egg salad with quark mustard dressing
instructions: Cut the broccoli into small florets and slice the chives into thin rings.
Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, refresh in cold water and peel.
For the dressing, stir together the low-fat quark and mustard with 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Quarter the eggs, toss with the broccoli and dressing and sprinkle with chives.

title: Asparagus strawberry salad with light mozzarella and rocket
instructions: Cut the green asparagus into rough pieces, quarter the strawberries and tear the light mozzarella into bite-sized pieces.
Blanch the green asparagus in boiling water for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Arrange the rocket, green asparagus, strawberries and light mozzarella in a plate.
Drizzle with lemon juice and serve with freshly ground pepper.

title: Cucumber dill salad with cottage cheese and egg
instructions: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, refresh in cold water and peel.
Thinly slice the cucumber, finely chop the dill and slice the eggs.
Toss the cucumber slices with apple cider vinegar, dill, salt and pepper.
Arrange the cucumber, cottage cheese and eggs in a bowl.

title: Beetroot carpaccio with light feta, skyr and walnuts
instructions: Thinly slice the beetroot, roughly chop the walnuts and pat the light feta dry and crumble roughly with your fingers.
Arrange the beetroot slices in a circle on a plate and drizzle with lemon juice.
Dot the skyr over, then scatter with rocket, feta and walnuts.

title: Broccoli cheese soup with low-fat quark
instructions: Cut the broccoli into small florets and dice the onion.
Sweat the onion in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the vegetable stock and broccoli to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth with a stick blender and season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the grated cheese and low-fat quark until the cheese has melted and season with nutmeg.

title: Cold cucumber yoghurt soup with dill and walnuts
instructions: Coarsely grate the cucumber, finely chop the garlic and roughly chop the walnuts.
Blend the Greek yoghurt, garlic and dill in a blender for 20 seconds until creamy.
Stir in the grated cucumber, add 2 tbsp cold water and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with the walnuts and dill and serve straight away.

title: Tomato pepper soup with a skyr topping and grated cheese
instructions: Dice the red pepper and onion.
Sweat the onion and red pepper in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the passata to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth with a stick blender and season with salt and pepper.
Stir in half the skyr, pour the soup into a bowl and serve with the remaining skyr, grated cheese and basil.

title: Spinach soup with poached eggs and light feta
instructions: Dice the onion and pat the light feta dry and crumble roughly with your fingers.
Sweat the onion in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the vegetable stock and baby spinach to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 4 minutes.
Blend finely with the skyr and season with nutmeg.
Slide the eggs one at a time into gently simmering water and poach for 3 minutes.
Pour the soup into a deep plate, add the eggs and sprinkle with feta.

title: Courgette lasagne with cottage cheese and lentil bolognese
instructions: Thinly slice the courgette.
Add the passata, red lentils and oregano to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Stir the cottage cheese with the egg whites.
Layer the courgette slices, lentil bolognese and cottage cheese in a small baking dish and sprinkle with grated cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven at 190 °C for 30 minutes.

title: Stuffed peppers with quinoa, light feta and quark
instructions: Rinse the quinoa in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 12 minutes.
Halve the red pepper, roughly chop the baby spinach and pat the light feta dry and crumble roughly with your fingers.
Put the quinoa, baby spinach, light feta, low-fat quark and oregano in a bowl and mix well.
Fill the red pepper with the quinoa.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C conventional, spread the red pepper on a lined baking tray and bake for 25 minutes.

title: Cauliflower cheese gratin with egg and quark
instructions: Cut the cauliflower into small florets.
Steam the cauliflower for 8 minutes until tender-crisp.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites and low-fat quark with salt and pepper.
Put the cauliflower into a small baking dish, pour the egg mixture over and sprinkle with grated cheese and nutmeg.
Bake in the preheated oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes.

title: Palak-style spinach cottage cheese curry with cauliflower rice
instructions: Dice the onion and tomatoes and finely chop the garlic and ginger.
Sweat the onion, garlic, ginger and garam masala in a pot with 3 tbsp water for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the tomatoes and baby spinach to the pot, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 6 minutes.
Blend half of the soup with a stick blender to thicken it and season to taste.
Fold in the cottage cheese and warm for 2 minutes, cook the cauliflower rice in a pan for 4 minutes and serve alongside.

title: Aubergine rolls with herb quark in tomato sauce
instructions: Thinly slice the aubergine and finely chop the parsley and basil.
Fry the aubergine slices in a dry non-stick pan for 2 minutes per side.
Put the low-fat quark and parsley in a bowl and mix well.
Spread the quark onto the slices, roll up and place in a dish with the passata.
Sprinkle with grated cheese, bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes and serve with basil.

title: Oven frittata with broccoli, light feta and peas
instructions: Cut the broccoli into small florets and pat the light feta dry and crumble roughly with your fingers.
Blanch the broccoli and peas in boiling water for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Whisk the eggs, egg whites and dill with salt and pepper.
Put the vegetables into a small dish, pour the egg mixture over, crumble the feta on top and bake at 190 °C for 18 minutes until set.

title: Chard feta pan with chickpeas and egg
instructions: Cut the chard into strips, finely chop the garlic and pat the light feta dry and crumble roughly with your fingers.
Dry-fry the chard, garlic and chickpeas in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes until soft.
Pour the egg whites and egg over, cook covered for 4 minutes until set and sprinkle with feta and chilli flakes.

title: Courgette noodles with quark basil pesto and mozzarella
instructions: Cut the courgette into thin strips and dice the light mozzarella.
Blend the low-fat quark, basil, pumpkin seeds and garlic in a blender for 30 seconds until creamy.
Dry-fry the courgette in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes until tender-crisp.
Toss the courgette noodles with the pesto and serve with the mozzarella.

title: Baked light feta with roast vegetables and skyr dip
instructions: Cut the red pepper and courgette into 2 cm cubes and cut the red onion into wedges.
Put the vegetables and cherry tomatoes into a dish, place the feta in the middle and sprinkle with oregano.
Bake in the preheated oven at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
For the dip, stir together the skyr until smooth.
Arrange everything in a plate, drizzle with the dip.

title: Air fryer kohlrabi schnitzel with cheese crust and skyr dip
instructions: Peel and slice the kohlrabi.
Blanch the kohlrabi in boiling water for 4 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Coat the kohlrabi slices in rice flour, egg whites and grated cheese.
Cook the kohlrabi in the air fryer at 190 °C for 12 minutes until crisp, shaking halfway through.
For the dip, stir together the skyr and chives until smooth.

title: Air fryer pea mint quark fritters
instructions: Roughly mash the peas with a fork.
Finely chop the mint.
Put the peas, low-fat quark, egg whites, rice flour and mint in a bowl and mix well.
With damp hands shape the mixture into 6 flat fritters.
Air-fry the fritters at 190 °C for 12 minutes until golden and drizzle with lemon juice.

title: Baked sweet potato with cottage cheese, spinach and egg whites
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C conventional, spread the sweet potato on a lined baking tray and roast until soft for 35 minutes.
Dry-fry the baby spinach in a non-stick pan for 1 minutes until soft.
Cook the egg whites in the same pan for 2 minutes until set.
Cut open the sweet potato, fill with spinach, egg whites and cottage cheese and sprinkle with paprika.

title: Tandoori cauliflower with yoghurt mint raita and beluga lentils
instructions: Cut the cauliflower into small florets, coarsely grate the cucumber and finely chop the mint.
Toss the cauliflower with 3 tbsp yoghurt and tandoori spice and roast at 220 °C for 25 minutes.
Rinse the beluga lentils in a sieve and cook in twice the volume of lightly salted water for 20 minutes.
For the dip, stir together the Greek yoghurt, cucumber and mint until smooth.
Arrange the cauliflower and beluga lentils in a plate, drizzle with the dip.

title: Çılbır: poached eggs on garlic yoghurt with pul biber
instructions: Finely grate the garlic, halve the cherry tomatoes and finely chop the dill.
Put the Greek yoghurt and garlic in a bowl and mix well.
Slide the eggs one at a time into gently simmering water and poach for 3 minutes.
Spread the garlic yoghurt on a plate, place the eggs on top, sprinkle with pul biber and dill and serve with the cherry tomatoes.

title: Okonomiyaki with white cabbage and egg whites and a skyr topping
instructions: Cut the white cabbage into thin strips, slice the spring onions into thin rings and cut the nori into thin strips.
Put the white cabbage, egg whites, eggs and rice flour in a bowl and mix well.
Shape the mixture into a thick pancake in a non-stick pan and fry covered for 5 minutes per side.
For the topping, stir together the skyr and tamari until smooth.
Sprinkle with the spring onions and nori and serve straight away.

title: Polenta pizza with light mozzarella and mushrooms
instructions: Stir the polenta into 120 ml boiling salted water and leave to swell for 5 minutes, then stir in the egg whites.
Spread the mixture into a round on baking paper and pre-bake at 220 °C for 15 minutes.
Slice the mushrooms and slice the light mozzarella.
Top with the passata, mushrooms, mozzarella and oregano and bake for 10 more minutes.
Sprinkle with the basil and serve straight away.

title: Crustless spanakopita bake with light feta and cottage cheese
instructions: Slice the spring onions into thin rings, finely chop the dill and pat the light feta dry and crumble roughly with your fingers.
Dry-fry the baby spinach and spring onions in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes until soft.
Put the baby spinach, light feta, cottage cheese, eggs and dill in a bowl and mix well.
Put everything into a small baking dish and bake in the preheated oven at 190 °C for 25 minutes.

title: Meal prep: quinoa boxes with green beans, light feta and omelette strips
