Serve lukewarm sprinkled with crumbled feta and pomegranate seeds.

title: Warm sweetheart cabbage and apple salad with smoked tofu and mustard dressing
instructions: Dice the smoked tofu and fry in 5 g of the oil in a pan for 5 minutes until crisp, then remove.
Cut the sweetheart cabbage into fine strips and fry it with the caraway in the pan for 4 minutes until slightly wilted.
Stir the mustard, cider vinegar, maple syrup, remaining oil, salt and pepper together. Cut the apple into thin wedges.
Mix the warm cabbage with the apple and dressing, spread the tofu on top and sprinkle with pumpkin seeds and chives.

title: Fasolia – Lebanese white bean stew with beef and tomato
instructions: Cut the beef into small cubes and brown in the oil in a pot for 5 minutes, then fry the chopped onion and garlic for 3 minutes.
Toast the tomato purée and spices for 1 minute, then deglaze with the strained tomatoes and stock.
Braise covered for 40 minutes, then add the beans and simmer for another 15 minutes.
Season and serve sprinkled with fresh coriander.

title: Indian chicken shorba with spinach, tomato and ginger
instructions: Finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger and sweat in the oil for 4 minutes, then toast the spices for 1 minute.
Dice the tomatoes, add them with the stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Cut the chicken into small cubes, add them and poach for 8 minutes until cooked.
Stir in the spinach, let it wilt for 1 minute, season and serve with coriander.

title: Chicken thighs with creamed spinach and mushrooms
instructions: Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper and fry skin side down in a dry pan for 10 minutes until crisp, turn and cook for another 8 minutes.
Quarter the mushrooms and fry them in the butter with thyme for 4 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and spinach and let it wilt, pour in the cream and reduce for 2 minutes with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Put the creamed spinach and mushrooms on a plate and lay the chicken thighs on top.

title: Salmon with herb cream cheese crust and broccoli
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Stir the cream cheese with the chopped herbs, almond flour, salt and pepper.
Place the salmon in a small baking dish, spread with the herb mixture and bake for 15 minutes until the crust is lightly browned.
Divide the broccoli into florets, cook in salted water for 4 minutes, drain and toss in the butter.
Serve the salmon with the broccoli and a lemon wedge.

title: Lamb köfte with tzatziki and cucumber salad
instructions: Finely grate the onion, knead it with the lamb mince, cumin, pul biber, salt and pepper and shape 6 long köfte.
Fry the köfte in 10 g of the oil in a grill pan for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Grate half the cucumber, squeeze it out and stir with the yoghurt, crushed garlic, dill, 5 g of the oil and salt to make tzatziki.
Slice the remaining cucumber, mix with the olives, mint and remaining oil and serve with the köfte and tzatziki.

title: Tofu and mushroom pan with walnuts and spinach
instructions: Pat the tofu dry, dice it and fry in 10 g of the oil in a pan for 6 minutes until golden on all sides, then remove.
Slice the mushrooms and fry them in the remaining oil with thyme for 5 minutes, then fry the garlic for 1 minute.
Roughly chop the walnuts and toast them for 2 minutes, then add the spinach and let it wilt.
Return the tofu to the pan, season with tamari, chilli flakes and pepper and serve.

title: Baked feta with peppers, olives and eggs
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Cut the pepper into strips, halve the cherry tomatoes and put them in a small baking dish with the olives and oil.
Place the feta as a block in the middle, sprinkle with oregano and chilli flakes and bake for 15 minutes.
Make two hollows in the vegetables, crack the eggs into them and bake for another 8 to 10 minutes until the whites are set.
Season with pepper and serve straight from the dish.

title: Mackerel with avocado cucumber salad and capers
instructions: Pat the mackerel fillets dry, salt them and fry skin side down in 5 g of the oil in a pan for 4 minutes until crisp, turn and cook for 1 more minute.
Dice the avocado and cucumber and mix with the capers, rocket, dill, lemon juice, remaining oil, salt and pepper.
Put the salad on a plate and lay the mackerel fillets on top.

title: Lentil quinoa box with beetroot and cottage cheese
instructions: Cook the beluga lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until al dente and the quinoa in twice its volume of salted water for 15 minutes, drain both and let cool.
Dice the beetroot. Stir the oil, cider vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper into a dressing and mix with the lentils and quinoa.
Pack the lentil quinoa, beetroot, rocket and cottage cheese side by side into a container and sprinkle with pumpkin seeds.
Keep sealed in the fridge for up to 3 days and eat cold.

title: Beef bibimbap box with spinach and carrot
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions and let it cool. Hard-boil the egg for 9 minutes, refresh and halve.
Blanch the spinach and sprouts for 1 minute each, squeeze out and season with half the sesame oil and a little tamari. Cut the carrot into fine sticks.
Cut the beef into thin strips and fry in a hot pan with the garlic, remaining tamari and sesame oil for 3 minutes, then let cool.
Pack the rice, vegetables, beef and egg side by side into a container, put the gochujang into a small pot and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
At the office eat cold or reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot.

title: Chickpea tikka box with basmati and spinach
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions and let it cool.
Dice the pepper, chop the ginger and garlic, sweat everything in the oil for 4 minutes and toast the spices for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, strained tomatoes and coconut milk, simmer for 10 minutes, stir in the spinach and let it wilt for 1 minute.
Pack the curry and rice side by side into a container, let cool and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.
To eat, reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot, stirring once.

title: Miso salmon box with brown rice, broccoli and cucumber
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions and let it cool. Preheat the oven to 200 °C.
Stir the miso with the maple syrup and 1 tsp water, brush it over the salmon and bake on a tray with the broccoli florets for 12 minutes.
Thinly slice the cucumber and mix with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Pack the rice, salmon, broccoli and cucumber side by side into a container, sprinkle with sesame, let cool and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
At the office eat cold or reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot.

title: Harissa chicken box with millet, carrots and yoghurt dip
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Rub the chicken with the harissa, 5 g of the oil and salt, cut the carrots into sticks and mix with the remaining oil and cumin.
Bake the chicken and carrots on a tray for 22 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, let cool and slice.
Rinse the millet with hot water, let it swell in 150 ml salted water for 15 minutes and mix with lemon juice and parsley.
Stir the yoghurt with mint and salt and fill it into a small pot. Put the millet, carrots and chicken into a container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.
At the office eat cold or reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot.

title: Tempeh buckwheat box with red cabbage, cucumber and peanut dressing
instructions: Cook the buckwheat in twice its volume of salted water for 12 minutes, drain and let cool.
Slice the tempeh and fry it in the oil for 3 minutes per side until golden, then deglaze with 1 tsp tamari.
Finely shred the red cabbage and cut the cucumber into sticks. Stir the peanut butter, remaining tamari, lime juice, maple syrup, grated ginger and 2 tbsp water together.
Pack the buckwheat, vegetables and tempeh side by side into a container and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.
Take the dressing separately in a small screw-top jar.

title: Cinnamon roll overnight oats with soy skyr and pea protein
instructions: Mix the oats, pea protein, cinnamon and vanilla in a jar.
Stir in the soy drink and half of the soy skyr until no lumps remain.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Finely dice the apple, spoon the remaining soy skyr on top as a layer and scatter with the apple and a pinch of cinnamon.

title: Pistachio cardamom chia pudding with orange segments and pea protein
instructions: Whisk the chia seeds, pea protein and cardamom with the soy drink in a jar until smooth.
Stir again after 10 minutes and chill covered for at least 4 hours.
Peel the orange and cut out the segments with a sharp knife.
Top the pudding with the orange segments and chopped pistachios.

title: Black Forest millet flake porridge with cherries, cocoa and pea protein
instructions: Bring the millet flakes and soy drink to the boil in a small pan and let them swell for 3 minutes, stirring.
Take off the heat, whisk the pea protein, cocoa and vanilla with 3 tbsp water until smooth and stir it in.
Warm the cherries in a small pan for 3 minutes until some juice forms.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and spread the warm cherries on top.

title: Red lentil pancakes with blueberries and vanilla soy skyr
instructions: Soak the red lentils for 4 hours, drain and blend with the soy protein, baking powder and 80 ml water until smooth.
Brush a non-stick pan with the rapeseed oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter, 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Stir the soy skyr with the vanilla.
Stack the pancakes and serve with the vanilla skyr and blueberries.

title: PB&J overnight oats with strawberries, peanut butter and soy skyr
instructions: Stir the oats, pea protein, soy drink and soy skyr together in a jar.
Mash half of the strawberries with a fork into a rough purée and spoon it on top as a layer.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Slice the remaining strawberries, lay them on the oats and drizzle with the peanut butter.

title: Apple strudel quinoa porridge with raisins, cinnamon and soy protein
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and simmer covered with the soy drink and 100 ml water for 15 minutes.
Dice the apple and steam with the raisins, cinnamon and 2 tbsp water for 4 minutes until soft.
Whisk the soy protein with 3 tbsp water until smooth and stir it into the quinoa.
Put the porridge into a bowl and spread the cinnamon apples on top.

title: Banana bread baked oats with walnuts and silken tofu
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Blend the oats, silken tofu, pea protein, half of the banana, baking powder, cinnamon and 40 ml water until smooth.
Pour into a small ovenproof dish and top with the remaining banana slices and walnuts.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden brown and let cool briefly.

title: Tahini date overnight oats with soy protein and cinnamon
instructions: Finely chop the dates and mix with the oats, soy protein and cinnamon in a jar.
Stir in the soy drink until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
In the morning stir and drizzle the tahini over the top in a thin line.

title: Mocha protein pudding with espresso, cocoa and cherries
instructions: Whisk the soy drink with the agar agar, bring to the boil and simmer for 2 minutes, stirring.
Take off the heat and briskly whisk in the espresso, soy protein and cocoa until smooth.
Pour into a glass and leave to set in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Let the cherries thaw and spoon them onto the pudding before serving.

title: Cinnamon rice porridge with soy protein and warm plums
instructions: Bring the rice to the boil with the soy drink and 150 ml water and let it swell over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stone and quarter the plums and steam them with half of the cinnamon and 2 tbsp water for 4 minutes until soft.
Whisk the soy protein with 4 tbsp water until smooth and stir it into the hot rice.
Spoon the rice porridge into a bowl, lay the plums on top and dust with the remaining cinnamon.

title: Peach ginger soy skyr bowl with popped amaranth
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein and grated ginger until smooth.
Halve and stone the peach and cut it into thin wedges.
Spread the skyr in a shallow bowl, top with the peach wedges and sprinkle with the popped amaranth.

title: Chai amaranth porridge with pear and pea protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with the soy drink, 120 ml water and the chai spice and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Whisk the pea protein with 4 tbsp water until smooth and stir it into the porridge.
Cut the pear into thin wedges.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the pear wedges.

title: Mango passion fruit overnight quinoa with soy skyr and coconut
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water, cook covered in 80 ml water for 12 minutes and let cool.
Stir the quinoa with the soy skyr and soy protein in a jar.
Dice the mango and layer it on top, halve the passion fruit and spoon the pulp over it.
Sprinkle with the desiccated coconut, seal and chill overnight.

title: Spiced pear Bircher made with buckwheat flakes and soy skyr
instructions: Stir the buckwheat flakes with the soy skyr, soy protein, soy drink and spices.
Coarsely grate half of the pear and fold it in.
Chill covered for at least 30 minutes or overnight.
Cut the remaining pear into thin wedges and arrange them on the Bircher.

title: Coconut matcha millet porridge with kiwi and pea protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and simmer covered with the soy drink, coconut milk and 80 ml water for 15 minutes.
Whisk the pea protein and matcha with 4 tbsp water until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Peel the kiwi and cut it into slices.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the kiwi slices.

title: Redcurrant vanilla protein waffles made with chickpea flour
instructions: Mix the chickpea flour, pea protein, baking powder and vanilla and stir with the soy drink into a thick batter.
Brush the waffle iron with the rapeseed oil and bake 2 waffles for 4 minutes each until golden brown.
Strip the redcurrants from their stalks.
Serve the waffles with the soy yoghurt and redcurrants.

title: Moong dal chilla with tofu filling and mint soy yoghurt
instructions: Soak the mung dal for 4 hours, drain and blend with the pea protein, turmeric, ginger, a little salt and 80 ml water until smooth.
Crumble the tofu, finely dice the tomato and onion and fry with the cumin in a pan for 4 minutes.
Brush the pan with the rapeseed oil and cook 2 thin chillas from the batter, 2 minutes per side.
Stir the soy yoghurt with the chopped mint.
Fill the chillas with the tofu mixture, fold them and serve with the mint yoghurt.

title: Spanish potato and tofu tortilla with peppers
instructions: Peel the potato, cut it into thin slices and cook with the onion and pepper in a small non-stick pan with the olive oil and 3 tbsp water, covered, for 10 minutes until soft.
Blend the tofu with the chickpea flour, pea protein, turmeric, salt and 80 ml water until smooth.
Pour the mixture over the vegetables and let it set over low heat, covered, for 10 minutes.
Turn it with the help of a plate, fry for another 4 minutes and cut into 4 pieces.

title: Tofu migas with corn tortilla strips, peppers and tomato salsa
instructions: Cut the tortilla into thin strips and toast them in a dry non-stick pan for 3 minutes until crisp, then remove.
Dice the tomatoes and mix with the lime juice, coriander and salt to make a salsa.
Dice the pepper and toast it for 3 minutes, crumble in the tofu, season with the cumin, turmeric, chilli and nutritional yeast and fry for 5 minutes.
Fold in the tortilla strips and serve with the salsa.

title: Red lentil wraps with tofu scramble, tomato and rocket
instructions: Soak the red lentils for 3 hours, drain and blend with 70 ml water and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Cook 2 thin wraps from the batter in a dry non-stick pan, 2 minutes per side.
Crumble the tofu and fry it with the turmeric, cumin and nutritional yeast for 5 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
Fill the wraps with the tofu scramble, diced tomato and rocket and roll them up.

title: Farinata slices with rocket and lemon tofu ricotta
instructions: Preheat the oven to 230 °C with a small tin inside, whisk the chickpea flour with 120 ml water, rosemary and salt until smooth and let rest for 15 minutes.
Brush the tin with the olive oil, pour in the batter and bake for 15 minutes until set and golden.
Mash the tofu with the pea protein, lemon juice, 2 tbsp water, salt and pepper into a creamy ricotta.
Cut the farinata into 4 pieces and top with the tofu ricotta, rocket and halved cherry tomatoes.

title: Green shakshuka with tofu, spinach and courgette
instructions: Dice the courgette small and finely chop the garlic and chilli.
Heat the olive oil in a small pan and fry the courgette, garlic, chilli and cumin for 5 minutes.
Add the spinach and edamame and let the spinach wilt for 2 minutes.
Cut the tofu into 4 thick slices, nestle them into the vegetables and leave covered for 5 minutes to warm through.
Season with salt, pepper and coriander and serve in the pan.

title: Sweet potato toast with edamame smash and radishes
instructions: Cut the sweet potato lengthways into 3 slices just under 1 cm thick and roast in the toaster or oven at 220 °C for 15 minutes until soft.
Boil the edamame for 3 minutes, drain and roughly mash with the pea protein, lime juice, 2 tbsp water, salt and pepper.
Cut the smoked tofu into thin slices and the radishes into fine slices.
Spread the sweet potato slices with the edamame smash, top with the tofu and radishes and sprinkle with chilli flakes.

title: Savoury quinoa porridge with mushrooms, spinach and smoked tofu
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and simmer covered in the stock for 15 minutes until soft.
Whisk the pea protein and nutritional yeast with 3 tbsp water until smooth and stir into the quinoa to make a creamy porridge.
Slice the mushrooms, dice the smoked tofu and brown them in a dry pan for 5 minutes.
Wilt the spinach in the pan for 1 minute, arrange everything on the porridge and season with pepper.

title: Soy chunk breakfast hash with sweet potato and peppers
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in hot water with the tamari for 10 minutes, then squeeze them out well.
Cut the sweet potato into small dice and cook covered in a non-stick pan with the rapeseed oil and 3 tbsp water for 8 minutes.
Dice the pepper, onion and tofu, add them with the soy chunks and smoked paprika and fry briskly uncovered for 7 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Oven-baked peppers filled with herby tofu scramble
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C, halve the pepper lengthways, deseed and pre-bake for 10 minutes.
Crumble the tofu and mix with the turmeric, nutritional yeast, herbs, salt and pepper.
Fill the pepper halves with the tofu, top with the halved cherry tomatoes and bake for another 12 minutes.

title: Japanese breakfast plate with tofu steak, spinach gomaae and cucumber
instructions: Cut the tofu into 2 thick steaks, pat dry and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 4 minutes per side until golden brown, then glaze with half of the tamari and the ginger.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, refresh in cold water and squeeze well.
Toast and crush the sesame seeds, stir with the remaining tamari into a dressing and toss the spinach in it.
Slice the cucumber thinly, dress with the rice vinegar and arrange everything on a plate.

title: Courgette chickpea flour fritters with tofu and dill soy skyr
instructions: Coarsely grate the courgette, salt it, leave for 5 minutes and squeeze it out well.
Finely crumble the tofu and mix with the courgette, chickpea flour, pea protein, half of the dill and pepper.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan and fry 4 fritters from the mixture for 4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Stir the soy skyr with the remaining dill and serve with the fritters.

title: Indonesian tempeh and tofu breakfast plate with cucumber, tomato and sambal
instructions: Cut the tempeh and tofu into 4 thin slices each and marinate with the tamari, ground coriander seeds and garlic powder.
Fry in a dry non-stick pan for 3 minutes per side until crisp.
Slice the cucumber and tomatoes.
Arrange the tempeh and tofu on a plate with the vegetables and sambal.

title: Polenta slices with tofu tomato ragout and basil
instructions: Stir the polenta into 100 ml boiling salted water, let it swell for 5 minutes, spread it 1 cm thick on a board and let cool.
Dice the tomatoes and garlic, crumble the tofu and simmer everything for 8 minutes into a thick ragout.
Whisk the pea protein with 2 tbsp water until smooth, stir into the ragout and season.
Cut the polenta into 4 slices, fry in the olive oil for 2 minutes per side and serve with the ragout and basil.

title: Strawberry cheesecake protein shake with soy skyr and lemon
instructions: Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Pistachio protein ice cream with soy drink and vanilla
instructions: Blend the soy drink, pea protein, silken tofu, maple syrup, vanilla and two thirds of the pistachios until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a freezer-safe tub and freeze for at least 12 hours.
Let the block soften for 10 minutes, break it into pieces and blend in a food processor until creamy.
Spoon into a bowl and sprinkle with the remaining chopped pistachios.

title: Chocolate peanut silken tofu cream with pea protein
instructions: Drain the silken tofu and blend with the pea protein, cocoa, maple syrup and half of the peanut butter for 1 minute until creamy.
Spoon into a dessert glass and chill for 1 hour.
Drizzle with the remaining peanut butter before serving.

title: Taiwanese salt and pepper tofu from the air fryer
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Mix the cornflour with the five-spice powder, white pepper and salt, toss the tofu in it and drizzle with the rapeseed oil.
Cook in the air fryer at 200 °C for 15 minutes until crisp, shaking twice.
Sprinkle with the spring onion greens and eat hot.

title: Air fryer soy chunk bites with paprika soy skyr dip
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in hot water with the tamari for 10 minutes and squeeze out firmly.
Toss with the rapeseed oil, half of the smoked paprika and the garlic powder.
Cook in the air fryer at 190 °C for 12 minutes until crisp, shaking once.
Stir the soy skyr with the remaining smoked paprika and a little salt and serve as a dip.

title: Vegan banana split with chocolate soy skyr and raspberries
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein and cocoa until smooth.
Peel the banana and halve it lengthways.
Lay the banana halves in an oblong dish and place the chocolate cream between them in 2 quenelles.
Top with the raspberries and eat straight away.

title: Greek tofu feta skewers with cucumber, cherry tomatoes and oregano
instructions: Cut the tofu into 16 cubes and marinate with the lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper for at least 15 minutes.
Cut the cucumber into 8 thick pieces.
Thread the tofu, cucumber and cherry tomatoes alternately onto 4 short skewers.
Drizzle with the remaining marinade and serve chilled.

title: Speculoos protein shake with soy drink and almonds
instructions: Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass, dust with a pinch of speculoos spice and drink straight away.

title: Beetroot raspberry protein shake with ginger and soy drink
instructions: Cut the beetroot into rough pieces.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Sour cherry vanilla ice lollies with soy skyr and soy protein
instructions: Blend the sour cherries with the soy skyr, soy protein, soy drink and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the mixture into 2 ice lolly moulds, insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Briefly hold the moulds under warm water and release the lollies.

title: Air fryer tempeh cubes with peanut lime dip
instructions: Cut the tempeh into 2 cm cubes and toss with the tamari and garlic powder.
Cook in the air fryer at 190 °C for 10 minutes until crisp, shaking once.
Stir the soy yoghurt, pea protein, peanut butter and lime juice into a smooth dip.
Serve the tempeh cubes with the dip.

title: Lemon poppy seed silken tofu mousse with raspberries
instructions: Drain the silken tofu and blend with the pea protein, lemon juice, lemon zest and maple syrup for 1 minute until airy.
Stir in the poppy seeds, spoon into a dessert glass and chill for 1 hour.
Top with the raspberries.

title: Vanilla millet pudding with apricot compote and soy protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and simmer with the soy drink, vanilla and 60 ml water over low heat for 20 minutes until soft.
Whisk the soy protein with 4 tbsp water until smooth, stir it into the pudding and spoon into a dessert glass.
Stone and dice the apricots and simmer with 2 tbsp water for 4 minutes into a compote.
Spoon the compote over the pudding warm or cold.

title: Cardamom iced coffee frappé with silken tofu and pea protein
instructions: Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Blueberry cheesecake nice cream with soy skyr
instructions: Let the frozen fruit soften for 5 minutes.
Blend with the remaining ingredients in a food processor for 1 to 2 minutes until creamy, scraping down in between.
Spoon into a bowl straight away or freeze for another 30 minutes for a firmer texture.

title: Tofu scramble with diced potatoes, spinach and chives
instructions: Peel the potato, cut it into small dice and cook covered in a non-stick pan with the rapeseed oil and 3 tbsp water for 8 minutes.
Roughly crumble the tofu, add it with the turmeric and nutritional yeast and fry uncovered for 5 minutes until the potatoes are lightly browned.
Fold in the spinach and let it wilt for 1 minute.
Season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with chives.

title: Strawberry quinoa porridge with almond drink and pea protein
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and simmer covered with 200 ml of the almond drink and the vanilla for 15 minutes.
Whisk the pea protein with the remaining almond drink until smooth and stir it into the quinoa.
Quarter the strawberries.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the strawberries and sprinkle with the chia seeds.

title: Kiwi hemp chia pudding with almond drink and pea protein
instructions: Whisk the pea protein with the almond drink until smooth and stir in the chia seeds.
Stir again after 10 minutes and chill covered for at least 4 hours.
Peel and dice the kiwi.
Top the pudding with the kiwi and sprinkle with the hemp seeds.

title: Buckwheat galette with tofu scramble, courgette and tomato
instructions: Whisk the buckwheat flour with 80 ml water and a pinch of salt into a thin batter and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Dice the courgette small and fry it in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes, crumble in the tofu, fry with the turmeric and nutritional yeast for 4 minutes, fold in the diced tomato and remove.
Brush the pan with the rapeseed oil, pour in the batter thinly, cook for 2 minutes and turn.
Put the filling in the centre, fold the edges in to a square and sprinkle with chives.

title: Millet porridge with blueberries, pumpkin seeds and pea protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and simmer covered with 200 ml of the almond drink and the cinnamon for 15 minutes.
Whisk the pea protein with the remaining almond drink until smooth and stir it in.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the blueberries and pumpkin seeds.

title: Quince vanilla millet porridge with pea protein and walnuts
instructions: Peel and core the quince, dice it small and steam it covered with 50 ml water and the vanilla for 15 minutes until soft.
Bring the millet flakes to the boil with 140 ml of the soy drink and let them swell for 5 minutes, stirring.
Whisk the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the quince cubes and chopped walnuts.

title: Strawberry coconut rice flake porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 160 ml of the soy drink and let them swell for 3 minutes, stirring.
Whisk the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it in.
Halve the strawberries.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the strawberries and sprinkle with the desiccated coconut.

title: Chestnut apple porridge with soy protein and cinnamon
instructions: Bring the oats to the boil with 130 ml of the soy drink and the cinnamon and simmer for 4 minutes.
Roughly crumble the chestnuts, dice the apple small and steam both in a small pan with 2 tbsp water for 3 minutes.
Whisk the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the chestnuts and apple and dust with a little cinnamon.

title: Beetroot chocolate overnight oats with raspberries
instructions: Blend the beetroot with the soy drink, cocoa and pea protein until smooth.
Stir together with the oats and half of the soy skyr in a jar.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Spoon the remaining soy skyr on top and add the raspberries.

title: Blackberry almond quinoa porridge with pea protein
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and simmer covered with 160 ml of the soy drink and the vanilla for 15 minutes.
Whisk the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it in.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the blackberries and almonds.

title: Fig cinnamon chia pudding with soy protein
instructions: Whisk the soy protein and cinnamon with the soy drink until smooth and stir in the chia seeds.
Stir again after 10 minutes and chill covered for at least 4 hours.
Cut the fig into quarters.
Top the pudding with the fig quarters and dust with a little cinnamon.

title: Sweet potato cinnamon porridge with pecans and pea protein
instructions: Peel and dice the sweet potato, boil it in a little water for 10 minutes until soft, drain and mash finely.
Bring the oats to the boil with 160 ml of the soy drink and the cinnamon and simmer for 4 minutes.
Whisk the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it in with the sweet potato mash.
Spoon into a bowl, dust with cinnamon and top with the pecans.

title: Mandarin poppy seed overnight oats with soy skyr
instructions: Mix the oats, pea protein and poppy seeds in a jar.
Stir in the soy drink and half of the soy skyr until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Peel the mandarin and separate it into segments, spoon the remaining soy skyr on top and add the segments.

title: Cornmeal porridge with cherry compote and vanilla soy skyr
instructions: Simmer the cherries with 2 tbsp water for 5 minutes to make a compote.
Bring the soy drink to the boil with 100 ml water, sprinkle in the cornmeal and let it swell for 5 minutes, stirring.
Whisk the soy protein with 3 tbsp water until smooth and stir it in, mix the soy skyr with the vanilla.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the vanilla soy skyr and cherry compote.

title: Raspberry lemon protein muffins made with chickpea flour
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees top and bottom heat.
Mix the chickpea flour, pea protein, baking powder and lemon zest and stir until smooth with the soy skyr, soy drink and maple syrup.
Divide the batter between 3 silicone muffin moulds and press in the raspberries.
Bake for 20 minutes, let cool for 5 minutes and release from the moulds.

title: Pineapple lime overnight oats with soy skyr and coconut
instructions: Mix the oats and pea protein in a jar and stir in the soy drink and half of the soy skyr until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Dice the pineapple small.
Spoon the remaining soy skyr on top and scatter with the pineapple, desiccated coconut and lime zest.

title: Grape walnut buckwheat porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat with hot water and simmer covered with 160 ml of the soy drink and the cinnamon for 15 minutes until soft.
Whisk the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it in.
Halve the grapes.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the grapes and walnuts.

title: Sweet tofu ricotta toast with blueberries and lemon zest
instructions: Blend the tofu with the pea protein, maple syrup, vanilla and 2 tbsp water into a creamy tofu ricotta.
Toast the bread until golden brown.
Spread the tofu ricotta thickly on the bread.
Top with the blueberries and sprinkle with the lemon zest.

title: Hazelnut chocolate overnight oats with soy protein
instructions: Mix the oats, soy protein and cocoa in a jar.
Stir in the soy drink until no lumps remain.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Roughly chop the hazelnuts, toast them in a dry pan for 2 minutes and scatter over the oats.

title: Vegan Kaiserschmarrn made with chickpea flour and apple sauce
instructions: Mix the chickpea flour, pea protein, baking powder, vanilla and a pinch of salt and stir with the soy drink and soy skyr into a thick batter.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan, pour in the batter and let it set covered over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Turn it, tear it into pieces with two spatulas and fry for another 3 minutes until golden brown.
Dust with cinnamon and serve with the apple sauce.

title: Papaya lemon amaranth porridge with pea protein
instructions: Rinse the amaranth with hot water and simmer covered with 160 ml of the soy drink and 50 ml water for 20 minutes.
Whisk the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it in with half of the lemon zest.
Peel the papaya, remove the seeds and dice it.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the papaya and sprinkle with the remaining lemon zest.

title: Arepas with black beans and tofu scramble
instructions: Knead the cornmeal and pea protein with a pinch of salt and 45 ml warm water into a smooth dough and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Shape the dough into 2 flat rounds and cook in a non-stick pan without fat for 5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Crumble the tofu and fry it in the pan with the nutritional yeast, turmeric and salt for 4 minutes, warm the beans with the cumin.
Slit the arepas open at the side and fill with the beans, tofu scramble and diced tomato.

title: Gallo pinto with tofu, bell pepper and coriander
instructions: Cook the rice covered in 40 ml water for 12 minutes.
Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in a non-stick pan without fat for 6 minutes until golden all over, season with the nutritional yeast and salt.
Dice the bell pepper, add it to the pan with the beans, rice and cumin and fry for 4 minutes.
Transfer to a plate and sprinkle with chopped coriander.

title: Vegan farmer’s breakfast with potatoes, tofu and pickled gherkin
instructions: Slice the potatoes and fry them in the rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan for 8 minutes until golden brown.
Crumble the tofu, add it to the potatoes with the nutritional yeast, turmeric, salt and pepper and fry for 4 minutes.
Slice the pickled gherkin.
Put the farmer’s breakfast on a plate, sprinkle with chives and arrange the gherkin slices beside it.

title: Savoury buckwheat waffles with smoked tofu, cucumber and dill soy skyr
instructions: Mix the buckwheat flour, pea protein, baking powder and salt and whisk with the soy drink until smooth.
Brush the waffle iron with the rapeseed oil and bake 2 waffles from the batter for 4 minutes each.
Stir the soy skyr with chopped dill and salt, cut the smoked tofu and cucumber into thin slices.
Spread the waffles with the dill soy skyr and top with the smoked tofu and cucumber.

title: Cachapa – Venezuelan corn pancake with tofu queso
instructions: Blend the corn kernels with the cornmeal, pea protein, soy drink and a pinch of salt into a thick, slightly chunky batter.
Mash the tofu finely with the nutritional yeast, salt and lemon juice.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan, spread the batter into a round and cook for 4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Spoon the tofu queso onto one half and fold the cachapa over.

title: Fan tuan – Taiwanese sticky rice roll with tofu and cucumber
instructions: Cook the sticky rice covered in 30 ml water for 15 minutes and let it cool slightly.
Crumble the tofu and dry-fry it with the nutritional yeast and tamari in a non-stick pan for 5 minutes.
Cut the smoked tofu and cucumber into sticks.
Press the rice flat on cling film, top with the tofu, smoked tofu and cucumber, roll up tightly and sprinkle with sesame.

title: Potato tofu fritters with apple soy skyr
instructions: Peel the potatoes, grate them finely and squeeze them out well.
Mash the tofu finely and mix with the potatoes, pea protein, nutmeg, salt and pepper, shape into 4 flat fritters.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan and fry the fritters for 5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Grate the apple finely, stir it into the soy skyr and serve with the fritters.

title: Turkish kahvaltı plate with tofu feta, cucumber, tomato and olives
ingredients: Lemon juice, oregano, pul biber, salt
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and marinate with the nutritional yeast, lemon juice, oregano, salt and olive oil for 10 minutes.
Slice the cucumber and tomato and cut the pointed pepper into rings.
Arrange everything on a plate with the olives.
Sprinkle the tofu feta with pul biber.

title: Pupusas with pinto bean tofu filling and curtido
instructions: Finely shred the white cabbage, grate the carrot and knead with the cider vinegar, oregano and salt to make curtido.
Mash the beans finely with the tofu, nutritional yeast and salt.
Knead the cornmeal and pea protein with 45 ml warm water, divide into 2 balls, flatten, add the filling, seal and flatten again.
Cook in a non-stick pan without fat for 4 minutes per side and serve with the curtido.

title: Tofu kedgeree with curried rice, peas and parsley
instructions: Cook the rice with the curry powder covered in 60 ml water for 12 minutes, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Cut the tofu into cubes and fry with the turmeric, nutritional yeast and salt in a non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden yellow.
Fold the curried rice and peas into the tofu.
Transfer to a plate, sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve with the lemon wedges.

title: Enfrijoladas with tofu scramble and coriander
instructions: Blend the beans with the pea protein, cumin, salt and 60 ml water into a smooth sauce and warm it in a pan.
Crumble the tofu and fry with the nutritional yeast, turmeric and salt in a second pan for 4 minutes.
Briefly dip the tortillas in the bean sauce, fill with the tofu scramble and fold.
Place on a plate, pour over the remaining sauce and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Tortang talong – aubergine omelette made with chickpea flour and tofu
instructions: Roast the aubergine in the oven at 220 degrees for 20 minutes until soft, peel it and press it flat with a fork, leaving the stem on.
Blend the silken tofu, tofu, chickpea flour, pea protein, turmeric, kala namak and pepper until smooth.
Dip the aubergine in the batter and fry it in the rapeseed oil in a non-stick pan, covered with the remaining batter, for 4 minutes per side.
Serve with the diced tomato.

title: Ganmodoki – Japanese tofu vegetable balls with cucumber and ginger tamari
instructions: Press the tofu well and mash finely, grate the carrot finely and roughly chop the edamame.
Knead everything with the cornflour and a pinch of salt and shape into 6 balls.
Brush the balls with the rapeseed oil and cook in the airfryer at 190 degrees for 12 minutes until golden brown.
Stir the tamari with the ginger, slice the cucumber and serve everything with the balls.

title: Causa with tofu filling, cucumber and lime
instructions: Mash the potatoes finely and stir with the lime juice, turmeric and salt into a smooth yellow purée.
Mash the tofu finely and stir with the soy skyr, pea protein, salt and chopped coriander, dice the cucumber finely.
In a serving ring, layer potato purée, tofu filling and cucumber alternately, finishing with potato purée.
Chill for 15 minutes, remove the ring and garnish with coriander.

title: Pineapple basil protein shake
instructions: Wash the fruit, peel if needed and cut it into rough pieces.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Soy skyr tzatziki with smoked tofu cubes and vegetable sticks
instructions: Finely grate the cucumber, squeeze it out well and stir with the soy skyr, chopped dill, lemon juice and salt.
Cut the smoked tofu into cubes and fry in a non-stick pan without fat for 4 minutes until crisp.
Cut the carrot and bell pepper into sticks.
Spoon the tzatziki into a bowl and serve with the smoked tofu cubes and vegetable sticks.

title: Melon mint protein shake with lime
instructions: Wash the fruit, peel if needed and cut it into rough pieces.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Pomegranate raspberry protein shake
instructions: Halve the pomegranate and remove the seeds, setting aside 1 tsp for decoration.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass, sprinkle with the remaining pomegranate seeds and drink straight away.

title: Peach passion fruit ice lollies with soy skyr
instructions: Stone the peach and blend it with the soy skyr, soy protein and maple syrup until smooth.
Halve the passion fruit and stir in the pulp.
Pour the mixture into 2 ice lolly moulds, insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Briefly hold the moulds under warm water and release the lollies.

title: Blackberry vanilla nice cream with soy protein
instructions: Let the frozen fruit soften for 5 minutes.
Blend everything in a food processor for 1 to 2 minutes until creamy, scraping down in between.
Spoon into a bowl straight away or freeze for another 30 minutes for a firmer texture.

title: Coconut raspberry mousse made with silken tofu
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, pea protein and maple syrup until smooth.
Mash half of the raspberries and put them as a layer in a dessert glass, then add the mousse.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.
Garnish with the remaining raspberries and desiccated coconut.

title: Black sesame vanilla protein pudding with agar
instructions: Toast the black sesame in a dry pan for 2 minutes and grind finely, setting aside 1 pinch for decoration.
Bring the soy drink to the boil with the agar and simmer for 2 minutes, stirring.
Remove from the heat and stir in the soy protein, sesame, maple syrup and vanilla until smooth.
Pour into a dessert glass, chill for 2 hours and sprinkle with the remaining sesame.

title: Nectarine basil soy skyr cup with flaked almonds
instructions: Toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein until smooth.
Stone and dice the nectarine, cut the basil into fine strips and mix with the nectarine.
Layer the skyr cream and nectarines alternately in a glass and sprinkle with the flaked almonds.

title: Mini pepper boats with tofu nutritional yeast cream and chives
instructions: Blend the tofu with the pea protein, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, salt and 3 tbsp water until smooth.
Stir in chopped chives.
Halve the mini peppers lengthwise and remove the seeds.
Fill the pepper halves with the cream and sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds.

title: Coffee hazelnut protein ice cream
instructions: Blend the soy drink, espresso, pea protein, silken tofu and maple syrup until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a freezer-safe tub and freeze for at least 12 hours.
Let the block soften for 10 minutes, break it into pieces and blend in a food processor until creamy.
Roughly chop the hazelnuts, toast them in a dry pan and scatter them over the ice cream.

title: Cocoa chilli protein pudding with soy skyr and cinnamon
instructions: Stir the soy skyr, soy protein, cocoa, maple syrup and cinnamon until smooth.
Spoon into a dessert glass and chill for 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with a pinch of chilli flakes and cinnamon.

title: Orange cardamom protein shake
instructions: Wash the fruit, peel if needed and cut it into rough pieces.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Pumpkin seed tofu dip with vegetable sticks
instructions: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, setting aside 1 tsp for decoration.
Blend the tofu with the pumpkin seeds, pea protein, lemon juice, salt and 3 tbsp water into a greenish dip.
Cut the carrot, kohlrabi and cucumber into sticks.
Spoon the dip into a bowl, sprinkle with the remaining pumpkin seeds and serve with the vegetable sticks.

title: Apricot ginger protein shake
instructions: Wash the fruit, peel if needed and cut it into rough pieces.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Tofu scramble with courgette and tomato on rice cakes
instructions: Dice the courgette small and fry in a non-stick pan without fat for 3 minutes.
Crumble in the tofu and fry with the turmeric and nutritional yeast for 4 minutes.
Dice the tomato, fold it in and season with salt and pepper.
Arrange the scramble on the rice cakes and sprinkle with chives.

title: Teff cocoa porridge with raspberries and almond drink
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with 200 ml of the almond drink and simmer covered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Whisk the pea protein and cocoa with the remaining almond drink until smooth and stir them in.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl.
Top with the raspberries.

title: Onigiri breakfast plate with pan-fried tofu, cucumber and nori
instructions: Wash the rice and cook it covered in 35 ml water for 15 minutes, season with a little salt.
Slice the tofu, dust with the pea protein and fry in a non-stick pan without fat for 4 minutes per side until golden brown, then salt.
Shape the rice into 2 triangles with wet hands and wrap each with a strip of nori.
Slice the cucumber, toss with rice vinegar and sesame and arrange everything together.

title: Peanut banana millet flake porridge with almond drink and pea protein
instructions: Bring the millet flakes to the boil with 200 ml of the almond drink and the cinnamon and let them swell for 3 minutes.
Whisk the pea protein with the remaining almond drink until smooth and stir it in.
Slice the banana.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the banana slices and drizzle over the peanut butter.

title: Savoury millet porridge with tofu, spinach and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and simmer covered with 120 ml water, the turmeric and a pinch of salt for 15 minutes until soft.
Whisk the pea protein and nutritional yeast with 3 tbsp water until smooth and stir into the porridge, fold in the spinach and let it wilt for 1 minute.
Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in a non-stick pan without fat for 6 minutes until golden brown, briefly toasting the pumpkin seeds with it.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the tofu and pumpkin seeds and sprinkle with chives.

title: Apricot cardamom millet flake porridge with soy protein and pistachios
instructions: Bring the millet flakes to the boil with 140 ml of the soy drink and the cardamom and let them swell for 3 minutes, stirring.
Whisk the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it into the porridge.
Stone the apricots and cut them into wedges.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the apricot wedges and sprinkle with the chopped pistachios.

title: Blackberry vanilla overnight oats with soy skyr and linseed
instructions: Stir the oats, linseed, vanilla, pea protein, soy drink and half of the soy skyr in a jar until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
In the morning stir briefly and loosen with a splash of water if needed.
Top with the remaining soy skyr and the blackberries.

title: Churro protein waffles made with buckwheat flour, cinnamon and a soy skyr dip
instructions: Mix the buckwheat flour, pea protein, linseed, baking powder and half of the cinnamon, stir in the soy drink and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
Bake the batter in a preheated, lightly greased waffle iron into 2 waffles for 4 minutes each until golden brown.
Stir the soy skyr with the maple syrup.
Dust the waffles with the remaining cinnamon and serve with the dip.

title: Tahini grape molasses rice flake porridge with apple, soy protein and sesame
instructions: Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 130 ml of the soy drink and let them swell for 3 minutes, stirring.
Whisk the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it in.
Cut the apple into thin wedges.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the apple wedges, drizzle over the tahini and grape molasses and sprinkle with sesame.

title: Blood orange vanilla chia pudding with pea protein and cocoa nibs
instructions: Whisk the pea protein with the soy drink and vanilla until smooth, then stir in the chia seeds.
Stir again after 10 minutes and chill for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Peel the blood orange and cut it into segments.
Top the pudding with the blood orange segments and sprinkle with the cocoa nibs.

title: Raspberry lemon quinoa porridge with soy skyr
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and simmer covered with 120 ml water for 15 minutes until soft.
Whisk the soy protein with the soy drink and half of the lemon zest until smooth, add to the quinoa and warm for 2 minutes until creamy.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and add the soy skyr on top.
Top with the raspberries and the remaining lemon zest.

title: Poppy seed orange buckwheat pancakes with soy skyr
instructions: Mix the buckwheat flour, pea protein, poppy seeds, baking powder and orange zest and stir with the soy drink into a thick batter.
Cook 4 small pancakes in a non-stick pan without fat for 2 minutes per side.
Peel the orange and cut it into segments.
Stack the pancakes, add the soy skyr on top and top with the orange segments.

title: Pomegranate cocoa amaranth porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 120 ml water and simmer covered for 20 minutes until soft.
Whisk the soy protein and cocoa with the soy drink until smooth, stir into the amaranth and warm briefly.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and scatter over the pomegranate seeds.

title: Plum cinnamon rice flake porridge with walnuts and pea protein
instructions: Stone the plums, quarter them and steam with 2 tbsp water and half of the cinnamon for 4 minutes until soft.
Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 140 ml of the soy drink and let them swell for 3 minutes.
Whisk the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it in.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the plums and walnuts and dust with the remaining cinnamon.

title: Fig hazelnut buckwheat porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat and simmer covered with 120 ml water for 12 minutes until soft.
Whisk the soy protein with the soy drink until smooth, stir it in and warm for 2 minutes until creamy.
Cut the fig into wedges and briefly toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the fig wedges and hazelnuts.

title: Apple crumble porridge with almond crumbs and soy protein
instructions: Dice the apple and steam with the cinnamon and 2 tbsp water for 4 minutes until soft.
Toast 6 g of the oats with the chopped almonds and maple syrup in a dry pan for 3 minutes into crumbs.
Simmer the remaining oats with 130 ml of the soy drink for 4 minutes, whisk the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it in.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the stewed apple and the crumbs.

title: Cherry almond polenta porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the polenta to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink and the vanilla, stirring, and let it swell over low heat for 5 minutes.
Whisk the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it into the porridge.
Halve the cherries and briefly toast the almonds in a dry pan.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the cherries and almonds.

title: Tofu gimbap breakfast rolls with spinach, carrot and cucumber
instructions: Wash the rice and cook it covered in 35 ml water for 15 minutes, then season with rice vinegar, salt and the sesame oil.
Cut the tofu into long sticks, dust with the pea protein and fry all over in a non-stick pan without fat for 5 minutes until golden brown.
Briefly wilt the spinach in the hot pan and cut the carrot and cucumber into thin sticks.
Spread the rice on the nori sheet, lay the tofu and vegetables on top, roll up tightly and cut into 8 slices.

title: Sabudana khichdi with tofu, peanuts and potato
ingredients: Cumin, turmeric, fresh coriander, lemon juice
instructions: Rinse the tapioca pearls, cover just with water and leave to swell for 4 hours or overnight, then drain well.
Dice the potato small and fry in the oil with the cumin and chopped chilli for 6 minutes.
Crumble in the tofu, dust with the turmeric and pea protein and fry for 3 minutes.
Fold in the tapioca pearls and half of the peanuts and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until translucent.
Season with salt and lemon juice and sprinkle with the remaining peanuts and coriander.

title: Ven pongal with mung dal, tofu and ginger
ingredients: Ginger, cumin, black pepper, curry leaves
instructions: Wash the rice and mung dal and cook covered with 250 ml water for 20 minutes until very soft, then stir roughly.
Whisk the pea protein with 3 tbsp water until smooth, stir it in and season with salt.
Dice the tofu and fry in a non-stick pan without fat for 5 minutes until golden brown.
Heat the oil, toast the cumin, pepper, chopped ginger and curry leaves for 30 seconds, pour over the pongal and serve with the tofu.

title: Buckwheat gözleme with spinach tofu filling and pul biber
instructions: Knead the buckwheat flour, psyllium husk and a pinch of salt with 45 ml warm water into a smooth dough and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Finely chop the spinach, crumble the tofu and mix both with the pea protein, lemon juice, pul biber and salt.
Roll the dough out thinly into a round between baking paper, put the filling on one half, fold over and press the edges together.
Cook in a non-stick pan with the oil for 4 minutes per side until golden brown and cut into pieces.

title: Socca breakfast pizza with tofu feta, spinach and pepper
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour, pea protein, a pinch of salt and 90 ml water until smooth and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Finely crumble the tofu and marinate with lemon juice, oregano and salt to make tofu feta.
Pour the batter into an oiled ovenproof pan and bake at 220 degrees for 8 minutes.
Top with the spinach, pepper strips and tofu feta and bake for another 6 minutes.

title: Brazilian tapioca crêpe with tofu scramble and tomato
instructions: Rub the tapioca starch with 2 tbsp water and a pinch of salt into fine crumbs and sieve into a hot non-stick pan.
Cook without fat for 2 minutes until the crêpe holds together, turn and cook for 1 more minute.
Crumble the tofu and fry in the pan with the turmeric, nutritional yeast and pea protein for 4 minutes.
Dice the tomato, put the scramble and tomato on the crêpe, fold it over and sprinkle with chives.

title: Quinoa breakfast bowl with roasted mushrooms, tofu and herby soy skyr
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and cook covered in 50 ml water for 15 minutes.
Quarter the mushrooms, dice the tofu and fry both with the oil and thyme in a pan for 8 minutes until well browned, then salt.
Briefly wilt the spinach in the pan.
Stir the soy skyr with chopped parsley, lemon juice and salt and arrange everything in a bowl.

title: Gluten-free toast with tofu ricotta, roasted tomatoes and basil
instructions: Roast the cherry tomatoes with the oil and salt in an ovenproof dish at 220 degrees for 12 minutes.
Blend the tofu with the pea protein, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, salt and 2 tbsp water into a creamy ricotta.
Toast the bread and spread thickly with the tofu ricotta.
Spread the roasted tomatoes on top, arrange the remaining ricotta alongside and top with basil.

title: Red lentil breakfast dal with tofu and spinach
instructions: Rinse the lentils and cook with 200 ml water, the turmeric and chopped ginger for 15 minutes until thick.
Whisk the pea protein with 2 tbsp water until smooth, stir in with the diced tomato and spinach and leave for 2 minutes, then salt.
Dice the tofu and fry in a non-stick pan without fat for 5 minutes until golden brown.
Heat the oil with the cumin for 30 seconds, pour over the dal and serve with the tofu and coriander.

title: Vegan miso breakfast soup with tofu, wakame and rice
instructions: Cook the rice covered in 50 ml water for 15 minutes.
Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes and drain, dice the tofu.
Bring 300 ml water to the boil with the ginger, let the tofu and wakame steep in it for 2 minutes and take off the heat.
Whisk the miso and pea protein with a little of the broth until smooth, stir in and sprinkle with spring onion, serve with the rice.

title: Bindaetteok – Korean mung bean pancakes with tofu and quick cucumber kimchi
instructions: Soak the mung dal in water for 4 hours, drain and blend finely with 60 ml water, the pea protein and salt.
Crumble the tofu and fold it into the batter with half of the spring onion.
Fry 2 pancakes in a non-stick pan with the oil for 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden brown.
Slice the cucumber thinly, toss with the gochugaru, rice vinegar, salt and remaining spring onion and serve alongside.

title: Horchata protein shake with rice flakes, cinnamon and dates
instructions: Soak the rice flakes and date in the soy drink for 5 minutes.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass, dust with cinnamon and drink straight away.

title: Vegan crème brûlée made with silken tofu, vanilla and orange segments
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, soy protein, soy drink, cornflour and vanilla until very smooth.
Heat in a small pan for 3 minutes, stirring, until the cream thickens, pour into a shallow ramekin and chill for 2 hours.
Sprinkle the sugar evenly over the top and caramelise it golden brown with a kitchen blowtorch.
Cut the orange into segments and serve next to the crème brûlée.

title: Cucumber sushi bites with tofu wasabi cream and black sesame
instructions: Cut the cucumber into 10 thick slices and hollow each slice slightly with a teaspoon.
Blend the tofu with the soy skyr, pea protein, wasabi, lime juice and salt until creamy.
Pipe or spoon the cream onto the cucumber slices.
Sprinkle with the spring onion rings and black sesame.

title: Crispy baked tofu chips with lime chilli dip
ingredients: Smoked paprika, chilli flakes, lime juice, salt
instructions: Pat the tofu dry thoroughly and cut it into very thin slices.
Toss with the tamari, nutritional yeast and paprika and spread out on a baking tray lined with baking paper.
Bake at 180 degrees for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until the chips are crisp.
Stir the soy skyr with lime juice, chilli flakes and salt and serve with the chips.

title: Espresso cocoa ice lollies with soy protein
instructions: Let the espresso cool.
Blend with the soy drink, soy skyr, soy protein, cocoa and maple syrup until smooth.
Pour the mixture into 2 ice lolly moulds, insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Briefly hold the moulds under warm water and release the lollies.

title: Pumpkin seed cinnamon protein bars with dates
instructions: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes and chop roughly.
Finely chop the dates and stir with 2 tbsp hot water and the cinnamon into a paste.
Mix in the soy protein, oats and half of the pumpkin seeds and knead firmly.
Shape into 2 bars, top with the remaining pumpkin seeds and chill for 30 minutes until firm.

title: Passion fruit silken tofu mousse with coconut and soy protein
instructions: Blend the silken tofu with the soy protein, maple syrup and lime zest until very smooth.
Halve the passion fruit and fold half of the pulp into the cream.
Spoon into a glass and chill for 30 minutes.
Garnish with the remaining pulp and the desiccated coconut.

title: Hazelnut cocoa protein bars with puffed quinoa
instructions: Finely chop the dates and stir with the hazelnut butter and 2 tbsp hot water into a paste.
Mix in the soy protein, cocoa and puffed quinoa and knead firmly.
Shape the mixture into 2 bars and chill for 30 minutes until firm.

title: Apricot almond protein balls
instructions: Finely chop the apricots and stir with the almond butter and 2 tbsp hot water.
Mix in the pea protein and oats and knead into a mouldable mixture.
Roll into 6 balls and coat them in the desiccated coconut.
Chill for at least 20 minutes.

title: Blueberry cinnamon protein shake with oats and soy drink
instructions: Soak the oats in the soy drink for 5 minutes.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Lemon raspberry cheesecake cups with soy skyr and almond crunch
instructions: Toast the oats and chopped almonds with the maple syrup in a dry pan for 3 minutes until crisp and leave to cool.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein, lemon zest and juice until smooth.
Crush half of the raspberries with a fork.
Layer the crunch, cream and crushed raspberries in a glass and top with the remaining raspberries.

title: Cucumber mint lassi with soy yoghurt and soy protein
instructions: Roughly dice the cucumber.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass, sprinkle with a pinch of toasted cumin and drink straight away.

title: Beetroot soy skyr dip with smoked tofu sticks and kohlrabi
instructions: Blend the beetroot with the soy skyr, horseradish, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
Cut the smoked tofu and kohlrabi into sticks.
Toast the tofu sticks in a non-stick pan without fat for 3 minutes.
Spoon the dip into a small bowl and serve with the tofu and kohlrabi sticks.

title: Rice cakes with tofu herb spread, radishes and cress
ingredients: Cress, parsley, chives, lemon juice, salt
instructions: Blend the tofu with the soy skyr, pea protein, lemon juice and salt until creamy.
Finely chop the parsley and chives and stir them in.
Slice the radishes thinly.
Spread the rice cakes thickly with the spread, top with the radishes and cress and serve the remaining spread alongside.

title: Crispy edamame with za'atar and roasted soybeans
instructions: Thaw the edamame and pat thoroughly dry.
Toss with the za'atar and salt and roast on a baking tray lined with baking paper at 200 degrees for 20 minutes until crisp.
Mix with the roasted soybeans and lemon zest and serve in a bowl.

title: Strawberry buckwheat pancakes with almond drink and pea protein
instructions: Mix the buckwheat flour and pea protein and stir with the almond drink into a thick batter, then leave to swell for 5 minutes.
Cook 4 small pancakes in a non-stick pan without fat for 2 minutes per side.
Slice the strawberries.
Stack the pancakes, top with the strawberries and pumpkin seeds and drizzle with the maple syrup.

title: Quinoa kiwi porridge with pumpkin seeds and almond drink
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and simmer covered with 180 ml of the almond drink and the vanilla for 15 minutes until soft.
Whisk the pea protein with the remaining almond drink until smooth and stir it in.
Peel the kiwi and slice it.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the kiwi and pumpkin seeds.

title: Polenta breakfast porridge with blueberries, almonds and pea protein
instructions: Bring the polenta to the boil with 200 ml of the almond drink, stirring, and let it swell over low heat for 5 minutes.
Blend the tofu with the pea protein and the remaining almond drink until smooth and stir it into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the blueberries and flaked almonds.

title: Tempeh rice breakfast bowl with spinach, carrot and ginger
instructions: Cook the rice covered in 25 ml water for 15 minutes.
Cut the tempeh and tofu into cubes and fry with the grated ginger in a non-stick pan without fat for 7 minutes until golden brown, then salt.
Cut the carrot into thin strips and cook with the spinach in the pan for 2 minutes.
Arrange the rice, tempeh, tofu and vegetables in a bowl and sprinkle with chives.

title: Tofu potato breakfast pan with courgette and chives
instructions: Cut the potato into small cubes and fry covered in a non-stick pan with the oil for 8 minutes.
Dice the courgette and fry for 3 minutes with it.
Crumble in the tofu, dust with the pea protein, turmeric and paprika and fry for 4 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with chives.

title: Paneer bhurji with spinach, tomato and ghee
ingredients: Turmeric, cumin, garam masala, fresh coriander
instructions: Heat the ghee in a pan and sweat the cumin and chopped onion for 2 minutes.
Dice the tomato, add with the turmeric and garam masala and cook down for 2 minutes.
Crumble the paneer roughly, fold in with the spinach and fry for 3 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Season with salt and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Cloud eggs with hard cheese on buttered spinach
instructions: Separate the eggs, beat the whites with a pinch of salt until stiff and fold in the hard cheese.
Place two egg white clouds on a baking tray lined with baking paper, make a hollow in each and bake at 220 degrees for 3 minutes.
Put one yolk into each hollow and bake for another 3 minutes.
Wilt the spinach in the butter with nutmeg and salt, arrange the cloud eggs on top and sprinkle with chives.

title: Burrata breakfast plate with fried egg, rocket and cherry tomatoes
instructions: Finely chop the basil and stir with 6 g of the olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Fry the egg in the remaining oil in a non-stick pan for 3 minutes.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and spread them on a plate with the rocket.
Place the burrata and fried egg on top, drizzle with the basil oil and season with pepper.

title: Egg crêpes with mushroom ricotta filling and thyme
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the cream, salt and pepper until smooth.
Cook 2 thin crêpes in a non-stick pan with half of the oil for 1 minute per side.
Slice the mushrooms and fry in the remaining oil with the thyme for 5 minutes until golden brown, then salt and mix with the ricotta.
Spread the filling over the crêpes, roll them up and serve sprinkled with thyme leaves.

title: Courgette nests with baked egg and mozzarella
instructions: Spiralise the courgette, salt it, leave for 5 minutes and squeeze out well.
Toss with the oil and oregano and shape into 2 nests on a baking tray lined with baking paper.
Tear the mozzarella and put it into the nests, then crack one egg into each.
Bake at 200 degrees for 12 minutes until the egg whites are set and sprinkle with pepper and chilli flakes.

title: Tofu avocado scramble with spinach and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Crumble the tofu by hand and fry in the oil with the turmeric in a pan for 5 minutes.
Fold in the spinach and let it wilt for 1 minute, then season with kala namak and pepper.
Slice the avocado and briefly toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan.
Arrange the scramble with the avocado and sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds and chilli flakes.

title: Spinach egg bites with vegetarian mountain cheese
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160 degrees and grease 4 cups of a silicone muffin tray with the butter.
Blend the eggs with the cream, mountain cheese, nutmeg, salt and pepper for 20 seconds until frothy.
Finely chop the spinach, divide it among the cups and pour the egg mixture over it.
Place a tray of hot water underneath and bake for 22 minutes until set, then serve with chives.

title: Snickers overnight oats with peanuts, date caramel and cocoa
instructions: Stir the oats, soy protein, cocoa and soy drink in a jar until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Chop the date very finely and stir with the peanut butter and 1 tbsp warm water into a caramel.
In the morning stir, spread the date caramel on top and sprinkle with the chopped peanuts.

title: Bounty protein pudding made with silken tofu, coconut and cocoa
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, soy protein, cocoa, maple syrup and soy drink until very smooth.
Stir in two thirds of the desiccated coconut and spoon into a glass.
Chill for at least 1 hour and sprinkle with the remaining coconut.

title: Marzipan apricot overnight oats with soy skyr and almonds
instructions: Stir the oats, soy protein, soy drink, almond butter, bitter almond extract and 70 g of the soy skyr in a jar until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
In the morning stir briefly and loosen with a splash of water if needed.
Cut the apricots into wedges and layer on the oats with the remaining soy skyr.

title: Cocoa sour cherry muffins made with buckwheat and pea protein
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line 3 muffin holes with paper cases.
Mix the buckwheat flour, pea protein, cocoa, baking powder and vanilla, then stir in the soy skyr, maple syrup and 3 tbsp water.
Drain the sour cherries, fold them in and divide the batter between the cases.
Bake for 20 minutes and leave to cool.

title: Apple poppy seed waffles made with rice flour and soy skyr
instructions: Mix the rice flour, pea protein, poppy seeds, baking powder and cinnamon and stir with the soy drink until smooth.
Finely grate half of the apple and stir into the batter.
Bake 2 waffles in a preheated, lightly greased waffle iron for 4 minutes each until golden.
Cut the remaining apple into thin wedges and arrange on the waffles with the soy skyr.

title: Blueberry lavender overnight oats with soy skyr
instructions: Briefly warm the soy drink with the lavender flowers, leave to infuse for 5 minutes and strain.
Stir the lavender soy drink with the oats, soy protein, linseed, lemon zest and 70 g of the soy skyr in a jar.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
In the morning layer with the remaining soy skyr and the blueberries.

title: Apple cinnamon silken tofu cream with buckwheat crunch
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, soy protein, apple purée and half of the cinnamon until very smooth and spoon into a glass.
Toast the buckwheat with the maple syrup and remaining cinnamon in a pan for 3 minutes until crisp and leave to cool.
Finely dice the apple.
Scatter the apple cubes and buckwheat crunch over the cream.

title: Christmas stollen porridge with raisins, almonds and orange zest
instructions: Bring the oats to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink, the raisins and the spices and simmer for 3 minutes, stirring.
Whisk the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it in.
Toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and sprinkle with the almonds and orange zest.

title: Mulled plum baked oats with pea protein and linseed
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees.
Stir together the oats, pea protein, linseed, baking powder, gingerbread spice and soy drink and pour into a small ovenproof dish.
Halve and stone the plums and press them into the batter cut side up.
Bake for 25 minutes until the top is browned and leave to cool briefly.

title: Raspberry almond bircher made with millet flakes and soy skyr
instructions: Coarsely grate the apple and stir with the millet flakes, soy protein, soy drink and soy skyr.
Chill for at least 30 minutes or overnight.
Roughly chop the almonds.
Spoon the bircher into a bowl and top with the raspberries and almonds.

title: Pineapple coconut pancakes made with rice flour and soy protein
instructions: Mix the rice flour, soy protein, desiccated coconut and baking powder and stir with the soy drink until smooth.
Leave to swell for 5 minutes and cook 4 small pancakes in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes per side.
Cut the pineapple into small pieces.
Stack the pancakes, top with the pineapple, drizzle with the maple syrup and sprinkle with lime zest.

title: Gingerbread protein muffins made with buckwheat, apple and hazelnut
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line 3 holes of a muffin tin with paper cases.
Mix the buckwheat flour, soy protein, ground hazelnuts, gingerbread spice and baking powder, then stir in the soy skyr and 3 tbsp water.
Finely dice the apple, fold it in and divide the batter between the cases.
Bake for 20 minutes and leave to cool briefly.

title: Redcurrant millet cups with vanilla soy skyr
instructions: Bring the millet flakes to the boil with the soy drink, let them swell for 3 minutes and leave to cool.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein, vanilla and maple syrup until smooth.
Strip the redcurrants from their stalks.
Layer the millet, cream and redcurrants in a glass.

title: Pear ginger amaranth pudding with soy protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink and the ginger and simmer gently, covered, for 20 minutes.
Whisk the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and stir it in.
Cut the pear into thin wedges.
Spoon the pudding into a bowl, top with the pear wedges and sprinkle with pumpkin seeds.

title: Blueberry lemon muffins with pea protein and rice flour
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line 3 muffin holes with paper cases.
Mix the rice flour, pea protein, linseed, baking powder and lemon zest, then stir in the soy skyr, maple syrup and 3 tbsp water.
Gently fold in the blueberries and divide the batter between the cases.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden and leave to cool.

title: Cinnamon roll chia pudding with soy protein and pecan crunch
instructions: Whisk the soy protein, cinnamon and vanilla with the soy drink in a jar.
Stir in the chia seeds, stir again after 5 minutes and chill for at least 2 hours.
Chop the pecans and caramelise with the maple syrup in a pan for 1 minute.
Dust the pudding with a swirl of cinnamon and sprinkle with the pecan crunch.

title: Spinach tofu muffins made with chickpea flour and sun-dried tomatoes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line 3 muffin holes with paper cases.
Blend the tofu with the chickpea flour, pea protein, yeast flakes, spices, baking powder and 4 tbsp water until smooth.
Finely chop the spinach and sun-dried tomatoes and fold them in.
Fill the batter into the cases and bake for 22 minutes until golden.

title: Chicory boats with curried tofu salad and mango
ingredients: Curry powder, lime juice, fresh coriander, salt
instructions: Finely dice the tofu.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, curry powder, lime juice and salt until smooth and mix with the tofu.
Peel the mango, dice it finely and fold it in.
Separate the chicory into individual leaves, fill with the salad and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Savoury polenta with fried tofu, mushrooms and spinach
instructions: Bring the soy drink to the boil with 60 ml water and salt, stir in the polenta and let it swell for 5 minutes, stirring, then stir in the soy protein and nutmeg.
Dice the tofu and fry in a non-stick pan with the paprika for 5 minutes until golden.
Slice the mushrooms, fry with the thyme for 4 minutes and let the spinach wilt.
Spoon the polenta into a bowl, top with the tofu, mushrooms and spinach and season with pepper.

title: Millet upma with tofu, lupins and peas
ingredients: Mustard seeds, turmeric, ginger, curry leaves, fresh coriander, lemon juice
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and cook, covered, with 80 ml water and salt for 10 minutes.
Toast the mustard seeds and curry leaves in a non-stick pan until the seeds pop, then add the ginger and finely diced carrot and fry for 2 minutes.
Dice the tofu and add with the lupins, peas and turmeric and fry for 4 minutes.
Fold in the millet, season with lemon juice and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Olive tofu tapenade on rice cakes with tomato and capers
instructions: Pit the olives and blend with the tofu, soy protein, capers, lemon juice, oregano and pepper into a coarse paste.
Cut the tomato into thin slices and salt lightly.
Spread the rice cakes thickly with the tapenade.
Top with the tomato slices and sprinkle with basil.

title: Sweet potato tempeh hash with lupins, pepper and spring onions
instructions: Cut the sweet potato into small cubes and cook covered in a non-stick pan with 2 tbsp water for 6 minutes, then fry uncovered for 2 minutes.
Dice the tempeh and tofu, cut the pepper into pieces and fry everything with the drained lupins and the spices for 6 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with the spring onions.

title: Garlic mushroom tofu toast on gluten-free bread with thyme
instructions: Cut the tofu into thin slices and fry on both sides in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes until golden, then remove.
Slice the mushrooms and fry with the chopped garlic and thyme for 5 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein and a pinch of salt until smooth, toast the bread and spread it with the mixture.
Layer the tofu slices and mushrooms on the toast and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Beetroot tofu hash with edamame and horseradish soy skyr
instructions: Cut the tofu and beetroot into small cubes.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and fry the tofu with the caraway for 5 minutes until golden, then add the beetroot and edamame and fry for another 4 minutes.
Stir the soy skyr with the horseradish and salt.
Season the hash with salt and pepper, sprinkle with dill and serve with the horseradish skyr.

title: Candied almond protein balls with cinnamon
instructions: Roughly chop the almonds and caramelise with the coconut blossom sugar, 1 tbsp water and a little cinnamon in a pan for 3 minutes, then leave to cool on baking paper.
Finely chop the dates and knead with the soy protein, almond butter, remaining cinnamon, vanilla and 2 to 3 tbsp water into a pliable dough.
Roll 5 balls and coat them in the caramelised almonds.
Chill for at least 30 minutes so that they firm up.
