title: Matcha coconut protein bars with puffed rice
instructions: Stir the cashew butter, maple syrup, soy drink and matcha until smooth.
Knead in the pea protein, puffed rice and desiccated coconut.
Press the mixture into a flat rectangle on baking paper and chill for 1 hour.
Cut into 2 bars.

title: Poppy seed vanilla protein shake with lemon and banana
instructions: Leave the poppy seeds to soak in the soy drink for 10 minutes.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and sprinkle with a little lemon zest.

title: Oven baked pear chips with cardamom soy skyr dip
instructions: Slice the pear crosswise into wafer-thin slices and lay them on a baking tray lined with baking paper.
Dry at 100 degrees fan for 80 minutes, leaving the oven door slightly ajar.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, maple syrup and cardamom until smooth.
Leave the pear chips to cool so they turn crisp and serve with the dip.

title: Pea basil dip with tofu and fennel sticks
instructions: Cook the peas in boiling water for 2 minutes, refresh in cold water and drain.
Blend with the tofu, soy skyr, soy protein, basil, lemon juice and salt until creamy.
Cut the fennel into sticks and serve with the dip.

title: Protein nougat cream made with silken tofu with strawberries for dipping
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, soy protein, hazelnut butter, cocoa and maple syrup until very smooth.
Spoon into a small bowl and chill for 20 minutes.
Wash the strawberries and serve them with their green tops for dipping.

title: Protein marzipan potatoes with cocoa
instructions: Mix the soy protein and almond flour, add the maple syrup, soy drink, bitter almond extract and rose water and knead into a smooth marzipan dough.
Roll into 8 small, slightly irregular balls.
Roll in the cocoa and press 3 small dimples into each with a wooden skewer.
Chill for at least 30 minutes so that they firm up.

title: Miso sesame edamame with pan-fried tofu cubes
instructions: Cut the tofu into small cubes and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden.
Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain.
Stir the miso with the lime juice and 1 tbsp hot water until smooth.
Toss the edamame and tofu in the miso sauce and sprinkle with sesame and chilli flakes.

title: Oven baked Brussels sprout chips with tofu croutons and mustard soy skyr dip
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees, trim the Brussels sprouts and peel off the outer leaves individually, then halve the rest.
Cut the tofu into small cubes, toss with the sprouts, oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt and spread out on baking paper.
Bake for 15 minutes until the leaves are crisp and the edges browned.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, mustard and salt until smooth and serve as a dip.

title: Black sesame protein shake with banana and date
instructions: Toast the black sesame in a dry pan for 1 minute until fragrant.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Lemon poppy seed protein balls with coconut
instructions: Stir the cashew butter, maple syrup, soy drink, lemon zest and lemon juice until smooth.
Knead in the pea protein, oats and poppy seeds.
Roll into 5 balls and coat in the desiccated coconut.
Chill for at least 30 minutes so that they firm up.

title: Oven baked pumpkin tofu skewers with sage and herb dip
ingredients: Sage, paprika, chives, lemon juice, salt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees and cut the tofu and pumpkin into cubes of the same size.
Thread alternately with the sage leaves onto 4 skewers, season with paprika and salt and bake on baking paper for 20 minutes.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, chives, lemon juice and salt and serve alongside.

title: Tofu caprese skewers with cherry tomatoes and basil
ingredients: Basil, yeast flakes, lemon juice, salt
instructions: Cut the tofu into 16 cubes and marinate with the lemon juice, yeast flakes and salt for 10 minutes.
Thaw the edamame.
Thread the tofu, basil, cherry tomatoes and edamame alternately onto 8 small skewers.
Drizzle with the balsamic glaze.

title: Spinach lupin dip with carrot and kohlrabi sticks
instructions: Drain the lupins and blend with the soy skyr, spinach, lemon juice, garlic, nutmeg and salt until creamy.
Peel the carrot and kohlrabi and cut into sticks.
Spoon the dip into a small bowl and serve with the vegetable sticks.

title: Kiwi lime skyr pops
instructions: Mash the banana finely and stir with the soy skyr, soy protein, lime zest and lime juice until smooth.
Peel the kiwis, cut off 4 thin slices and finely dice the rest and fold it in.
Press 2 kiwi slices against the inside of each of 2 ice lolly moulds, fill with the mixture, insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Briefly hold the moulds under warm water and release the lollies.

title: Pineapple coconut millet porridge with pea protein and tofu
instructions: Blend the tofu with 100 ml of the almond drink and the pea protein until smooth.
Bring the millet flakes to the boil with the remaining almond drink and the vanilla and let them swell for 3 minutes, stirring.
Take off the heat and stir in the tofu cream.
Dice the pineapple, spoon it onto the porridge and sprinkle with the coconut and lime zest.

title: Potato tofu rösti with spinach and edamame
instructions: Peel the potato, grate it coarsely and squeeze well, finely crumble 100 g of the tofu and mix both with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan, shape the mixture into 2 flat rösti and fry for 5 minutes on each side until golden.
Dice the remaining tofu and fry with the edamame and spinach in the pan for 3 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Serve the rösti with the vegetables and sprinkle with chives.

title: Strawberry banana breakfast shake with tofu and almond drink
instructions: Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Taste and thin with a little cold water if needed.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Teff pancakes with blueberries and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Mix the teff flour, pea protein, baking powder and cinnamon and stir with the almond drink into a thick batter.
Leave to swell for 5 minutes and cook 4 small pancakes in a non-stick pan for 2 minutes per side.
Briefly toast the pumpkin seeds in the pan.
Stack the pancakes, top with the blueberries and pumpkin seeds and drizzle with the maple syrup.

title: Tofu scramble taco with corn tortilla, pepper and spinach
ingredients: Turmeric, cumin, paprika, fresh coriander, lime juice
instructions: Crumble the tofu, stir the pea protein with 3 tbsp water until smooth and fry with the tofu and spices in a non-stick pan for 4 minutes.
Cut the pepper into strips and fry with the spinach for 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with the scramble, sprinkle with coriander and drizzle with lime juice.

title: Halloumi spinach pan with fried egg and pine nuts
instructions: Cut the halloumi into 3 slices and fry in a pan with half of the oil for 2 minutes per side until golden, then remove.
Heat the remaining oil, crack in the egg and fry for 3 minutes until the white is set.
Wilt the spinach next to it for 2 minutes and season with salt.
Serve with the halloumi and sprinkle with toasted pine nuts, lemon zest and chilli flakes.

title: Keto breakfast pizza with an egg mozzarella base, spinach and mushrooms
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees and whisk the eggs with the cream, salt, pepper and half of the grated mozzarella.
Heat the oil in a small ovenproof pan, pour in the egg mixture and let it set over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Top with the spinach, mushroom slices, halved tomatoes and remaining mozzarella and sprinkle with oregano.
Bake in the oven for 8 minutes until the cheese has melted, cut into slices and serve with basil.

title: Creamy cheddar chive scrambled eggs with roasted cherry tomatoes
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees and roast the cherry tomatoes for 10 minutes until they just begin to burst.
Whisk the eggs with the cream, salt and pepper.
Melt the butter over low heat, add the eggs and let them set slowly and creamily, stirring constantly.
Fold in the grated cheddar, sprinkle with chives and serve with the tomatoes.

title: Kale cheddar egg muffins with chives
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and grease 4 muffin holes with the oil.
Remove the stalks from the kale and chop it very finely, grate the cheddar and divide both between the holes.
Whisk the eggs with the cream, paprika, salt and pepper and pour over.
Bake for 18 minutes until set and golden, then sprinkle with chives.

title: Avocado boats with egg salad and cress
instructions: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Finely chop the eggs and mix with the mayonnaise, yoghurt, mustard, salt and pepper.
Halve and stone the avocado and fill the halves with the egg salad.
Sprinkle with paprika and cress.

title: Spanish-style zucchini tortilla without potato with parsley
instructions: Cut the zucchini into thin slices and the onion into fine strips.
Heat the oil in a small non-stick pan and cook the zucchini and onion over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft but not browned.
Whisk the eggs with the paprika, salt and pepper, pour over the vegetables and let set, covered, over low heat for 6 minutes.
Turn over with the help of a plate, cook for 2 more minutes, cut into wedges and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Elderflower strawberry overnight oats with soy skyr
instructions: Stir the oats, pea protein, almond drink, elderflower syrup and 60 g of the soy skyr in a jar until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
In the morning stir briefly and loosen with a splash of water if needed.
Slice the strawberries and layer them on the oats with the remaining soy skyr.

title: Blackcurrant vanilla chia pudding with soy protein and soy skyr
instructions: Whisk the soy protein, vanilla and soy drink until smooth, stir in the chia seeds and stir again after 5 minutes.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Heat the blackcurrants with the maple syrup for 3 minutes until they burst, then leave to cool.
Layer the pudding in a glass with the soy skyr and the blackcurrant compote.

title: Franzbrötchen overnight oats with cinnamon and soy skyr
instructions: Stir the oats, soy protein, soy drink, cardamom and 60 g of the soy skyr in a jar until smooth.
Mix the cinnamon with the maple syrup and swirl it through the oats.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
In the morning top with the remaining soy skyr, dust with cinnamon and sprinkle with toasted flaked almonds.

title: Hojicha overnight oats with blueberries and soy yoghurt
instructions: Stir the hojicha powder with 2 tbsp warm water until smooth.
Stir it in a jar with the oats, pea protein and soy drink until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
In the morning top with the soy yoghurt and blueberries and dust with a little hojicha powder.

title: Vanilla crescent millet flake porridge with almonds and pea protein
instructions: Scrape out the vanilla pod and bring the seeds and pod to the boil with the soy drink.
Stir in the millet flakes and half of the almonds, let swell for 3 minutes and remove the pod.
Take off the heat and stir in the pea protein and maple syrup until smooth.
Sprinkle with the remaining ground almonds.

title: Florentine overnight oats with flaked almonds, orange and cocoa nibs
instructions: Wash the orange in hot water, finely grate half of the zest and cut the flesh into segments.
Stir the oats, pea protein, soy drink and orange zest in a jar until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Caramelise the flaked almonds with the maple syrup in a pan for 2 minutes and leave to cool.
In the morning top with the orange segments, caramelised almonds and cocoa nibs.

title: Sweet potato cinnamon pancakes with pea protein and soy skyr
instructions: Finely mash the cooked sweet potato and stir with the soy drink until smooth.
Stir in the rice flour, pea protein, baking powder and cinnamon and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
Brush a pan with the oil and cook 3 pancakes over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Serve with the soy skyr and dust with cinnamon.

title: Vegan Saxon curd cakes with soy skyr, raisins and apple sauce
instructions: Finely grate the potatoes or press them through a ricer.
Knead with the soy skyr, pea protein, rice flour, raisins, lemon zest and a pinch of cinnamon into a pliable dough.
With damp hands shape 4 flat cakes and fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Dust with cinnamon and serve with the apple sauce.

title: Linzer buckwheat porridge with redcurrants and hazelnuts
instructions: Bring the buckwheat flakes to the boil with the soy drink, cinnamon and ground cloves and let them swell for 4 minutes, stirring.
Take off the heat and stir in the soy protein until smooth.
Cook two thirds of the redcurrants with 1 tbsp water for 2 minutes into a compote.
Serve the porridge with the compote, the remaining fresh redcurrants and toasted hazelnuts.

title: Stracciatella soy skyr bowl with raspberries and puffed quinoa
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, maple syrup and 1 tbsp water until creamy.
Grate the chocolate very finely and fold most of it in.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the raspberries, puffed quinoa and remaining chocolate shavings.

title: Persimmon pecan quinoa porridge with soy protein and cinnamon
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and simmer with 150 ml of the soy drink and the cinnamon for 15 minutes until soft.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Cut the persimmon into thin slices, lay them on the porridge and sprinkle with chopped pecans and cinnamon.

title: Rooibos vanilla chia pudding with orange segments
instructions: Whisk the rooibos tea, soy drink, pea protein and vanilla until smooth.
Stir in the chia seeds, stir again after 5 minutes and chill for at least 2 hours.
Peel the orange and cut it into segments.
Layer the pudding in a glass with the soy skyr and orange segments.

title: Poppy seed cake baked oats with lemon and soy skyr
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees.
Chop the date very finely and mix with the oats, pea protein, poppy seeds, baking powder and half of the lemon zest, then stir in the almond drink and 40 g of the soy skyr.
Pour into a small ovenproof dish and bake for 22 minutes.
Leave to cool briefly and top with the remaining soy skyr and lemon zest.

title: Bee sting cup with vanilla soy skyr and almond buckwheat crunch
instructions: Toast the buckwheat and flaked almonds in a pan for 3 minutes, add half of the maple syrup, caramelise briefly and leave to cool on baking paper.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein, vanilla, remaining maple syrup and 1 tbsp water until creamy.
Spoon the cream into a glass and scatter the almond crunch on top just before eating.

title: Rose water raspberry amaranth porridge with pistachios
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink and let it swell, covered, over low heat for 20 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink and the rose water until smooth and fold in.
Serve with the raspberries and chopped pistachios.

title: Cherry coconut teff porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with 180 ml of the soy drink and the vanilla and simmer for 12 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold in.
Warm the sour cherries for 2 minutes, spoon them onto the porridge and sprinkle with the coconut.

title: Pumpkin cinnamon waffles made with rice flour, soy skyr and walnuts
instructions: Stir the pumpkin purée with the soy drink until smooth, then stir in the rice flour, pea protein, baking powder and cinnamon.
Bake 2 waffles in a preheated, lightly greased waffle iron for 4 minutes each until golden.
Roughly chop the walnuts and toast them briefly in a dry pan.
Serve the waffles with the soy skyr and walnuts and dust with cinnamon.

title: Buckwheat herb pancakes with smoked tofu, radishes and chive soy skyr
instructions: Stir the buckwheat flour, soy protein, soy drink and a pinch of salt until smooth, then finely chop the parsley and dill and stir in.
Brush a pan with the oil and cook 2 thin pancakes for 2 minutes per side.
Mix the soy skyr with the chives, salt and pepper, cut the smoked tofu into strips and slice the radishes.
Spread the pancakes with the chive skyr, top with the tofu and radishes and fold over.

title: Bubble and squeak with savoy cabbage, potatoes, smoked tofu and lupin beans
instructions: Cut the savoy cabbage into fine strips and steam in a little water for 3 minutes, then drain well.
Roughly mash the potatoes and mix with the cabbage, lupin beans, yeast flakes, mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Dice the smoked tofu and fry it in the oiled pan for 3 minutes, then add the potato mixture, press flat and fry for 5 minutes until the underside is crisp.
Turn in pieces, fry for another 4 minutes and serve hot.

title: Potato lupin waffles with chives and tofu herb dip
instructions: Finely grate the potato and squeeze it out well, then mash the lupin beans with a fork.
Mix the potato, lupin beans, pea protein, half of the chives, salt and 2 tbsp water into a batter.
Bake 2 waffles in the preheated waffle iron brushed with the oil for 6 minutes each until crisp.
Blend the tofu with the lemon juice, garlic powder, remaining chives, salt and 2 tbsp water until creamy and serve with the waffles.

title: Smørrebrød with smoked tofu, cucumber, cress and dill soy skyr on gluten-free bread
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, chopped dill, lemon zest, salt and pepper until smooth.
Toast the bread and spread it thickly with half of the dill cream.
Cut the smoked tofu into thin slices and the cucumber into fine slices and lay them alternately on the bread.
Add the remaining dill cream as a dollop and sprinkle with cress.

title: Potato blini with tofu horseradish cream and apple
instructions: Finely mash the potatoes and stir with the pea protein, cornflour, salt and 3 tbsp water into a thick batter.
Brush a pan with the oil and fry 6 small blini from the batter for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Blend the tofu with the soy skyr, horseradish and salt until creamy.
Cut the apple into fine matchsticks, top the blini with the cream and apple and sprinkle with chives.

title: Corn pepper muffins with tofu and spring onions
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line 3 muffin holes with paper cases.
Blend the tofu with the soy drink until smooth and stir with the cornmeal, pea protein, baking powder, paprika and salt.
Finely dice the pepper, slice the spring onion into rings and fold in with the corn.
Divide between the cases and bake for 22 minutes until golden.

title: Millet tofu pan with lupin beans, edamame, zucchini and ginger
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and cook, covered, in 50 ml water for 10 minutes.
Dice the tofu and fry it in the oiled non-stick pan for 5 minutes until golden all over.
Cut the zucchini into half-moons and the spring onion into rings, add with the ginger, lupin beans and edamame and fry for 4 more minutes.
Fold in the millet, add the tamari and serve straight away.

title: Raspberry strawberry fruit gummies with agar and pea protein
instructions: Thaw the raspberries, purée them with the strawberries and press through a sieve.
Bring the purée to the boil with the agar and lemon juice and simmer for 2 minutes, stirring.
Leave to cool slightly and quickly stir in the pea protein until smooth.
Spread into a small dish lined with baking paper, chill for 1 hour and cut into small cubes.

title: Beetroot chips with tofu dill dip
instructions: Preheat the fan oven to 150 degrees, peel the beetroot and slice it wafer-thin.
Toss the slices with the oil and a little salt, spread on a tray and bake for 30 minutes until crisp, turning once.
Blend the tofu with the soy skyr, yeast flakes, lemon juice, dill, salt and pepper until creamy.
Leave the chips to cool and serve with the dip.

title: Hot protein drinking chocolate with cinnamon
instructions: Whisk the soy protein, cocoa and cinnamon with 100 ml cold soy drink until lump-free.
Heat the remaining soy drink with the chopped chocolate and maple syrup until the chocolate has melted.
Stir in the cocoa mixture and bring to just below boiling, stirring, without letting it boil.
Whisk until frothy, pour into a mug and dust with cinnamon.

title: Fig almond protein bars with sesame
instructions: Soak the figs in 3 tbsp hot water for 10 minutes and purée finely with the water.
Knead with the soy protein, almond butter, vanilla and cinnamon, then work in the chopped almonds and puffed quinoa.
Press the mixture into a rectangle, sprinkle with the sesame and press it in.
Chill for 1 hour and cut into 2 bars.

title: Rhubarb ginger ice lollies with soy yoghurt and dates
instructions: Cut the rhubarb into small pieces, finely chop the dates and stew both with the ginger and 2 tbsp water for 6 minutes until soft, then leave to cool.
Stir the soy yoghurt with the soy protein until smooth.
Loosely fold in the rhubarb compote so that pink streaks remain.
Pour the mixture into 2 ice lolly moulds, insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.

title: Peanut protein cups with dark chocolate
instructions: Melt the chocolate and divide half between 4 small paper cases, then chill for 10 minutes.
Stir the peanut butter, soy protein, chopped peanuts, salt and the water into a pliable cream.
Divide the cream over the chocolate bases, smooth it and cover with the remaining chocolate.
Chill for 30 minutes until the cups are firm.

title: Rum ball protein bites with cocoa and raisins
instructions: Finely chop the raisins and date.
Knead with the soy protein, cocoa, almond butter, rum flavouring and 2 to 3 tbsp water into a pliable dough.
Roll 5 balls and coat them in the finely grated chocolate.
Chill for at least 30 minutes so that they firm up.

title: Edamame pea pesto with cucumber slices and tofu cubes
instructions: Cook the edamame and peas in boiling water for 3 minutes and refresh in cold water.
Blend with the basil, yeast flakes, oil, lemon juice, garlic powder, salt and 2 tbsp water into a coarse pesto.
Dice the tofu and fry it in a dry non-stick pan for 5 minutes until golden.
Cut the cucumber into thick slices and serve with the pesto and tofu cubes.

title: Zucchini rolls with tofu herb filling and cherry tomatoes
instructions: Slice the zucchini lengthwise into 8 thin strips, brush with the oil and cook in a griddle pan for 1 minute per side.
Blend the tofu with the soy skyr, yeast flakes, herbs, lemon zest, salt and pepper until creamy.
Spread the filling on the zucchini strips and roll them up.
Serve with halved cherry tomatoes.

title: Coffee agar jelly with vanilla soy skyr
instructions: Bring the coffee to the boil with the agar and half of the maple syrup and simmer for 2 minutes.
Pour into a shallow dish, leave to set for 1 hour and cut into small cubes.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, vanilla, remaining maple syrup and 1 tbsp water until creamy.
Layer the coffee cubes and vanilla cream in a glass and dust with cocoa.

title: Carrot ginger dip with tofu, edamame and cucumber sticks
instructions: Slice the carrots and steam for 10 minutes until soft, adding the edamame for the last 3 minutes.
Leave to cool slightly and blend with the tofu, yeast flakes, ginger, cumin, lemon juice and salt until creamy.
Cut the cucumber into sticks and serve with the dip.

title: Apple pie protein shake with cinnamon and oats
instructions: Wash the fruit, peel if needed and cut it into rough pieces.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a glass and dust with a little cinnamon.

title: Protein chocolate fondue with fruit skewers
instructions: Halve the strawberries, cut the pear into pieces, divide the mandarin into segments and thread everything alternately onto 4 short skewers.
Warm the soy drink with the chopped chocolate until it has melted.
Take off the heat and stir in the soy protein and cocoa until lump-free.
Pour the chocolate sauce into a small bowl and serve the skewers alongside for dipping.

title: Salted caramel protein pudding made with silken tofu and dates
instructions: Soak the dates in 2 tbsp hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend with the water, almond butter, vanilla and most of the fleur de sel into a caramel cream, setting 1 tbsp aside.
Add the silken tofu and soy protein and blend until very smooth.
Spoon into a glass, chill for 1 hour and top with the remaining caramel cream and a pinch of fleur de sel.

title: Cocoa coconut granola clusters with pea protein and soy skyr
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160 degrees.
Mix the oats, pea protein, coconut, cocoa and chopped almonds, then stir in the maple syrup and 2 tbsp water until small clumps form.
Spread out as clusters on a lined baking tray, bake for 15 minutes and leave to cool on the tray.
Serve with the soy skyr for dipping or spooning.

title: Mandarin buckwheat porridge with pea protein and tofu
instructions: Blend the tofu with 100 ml of the almond drink and the pea protein until smooth.
Bring the buckwheat flakes to the boil with the remaining almond drink and the cinnamon and let them swell for 4 minutes, stirring.
Take off the heat and stir in the tofu cream.
Peel the mandarins, divide into segments and arrange on the porridge.

title: Carrot cinnamon pancakes made with rice flour and tofu vanilla cream
instructions: Finely grate the carrot and stir with the rice flour, pea protein, baking powder, cinnamon and 60 ml of the almond drink.
Brush a pan with the oil and cook 3 pancakes over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side.
Blend the tofu with the remaining almond drink, maple syrup and vanilla until very smooth.
Stack the pancakes, top with the tofu vanilla cream and dust with cinnamon.

title: Raspberry rice flake porridge with pea protein and tofu
instructions: Blend the tofu with 100 ml of the almond drink and the pea protein until smooth.
Bring the rice flakes to the boil with the remaining almond drink and the vanilla and let them swell for 3 minutes.
Take off the heat and stir in the tofu cream and half of the raspberries.
Top with the remaining raspberries and the coconut.

title: Baked quinoa with blueberries, pea protein and almonds
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and rinse the quinoa with hot water.
Blend the tofu with the almond drink, pea protein, maple syrup, cinnamon and vanilla until smooth.
Put the quinoa and two thirds of the blueberries into a small ovenproof dish, pour over the tofu mixture and scatter with the remaining blueberries and flaked almonds.
Bake covered for 25 minutes, then uncovered for 10 minutes until the quinoa is cooked.

title: Banana cinnamon muffins made with rice flour, pea protein and tofu
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line 3 muffin holes with paper cases.
Blend the banana, tofu and almond drink until smooth.
Stir in the rice flour, pea protein, baking powder and cinnamon and divide the batter between the cases.
Bake for 20 minutes and leave to cool.

title: Kohlrabi rösti with fried egg and chive sour cream
instructions: Peel and coarsely grate the kohlrabi, squeeze it out firmly and mix with 1 egg, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Heat two thirds of the oil, add the mixture as 2 flat rösti and fry for 4 minutes per side until golden.
Fry the second egg in the remaining oil.
Mix the sour cream with the chives and salt and serve with the rösti and fried egg.

title: Pesto scrambled eggs with mozzarella and rocket
instructions: Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper and tear the mozzarella into small pieces.
Melt the butter over low heat, add the eggs and let them set slowly and creamily, stirring.
Just before the end fold in the pesto and mozzarella.
Serve on the rocket.

title: Spinach ricotta omelette with nutmeg and pine nuts
instructions: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden and remove.
Melt half of the butter and wilt the spinach in it for 1 minute, season with nutmeg and salt and remove.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper and let them set in the remaining butter over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Put the spinach and dollops of ricotta on one half, fold over and sprinkle with the pine nuts.

title: Omelette wrap with avocado, cream cheese and rocket
instructions: Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a large non-stick pan, spread the eggs thinly and let set over medium heat for 2 minutes, then turn and cook for 30 more seconds.
Leave to cool slightly, spread with the cream cheese and top with avocado slices and rocket.
Roll up tightly and cut in half diagonally.

title: Brussels sprouts pan with fried egg, walnuts and brown butter
instructions: Trim the Brussels sprouts and cut them in half.
Heat two thirds of the butter until nutty brown, place the sprouts cut side down and fry, covered, for 6 minutes, then turn and fry for 2 more minutes.
Roughly chop the walnuts, toast them briefly with the sprouts and season with salt and lemon zest.
Fry 2 eggs in the remaining butter, place them on the sprouts and sprinkle with chilli flakes.

title: Pointed cabbage egg pan with vegetarian mountain cheese and caraway
ingredients: Mountain cheese (vegetarian, made with microbial rennet)
instructions: Cut the pointed cabbage into fine strips.
Melt the butter in a pan and fry the cabbage with the caraway and salt over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Make two hollows, crack in the eggs, sprinkle over the grated cheese and let set, covered, for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with pepper and chives.

title: Pineapple ginger quinoa porridge with soy protein and lime
instructions: Rinse the quinoa thoroughly in a sieve.
Finely grate the ginger and bring it to the boil with the quinoa and 150 ml of the soy drink, then cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes until creamy.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Dice the pineapple, scatter over the porridge and sprinkle with lime zest.

title: Pomegranate orange millet porridge with pea protein and cinnamon
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and bring to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink and the cinnamon, then let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Peel the orange and cut it into segments.
Serve the porridge with the orange segments and pomegranate seeds and dust with cinnamon.

title: Mango lime pancakes made with rice flour and soy skyr
instructions: Mix the rice flour, pea protein and baking powder, then stir in the soy drink and 40 g of the soy skyr until smooth.
Brush a pan with the oil and cook 3 small pancakes over medium heat for 2 minutes per side.
Peel the mango and cut it into small dice.
Stack the pancakes, top with the remaining soy skyr and the mango and sprinkle with lime zest.

title: Lemon blueberry millet bake with silken tofu and pea protein
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees.
Blend the silken tofu with the pea protein, maple syrup, lemon zest and lemon juice until smooth, then stir in the millet flakes and baking powder.
Pour into a small baking dish, scatter the blueberries on top and press in lightly.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden and leave to cool for 5 minutes.

title: Black Forest cherry baked oats with soy protein and cocoa
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees.
Blend the oats, soy protein, cocoa, baking powder and soy drink until smooth.
Pour into a small baking dish, press in the sour cherries and bake for 20 minutes.
Leave to cool briefly and serve with a dollop of soy skyr.

title: Vegan carrot cake muffins with soy skyr frosting
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line 2 muffin moulds with paper cases.
Finely grate the carrot, finely grind the oats and mix both with the rice flour, pea protein, cinnamon and baking powder.
Stir in 50 g of the soy skyr, the maple syrup and 2 tbsp water, fill the cases with the batter and bake for 22 minutes.
Leave the muffins to cool, spread with the remaining soy skyr and sprinkle with chopped walnuts.

title: Vegan polenta semolina porridge with plum compote and soy protein
instructions: Stone and quarter the plums and stew with the maple syrup, cinnamon and 2 tbsp water for 5 minutes until soft.
Bring 200 ml of the soy drink to the boil with the vanilla, sprinkle in the semolina and let it swell for 5 minutes, stirring.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and serve with the warm plum compote.

title: Rhubarb vanilla millet flake porridge with pea protein
instructions: Cut the rhubarb into pieces and stew with the maple syrup and 2 tbsp water for 5 minutes until soft.
Bring the millet flakes to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink and the vanilla and let them swell for 3 minutes.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold in.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the rhubarb.

title: Persimmon cardamom chia pudding with soy yoghurt
instructions: Stir the soy protein, soy drink, cardamom and 50 g of the soy yoghurt until smooth and stir in the chia seeds.
Stir again after 5 minutes and chill for at least 2 hours.
Purée half of the persimmon finely with the remaining soy yoghurt and cut the rest into small cubes.
Layer the chia pudding and persimmon purée in a glass, top with the persimmon cubes and dust with cardamom.

title: Nougat amaranth porridge with hazelnuts, cocoa and banana
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 130 ml of the soy drink and cook covered over low heat for 20 minutes until creamy.
Stir the pea protein and cocoa with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold in.
Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan and chop roughly.
Serve the porridge with banana slices and the hazelnuts.

title: Vegan protein rice pudding with cherry compote and cinnamon
instructions: Bring the rice to the boil with 170 ml of the soy drink and the vanilla and let it swell over the lowest heat for 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the rice pudding.
Simmer the sour cherries with 1 tbsp water for 4 minutes to make a compote.
Serve the rice pudding with the cherry compote and dust with cinnamon.

title: Vegan quark crêpes with soy skyr and apricots
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour with the soy drink and a pinch of salt until smooth and leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Brush a pan with the oil and cook 2 thin crêpes for 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, vanilla and lemon zest to make a quark cream.
Fill the crêpes with the cream, fold into quarters and serve with apricot wedges.

title: Pear almond rice flake porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink, cinnamon and vanilla and let them swell for 3 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Core the pear, cut it into thin wedges and toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the pear wedges and flaked almonds.

title: Baked apple baked oats with walnuts and raisins
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees, halve and core the apple.
Stir together the oats, soy protein, soy drink, baking powder and cinnamon and pour into a small baking dish.
Set one apple half in the centre cut side up, fill with the raisins and chopped walnuts, dice the second half and scatter it around.
Bake for 25 minutes and dust with cinnamon.

title: Mandarin ginger chia pudding with pea protein
instructions: Whisk the pea protein with the soy drink and the finely grated ginger until smooth.
Stir in the chia seeds, stir again after 5 minutes and chill for at least 2 hours.
Peel the mandarins and divide them into segments.
Spoon the pudding into a glass and top with the mandarin segments.

title: Orange chocolate waffles made with buckwheat flour and soy skyr
instructions: Mix the buckwheat flour, pea protein, cocoa and baking powder, then stir in the soy drink, 30 g of the soy skyr and a little orange zest until smooth.
Preheat the waffle iron, brush with the oil and bake 2 waffles for 4 minutes each.
Peel the orange and cut it into segments.
Serve the waffles with the remaining soy skyr and the orange segments.

title: Blackberry coconut buckwheat porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the buckwheat flakes to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink and let them swell for 4 minutes, stirring.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold in.
Toast the desiccated coconut briefly in a dry pan.
Serve the porridge with the blackberries and coconut.

title: Matcha banana rice flake porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink and the vanilla and let them swell for 3 minutes.
Whisk the matcha and soy protein with the remaining soy drink until there are no lumps.
Take off the heat and fold the matcha mixture into the porridge.
Slice the banana and arrange it on the porridge.

title: Tahini halva quinoa porridge with soy protein and date
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and simmer with 150 ml of the soy drink, vanilla and cinnamon for 15 minutes until soft.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink and half of the tahini until smooth and fold into the quinoa.
Finely chop the date and toast the sesame in a dry pan until golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, drizzle with the remaining tahini and sprinkle with the date and sesame.

title: Poppy seed sour cherry amaranth porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 100 ml of the soy drink, 80 ml water, the poppy seeds and vanilla, cover and let it swell over low heat for 20 minutes.
Heat the sour cherries with the maple syrup for 4 minutes until juicy.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the amaranth.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the warm sour cherries.

title: Tomato tofu bruschetta on cucumber slices with basil
instructions: Blend the tofu with the soy skyr, salt and pepper to make a creamy tofu ricotta.
Finely dice the cherry tomatoes and mix with the oil, chopped garlic, salt and half of the basil.
Cut the cucumber diagonally into thick slices.
Spread the cucumber slices with the tofu ricotta, top with the tomatoes and garnish with the remaining basil.

title: Pea mint tofu smash with radishes and cucumber slices
instructions: Cook the peas and edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, refresh in cold water and drain.
Crumble the tofu roughly and mash coarsely with a fork together with the peas, edamame, soy skyr, mint, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Cut the cucumber into thick slices and the radishes into thin slices.
Spread the smash on the cucumber slices and top with the radishes.

title: Vegan baked beans in tomato sauce with herb tofu and mushrooms
instructions: Simmer the beans with the chopped tomatoes, smoked paprika, salt and pepper for 10 minutes until thick.
Dice the tofu, season with thyme and fry in a non-stick pan with the oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Halve the mushrooms and fry them in the same pan for 4 minutes.
Arrange the beans, tofu and mushrooms on a plate and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Cauliflower hash browns with scrambled tofu and chives
instructions: Finely grate the cauliflower, squeeze it out firmly in a cloth and mix with the chickpea flour, salt and pepper.
Heat two thirds of the oil and fry the mixture as 2 flat hash browns for 4 minutes per side until crisp.
Crumble the tofu with the turmeric, yeast flakes and kala namak and fry in the remaining oil for 4 minutes.
Serve the hash browns with the scrambled tofu and sprinkle with chives.

title: Redcurrant panna cotta with soy skyr and agar
instructions: Bring the soy drink to the boil with the agar and vanilla and simmer for 2 minutes, stirring.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein and half of the maple syrup until smooth and quickly stir in the hot agar milk.
Pour into a glass and chill for at least 2 hours.
Heat the redcurrants with the remaining maple syrup for 2 minutes, leave to cool and spoon over the panna cotta.

title: Vegan peanut protein cookies with soy yoghurt
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175 degrees and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Stir the peanut butter, maple syrup and soy yoghurt until smooth, then knead in the pea protein, oats and baking powder to make a firm dough.
Shape four balls, place on the tray, flatten them and press the chopped peanuts on top.
Bake for 10 minutes and leave to cool on the tray.

title: Lemon blondies made with white beans and pea protein
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line a small tin with baking paper.
Rinse the beans and blend with the almond butter, maple syrup, lemon zest and lemon juice until very smooth.
Stir in the pea protein, oats and baking powder and spread the batter in the tin.
Bake for 20 minutes, leave to cool completely and cut into 2 pieces.

title: Coconut curry tofu bites with lime dip
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Pat the tofu dry, cut into bite-sized cubes, toss with the tamari and curry powder and roll in the coconut.
Spread on the tray and bake for 20 minutes until golden and crisp.
Stir the soy skyr with the lime zest, lime juice, coriander and a pinch of salt and serve with the tofu bites.

title: Chocolate mint protein pudding made with silken tofu
instructions: Finely chop half of the mint leaves.
Blend the silken tofu with the soy protein, cocoa, maple syrup and the chopped mint until very smooth.
Spoon into a glass and chill for 30 minutes.
Garnish with grated chocolate and the remaining mint leaves.

title: Apple rings with peanut soy skyr dip and cocoa nibs
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, peanut butter and cinnamon until smooth.
Core the apple and cut it crosswise into 6 rings.
Drizzle the apple rings with lemon juice so that they do not turn brown.
Spoon the dip into a small bowl, sprinkle with the cocoa nibs and serve with the apple rings.

title: Sour cherry almond protein bars with vanilla
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line a small tin with baking paper.
Mix the ground almonds with the pea protein, vanilla and baking powder, then stir in the soy skyr and maple syrup to make a thick batter.
Spread the batter in the tin and press the sour cherries evenly into it.
Bake for 15 minutes, leave to cool and cut into 2 bars.

title: Lupin flaxseed crackers with tofu herb dip
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160 degrees.
Stir the lupin meal, flaxseed, sesame, a pinch of salt and 50 ml water together and leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Spread the mixture thinly on baking paper, score into rectangles and bake for 30 minutes until crisp.
Blend the tofu with the soy skyr, herbs, lemon juice, salt and pepper until creamy and serve with the crackers.

title: Rhubarb strawberry protein shake with soy skyr
instructions: Cut the rhubarb into pieces, stew with 2 tbsp water for 5 minutes until soft and leave to cool.
Wash the fruit, peel if needed and cut it into rough pieces.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Pistachio protein pudding made with silken tofu
instructions: Grind two thirds of the pistachios very finely and chop the rest roughly.
Blend the silken tofu with the soy protein, ground pistachios, maple syrup and vanilla until very smooth.
Spoon into a glass and chill for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with the chopped pistachios.

title: Cinnamon roll protein bars with pecans
instructions: Finely chop the dates and blend with the soy skyr, cinnamon and vanilla until smooth.
Knead in the oats and pea protein until a firm dough forms.
Press the dough into a rectangle, sprinkle with cinnamon, press the chopped pecans on top and cut into 2 bars.
Chill for at least 1 hour.

title: Pumpkin protein brownies with pea protein and dark chocolate
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line a small tin with baking paper.
Stir the pumpkin purée, soy skyr and maple syrup until smooth, then stir in the pea protein, cocoa, finely ground oats and baking powder.
Spread the batter in the tin and scatter the chopped chocolate over it.
Bake for 18 minutes, leave to cool and cut into 2 pieces.

title: Spiced apple pudding made with silken tofu and walnuts
instructions: Peel the apple, dice it finely and stew with the maple syrup, cinnamon and 2 tbsp water for 5 minutes until soft, then leave to cool.
Blend the silken tofu with the soy protein, half of the apples, the clove and vanilla until very smooth.
Spoon into a glass and chill for 30 minutes.
Top with the remaining diced apple and chopped walnuts.

title: Zucchini mini pizzas with tofu feta and oregano
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220 degrees and cut the zucchini diagonally into 8 thick slices.
Crumble the tofu finely and mix with the lemon juice, nutritional yeast, oregano, salt and pepper to make a tofu feta.
Brush the zucchini slices with the oil, spread with the chopped tomatoes and scatter the tofu feta on top.
Bake for 12 minutes until the zucchini is tender and the edges are golden.

title: Chocolate nice cream with soy protein and banana
instructions: Cut the fruit into pieces and freeze for at least 4 hours.
Blend the frozen banana with the soy protein, cocoa and soy drink in a food processor for 1 to 2 minutes until creamy, scraping down in between.
Spoon into a bowl straight away or freeze for another 30 minutes for a firmer texture.

title: Frozen raspberry soy skyr drops with dark chocolate
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein and maple syrup until smooth, lightly crush the raspberries and fold them in.
Spoon the mixture in 8 small dollops onto a board lined with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate and drizzle it over the drops in thin lines.
Freeze for at least 2 hours and let thaw for 5 minutes before eating.

title: Orange coconut quinoa porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and simmer with 150 ml of the almond drink and the vanilla for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the tofu with the remaining almond drink, the pea protein and a little orange zest until smooth.
Take off the heat and stir in the tofu cream.
Segment the orange, arrange on the porridge and sprinkle with the coconut.

title: Blueberry tofu smoothie bowl with puffed quinoa
instructions: Blend the tofu, pea protein, two thirds of the blueberries, the banana and the almond drink in a blender until thick and creamy.
Pour the smoothie into a bowl.
Top with the remaining blueberries and the puffed quinoa.
Serve immediately so that the quinoa stays crunchy.

title: Walnut waffles made with rice flour with tofu vanilla cream and strawberries
instructions: Stir the rice flour with the pea protein, baking powder, cinnamon, half of the finely chopped walnuts and 60 ml of the almond drink to a thick batter.
Brush the waffle iron with the oil and bake 2 waffles until golden.
Blend the tofu with the remaining almond drink and vanilla until very smooth.
Serve the waffles with the tofu cream, halved strawberries and the remaining walnuts.

title: Strawberry ginger millet porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and simmer with 130 ml of the almond drink and the finely grated ginger for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the tofu with the remaining almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the millet.
Crush half of the strawberries and fold them in.
Halve the remaining strawberries and arrange them on the porridge.

title: Zucchini halloumi fritters with fried egg
instructions: Coarsely grate the zucchini, salt lightly, leave for 5 minutes and squeeze out firmly.
Finely grate the halloumi and mix with the zucchini, 1 egg, the ground almonds, mint and pepper.
Heat two thirds of the oil and fry 3 fritters over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden.
Fry the second egg in the remaining oil and serve with the fritters.

title: Fennel frittata with vegetarian hard cheese and lemon
instructions: Slice the fennel very thinly and fry in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 6 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Whisk the eggs with the crème fraîche, half of the cheese, the lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Pour the egg mixture over the fennel, sprinkle with the remaining cheese and let set over low heat for 4 minutes.
Grill for 3 minutes until golden and sprinkle with the fennel fronds.

title: Pumpkin goat cheese frittata with sage
instructions: Cut the pumpkin into small cubes and fry in half of the butter in an ovenproof pan for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the remaining butter and fry the sage leaves in it for 1 minute until crisp.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper, pour over, crumble the goat cheese on top and let set over low heat for 4 minutes.
Grill for 3 minutes until golden.

title: Oyster mushroom scrambled eggs with crème fraîche and chives
instructions: Tear the oyster mushrooms into strips and fry in half of the butter with the thyme for 5 minutes until golden, season with salt and remove.
Whisk the eggs with the crème fraîche, salt and pepper.
Melt the remaining butter over low heat and let the eggs set slowly and creamily, stirring.
Serve the scrambled eggs with the mushrooms and sprinkle with chives.

title: Radicchio feta omelette with walnuts
instructions: Cut the radicchio into thin strips and roughly chop the walnuts.
Heat half of the oil and wilt the radicchio with the thyme for 2 minutes, season with salt and remove.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper and let them set in the remaining oil over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Put the radicchio and crumbled feta on one half, fold over and sprinkle with the walnuts.

title: Broccoli mountain cheese egg pan with almonds
ingredients: Mountain cheese (vegetarian, made with microbial rennet)
instructions: Divide the broccoli into small florets, blanch in salted water for 3 minutes and drain.
Toast the flaked almonds in a dry pan until golden and remove.
Melt the butter, fry the broccoli for 2 minutes, pour the eggs whisked with salt and pepper over it and sprinkle with the grated mountain cheese.
Cover and let set over low heat for 5 minutes, then sprinkle with the almonds.

title: Gooseberry vanilla millet porridge with pea protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and bring to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink and the vanilla, then let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stew the gooseberries with the maple syrup and 1 tbsp water for 4 minutes until the first ones burst.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the warm gooseberries.

title: Mirabelle plum almond quinoa porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the quinoa thoroughly in a sieve, bring to the boil with 140 ml of the soy drink and the cinnamon, then cook covered for 15 minutes until creamy.
Halve and stone the mirabelle plums and toast them in a dry pan for 3 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Serve the porridge with the mirabelle plums and flaked almonds.

title: Physalis coconut rice flake porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink and the vanilla and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Remove the physalis from their husks, wash and halve them.
Top the porridge with the physalis and sprinkle with the coconut.

title: Lychee lime chia pudding with soy skyr
instructions: Stir the chia seeds into the soy drink and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein, lime juice and lime zest until smooth.
Peel, stone and halve the lychees.
Layer the chia pudding and skyr cream in a glass and top with the lychees.

title: Plum cinnamon buckwheat pancakes with soy skyr
instructions: Mix the buckwheat flour, soy protein, cinnamon and baking powder and stir into a thick batter with the soy drink.
Stone the plums and cut into wedges, finely dice a quarter of them and fold into the batter.
Brush a pan with the oil and cook 4 small pancakes over medium heat for 2 minutes per side.
Stack the pancakes and serve with the soy skyr and the remaining plum wedges.

title: Pink grapefruit mint skyr bowl with hemp seeds
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein and half the maple syrup until smooth and spread in a shallow bowl.
Peel and segment the grapefruit, catching the juice.
Stir the grapefruit juice with the remaining maple syrup and cut the mint into thin strips.
Arrange the segments on the skyr, drizzle with the syrup and sprinkle with the hemp seeds and mint.

title: Grape walnut buckwheat porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat with hot water, bring to the boil with 140 ml of the soy drink and the cinnamon and simmer covered for 15 minutes until soft.
Halve the grapes and toast them in a dry pan for 3 minutes, roughly chop the walnuts.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Serve the porridge with the grapes and walnuts.

title: Papaya coconut amaranth porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 130 ml of the soy drink and 60 ml water, cover and let it swell over low heat for 20 minutes.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the amaranth.
Peel, deseed and dice the papaya.
Serve the porridge with the papaya, coconut and lime zest.

title: Apple tahini millet flake porridge with soy protein and cinnamon
instructions: Bring the millet flakes to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink and the cinnamon and let them swell for 3 minutes, stirring.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold in.
Core the apple and cut it into thin wedges.
Top the porridge with the apple wedges, drizzle with the tahini and dust with cinnamon.

title: Hazelnut pear buckwheat waffles with soy skyr
instructions: Preheat the waffle iron.
Stir the buckwheat flour, soy protein, cinnamon and baking powder into a smooth batter with the soy drink.
Bake 2 waffles in the waffle iron for 4 minutes each until golden brown.
Cut the pear into thin wedges, chop the hazelnuts and serve on the waffles with the soy skyr.

title: Peach thyme quinoa porridge with pea protein
instructions: Rinse the quinoa thoroughly and bring to the boil with 140 ml of the soy drink, then cook covered for 15 minutes until creamy.
Cut the peach into wedges and caramelise in a pan with the maple syrup and thyme leaves for 3 minutes.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Serve the porridge with the warm peach wedges.

title: Blackberry cardamom buckwheat muffins with pea protein
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line 2 muffin cups with paper cases.
Stir the silken tofu with the maple syrup and cardamom until smooth, then stir in the buckwheat flour, pea protein and baking powder.
Fold in two thirds of the blackberries, fill the cases with the batter and press the remaining berries on top.
Bake for about 22 minutes until a skewer comes out clean and leave to cool.

title: Banana sesame pancakes made with rice flour and soy protein
instructions: Mash half the banana with a fork and stir together with the soy drink, rice flour, soy protein and baking powder.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry non-stick pan for 1 minute and remove.
Cook 4 small pancakes in the pan over medium heat for 2 minutes per side.
Serve the pancakes with the soy skyr, the remaining banana slices and the toasted sesame.

title: Earl Grey pear protein pudding made with silken tofu
instructions: Steep the tea bag in 60 ml hot water for 5 minutes, remove and leave the tea to cool.
Blend the silken tofu with the soy protein, maple syrup and 3 tbsp of the tea until very smooth and chill for 30 minutes.
Core the pear, dice it finely and stew in the remaining tea for 3 minutes.
Spoon the pudding into a glass and top with the pear cubes.

title: Maple pecan baked millet with soy protein
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees.
Blend the silken tofu with the soy drink, soy protein, half the maple syrup, the cinnamon and baking powder until smooth, then stir in the millet flakes.
Finely dice the apple, fold it in and pour everything into a small baking dish.
Top with the pecan halves and bake for 25 minutes until golden, then drizzle with the remaining maple syrup.

title: Fig orange chia pudding with soy skyr
instructions: Wash the orange in hot water and finely grate the zest. Stir the chia seeds with the soy drink, orange zest and cinnamon and chill for at least 4 hours.
Halve the orange. Squeeze one half and stir the juice with the soy skyr and soy protein until smooth.
Peel and segment the other orange half and cut the fig into 4 wedges.
Layer the pudding and skyr cream in a glass and top with the fig wedges and all the orange segments.

title: Nectarine ginger overnight quinoa with soy skyr
instructions: Finely grate the ginger and stir together with the quinoa flakes, soy drink, soy skyr and soy protein until smooth.
Spoon into a jar, seal and chill overnight, for at least 6 hours.
In the morning stone and dice the nectarine.
Stir the overnight quinoa and top with the nectarine cubes.

title: Raspberry coconut ground rice porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the soy drink to the boil with the maple syrup, sprinkle in the ground rice and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Stir the pea protein with 3 tbsp cold water until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Crush half the raspberries with a fork and spoon over the porridge as a sauce.
Top with the whole raspberries and coconut.

title: Sour cherry vanilla teff porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with 150 ml of the soy drink, 50 ml water and the vanilla and let it swell covered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Heat the sour cherries with the maple syrup for 4 minutes until juicy.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Serve the porridge with the warm sour cherries.

title: Redcurrant almond millet flake muffins with pea protein
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line 2 muffin cups with paper cases.
Stir the silken tofu with the maple syrup and vanilla until smooth, then stir in the millet flakes, ground almonds, pea protein and baking powder.
Strip the redcurrants from their stems, fold them in and fill the cases with the batter.
Bake for about 22 minutes and leave to cool.

title: Pesarattu – mung bean crêpe with ginger tofu filling
instructions: Soak the mung beans overnight in plenty of water, drain and blend with the pea protein, half the ginger, the cumin, salt and 80 ml water into a smooth batter.
Crumble the tofu and fry with the remaining ginger, the turmeric and the diced tomato in half the oil for 5 minutes, then fold in the spinach and let it wilt.
Heat the remaining oil in a large pan, spread the batter thinly in a round and cook for 3 minutes, then turn and cook for 1 more minute.
Spoon the tofu filling onto one half, fold the crêpe over and serve sprinkled with chilli flakes.

title: Vegan breakfast tacos with crumbled tempeh, tomato salsa and soy skyr
instructions: Soak the soy mince in hot water for 10 minutes and squeeze out, finely crumble the tempeh and tofu and fry everything in a dry non-stick pan with the smoked paprika, cumin and a splash of water for 6 minutes until crisp, then season with salt.
Finely dice the tomato and mix with the lime juice, chopped coriander and pepper into a salsa.
Warm the tortillas in the hot pan for 30 seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with lettuce, the tempeh crumble, salsa and a dollop of soy skyr.

title: Strawberry mochi with soy skyr protein filling
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein into a thick cream and chill for 20 minutes.
Stir the glutinous rice flour with the maple syrup and 45 ml water until smooth, microwave for 1 minute, stir and microwave for another 30 seconds.
Turn the dough out onto a surface dusted with starch, halve it and press each half into a thin round.
Coat each strawberry with skyr cream, place on a dough round, close the dough over it and serve seam side down.

title: Dorayaki with vanilla soy skyr filling
instructions: Stir the rice flour, soy protein, baking powder, half the maple syrup and the soy drink into a thick batter.
Cook 4 round little pancakes in a non-stick pan over low heat for 2 minutes per side until golden brown and leave to cool.
Stir the soy skyr with the remaining maple syrup and the vanilla until smooth.
Sandwich the little pancakes together in pairs with the cream.

title: Beetroot brownies with pea protein and dark chocolate
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees and line a small tin with baking paper.
Purée the beetroot very finely with the soy skyr and maple syrup.
Stir in the pea protein, cocoa, almond flour and baking powder, chop the chocolate and fold it in.
Spread the batter in the tin, bake for 18 minutes, leave to cool and cut into 2 pieces.

title: Bounty-style protein bars with coconut and dark chocolate
instructions: Knead the coconut, soy protein, almond flour, soy skyr and maple syrup into a mouldable mixture.
Shape the mixture into 2 bars and freeze for 20 minutes.
Melt the chocolate over a water bath.
Coat the bars with the chocolate and leave to set in the fridge.

title: Cinnamon star protein cookies with skyr glaze
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160 degrees and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Knead the ground hazelnuts, 25 g of the pea protein, the cinnamon, lemon zest, maple syrup and 30 g of the soy skyr into a firm dough.
Roll out the dough 5 mm thick between baking paper, cut out 6 stars and bake for 12 minutes.
Stir the remaining soy skyr with the rest of the pea protein until smooth and spread thinly over the cooled stars.

title: Peanut raspberry protein bars with a fruit layer
instructions: Knead the peanut butter, soy protein, puffed quinoa and soy skyr together and press into a small tin lined with baking paper as a base.
Bring the raspberries to the boil with the maple syrup and agar and simmer for 2 minutes, stirring.
Spread the fruit mixture over the base and chill for 1 hour.
Cut into 2 bars.

title: Sesame brittle protein bars with puffed quinoa and tahini
instructions: Toast the sesame in a dry pan until golden, caramelise with half the maple syrup for 1 minute and leave to cool on baking paper.
Knead the soy protein, puffed quinoa, tahini, soy skyr and remaining maple syrup together.
Shape the mixture into 2 bars and press the crumbled sesame brittle on top.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.

title: Pumpkin seed cranberry protein cookies
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175 degrees and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Roughly chop the pumpkin seeds and halve the cranberries.
Stir the oats, pea protein, baking powder, cinnamon, soy skyr and maple syrup together, then fold in the pumpkin seeds and cranberries.
Shape 4 flat cookies and bake for 12 minutes.

title: Gooseberry crumble cup with soy skyr
instructions: Simmer the gooseberries with half the maple syrup for 5 minutes into a compote and leave to cool.
Toast the oats and almonds with the remaining maple syrup in a pan for 4 minutes until crisp.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein until smooth.
Layer the skyr cream and compote in a glass and top with the crumble.

title: No-bake blueberry cheesecake bars
instructions: Blend the almond flour and dates finely and press into a small tin lined with baking paper as a base.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, maple syrup and lemon zest until smooth.
Boil the agar in 40 ml water for 2 minutes, quickly stir into the cream and spread over the base.
Scatter the blueberries on top, chill for 1 hour and cut into 2 bars.

title: Lychee coconut protein shake with lime
instructions: Peel and stone the lychees.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Mirabelle plum vanilla ice lollies with soy skyr
instructions: Halve and stone the mirabelle plums.
Blend the mirabelle plums with the soy skyr, soy protein, maple syrup and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the mixture into 2 ice lolly moulds, insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Briefly hold the moulds under warm water and release the lollies.

title: Mango chilli protein shake with lime
instructions: Wash the fruit, peel if needed and cut it into rough pieces.
Blend the mango with the soy protein, soy skyr, water, lime juice and chilli flakes for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Date cardamom protein pudding made with silken tofu and pistachios
instructions: Soak the dates in 2 tbsp hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend the silken tofu with the soy protein, dates with their soaking water and the cardamom until very smooth.
Spoon into a glass and chill for 30 minutes.
Chop the pistachios and sprinkle over.

title: Physalis vanilla protein pudding made with silken tofu and almond butter
instructions: Blend the silken tofu with the pea protein, almond butter and vanilla until very smooth.
Spoon into a glass and chill for 30 minutes.
Remove the physalis from their husks, wash and halve them.
Top the pudding with the physalis.

title: Baklava protein balls with walnuts and pistachios
instructions: Finely chop the walnuts, chop the pistachios very finely and set aside.
Knead the walnuts, pea protein, soy skyr, maple syrup, lemon juice, cinnamon and clove into a mouldable mixture.
Roll the mixture into 6 balls and roll them in the pistachios.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.

title: Cherry coconut microwave mug cake with soy protein
instructions: Mash the banana with a fork in a large mug and mix with the buckwheat flour, soy protein, baking powder and half the coconut.
Stir in the soy skyr and 2 tbsp water and fold in the cherries.
Microwave at 800 watts for 90 seconds and leave to rest for 1 minute.
Sprinkle with the remaining coconut.

title: Sea buckthorn orange protein shake with soy skyr
instructions: Wash the fruit, peel if needed and cut it into rough pieces.
Put all the ingredients into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Papaya passion fruit millet porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and bring to the boil with 160 ml of the almond drink, then let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Blend the tofu with the remaining almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Peel, deseed and dice the papaya.
Top the porridge with the papaya cubes and spoon the passion fruit pulp over it.

title: Kiwi strawberry rice flake porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 150 ml of the almond drink and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Blend the tofu with the remaining almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir in.
Peel and slice the kiwi and halve the strawberries.
Serve the porridge topped with the kiwi slices and strawberries.

title: Mandarin vanilla buckwheat porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat with hot water, bring to the boil with 160 ml of the almond drink and the vanilla and simmer covered for 15 minutes until soft.
Blend the tofu with the remaining almond drink, the pea protein and the maple syrup until smooth.
Take off the heat and stir in the tofu cream.
Peel the mandarins, separate into segments and arrange on the porridge.

title: Blueberry lemon amaranth porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 160 ml of the almond drink and 40 ml water, cover and let it swell over low heat for 20 minutes.
Blend the tofu with the remaining almond drink, the pea protein and lemon zest until smooth.
Take off the heat and stir in the tofu cream.
Serve the porridge with the blueberries and a little lemon zest.

title: Swiss chard ricotta frittata with vegetarian hard cheese
instructions: Finely slice the chard stalks and roughly chop the leaves.
Fry the stalks in the oil in an ovenproof pan for 3 minutes, add the leaves and let them wilt for 2 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the hard cheese, nutmeg, salt and pepper, pour over the chard and dot the ricotta on top.
Let it set over low heat for 5 minutes, then grill for 3 minutes until golden.

title: Brussels sprout egg pan with vegetarian hard cheese and walnuts
instructions: Trim the Brussels sprouts and cut into quarters.
Fry the sprouts in the butter over medium heat for 7 minutes until golden and tender-crisp.
Whisk the eggs with half the hard cheese, salt and pepper, pour over the sprouts and let set covered for 4 minutes.
Roughly chop the walnuts and scatter over the egg pan with the remaining cheese.

title: Spinach blue cheese omelette with pine nuts
ingredients: Blue cheese (vegetarian, made with microbial rennet)
instructions: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden and remove.
Wilt the spinach in half the butter for 1 minute and remove.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper, let them set in the remaining butter over medium heat and put the spinach and crumbled cheese on one half.
Fold the omelette over and serve sprinkled with the pine nuts.

title: Oeufs cocotte with mushrooms and mountain cheese
ingredients: Mountain cheese (vegetarian, made with microbial rennet)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees.
Slice the mushrooms and fry in the butter with the thyme for 4 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.
Put the mushrooms into a ramekin, pour in the cream, crack the eggs on top and sprinkle with the grated mountain cheese.
Bake in a water bath in the oven for 14 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.

title: Egg crêpes with goat cheese, rocket and walnuts
instructions: Whisk the eggs with 2 tbsp water, salt and pepper until very smooth.
Cook 2 thin crêpes in a little butter each in a non-stick pan for 1 minute per side.
Spread the crêpes with the goat cheese and top with the rocket and chopped walnuts.
Fold into triangles and serve.

title: Zucchini feta scrambled eggs with mint
instructions: Cut the zucchini into small cubes and fry in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until golden.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper, add to the zucchini and let them set creamily over low heat, stirring.
Crumble the feta over the top.
Serve sprinkled with finely sliced mint.

title: Quince cinnamon buckwheat porridge with soy protein
instructions: Peel, core and finely dice the quince. Stew covered with 60 ml water, the maple syrup and cinnamon for 15 minutes until soft.
Rinse the buckwheat with hot water, bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the stewed quince.

title: Apricot almond amaranth porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and 50 ml water and let it swell covered over low heat for 20 minutes.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Halve and stone the apricots. Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the 6 apricot halves and sprinkle with the almonds.

title: Pineapple mint chia pudding with soy skyr
instructions: Stir the chia seeds into the soy drink and leave covered in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight to swell.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein until smooth.
Cut the pineapple into small cubes. Cut the mint leaves into fine strips and mix with the pineapple.
Layer the chia pudding and skyr cream in a jar and top with the minted pineapple.

title: Honeydew lime skyr bowl with pumpkin seeds
instructions: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until they start to pop.
Finely grate the zest of the lime half and squeeze out the juice.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, maple syrup and half of the lime zest until smooth.
Peel, deseed and dice the melon and drizzle with the lime juice. Spread over the skyr cream and sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds and remaining zest.

title: Pomegranate pistachio teff porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with 140 ml soy drink, 60 ml water and the cinnamon and let it swell over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Roughly chop the pistachios.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and sprinkle with the pomegranate seeds and pistachios.

title: Cherry cocoa rice flour pancakes with soy skyr
instructions: Mix the rice flour, pea protein, cocoa and baking powder and stir in the soy drink to make a smooth batter.
Simmer the cherries with 30 ml water in a small pan for 3 minutes to make a compote.
Brush a non-stick pan with the coconut oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes on each side.
Stack the pancakes and serve with the soy skyr and the warm cherry compote.

title: Blueberry millet flake waffles with soy skyr
instructions: Finely grind the millet flakes in a blender and mix with the soy protein, baking powder and vanilla.
Stir in the soy drink and fold in a third of the blueberries.
Brush the waffle iron with the rapeseed oil and bake 2 waffles from the batter for 4 minutes each until golden.
Serve the waffles with the soy skyr and the remaining blueberries.

title: Pear cinnamon quinoa bake with hazelnuts
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C top and bottom heat. Core the pear, dice one half and cut the other into thin wedges.
Mix the quinoa flakes, pea protein, cinnamon and baking powder, stir in the soy drink and maple syrup and fold in the diced pear.
Spread the mixture in a small baking dish, fan the pear wedges on top, chop the hazelnuts and scatter over.
Bake in the oven for 25 minutes until golden and serve warm.

title: Peach vanilla overnight buckwheat with soy skyr
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat thoroughly and soak covered with the soy drink and vanilla in the fridge overnight.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein until smooth.
Stone and dice the peach.
Layer the soaked buckwheat and skyr cream in a jar and top with the diced peach.

title: Mango lime silken tofu protein pudding
instructions: Peel the mango and cut the flesh off the stone. Finely dice half of the flesh.
Grate the zest of the lime half and squeeze out the juice.
Blend the silken tofu, soy protein, remaining mango, lime juice and maple syrup until smooth, pour into a dessert cup and chill for 30 minutes.
Top with the diced mango and lime zest.

title: Rhubarb cinnamon quinoa crumble with skyr cream
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C top and bottom heat. Cut the rhubarb into 2 cm pieces and place in a small baking dish with half of the maple syrup.
Rub the quinoa flakes, almond flour, cinnamon and coconut oil into crumbs and scatter over the rhubarb.
Bake for 20 minutes until the rhubarb is soft and the crumble is golden.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein and remaining maple syrup until smooth and spoon a dollop onto the warm crumble.

title: Persimmon vanilla rice flake porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and the vanilla and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Wash the persimmon and cut into 8 wedges. Roughly chop the hazelnuts.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, arrange the persimmon wedges on top and sprinkle with the hazelnuts.

title: Strawberry basil amaranth porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and 50 ml water and let it swell covered over low heat for 20 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Quarter the strawberries, cut the basil into fine strips and mix both with the maple syrup.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the basil strawberries.

title: Blackberry apple rice flour muffins with soy protein
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C top and bottom heat and place 2 paper muffin cases in a muffin tin.
Mix the rice flour, soy protein, baking powder and cinnamon. Stir in the apple purée, soy skyr and rapeseed oil.
Fold in 8 blackberries, divide the batter between the cases and press 2 blackberries into the top of each.
Bake for 20 minutes and leave to cool briefly.

title: Cocoa coconut quinoa porridge with raspberries
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and the cocoa. Let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan until light golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the raspberries and sprinkle with the coconut.

title: Blackberry poppy seed millet porridge with pea protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and the poppy seeds. Let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Wash the blackberries and gently pat dry.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the blackberries.

title: Raspberry vanilla rice flour crêpes with soy skyr
instructions: Whisk the rice flour, soy protein, vanilla and soy drink until smooth and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Brush a non-stick pan with the coconut oil and cook 2 thin crêpes from the batter for 1 to 2 minutes on each side.
Stir the soy skyr until smooth and spread over the crêpes. Scatter the raspberries on top.
Fold the crêpes into quarters and serve immediately.

title: Orange cardamom millet flake pancakes with soy skyr
instructions: Wash the orange in hot water, finely grate the zest and halve the orange. Squeeze one half and peel the other and divide it into segments.
Finely grind the millet flakes in a blender and mix with the pea protein, baking powder, cardamom and orange zest. Stir in the soy drink and orange juice.
Brush a non-stick pan with the coconut oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes on each side.
Stack the pancakes and serve with the soy skyr and orange segments.

title: Matcha pear buckwheat porridge with pea protein
