instructions: Rinse the buckwheat with hot water, bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the matcha and pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Core the pear and cut into 8 thin wedges.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, arrange the pear wedges on top and sprinkle with the hemp seeds.

title: Nectarine walnut millet flake porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the millet flakes to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and the cinnamon and simmer for 3 minutes, stirring.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Stone the nectarine and cut into 8 wedges. Roughly chop the walnuts.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the 8 nectarine wedges and sprinkle with the walnuts.

title: Sour cherry almond overnight rice flakes with soy skyr
instructions: Stir the rice flakes into the soy drink and leave covered in the fridge overnight to swell.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein until smooth. Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Layer the rice flakes, skyr cream and half of the sour cherries in a jar.
Top with the remaining sour cherries and sprinkle with the toasted almonds.

title: Apple ginger polenta porridge with soy protein
instructions: Peel and finely grate the ginger. Core and dice the apple and stew with the ginger, cinnamon and 60 ml water for 5 minutes until soft.
Bring 150 ml soy drink to the boil, stir in the polenta and let it swell over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the ginger apple compote.

title: Redcurrant lemon overnight quinoa with soy skyr
instructions: Stir the quinoa flakes into the soy drink and leave covered in the fridge overnight to swell.
Finely grate the zest of the lemon quarter and squeeze out the juice. Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, lemon juice, maple syrup and half of the zest until smooth.
Wash the redcurrants and strip them from the stems with a fork.
Layer the quinoa and skyr cream in a jar, top with the redcurrants and sprinkle with the remaining zest.

title: Blueberry cardamom quinoa porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and the cardamom. Let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Warm half of the blueberries in a small pan for 2 minutes until they just start to burst.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the warm and fresh blueberries and sprinkle with the linseed.

title: Kiwi pistachio overnight millet flakes with soy skyr
instructions: Stir the millet flakes into the soy drink with the vanilla and leave covered in the fridge overnight to swell.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein until smooth.
Peel and dice the kiwi. Roughly chop the pistachios.
Layer the millet flakes and skyr cream in a jar, top with the diced kiwi and sprinkle with the pistachios.

title: Savoury buckwheat porridge with oyster mushrooms and smoked tofu
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat with hot water, bring to the boil with the vegetable stock and let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes. Stir in the pea protein and nutritional yeast until creamy.
Tear the oyster mushrooms into strips and dice the smoked tofu.
Fry the mushrooms and tofu in the olive oil for 5 minutes until golden and season with thyme, salt and pepper.
Slice the spring onion into fine rings. Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the mushroom and tofu mixture and sprinkle with the spring onion.

title: Vegan breakfast beans with tofu on rice cakes
instructions: Cut the tofu into small cubes and fry in a non-stick pan without fat for 5 minutes until golden on all sides.
Bring the passata, tomato paste and smoked paprika to the boil in a small pan.
Add the beans and lupins, simmer for 5 minutes until thick, fold in the tofu cubes and season with salt and pepper.
Place the 2 rice cakes on a plate and spoon the beans over them.

title: Rice flour spinach pancakes with herb soy skyr
instructions: Wash the spinach and blend finely with the soy drink. Mix the rice flour, pea protein, baking powder and a pinch of salt and stir in the spinach mixture.
Brush a non-stick pan with the rapeseed oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes on each side.
Finely chop the chives and dill and stir into the soy skyr with salt and pepper.
Thinly slice the radishes and serve with the pancakes and herb skyr.

title: Stuffed strawberries with lemon soy skyr cream and pistachios
instructions: Wash and pat dry the strawberries and cut off the tops straight so they stand. Hollow them out a little from the top with a small spoon.
Finely grate the zest of the lemon quarter and squeeze out the juice. Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, maple syrup, lemon juice and zest until smooth and fill into a piping bag.
Pipe the cream into the 10 strawberries.
Finely chop the pistachios and sprinkle over the top.

title: Lemon poppy seed rice flour mug cake
instructions: Finely grate the zest of the lemon half and squeeze out the juice.
Mix the rice flour, soy protein, poppy seeds and baking powder in a large mug. Stir in the soy skyr, lemon juice, maple syrup, 30 ml water and half of the zest until smooth.
Microwave at 800 watts for 90 seconds and leave to rest for 1 minute.
Sprinkle with the remaining lemon zest.

title: Carrot cake protein balls with walnuts
instructions: Peel the carrot, grate finely and squeeze out well. Chop the walnuts very finely and set aside a third for rolling.
Knead the carrot, remaining walnuts, soy protein, almond flour, soy skyr, maple syrup and cinnamon into a mouldable mixture.
Roll the mixture into 6 balls and roll them in the reserved walnuts.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.

title: Espresso almond protein balls with cocoa
instructions: Mix the ground almonds, pea protein and half of the cocoa.
Stir in the espresso, maple syrup and soy skyr and knead into a mouldable mixture.
Roll the mixture into 6 balls and roll them in the remaining cocoa.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.

title: Pistachio raspberry protein bars
instructions: Roughly chop the pistachios and chop the date very finely. Mash the raspberries with a fork.
Knead the soy protein, almond flour, millet flakes, soy skyr, date, mashed raspberries and two thirds of the pistachios into a firm mixture.
Shape the mixture into 2 bars and press the remaining pistachios on top.
Chill for at least 1 hour.

title: Coconut lime protein muffins
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C top and bottom heat and place 2 paper muffin cases in a muffin tin. Grate the zest of the lime half and squeeze out the juice.
Mix the rice flour, soy protein, baking powder and three quarters of the coconut. Stir in the soy skyr, lime juice, maple syrup and half of the zest.
Divide the batter between the cases, sprinkle with the remaining coconut and bake for 18 minutes.
Leave to cool briefly and sprinkle with the remaining lime zest.

title: Mandarin cheesecake cup with soy skyr
instructions: Finely crumble the rice cake, mix with the almond butter and press into a dessert cup as a base.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein and vanilla until smooth.
Peel the mandarins and divide into segments.
Place half of the segments on the base, add the skyr cream and top with the remaining segments.

title: Banana bread protein bars with walnuts
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C top and bottom heat and line a small tin with baking paper.
Mash the banana and stir with the soy skyr, soy protein, rice flour, cinnamon and baking powder. Roughly chop the walnuts.
Spread the batter in the tin, sprinkle with the walnuts and bake for 18 minutes.
Leave to cool and cut into 2 bars.

title: Savoury edamame lupin balls with sesame
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C top and bottom heat and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Coarsely chop the edamame and lupins in a mini chopper. Add the chickpea flour, pea protein, tamari and cumin and work into a mouldable mixture.
Shape the mixture into 6 balls and roll them in the sesame seeds.
Bake on the tray for 18 minutes until golden.

title: Cherry almond protein muffins
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C top and bottom heat and place 2 paper muffin cases in a muffin tin.
Mix the almond flour, rice flour, soy protein and baking powder and stir in the soy skyr and maple syrup.
Halve 6 cherries and fold them in. Divide the batter between the cases and press 2 whole cherries into the top of each.
Bake for 20 minutes and leave to cool briefly.

title: Mint chocolate protein bars
instructions: Chop the mint leaves very finely.
Knead the soy protein, puffed quinoa, almond butter, soy skyr, maple syrup and mint into a firm mixture, shape into 2 bars and freeze for 20 minutes.
Melt the chocolate over a water bath and brush it over the tops of the bars.
Leave to set in the fridge.

title: Stuffed mini peppers with lupin herb cream
instructions: Blend the lupins, soy skyr, pea protein and lemon juice until smooth.
Finely chop the parsley and chives, stir in and season with salt and pepper.
Halve the mini peppers lengthways and deseed.
Fill the 8 pepper halves with the cream.

title: Kiwi lime teff porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with 160 ml almond drink and let it swell over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Peel the kiwi and cut into slices. Finely grate the zest of the lime quarter.
Top the porridge with the kiwi slices, drizzle with the lime juice and sprinkle with the zest.

title: Orange cinnamon rice flake porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 160 ml almond drink and the cinnamon and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Peel the orange and divide into segments.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the orange segments.

title: Banana cocoa millet porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and bring to the boil with 160 ml almond drink and the cocoa, then let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Peel the banana and cut into thin slices.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the banana slices.

title: Grape cinnamon amaranth porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 160 ml almond drink and the cinnamon and let it swell covered over low heat for 20 minutes.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Wash the grapes and pat dry.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, arrange the grapes on top and dust with a pinch of cinnamon.

title: Cauliflower mountain cheese egg muffins with chives
ingredients: Mountain cheese (vegetarian, made with microbial rennet)
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C top and bottom heat and grease 3 cups of a muffin tin with the butter.
Chop the cauliflower very finely, snip the chives and grate the mountain cheese.
Whisk the eggs with the cream, salt and pepper, stir in the cauliflower, chives and two thirds of the cheese and divide between the 3 cups.
Sprinkle with the remaining cheese and bake for 20 minutes until set and golden.

title: Savoy cabbage cheddar frittata
instructions: Remove the thick rib from the savoy cabbage and cut into fine strips. Grate the cheddar.
Fry the savoy cabbage in the olive oil in an ovenproof pan for 4 minutes until soft.
Whisk the eggs with the nutmeg, salt, pepper and half of the cheddar and pour over the cabbage.
Let it set over low heat for 5 minutes, sprinkle with the remaining cheddar and grill for 3 minutes until golden.

title: Fennel feta egg pan with dill
instructions: Trim and halve the fennel and cut into very thin strips.
Fry the fennel in the olive oil over medium heat for 6 minutes until golden and soft.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper, pour over the fennel and let set covered over low heat for 4 minutes.
Crumble the feta over the top and sprinkle with chopped dill.

title: Baked tomato mozzarella omelette with basil
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C top and bottom heat. Halve the cherry tomatoes and tear the mozzarella into small pieces.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper and pour into the ovenproof pan greased with the olive oil.
Arrange the 12 tomato halves cut side up and the mozzarella on top.
Bake for 12 minutes and serve topped with the basil leaves.

title: Zucchini mozzarella chaffles with herbs
instructions: Finely grate the zucchini, salt it, leave for 5 minutes and squeeze out firmly. Finely chop the mozzarella.
Mix the eggs with the zucchini, mozzarella, almond flour, oregano and pepper.
Brush the waffle iron with the butter and bake 2 chaffles from the batter for 5 minutes each until golden and crisp.
Leave to cool briefly and serve warm.

title: Pepper halloumi egg pan with parsley
instructions: Cut the pepper into thin strips and slice the halloumi into 6 slices.
Fry the halloumi in the olive oil for 2 minutes on each side until golden and remove. Fry the pepper in the same pan for 4 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with pepper, pour over the peppers and let set covered over low heat for 4 minutes.
Arrange the halloumi slices on top and sprinkle with chopped parsley.

title: Clementine cinnamon polenta porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the polenta to the boil with 150 ml soy drink, 40 ml water and half of the cinnamon and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Peel the clementine and divide it into segments.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the clementine segments and dust with the remaining cinnamon.

title: Physalis almond quinoa porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water, bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Remove the physalis from their husks, wash and halve them. Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the physalis and sprinkle with the almonds.

title: Gooseberry vanilla buckwheat pancakes with soy skyr
instructions: Mix the buckwheat flour, pea protein, baking powder and vanilla and stir in the soy drink to make a smooth batter.
Warm the gooseberries with the maple syrup in a small pan for 3 minutes until some burst.
Brush a non-stick pan with the rapeseed oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes on each side.
Stack the pancakes and serve with the soy skyr and the warm gooseberries.

title: Plum poppy seed millet flake waffles with soy skyr
instructions: Finely grind the millet flakes in a blender and mix with the soy protein, poppy seeds and baking powder.
Stir in the soy drink and leave the batter to rest for 5 minutes. Stone the plums and cut into wedges.
Brush the waffle iron with the coconut oil and bake 2 waffles from the batter for 4 minutes each until golden.
Serve the waffles with the soy skyr and the plum wedges.

title: Lychee raspberry rice flake porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Peel, halve and stone the lychees. Pick over the raspberries.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the lychees and raspberries.

title: Fig sesame amaranth porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and 50 ml water and let it swell covered over low heat for 20 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Cut the figs into quarters. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the 8 fig quarters and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.

title: Sea buckthorn banana millet porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water and bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and the vanilla. Let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Stir the sea buckthorn purée with the maple syrup. Slice the banana.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the banana slices and drizzle with the sea buckthorn purée.

title: Apricot cinnamon rice flour crêpes with soy skyr
instructions: Whisk the rice flour, pea protein, half of the cinnamon and the soy drink until smooth and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Stone the apricots and cut into thin wedges.
Brush a non-stick pan with the rapeseed oil and cook 2 thin crêpes from the batter for 1 to 2 minutes on each side.
Spread the crêpes with the soy skyr, top with the apricots, fold over and dust with the remaining cinnamon.

title: Blood orange cocoa teff porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with 140 ml soy drink, 50 ml water and the cocoa and let it swell over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Peel the blood orange and cut out the segments with a sharp knife.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and arrange the blood orange segments on top.

title: Watermelon lime skyr bowl with puffed quinoa
instructions: Finely grate the zest of the lime half and squeeze out the juice.
Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein, maple syrup and half of the lime zest until smooth and spoon into a shallow bowl.
Deseed and dice the watermelon and mix with the lime juice.
Spread the melon cubes over the skyr cream and sprinkle with the puffed quinoa and remaining zest.

title: Mango cardamom buckwheat waffles with soy skyr
instructions: Mix the buckwheat flour, pea protein, baking powder and cardamom.
Stir in the soy drink and leave the batter to rest for 5 minutes. Peel the mango and cut into small cubes.
Brush the waffle iron with the coconut oil and bake 2 waffles from the batter for 4 minutes each until golden.
Serve the waffles with the soy skyr and the mango cubes.

title: Blueberry lemon cornmeal pancakes with soy skyr
instructions: Finely grate the zest of the lemon quarter. Stir the cornmeal, pea protein, baking powder and zest with the soy drink and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Fold a third of the blueberries into the batter.
Brush a non-stick pan with the coconut oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes on each side.
Stir the soy skyr with the juice of the lemon quarter. Stack the pancakes and serve with the skyr cream and the remaining blueberries.

title: Peach coconut quinoa flake muffins with soy protein
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C top and bottom heat and place 2 paper muffin cases in a muffin tin.
Mix the quinoa flakes, soy protein and baking powder. Stir in the apple purée, soy skyr and rapeseed oil.
Stone the peach and dice finely, then fold two thirds into the batter. Divide the batter between the 2 cases.
Sprinkle with the remaining peach cubes and the desiccated coconut and bake for 22 minutes until golden.

title: Pear cocoa overnight quinoa flakes with soy skyr
instructions: Stir the quinoa flakes with the soy drink, soy protein and cocoa in a jar until smooth.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Core the pear and dice finely.
Spoon the soy skyr over the quinoa flakes as a layer and top with the pear cubes.

title: Blackberry lemon buckwheat crêpes with soy skyr
instructions: Whisk the buckwheat flour, soy protein and soy drink until smooth and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Finely grate the zest of the lemon quarter, squeeze out the juice and stir both into the soy skyr.
Brush a non-stick pan with the coconut oil and cook 2 thin crêpes from the batter for 1 to 2 minutes on each side.
Fill the crêpes with the lemon skyr cream and the blackberries and roll up.

title: Pineapple coconut rice flour pancakes with soy skyr
instructions: Mix the rice flour, pea protein, baking powder and half of the desiccated coconut and stir in the soy drink to make a smooth batter.
Peel the pineapple and cut into small cubes.
Brush a non-stick pan with the coconut oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes on each side.
Stack the pancakes, top with the soy skyr and pineapple cubes and sprinkle with the remaining desiccated coconut.

title: Apple cinnamon quinoa flake waffles with soy skyr
instructions: Finely grind the quinoa flakes in a blender and mix with the soy protein, baking powder and half of the cinnamon.
Stir in the soy drink and leave the batter to rest for 5 minutes. Core the apple and cut into thin wedges.
Brush the waffle iron with the rapeseed oil and bake 2 waffles from the batter for 4 minutes each until golden.
Serve the waffles with the soy skyr and apple wedges and dust with the remaining cinnamon.

title: Strawberry mint teff porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with 140 ml soy drink and 50 ml water and let it swell over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Wash and hull the strawberries and slice them. Cut the mint leaves into fine strips.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the strawberry slices and sprinkle with the mint.

title: Raspberry pistachio overnight buckwheat with soy skyr
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat thoroughly and soak covered with the soy drink in the fridge overnight.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein until smooth.
Mash half of the raspberries with a fork. Roughly chop the pistachios.
Layer the buckwheat, mashed raspberries and skyr cream in a jar and top with the remaining raspberries and the pistachios.

title: Nectarine vanilla chia pudding with pea protein
instructions: Stir the chia seeds into the soy drink and leave covered in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight to swell.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein and vanilla until smooth.
Stone the nectarine and cut into small cubes.
Layer the chia pudding and vanilla skyr cream in a jar and top with the nectarine cubes.

title: Kiwi coconut quinoa porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water, bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Peel the kiwi and cut into slices. Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan until light golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the kiwi slices and sprinkle with the desiccated coconut.

title: Peach raspberry millet porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water, bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Stone the peach and cut into thin wedges. Pick over the raspberries.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the peach wedges and raspberries.

title: Persimmon ginger buckwheat pancakes with soy skyr
instructions: Peel the ginger and grate very finely. Mix the buckwheat flour, soy protein, baking powder and ginger and stir in the soy drink to make a smooth batter.
Wash the persimmon, remove the stem end and cut into small cubes.
Brush a non-stick pan with the coconut oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes on each side.
Stack the pancakes and serve with the soy skyr and persimmon cubes.

title: Pomegranate vanilla overnight rice flakes with soy skyr
instructions: Stir the rice flakes with the soy drink and vanilla in a jar and refrigerate covered overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein until smooth.
Spoon the skyr cream over the rice flakes as a layer.
Sprinkle with the pomegranate seeds.

title: Banana sesame rice flour crêpes with soy skyr
instructions: Whisk the rice flour, pea protein and soy drink until smooth and leave to rest for 10 minutes. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden.
Brush a non-stick pan with the coconut oil and cook 2 thin crêpes from the batter for 1 to 2 minutes on each side.
Slice the banana.
Spread the crêpes with the soy skyr, top with the banana slices, fold over and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.

title: Mango lime overnight millet flakes with soy skyr
instructions: Stir the millet flakes with the soy drink in a jar and refrigerate covered overnight, for at least 6 hours.
Finely grate the zest of the lime half and squeeze out the juice. Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein, lime juice and half of the zest until smooth.
Peel the mango and cut into small cubes.
Layer the skyr cream over the millet flakes, top with the mango cubes and sprinkle with the remaining zest.

title: Savoury amaranth porridge with pumpkin, kale and smoked tofu
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with the vegetable stock and let it swell covered over low heat for 20 minutes. Stir in the pea protein and nutritional yeast until creamy.
Deseed the pumpkin and cut into small cubes. Strip the kale from the stalks and chop. Dice the smoked tofu.
Fry the pumpkin and tofu in the olive oil for 6 minutes until golden, add the kale and fry for another 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the pumpkin and tofu mixture.

title: Chickpea waffles with herb soy skyr and radishes
instructions: Stir the chickpea flour, pea protein, baking powder and a pinch of salt with 70 ml water until smooth and leave to rest for 10 minutes.
Brush the waffle iron with the rapeseed oil and bake 2 waffles from the batter for 5 minutes each until golden.
Snip the chives and stir into the soy skyr with salt and pepper. Slice the radishes thinly.
Spread the waffles with the herb skyr and top with the radish slices.

title: Savoury millet porridge with edamame, zucchini and sesame
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water, bring to the boil with the vegetable stock and let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes. Stir in the pea protein.
Cut the zucchini into small cubes and the spring onion into fine rings. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden and remove.
Fry the zucchini and edamame in the sesame oil for 4 minutes and deglaze with the tamari.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the vegetables and sprinkle with the sesame seeds and spring onion.

title: Savoury teff porridge with tomatoes, lupins and basil
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with the vegetable stock and let it swell over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the pea protein and nutritional yeast and season with salt and pepper.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and fry with the lupins in the olive oil for 3 minutes until the tomatoes soften.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the tomatoes and lupins and garnish with the basil leaves.

title: Tahini cinnamon protein balls with sesame
instructions: Chop the dates very finely. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until golden and leave to cool.
Knead the soy protein, tahini, dates, soy skyr and cinnamon into a mouldable mixture.
Roll the mixture into 6 balls and roll them in the toasted sesame seeds.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.

title: Apricot almond protein bars
instructions: Chop the apricots very finely and roughly chop the almonds.
Knead the soy protein, almond flour, quinoa flakes, apricots and soy skyr into a firm mixture.
Press the mixture into a rectangle on baking paper, sprinkle with the chopped almonds and press them in lightly.
Chill for at least 1 hour and cut into 2 bars.

title: Lupin edamame dip with cucumber and pepper sticks
instructions: Heat the edamame in a covered bowl in the microwave for 2 minutes and leave to cool.
Squeeze the juice of the lemon quarter. Blend the edamame, lupins, pea protein, lemon juice, cumin, salt and pepper until smooth.
Cut the cucumber and pepper into finger-thick sticks.
Spoon the dip into a small bowl and serve with the vegetable sticks.

title: Chocolate hazelnut protein balls
instructions: Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan and chop very finely. Chop the dates very finely.
Knead the soy protein, half of the cocoa, the hazelnuts, dates and soy skyr into a mouldable mixture.
Roll the mixture into 6 balls and roll them in the remaining cocoa.
Chill for at least 30 minutes.

title: Blueberry lemon protein ice lollies
instructions: Finely grate the zest of the lemon quarter and squeeze out the juice. Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein, maple syrup, lemon juice and zest until smooth.
Roughly crush the blueberries with a fork and swirl them loosely through the cream.
Pour the mixture into 2 ice lolly moulds, insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Leave at room temperature for 5 minutes before serving and release from the moulds.

title: Apple cinnamon buckwheat mug cake
instructions: Core the apple and dice finely.
Mix the buckwheat flour, soy protein, baking powder and cinnamon in a large mug. Stir in the apple purée and soy skyr until smooth and fold in two thirds of the apple cubes.
Microwave at 800 watts for 90 seconds and leave to rest for 1 minute.
Top with the remaining apple cubes.

title: Strawberry silken tofu mousse with pistachios
instructions: Wash and hull the strawberries. Slice one strawberry and set aside.
Blend the remaining strawberries with the silken tofu, pea protein and maple syrup until very smooth.
Pour into a dessert glass and chill for at least 1 hour.
Finely chop the pistachios. Garnish the mousse with the strawberry slices and pistachios.

title: Oven tofu cubes with sesame crust and tamari lime dip
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C top and bottom heat and line a baking tray with baking paper. Pat the tofu dry and cut into 16 cubes.
Toss the tofu cubes with half of the tamari, then coat in the cornflour, paprika and sesame seeds.
Spread on the tray and bake for 25 minutes, turning halfway through.
Stir the juice of the lime half with the remaining tamari and serve as a dip with the tofu cubes.

title: Sour cherry silken tofu pudding with cacao nibs
instructions: Set aside a few sour cherries for garnish. Roughly chop the date.
Blend the silken tofu, pea protein, remaining sour cherries and the date until very smooth.
Pour into a dessert glass and chill for at least 1 hour.
Garnish with the reserved sour cherries and the cacao nibs.

title: Pumpkin cinnamon protein muffins
instructions: Deseed the pumpkin, grate finely and squeeze lightly. Preheat the oven to 180 °C top and bottom heat and place 2 paper muffin cases in a muffin tin.
Mix the quinoa flakes, pea protein, baking powder and cinnamon. Stir in the pumpkin, soy skyr and maple syrup.
Divide the batter between the 2 cases and sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds.
Bake for 22 minutes until golden and leave to cool briefly.

title: Strawberry chia millet flake porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Bring the millet flakes and chia seeds to the boil with 160 ml almond drink and the vanilla and simmer for 3 minutes, stirring.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Wash and hull the strawberries and slice them.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the strawberry slices.

title: Pineapple mint teff porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with 160 ml almond drink and let it swell over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Peel the pineapple and cut into small cubes. Cut the mint leaves into fine strips and mix with the pineapple.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the minted pineapple.

title: Blueberry cinnamon buckwheat porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat with hot water, bring to the boil with 160 ml almond drink and the cinnamon and let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Pick over and wash the blueberries.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the blueberries.

title: Papaya lime polenta porridge with tofu and pea protein
instructions: Bring the polenta to the boil with 160 ml almond drink and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Peel, deseed and dice the papaya. Finely grate the zest of the lime quarter and drizzle the juice over the papaya.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the papaya and sprinkle with the lime zest.

title: Broccoli Emmental egg muffins with thyme
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C top and bottom heat and grease 3 cups of a muffin tin with the butter.
Divide the broccoli into very small florets and grate the Emmental.
Whisk the eggs with the cream, thyme, salt and pepper, stir in the broccoli and two thirds of the cheese and divide between the 3 cups.
Sprinkle with the remaining cheese and bake for 20 minutes until set and golden.

title: Chard goat cream cheese frittata with pine nuts
instructions: Wash the chard, cut the stalks into thin strips and roughly chop the leaves. Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden and remove.
Fry the chard stalks in the butter in an ovenproof pan for 3 minutes, add the leaves and let them wilt for 1 minute.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper, pour over the chard and dot the goat cream cheese on top in small spoonfuls.
Let it set over low heat for 5 minutes, grill for 3 minutes until golden and sprinkle with the pine nuts.

title: Scrambled eggs with green asparagus and chervil
instructions: Peel the lower third of the asparagus, trim the ends and cut the spears diagonally into 3 cm pieces.
Fry the asparagus in the butter over medium heat for 4 minutes until tender-crisp and season with salt and pepper.
Whisk the eggs with the cream, add to the asparagus and let set creamily over low heat for 3 minutes, stirring slowly.
Sprinkle with chopped chervil and serve immediately.

title: Leek mountain cheese omelette
ingredients: Mountain cheese (vegetarian, made with microbial rennet)
instructions: Trim the leek, wash thoroughly and cut into fine rings. Grate the mountain cheese.
Sweat the leek in half of the butter for 4 minutes until soft and remove.
Whisk the eggs with the nutmeg, salt and pepper and let them set in the remaining butter over low heat for 3 minutes.
Spread the leek and cheese over one half, fold the omelette over and leave for 1 minute until the cheese melts.

title: Paneer spinach egg pan with cumin
instructions: Cut the paneer into 8 cubes.
Toast the cumin in the ghee for 30 seconds, add the paneer and fry for 3 minutes until golden all over.
Add the spinach and let it wilt for 1 minute, then season with salt and pepper.
Whisk the eggs, pour over and let set covered over low heat for 3 minutes.

title: Baked avocado with egg and cheddar
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C top and bottom heat. Halve the avocado, remove the stone and enlarge the hollows a little with a spoon.
Place the 2 avocado halves in a small baking dish and slide one egg into each hollow. Season with salt and pepper.
Grate the cheddar, sprinkle over and bake for 15 minutes until the egg whites are set.
Sprinkle with snipped chives and serve warm.

title: Lupin and asparagus pan with lemon tahini sauce
instructions: Peel the lower third of the asparagus, trim the ends and cut the spears into 4 cm pieces. Finely chop the garlic.
Fry the asparagus in the olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, add the garlic and lupins and fry for 3 more minutes.
Stir the tahini with the lemon juice, pea protein and 30 ml water until smooth and season with salt and pepper.
Transfer the lupin and asparagus mixture to a plate, drizzle with the sauce and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Tempeh and chard pan with chilli and garlic
instructions: Cut the tempeh into thin slices and dice the tofu. Cut the chard stalks into pieces and the leaves into wide strips. Slice the garlic.
Fry the tempeh and tofu in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden all over and remove.
Fry the chard stalks and garlic for 3 minutes, add the leaves and let them wilt for 2 minutes.
Return the tempeh and tofu, deglaze with the tamari and lemon juice and season with chilli flakes, salt and pepper.

title: Beetroot soup with lupins and horseradish soy skyr
instructions: Peel and dice the beetroot, finely chop the onion.
Bring the beetroot and onion to the boil with the vegetable stock and simmer covered for 25 minutes until soft.
Add half of the lupins and the pea protein and purée everything finely. Warm the remaining lupins in the soup for 2 minutes.
Stir the soy skyr with the horseradish, season the soup with salt and pepper and serve with a dollop of horseradish skyr and dill.

title: Edamame spaghetti with kale and nutritional yeast pesto
instructions: Cook the edamame spaghetti in salted water until al dente according to the packet and drain, reserving 3 tbsp of the cooking water.
Strip the kale from the stalks and blend with the nutritional yeast, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and the cooking water into a pesto.
Halve the cherry tomatoes. Toss the spaghetti with the pesto, season with salt and pepper and serve with the tomatoes.

title: Soy chunk gyros bowl with cucumber soy skyr and tomatoes
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in the hot vegetable stock for 10 minutes, squeeze them out well and mix with the gyros seasoning.
Fry the soy chunks in the olive oil for 6 minutes until crisp.
Finely grate a third of the cucumber and stir into the soy skyr with the pressed garlic and salt. Dice the remaining cucumber and the tomato, slice the onion into rings.
Put the shredded lettuce into a bowl, arrange the vegetables, gyros and cucumber skyr on top and season with pepper.

title: Lupin and fennel salad with orange and smoked tofu
instructions: Halve the fennel, remove the core and shave into very thin strips. Dice the smoked tofu.
Peel the orange and cut out the segments, catching the juice.
Whisk the orange juice with the cider vinegar, olive oil, pea protein, salt and pepper.
Toss the fennel, lupins, smoked tofu and orange segments with the dressing and sprinkle with fennel fronds and parsley.

title: Tofu shirataki salad with cucumber, mint and lime chilli dressing
instructions: Rinse the shirataki noodles thoroughly in a sieve, dry-roast them in a pan without fat for 3 minutes and leave to cool.
Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in the dry pan for 6 minutes until golden on all sides.
Cut the cucumber and carrot into fine strips and finely chop the chilli. Stir the lime juice with the tamari, pea protein and chilli.
Toss the noodles, vegetables and tofu with the dressing, season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with mint.

title: Palak tofu with spinach, cumin and tomatoes
instructions: Wash the spinach, let it wilt in a pot and purée finely. Finely chop the onion, ginger and garlic and dice the tomato.
Dice the tofu and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden, then remove.
Toast the cumin in the rapeseed oil for 30 seconds, fry the onion, ginger and garlic for 3 minutes, add the tomato and reduce for 3 minutes.
Stir in the spinach purée and garam masala, add the tofu, heat for 2 minutes and season with salt and pepper.

title: Tempeh broccoli bowl with quinoa and miso ginger dressing
instructions: Rinse the quinoa with hot water and cook covered with 40 ml water for 12 minutes. Divide the broccoli into florets and steam with the edamame for 4 minutes.
Cut the tempeh into cubes and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden.
Finely grate the ginger and stir until smooth with the miso, pea protein and lime juice.
Arrange the quinoa, broccoli, edamame and tempeh in a bowl, drizzle with the dressing and season with pepper.

title: Kale and lupin stew with smoked tofu and pepper
instructions: Dice the onion and pepper, strip the kale from the stalks and roughly chop, dice the smoked tofu.
Fry the smoked tofu in a pot without fat for 4 minutes, add the onion and pepper for 3 minutes and dust with paprika.
Add the strained tomatoes, vegetable stock and kale and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the lupins, warm for 3 minutes and season with salt and pepper.

title: Tofu fajita pan with peppers, onions and salsa
instructions: Cut the tofu into strips, dust with the pea protein, cumin and paprika and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden, then remove.
Cut the peppers and half of the onion into strips and fry in the same dry pan for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Finely dice the tomato and remaining onion and mix with the lime juice, coriander and salt into a salsa.
Add the tofu to the vegetables, toss briefly, season with pepper and serve with the salsa.

title: Asparagus and strawberry salad with smoked tofu and lupins
instructions: Peel the lower third of the asparagus, cut into pieces and fry in a dry pan for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Dice the smoked tofu and fry in the pan for 4 minutes until crisp. Quarter the strawberries.
Stir the balsamic vinegar with the pea protein, salt and pepper until smooth.
Toss the rocket, asparagus, lupins, strawberries and tofu and drizzle with the dressing.

title: Aubergine and tofu rolls in tomato sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Cut the aubergine lengthways into 6 thin slices and fry in a dry pan for 2 minutes per side.
Mash the tofu with the pea protein, nutritional yeast, pressed garlic, salt and pepper and mix in the chopped basil.
Spread the filling over the aubergine slices, roll them up and place them on the strained tomatoes in a small baking dish.
Bake in the oven for 20 minutes and serve with pepper.

title: Kohlrabi and edamame pan with sesame and tamari
instructions: Peel the kohlrabi and cut into sticks, dice the tofu, slice the spring onion into rings and finely chop the ginger.
Fry the tofu in a dry non-stick pan for 5 minutes until golden and remove. Briefly toast the sesame seeds.
Stir-fry the kohlrabi, edamame and ginger for 5 minutes, add the tofu and deglaze with the tamari.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and spring onion and season with pepper.

title: Roasted cauliflower steak with edamame mint cream
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Cut the cauliflower into one 3 cm thick slice and rub with the olive oil, turmeric, cumin and salt.
Roast on a lined baking tray for 25 minutes until golden, turning halfway through.
Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain and purée with the pea protein, lemon juice, mint and 50 ml water into a smooth cream, then season with salt and pepper.
Spread the edamame cream on a plate and place the cauliflower steak on top.

title: Tempeh red cabbage stir-fry with apple and ginger
instructions: Cut the tempeh into strips, the tofu into cubes, the red cabbage into fine strips and the apple into thin wedges, finely chop the ginger.
Fry the tempeh and tofu in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden and remove.
Stir-fry the red cabbage and ginger for 5 minutes, add the apple and fry for 2 more minutes.
Return the tempeh and tofu, deglaze with the tamari and cider vinegar, stir in the pea protein and season with salt and pepper.

title: Soy chunk stroganoff with mushrooms and gherkin
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in 150 ml of the hot vegetable stock for 10 minutes and squeeze out well, reserving the stock.
Dice the tofu, slice the mushrooms, cut the onion into strips and the gherkin into sticks.
Fry the soy chunks and tofu in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes, add the onion and mushrooms for 5 minutes, dust with paprika and deglaze with all of the stock.
Remove from the heat, stir in the soy skyr, mustard and gherkin, season and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Red lentil pasta with spinach tofu ricotta
instructions: Cook the red lentil pasta in salted water until al dente according to the packet and drain, reserving 4 tbsp of the cooking water.
Purée the tofu with the nutritional yeast, lemon juice, garlic, nutmeg, salt and the cooking water into a creamy ricotta.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan, mix in the pasta and tofu ricotta and warm for 1 minute.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, scatter over the pasta and season with pepper.

title: Chickpea pasta arrabbiata with lupins
instructions: Cook the chickpea pasta in salted water until al dente according to the packet and drain.
Finely chop the garlic and chilli and sweat in the olive oil for 1 minute, add the strained tomatoes and reduce for 8 minutes.
Stir in the pea protein, add the lupins and warm for 2 minutes, season with salt and pepper.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and garnish with basil.

title: Pea and mint soup with edamame and tofu croutons
instructions: Dice the onion and bring to the boil with the peas, edamame and vegetable stock, then simmer for 6 minutes.
Cut the tofu into small cubes and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 7 minutes until crisp, then salt.
Add the mint leaves and pea protein to the soup, purée everything finely and season with salt and pepper.
Pour the soup into a bowl and top with the tofu croutons.

title: Savoy cabbage and tofu pan with caraway and mustard
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden, then remove.
Cut the savoy cabbage into strips, dice the onion and fry with the caraway in the pan for 4 minutes.
Add the edamame and vegetable stock and braise covered for 4 minutes.
Stir in the mustard, add the tofu and season with salt and pepper.

title: Japchae-style shirataki with tofu, spinach and pepper
instructions: Rinse the shirataki noodles thoroughly and dry-roast them in a pan without fat for 3 minutes, then remove.
Cut the tofu into strips and fry in the pan for 6 minutes until golden. Cut the pepper and carrot into fine strips.
Fry the vegetables and chopped garlic in the sesame oil for 3 minutes, add the spinach and let it wilt.
Stir the tamari with the pea protein, add to the pan with the noodles and tofu, toss and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Bamya – okra and tomato stew with lupins
instructions: Wash the okra and trim the stem ends closely. Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Sweat the onion and garlic in the olive oil for 3 minutes, add the okra and fry for 3 minutes.
Add the strained tomatoes and simmer covered for 15 minutes, then stir in the pea protein and simmer the lupins for 3 minutes.
Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Crustless tofu and mushroom quiche with spinach
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Slice the mushrooms and fry with the spinach in a dry pan for 4 minutes.
Purée the tofu with the chickpea flour, pea protein, soy drink, nutritional yeast, turmeric, nutmeg, salt and pepper until smooth.
Fold in the vegetables, pour the mixture into a small lined dish and smooth the top.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes until golden, rest for 5 minutes and slice.

title: Red lentil dal with tofu, cauliflower and spinach
instructions: Finely chop the onion and ginger, divide the cauliflower into small florets and dice the tofu.
Toast the onion, ginger, turmeric, cumin and garam masala in a pot without fat for 2 minutes, add the lentils, cauliflower and 250 ml water.
Simmer covered for 15 minutes until the lentils break down. Fry the tofu in a dry pan for 6 minutes until golden.
Stir the spinach into the dal, season with salt and pepper and serve with the tofu.

title: Pointed cabbage rolls with soy mince and tomato filling
instructions: Blanch 4 large pointed cabbage leaves in boiling salted water for 2 minutes, refresh in cold water and pat dry. Finely chop the remaining cabbage.
Soak the soy mince in the hot vegetable stock for 10 minutes and mix with the chopped onion, chopped cabbage, pea protein, paprika and marjoram.
Divide the filling among the cabbage leaves, fold in the sides and roll up.
Place the rolls in the strained tomatoes in a small pot and braise covered for 20 minutes, then season with salt and pepper.

title: Rhubarb vanilla millet porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the millet with hot water, bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and the vanilla and let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Cut the rhubarb into 2 cm pieces and stew with the maple syrup and 30 ml water for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the rhubarb compote.

title: Baked apple cinnamon amaranth porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the amaranth to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and 60 ml water and let it swell covered over low heat for 20 minutes.
Core the apple, cut into wedges, dust with half of the cinnamon and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the apple wedges and dust with the remaining cinnamon.

title: Chestnut cocoa buckwheat porridge with soy protein
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat with hot water, bring to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and 60 ml water and simmer covered for 12 minutes until soft.
Finely mash two chestnuts and stir into the porridge with the cocoa, cut the third chestnut into quarters.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the chestnut quarters.

title: Redcurrant coconut teff porridge with soy protein
instructions: Bring the teff to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and 60 ml water and let it swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir the soy protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Wash the redcurrants and strip them from the stems. Toast the coconut flakes in a dry pan until golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, drizzle with the maple syrup, top with the redcurrants and sprinkle with the coconut flakes.

title: Mirabelle plum almond rice flake porridge with pea protein
instructions: Bring the rice flakes to the boil with 150 ml soy drink and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring.
Stir the pea protein with the remaining 30 ml soy drink until smooth and fold into the porridge.
Halve and stone the mirabelle plums. Toast the almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl, top with the mirabelle halves and sprinkle with the almonds.

title: Pumpkin cinnamon rice flour pancakes with soy skyr
instructions: Mix the rice flour, soy protein, baking powder and cinnamon, then stir in the pumpkin purée and soy drink to a thick batter.
Brush a non-stick pan with the rapeseed oil and cook 4 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan and chop roughly. Stack the pancakes, top with the soy skyr and sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds.

title: Grapefruit mint skyr bowl with puffed quinoa
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein and maple syrup until smooth and spoon into a shallow bowl.
Peel the grapefruit and cut the segments out from between the membranes. Cut the mint into fine strips.
Arrange the grapefruit segments on the skyr and sprinkle with the puffed quinoa and mint.

title: Sour cherry cocoa overnight millet flakes with chia
instructions: Stir the millet flakes with the chia seeds, soy drink, soy protein and cocoa and leave covered in the fridge overnight to swell.
In the morning stir well and spoon into a jar.
Top with the sour cherries and serve immediately.

title: Creamy polenta with cherry tomatoes, rocket and smoked tofu
instructions: Bring the vegetable stock to the boil, sprinkle in the polenta and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring. Stir in the pea protein and nutritional yeast.
Dice the smoked tofu and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 4 minutes, add the halved cherry tomatoes and fry for 2 more minutes.
Spoon the polenta into a bowl, top with the tofu and tomatoes, garnish with rocket and season with pepper.

title: Lupin avocado spread on rice cakes with radishes
instructions: Mash the lupins, avocado, pea protein and lemon juice with a fork or in a blender into a creamy spread and season with salt and pepper.
Thinly slice the radishes and cut the chives into small rolls.
Spread the mixture over the 3 rice cakes, top with the radishes and sprinkle with chives.

title: Green tofu pan with zucchini, peas and cumin
instructions: Cut the tofu into cubes, dust with the pea protein and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 6 minutes until golden.
Dice the zucchini and fry with the cumin and peas for 4 minutes.
Fold in the spinach, let it wilt, season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Edamame hummus with kohlrabi sticks
instructions: Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.
Blend the edamame with the pea protein, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and 30 ml water until creamy and season with salt and pepper.
Peel the kohlrabi, cut into finger-thick sticks and serve with the hummus.

title: Cocoa orange protein bars with buckwheat
instructions: Toast the buckwheat in a dry pan for 4 minutes until crunchy and leave to cool. Chop the dates very finely.
Knead the soy protein, cocoa, dates, soy skyr, orange zest and orange juice into a mouldable mixture and work in the buckwheat.
Press the mixture into a rectangle, cut into 2 bars and chill for 30 minutes.

title: Beetroot lupin dip with chicory
instructions: Roughly dice the beetroot and blend finely with the lupins, pea protein, lemon juice and cumin.
Season the dip with salt and pepper.
Separate the chicory into single leaves and serve with the dip.

title: Mango turmeric protein shake with soy skyr
instructions: Peel the mango and cut the flesh from the stone. Peel the ginger.
Blend the mango, ginger, soy skyr, soy protein, soy drink and turmeric until creamy.
Pour into a glass and serve immediately.

title: Stuffed cucumber boats with tofu herb cream
instructions: Stir the silken tofu with the pea protein and lemon juice until smooth, finely chop the chives and dill, fold in and season with salt and pepper.
Halve the cucumber lengthways and scrape out the seeds with a teaspoon.
Fill both cucumber halves with the cream, quarter the cherry tomatoes and arrange on top.

title: Blueberry silken tofu mousse with slivered almonds
instructions: Blend the silken tofu with the soy protein, maple syrup, vanilla and two thirds of the blueberries until creamy.
Spoon the mousse into a glass and chill for 15 minutes. Toast the slivered almonds in a dry pan until golden.
Top with the remaining blueberries and the slivered almonds.

title: Crispy oven edamame with sesame and chilli
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C top and bottom heat. Pat the edamame dry.
Toss the edamame with the tamari, dust with the pea protein, garlic powder and chilli flakes and spread on a lined baking tray.
Roast for 20 minutes until crispy, turning once, sprinkle with sesame and leave to cool.

title: Raspberry rhubarb millet flake porridge with tofu
instructions: Cut the rhubarb into small pieces and stew covered with the maple syrup in a small pan for 5 minutes until soft.
Bring the millet flakes to the boil with 160 ml almond drink and simmer for 3 minutes, stirring.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the rhubarb compote and raspberries.

title: Banana cocoa buckwheat porridge with tofu
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat with hot water, bring to the boil with 160 ml almond drink and simmer covered for 12 minutes until soft, then stir in the cocoa.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Slice the banana.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the banana slices.

title: Mandarin ginger polenta porridge with tofu
instructions: Finely grate the ginger, bring to the boil with 160 ml almond drink, sprinkle in the polenta and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring.
Blend the tofu with the remaining 60 ml almond drink and the pea protein until smooth and stir into the porridge.
Peel the mandarin and divide into segments.
Spoon the porridge into a bowl and top with the mandarin segments.

title: Tomato mozzarella omelette with basil
instructions: Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper. Slice the mozzarella and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Melt the butter in a pan, pour in the eggs and let them set over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Arrange the mozzarella and tomatoes on one half and cook covered for 2 minutes until the cheese melts.
Fold the omelette and serve topped with basil.

title: Spinach cheddar frittata with spring onions
instructions: Slice the spring onion into rings and grate the cheddar.
Melt the butter in a small ovenproof pan, sweat the spring onion for 1 minute, add the spinach and let it wilt.
Whisk the eggs with salt, pepper and two thirds of the cheese, pour over the vegetables and let set over low heat for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle with the remaining cheese and grill under the oven grill for 3 minutes until golden.

title: Egg salad with avocado and chives
instructions: Hard-boil the eggs in boiling water for 10 minutes, rinse under cold water, peel and dice.
Dice the avocado and cut the chives into small rolls.
Stir the mayonnaise with the mustard, salt and pepper and gently fold in the eggs, avocado and chives.
Place the lettuce leaves on a plate and arrange the egg salad on top.

title: Quick win: turmeric tofu scramble with cherry tomatoes, rocket and rice cakes
instructions: Crumble the tofu coarsely with your hands. Halve the cherry tomatoes.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the tofu with the turmeric, nutritional yeast, salt and pepper for 4 minutes, stirring.
Arrange the tofu scramble on a plate with the cherry tomatoes, rocket and rice cakes and sprinkle with chives.

title: Quick win: soy skyr bowl with pea protein, kiwi, blueberries and hemp seeds
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein until smooth and spoon into a shallow bowl.
Peel the kiwi and slice it, wash the blueberries.
Arrange the kiwi slices and blueberries on the skyr and sprinkle with the hemp seeds.

title: Quick win: pear soy yoghurt with soy protein, peanut butter and hemp seeds
instructions: Stir the soy yoghurt with the soy protein until smooth and spoon into a shallow bowl.
Wash and core the pear and cut it into thin wedges.
Arrange the pear wedges on the yoghurt, drizzle with the peanut butter and sprinkle with the hemp seeds and cinnamon.

title: Quick win: chickpea and egg pan with pepper, cumin and skyr dip
instructions: Cut the pepper into strips and fry with the rinsed chickpeas and cumin in the olive oil for 4 minutes.
Whisk the eggs and egg whites with salt and pepper, pour into the pan and let set over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Stir the skyr with a pinch of salt, slide the egg pan onto a plate, sprinkle with parsley and serve the skyr dip alongside.

title: Quick win: crispy tempeh slices with tomato, cucumber and wholemeal bread
instructions: Cut the tempeh into 6 thin slices and toss with the tamari and paprika.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the tempeh slices for 2 minutes per side until crisp.
Slice the tomato and cucumber and season with salt and pepper.
Arrange the wholemeal bread, tempeh, tomato and cucumber on a plate.

title: Quick win: skyr plate with orange segments, pomegranate and pistachios
instructions: Peel the orange with a knife and cut out the segments between the membranes.
Spread the skyr smoothly on a deep plate and dust with cinnamon.
Scatter the orange segments, pomegranate seeds and pistachios over the top.

title: Quick win: prawn and grapefruit plate with avocado, lamb's lettuce and crispbread
instructions: Fry the prawns with the chopped garlic in the olive oil for 3 minutes until pink throughout and season with salt and pepper.
Peel the grapefruit and cut out the segments, cut the avocado into wedges.
Arrange the lamb's lettuce, grapefruit segments, avocado and prawns on a plate and add the rye crispbread.

title: Quick win: smoked trout plate with cucumber, apple and horseradish yoghurt
instructions: Stir the yoghurt with the horseradish, salt and pepper.
Slice the cucumber and cut the apple into thin wedges.
Flake the trout fillet into pieces and arrange on a plate with the cucumber, apple, crispbread and horseradish yoghurt, sprinkle with dill.

title: Quick win: quark plate with papaya, blueberries and linseed
instructions: Peel and deseed the papaya, cut into cubes and drizzle with the lime juice.
Stir the quark until smooth and spread it on a deep plate.
Scatter the papaya and blueberries on top and sprinkle with the linseed.

title: Quick win: sardine plate with white beans, tomato and rocket
instructions: Rinse the beans and mix with the lemon juice, oil, parsley, salt and pepper.
Cut the tomato into wedges.
Spread the rocket on a plate and arrange the beans, tomato and sardines on top.

title: Quick win: edamame and egg plate with kohlrabi, radishes and mustard skyr dip
instructions: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, refresh, peel and halve. Add the edamame to the boiling water for the last 3 minutes and drain.
Peel the kohlrabi and cut into sticks, halve the radishes.
Stir the skyr with the mustard, salt and pepper and arrange on a plate with the eggs, edamame, kohlrabi and radishes, sprinkle with chives.

title: Quick win: chickpea smash plate with tomato, cucumber and soy yoghurt dip
instructions: Rinse the chickpeas and mash coarsely with a fork, season with lemon juice, cumin, salt and pepper.
Stir the soy yoghurt with a pinch of salt. Dice the tomato and cucumber.
Toast the pita briefly and arrange on a plate with the chickpea smash, diced vegetables and the dip.

title: Black bean sweet potato chilli with avocado and lime
instructions: Peel the sweet potato and cut into 1 cm cubes, dice the onion, garlic and pepper.
Sweat the onion, garlic and pepper in the oil for 4 minutes and toast the spices for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, tomatoes and rinsed beans and simmer covered for 20 minutes until the sweet potato is tender, season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the chilli into a bowl, top with avocado slices and drizzle with lime juice.

title: Chickpea and chard curry with brown rice
instructions: Cook the rice in plenty of salted water for 30 minutes and drain.
Cut the chard stalks into pieces and the leaves into strips. Chop the onion, ginger and garlic.
Sweat the onion, ginger, garlic and chard stalks in the oil for 4 minutes and toast the curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, strained tomatoes and coconut milk, simmer for 10 minutes, stir in the chard leaves and let them wilt for 2 minutes, season with salt and serve with the rice.

title: Roasted Jerusalem artichokes with beluga lentils, lamb's lettuce and hazelnuts
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Scrub the Jerusalem artichokes well, halve, toss with 3 g of the oil, thyme and salt and roast for 25 minutes until golden.
Cook the beluga lentils in plenty of water for 20 minutes until al dente and drain.
Roughly chop the hazelnuts and toast in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Whisk the remaining oil, cider vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper, mix with the lentils and arrange with the lamb's lettuce and Jerusalem artichokes, sprinkle with the hazelnuts.

title: Pearl barley and red cabbage pan with apple, walnuts and feta
instructions: Cook the pearl barley in plenty of salted water for 30 minutes and drain.
Cut the red cabbage into fine strips, dice the onion, core the apple and cut into wedges.
Fry the onion and red cabbage in the oil with the caraway for 8 minutes, add the apple wedges for 3 minutes and deglaze with the cider vinegar.
Fold in the barley, season with salt and pepper, spoon into a bowl and sprinkle with crumbled feta, chopped walnuts and parsley.

title: Chicken and borlotti bean stew with savoy cabbage and parsnip
instructions: Cut the chicken into bite-sized cubes, peel and dice the parsnip, cut the savoy cabbage into strips and chop the onion and garlic.
Sear the chicken in the oil for 3 minutes and fry the onion and garlic with it for 2 minutes.
Add the stock, parsnip and thyme and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the rinsed beans and savoy cabbage and cook for another 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through, season with salt and pepper.

title: Cod on puy lentils and leeks with mustard
instructions: Cook the lentils in plenty of water for 25 minutes until al dente and drain.
Cut the leek into rings and the carrot into small cubes and sweat in 5 g of the oil for 5 minutes, add the stock and mustard, stir in the lentils and simmer for 3 minutes.
Salt the cod and fry in the remaining oil for 3 minutes per side until opaque and cooked through.
Arrange the lentil vegetables on a plate, place the cod on top, drizzle with lemon juice and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Wholemeal penne with broccoli, peas, nutritional yeast and lemon
instructions: Divide the broccoli into small florets. Cook the penne in plenty of salted water according to the packet instructions, adding the broccoli and peas for the last 4 minutes, then drain everything.
Thinly slice the garlic and toast in the oil for 1 minute.
Add the pasta and vegetables to the pan, toss with the lemon juice, lemon zest, nutritional yeast, chilli flakes, salt and pepper and serve in a deep plate.

title: Kidney bean and squash stew with spinach, ginger and sesame
instructions: Deseed the squash and cut it with the skin into 2 cm cubes, finely chop the onion and ginger.
Sweat the onion and ginger in the sesame oil for 3 minutes, add the squash and stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the rinsed kidney beans and tamari, simmer for another 5 minutes and stir in the spinach.
Ladle into a bowl and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Freekeh salad with beetroot, lentils, feta and rocket
instructions: Cook the freekeh and lentils separately in plenty of salted water for 20 to 25 minutes until al dente, drain and let cool.
Dice the beetroot.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, cumin, salt and pepper and mix with the freekeh, lentils and beetroot.
Fold in the rocket, spoon the salad into a bowl and sprinkle with crumbled feta and mint.

title: Chicken buckwheat stir-fry with edamame, broccoli and ginger
instructions: Cook the buckwheat in plenty of salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Cut the chicken into strips, divide the broccoli into small florets, chop the ginger and garlic and slice the spring onion into rings.
Sear the chicken in the oil for 4 minutes until cooked through, add the broccoli, edamame, ginger and garlic and stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Stir in the buckwheat and tamari, heat for 1 minute and serve sprinkled with the spring onion.

title: Air fryer mushrooms with cottage cheese and spinach filling
instructions: Clean the mushrooms, twist out the stalks and chop them finely.
Roughly chop the spinach and stir with the mushroom stalks, chopped garlic, cottage cheese, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Brush the outside of the mushroom caps thinly with the oil, fill with the mixture and sprinkle with the hard cheese.
Cook in the air fryer at 180 °C for 10 minutes until the filling is golden brown.

title: Blackcurrant soy skyr ice lollies with pea protein
instructions: Let the blackcurrants thaw slightly and blend with the soy skyr, pea protein, banana and lemon juice until smooth.
Pour the mixture into 2 ice lolly moulds, insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Briefly hold the moulds under warm water and release the lollies.

title: Pineapple, carrot and turmeric smoothie with soy skyr and hemp seeds
instructions: Peel and dice the pineapple, peel the carrot and ginger and chop roughly.
Blend the pineapple, carrot, ginger, soy skyr, hemp seeds, turmeric and 100 ml cold water in a blender for 60 seconds until smooth.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Air fryer turkey and pepper skewers with herb quark dip
instructions: Cut the turkey, pepper and courgette into 2 cm pieces, toss with the oil, paprika and salt and thread alternately onto 4 wooden skewers.
Cook in the air fryer at 200 °C for 10 minutes, turning halfway, until the turkey is cooked through.
Stir the quark with the chopped herbs, salt and pepper and serve as a dip with the skewers.

title: Pear and poppy seed quark cream with walnuts
instructions: Stir the quark with the poppy seeds, vanilla and half of the maple syrup until creamy.
Core the pear, cut into small cubes and caramelise with the remaining maple syrup in a pan for 3 minutes.
Spoon the quark cream into a glass, top with the pear cubes and sprinkle with chopped walnuts.

title: Pumpkin seed cocoa protein balls with dates and pea protein
instructions: Grind the pumpkin seeds finely in a mini chopper and set aside 1 tsp for rolling.
Add the dates, pea protein, cocoa and 15 ml water and blend into a mouldable mixture.
Shape the mixture into 4 balls, roll in the reserved pumpkin seeds and chill for 20 minutes.

title: Persimmon cinnamon protein shake with skyr and oats
instructions: Wash the persimmon, remove the stalk end and cut into pieces.
Blend the persimmon, skyr, oats, milk and cinnamon in a blender for 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Mango ginger nice cream with soy protein and pistachios
instructions: Let the frozen banana and mango soften for 5 minutes, peel and finely grate the ginger.
Blend the fruit, ginger, soy protein and soy drink in a food processor for 1 to 2 minutes until creamy, scraping down in between.
Spoon into a bowl and sprinkle with chopped pistachios.

title: Chicken quinoa box with sugar snap peas, mango and lime dressing
instructions: Cook the quinoa in plenty of salted water for 15 minutes, adding the sugar snap peas for the last 2 minutes, drain everything and let cool.
Salt the chicken and fry in 3 g of the oil for 5 minutes per side until cooked through, let cool and slice.
Dice the mango. Whisk the lime juice, remaining oil, chilli flakes and salt into a dressing.
Pack the quinoa, sugar snap peas, mango and chicken side by side into a container, sprinkle with coriander, pack the dressing separately and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Eat cold straight from the container, mixing in the dressing just before eating.

title: Mountain lentil and feta box with cherry tomatoes, radishes and mint
instructions: Cook the lentils in plenty of water for 25 minutes until al dente, drain and let cool.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, slice the radishes, finely chop the onion and crumble the feta.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, oregano, salt and pepper and mix with the lentils, vegetables and mint.
Pack the salad into a container, sprinkle with the feta and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Eat cold straight from the container, mixing in the dressing just before eating.

title: Turkey gyros box with brown rice, coleslaw and yoghurt dip
instructions: Cook the rice in plenty of salted water for 30 minutes, drain and let cool.
Toss the turkey strips with the gyros seasoning and 5 g of the oil and fry in a hot pan for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Finely shred the white cabbage, grate the carrot and knead with the remaining oil, cider vinegar and salt.
Grate the cucumber, stir with the yoghurt, crushed garlic and salt and fill into a small pot.
Pack the rice, gyros and coleslaw side by side into a container, let cool and keep with the dip in the fridge for up to 3 days.
At the office eat cold or reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot.

title: Tofu rice noodle box with carrot, cucumber, red cabbage and peanut sauce
instructions: Cook the rice noodles in plenty of water according to the packet instructions, drain, rinse with cold water and let drain.
Cut the tofu into cubes and fry in the oil for 6 minutes until golden on all sides.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into fine strips and finely shred the red cabbage.
Stir the peanut butter with the tamari, lime juice, chilli flakes and 30 ml water until smooth and fill into a small pot.
Pack the noodles, vegetables and tofu side by side into a container, sprinkle with coriander and keep with the sauce in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Eat cold straight from the container, mixing in the dressing just before eating.

title: Roast cauliflower and chickpea box with millet and tahini lemon sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Divide the cauliflower into florets, toss with the rinsed chickpeas, oil, cumin, paprika and salt and roast for 25 minutes.
Rinse the millet with hot water, cook in plenty of salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Stir the tahini with the lemon juice, 30 ml water and a pinch of salt until smooth and fill into a small pot.
Pack the millet, cauliflower and chickpeas into a container, sprinkle with parsley, let cool and keep with the sauce in the fridge for up to 4 days.
At the office eat cold or reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot.

title: Tuna and bean salad box with fennel, orange and rocket
instructions: Rinse and drain the beans. Shave the fennel into very thin slices.
Peel the orange and cut into pieces, catching the juice.
Whisk the orange juice, lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper and mix with the beans, fennel and orange pieces.
Pack the salad with the rocket into a container, lay the tuna in chunks on top and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Eat cold straight from the container, mixing in the dressing just before eating.

title: Beef shawarma box with wholemeal couscous, cucumber, tomato and tahini yoghurt
instructions: Cut the beef into thin strips and mix with the cumin, paprika, lemon juice, half the oil, salt and pepper.
Pour 75 ml boiling water over the couscous, leave to swell for 5 minutes and fluff up with the remaining oil.
Sear the beef in a hot pan for 3 to 4 minutes. Dice the cucumber and tomato and cut the onion into fine rings.
Stir the yoghurt with the tahini and a pinch of salt. Pack the couscous, beef and vegetables into a container, sprinkle with parsley, let cool and keep with the dip in the fridge for up to 3 days.
To eat, reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot, stirring once.

title: Smoked tofu potato salad box with cucumber, radishes and mustard dressing
instructions: Cook the potatoes in their skins in plenty of water for 20 minutes, drain, peel and slice.
Whisk the warm stock with the mustard, cider vinegar, oil, salt and pepper, pour over the warm potatoes and leave to soak for 10 minutes.
Dice the smoked tofu and toast in a dry non-stick pan for 4 minutes. Thinly slice the cucumber and radishes.
Mix everything with the chives, pack into a container and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
Eat cold straight from the container, mixing in the dressing just before eating.

title: Halibut with creamed spinach and toasted pine nuts
instructions: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden and set aside.
Season the halibut with salt and pepper and fry in half the butter for 3 to 4 minutes per side until just cooked through.
Chop the garlic and sweat in the remaining butter, add the spinach and let it wilt, stir in the cream and simmer for 2 minutes with nutmeg, salt and pepper until creamy.
Arrange the creamed spinach on a plate, place the halibut on top and sprinkle with the pine nuts.

title: Chicken thighs with pesto courgettes and mozzarella
instructions: Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper and fry skin side down in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until crisp, turn and fry for another 8 minutes until cooked through.
Cut the courgette into half-moons, fry in the pan juices for 4 minutes and toss with the pesto.
Arrange the pesto courgettes and chicken on a plate, tear the mozzarella over the top and sprinkle with basil.

title: Halloumi avocado salad with cucumber, olives and mint
instructions: Cut the halloumi into 4 slices and fry in a dry non-stick pan for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Dice the avocado and cucumber and halve the olives.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper, toss with the rocket, avocado, cucumber and olives and arrange on a plate with the halloumi and mint.

title: Feta and aubergine pan with olives, walnuts and mint
instructions: Cut the aubergine into 2 cm cubes and fry in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until golden on all sides.
Add the chopped garlic, olives and oregano and fry for 2 minutes, season with pepper.
Break the feta into rough pieces, place on top of the aubergines and warm covered for 3 minutes until soft.
Transfer to a plate and sprinkle with chopped walnuts and mint.

title: Beef mince and pointed cabbage cream pan with cream cheese and caraway
instructions: Cut the pointed cabbage into fine strips and finely dice the onion.
Fry the beef mince in the butter for 5 minutes until crumbly and cooked through, add the onion and caraway for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage and fry for 5 minutes until tender-crisp.
Stir in the cream cheese until a creamy sauce forms, season with salt and pepper and serve on a plate sprinkled with parsley.

title: Smoked mackerel on cauliflower purée with chives
instructions: Divide the cauliflower into florets and cook in plenty of salted water for 12 minutes until soft, drain well.
Purée the cauliflower finely with the butter, cream, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Skin the mackerel and flake into large pieces.
Spread the purée on a plate, place the mackerel on top, drizzle with lemon juice and sprinkle with chives.

title: Dakbokkeumtang – Korean braised gochujang chicken with potatoes and carrots
instructions: Cut the chicken thighs into large pieces, peel the potatoes and carrot and cut into chunks, cut the onion into wedges and chop the garlic and ginger.
Stir the gochujang, tamari, gochugaru, garlic, ginger and 200 ml water together.
Put the chicken, potatoes, carrot and onion into a pot, pour over the sauce, bring to the boil and braise covered for 25 minutes until the chicken and potatoes are cooked.
Reduce uncovered for 5 minutes, stir in the sesame oil and serve in a bowl sprinkled with spring onion and sesame.

title: Kharcho – Georgian beef and walnut soup with rice and coriander
instructions: Cut the beef into 2 cm cubes, bring to the boil with the stock, skim and simmer gently covered for 60 minutes.
Dice the onion, stone and finely chop the plums and pound the walnuts finely with the garlic in a mortar.
Add the onion, rice, strained tomatoes and plums to the soup and simmer for 15 minutes until the rice is cooked.
Stir in the walnut garlic paste and spices, leave to infuse for 3 minutes, season with salt and pepper and serve sprinkled with coriander.

title: Kindzmari – Georgian pikeperch in coriander garlic sauce with potatoes
instructions: Cook the potatoes in their skins in plenty of water for 20 minutes, drain, peel and halve.
Salt the pikeperch and fry in the oil for 3 minutes per side until cooked through.
