Finely chop the coriander and garlic and heat with the vinegar, 100 ml water, chilli flakes and salt in a small pan for 2 minutes.
Arrange the pikeperch and potatoes on a plate and pour the warm coriander sauce over them.

title: Pescado a lo macho – Peruvian fish in prawn ají sauce with rice
instructions: Cook the rice in plenty of salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Salt the pollock and fry in 3 g of the oil for 3 minutes per side until cooked through, keep warm.
Dice the onion, pepper and garlic and sweat in the remaining oil with the ají paste and cumin for 4 minutes, deglaze with the white wine.
Add the strained tomatoes and prawns and simmer for 3 minutes until the prawns are pink and cooked through.
Arrange the fish with the rice on a plate, spoon the prawn sauce over the fish and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Doro alicha – mild Ethiopian turmeric chicken stew with egg and injera
instructions: Chop the onion very finely and sweat in a pot without fat for 8 minutes, stirring, until soft, then add the ghee, chopped garlic, ginger and turmeric for 2 minutes.
Cut the chicken into pieces, add with 150 ml water, the cardamom and salt and braise covered for 30 minutes until cooked through.
Hard-boil the egg for 9 minutes, peel, score all around and let it simmer in the sauce for the last 5 minutes.
Serve the doro alicha in a bowl with the egg and place the injera beside it on the plate.

title: Kongbiji jjigae – Korean ground soybean stew with tofu and kimchi
instructions: Thaw the edamame and blend finely with 100 ml of the stock.
Roughly chop the kimchi, dice the onion and fry both in the sesame oil with the gochugaru and garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the remaining stock, tamari, diced courgette and tofu cubes and simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in the edamame purée, let it steep over low heat for 3 minutes without boiling hard and serve in a bowl sprinkled with spring onion.

title: Buckwheat skyr pancakes with cherry compote and almond butter
instructions: Stir the buckwheat flour, eggs, 100 g skyr, vanilla and cinnamon into a smooth batter and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Simmer the sour cherries with the maple syrup in a small pan for 5 minutes to make a compote.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and cook 6 small pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Stack the pancakes and serve with the remaining skyr, the cherry compote and the almond butter.

title: Hearty breakfast skillet with turkey mince, sweet potato, fried eggs and spinach
instructions: Peel the sweet potato, cut it into 1 cm cubes and fry covered in half the oil for 10 minutes, turning.
Dice the onion, add with the turkey mince and fry for 5 minutes until crumbly and cooked through. Season with paprika, salt and pepper.
Fold in the baby spinach, let it wilt for 1 minute and transfer everything to a plate.
Fry 2 eggs sunny side up in the remaining oil and place them on top.

title: Overnight spelt flakes with low-fat quark, whey, banana and walnuts
instructions: Stir the spelt flakes, low-fat quark, whey protein powder, milk and cinnamon together in a large jar until smooth.
Seal the jar and refrigerate overnight, for at least 6 hours.
In the morning slice the banana, arrange the slices on the flakes and sprinkle with the roughly chopped walnuts.

title: Tofu and chickpea breakfast hash with beetroot, spinach and avocado
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut it into 2 cm cubes, dice the beetroot as well and rinse the chickpeas.
Fry the tofu in the hot oil for 6 minutes until golden on all sides, add the chickpeas, cumin and paprika and fry for another 3 minutes.
Add the beetroot and baby spinach, toss for 2 minutes and season with nutritional yeast, salt and pepper.
Arrange the hash on a plate and top with avocado slices.

title: Rump steak with oven potato wedges, green beans and herb quark
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Wash the potatoes, cut into wedges, toss with 10 g olive oil, rosemary and salt and bake for 30 minutes until golden brown.
Trim the green beans, cook in salted water for 7 minutes until tender-crisp and drain.
Stir the low-fat quark with chopped chives and parsley, salt and pepper.
Pat the steak dry, fry in the remaining oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side, rest for 3 minutes, season with salt and pepper and serve with the potato wedges, beans and herb quark.

title: Chicken and potato tray bake with Brussels sprouts, carrots and mustard skyr
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Quarter the potatoes, halve the Brussels sprouts, cut the carrots into sticks and spread on a baking tray with 10 g olive oil, thyme and salt.
Bake the vegetables for 15 minutes.
Cut the chicken breast into 3 pieces, rub with the remaining oil and paprika, place on the tray and bake for another 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir the skyr with the mustard, salt and pepper and serve with the chicken and vegetables.

title: Salmon with roasted pumpkin, quinoa, kale and dill skyr
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Deseed the pumpkin, cut into wedges, toss with the olive oil and salt and bake for 25 minutes.
Cook the quinoa according to the packet instructions, adding the kale for the last 3 minutes.
Season the salmon with salt and after 10 minutes place it on the tray with the pumpkin and bake for 15 minutes.
Stir the skyr with chopped dill, lemon juice and pepper and serve with the salmon, pumpkin and quinoa kale.

title: Turkey mince and kidney bean chilli with brown rice and skyr
instructions: Cook the brown rice according to the packet instructions.
Dice the onion, garlic and pepper. Fry the turkey mince in the oil for 5 minutes until crumbly, add the vegetables and spices and fry for another 3 minutes.
Add the strained tomatoes and rinsed kidney beans and simmer for 15 minutes, season with salt and pepper.
Serve the chilli with the rice in a bowl, topped with the skyr.

title: Seitan shawarma plate with freekeh, red cabbage and tahini sauce
instructions: Cook the freekeh according to the packet instructions.
Cut the seitan into thin strips, toss with the shawarma spice and oil and fry in a hot pan for 6 minutes until crisp.
Finely shred the red cabbage and knead with half the lemon juice and salt. Dice the tomato and cucumber.
Stir the tahini with the remaining lemon juice and 30 ml water until smooth and arrange everything on a plate.

title: Tuna steak with sweet potato mash, broccoli and sesame
instructions: Peel and dice the sweet potato, boil in salted water for 15 minutes until soft, drain and mash with the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Divide the broccoli into florets and steam for 5 minutes.
Coat the tuna steak in the sesame seeds and sear in the sesame oil for 1 to 2 minutes per side so it stays pink inside.
Slice the tuna, arrange with the mash and broccoli and drizzle with the tamari.

title: Prawn coconut curry with sweet potato, peas and basmati rice
instructions: Cook the basmati rice according to the packet instructions.
Dice the onion and sweat in the oil for 2 minutes, add the curry paste and toast for 1 minute.
Peel the sweet potato, cut into 1 cm cubes, add with the coconut milk and simmer for 12 minutes.
Add the prawns and peas and cook for 4 minutes until the prawns are pink. Season and serve with the rice and coriander.

title: Turkey breast with pearl barley mushroom risotto and Brussels sprouts
instructions: Dice the onion, slice the mushrooms and fry both in 5 g olive oil for 4 minutes. Add the pearl barley and toast briefly.
Gradually add the vegetable stock and cook the barley for 30 minutes, stirring, until creamy, then stir in the hard cheese.
Halve the Brussels sprouts and steam for 8 minutes.
Season the turkey breast with salt and fry with thyme in the remaining oil for 5 minutes per side until cooked through, slice and serve with the risotto and Brussels sprouts.

title: Marzipan protein shake with almond drink, soy protein and banana
instructions: Peel the banana and break it into pieces.
Blend the banana, almond drink, soy protein, almond butter, bitter almond flavouring and vanilla in a blender for 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass, sprinkle with the ground almonds and drink straight away.

title: Hazelnut espresso protein shake with soy drink and pea protein
instructions: Brew the espresso and let it cool completely.
Blend the espresso, soy drink, pea protein, hazelnut butter, banana and ice cubes in a blender for 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Kale and pear smoothie with silken tofu and pea protein
instructions: Wash the kale and remove the tough stalks, core the pear and chop roughly, peel the ginger.
Blend the kale, pear, ginger, silken tofu, pea protein, lemon juice and 150 ml cold water in a blender for 60 seconds until smooth.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Blackberry and pomegranate smoothie bowl with soy protein and cacao nibs
instructions: Let the blackberries thaw for 5 minutes and set aside a few berries for garnish.
Blend the remaining blackberries with the soy skyr and soy protein in a blender into a thick cream.
Spoon into a shallow bowl and sprinkle with the pomegranate seeds, the remaining blackberries and the cacao nibs.

title: Mandarin and turmeric ice lollies with coconut yoghurt and pea protein
instructions: Peel the mandarins and blend with the soy yoghurt, coconut yoghurt, pea protein and turmeric until smooth.
Pour the mixture into 2 ice lolly moulds, insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Briefly hold the moulds under warm water and release the lollies.

title: Chestnut cocoa protein ice cream from the food processor
instructions: Roughly chop the chestnuts and blend with the soy drink, soy protein, cocoa, maple syrup and cinnamon until smooth.
Pour the mixture into a freezer-safe tub and freeze for at least 12 hours.
Let the block soften for 10 minutes, break it into pieces and blend in a food processor until creamy.
Spoon the ice cream into a small bowl and serve straight away.

title: Persimmon and ginger nice cream with soy protein and pecans
instructions: Let the frozen fruit soften for 5 minutes.
Blend the persimmon, banana, grated ginger, soy protein and soy yoghurt in a food processor for 1 to 2 minutes until creamy, scraping down in between.
Spoon into a bowl and sprinkle with chopped pecans.

title: Orange chocolate silken tofu mousse with pea protein and pistachios
instructions: Halve the orange, grate a little zest, squeeze one half and cut 3 segments from the rest.
Blend the silken tofu, pea protein, cocoa, maple syrup, orange juice and zest for 1 minute until airy.
Spoon the mousse into a dessert glass, chill for 30 minutes and garnish with the orange segments and chopped pistachios.

title: Chia soy skyr pudding with plum compote and soy protein
instructions: Stir the soy skyr, soy protein and chia seeds until smooth and leave to swell in the fridge for at least 20 minutes.
Stone and quarter the plums and stew with the cinnamon in a small pan for 5 minutes until soft.
Spoon the pudding into a glass and serve with the warm or cooled plum compote.

title: Baked quince with soy skyr vanilla cream and pea protein
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Rub the quince clean thoroughly, halve it and remove the core.
Place the quince halves cut side up in a small dish, sprinkle with cinnamon, pour in 50 ml water and bake covered for 45 minutes until soft.
Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein and vanilla until smooth.
Arrange the quince halves on a plate and spoon the vanilla cream into the hollows.

title: Keto omelette with mushrooms, Gruyère and baby spinach
instructions: Slice the mushrooms and fry in half the butter for 4 minutes until golden, add the baby spinach and let it wilt, then remove.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper and let them set in the remaining butter over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Spread the mushroom and spinach mixture and the Gruyère over one half, fold the omelette and leave for 1 minute.
Slide onto a plate and sprinkle with chives.

title: Keto chia coconut pudding with raspberries and almond butter
instructions: Stir the coconut milk with the vanilla until smooth, stir in the chia seeds and stir again after 5 minutes.
Leave the pudding to swell covered in the fridge for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Spoon into a small bowl, top with the raspberries and drizzle with the almond butter.

title: Duck breast with creamed savoy cabbage and hazelnuts
instructions: Score the duck skin in a diamond pattern, salt it and fry skin side down in a cold pan for 8 minutes until crisp, turn and fry for another 4 minutes, then rest for 5 minutes.
Roughly chop the hazelnuts and toast without fat for 2 minutes.
Cut the savoy cabbage into thin strips, sweat in the butter for 4 minutes, add the cream and simmer for 3 minutes with nutmeg, thyme, salt and pepper until creamy.
Slice the duck breast, arrange on the creamed cabbage and sprinkle with the hazelnuts.

title: Baked salmon with cauliflower cheese mash and broccoli
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Brush the salmon with the olive oil, season with salt and bake for 15 minutes.
Divide the cauliflower into florets and boil in salted water for 10 minutes until soft, adding the broccoli for the last 4 minutes.
Remove the broccoli, drain the cauliflower and purée finely with the butter, Cheddar, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Arrange the mash on a plate, place the salmon and broccoli beside it and sprinkle with dill.

title: Chicken thighs in mustard cream sauce with pointed cabbage
instructions: Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper and fry skin side down in a dry pan for 10 minutes until crisp, turn and fry for another 8 minutes until cooked through.
Remove the chicken, add the cream, mustard and thyme to the pan and simmer for 2 minutes to a sauce.
Cut the pointed cabbage into strips and sweat in the butter in a pot for 5 minutes until tender-crisp, season with salt.
Put the cabbage on a plate, place the chicken thighs on top, drizzle with the mustard cream sauce and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Lamb chops with feta spinach and olives
instructions: Season the lamb chops with rosemary, salt and pepper and fry in 10 g olive oil for 3 minutes per side, then rest for 3 minutes.
Chop the garlic and sweat briefly in the remaining oil, add the spinach and let it wilt for 2 minutes.
Crumble the feta over the top, add the olives, season with pepper and serve with the lamb chops.

title: Halloumi and courgette skillet with walnuts, basil and lemon
instructions: Cut the halloumi into 4 slices of equal thickness, cut the courgette into half moons and roughly chop the walnuts.
Fry the halloumi in a dry pan for 2 minutes per side until golden and remove.
Fry the courgette in the olive oil for 5 minutes, add the walnuts and toast for 1 minute, season with lemon juice, lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Place the halloumi on the courgette and sprinkle with fresh basil.

title: Trout with almond butter, braised fennel and capers
instructions: Cut the fennel into thin wedges and braise covered in the olive oil over medium heat for 12 minutes until soft, season with salt.
Season the trout fillets with salt and fry skin side down in 10 g butter for 3 minutes, turn and finish cooking for 1 minute.
Foam the remaining butter with the flaked almonds until the almonds are golden, then add the capers and lemon juice.
Arrange the fennel on a plate, place the trout fillets on top and drizzle with the almond caper butter.

title: Quick win: chickpea and tofu smash with pepper, cucumber and cress
instructions: Mash the tofu and rinsed chickpeas coarsely with a fork and mix with the nutritional yeast, lemon juice, paprika, salt and pepper.
Cut the pepper into strips and slice the cucumber.
Arrange the smash on a plate, place the pepper and cucumber beside it and sprinkle with cress.

title: Quick win: soy yoghurt with mandarin, pomegranate seeds, soy protein and linseed
instructions: Stir the soy yoghurt with the soy protein until smooth and spoon into a shallow bowl.
Peel the mandarin and divide it into segments.
Arrange the mandarin segments and pomegranate seeds on the yoghurt and sprinkle with the linseed.

title: Quick win: smoked paprika tofu scramble with mushrooms and baby spinach
instructions: Slice the mushrooms and fry in the oil for 3 minutes.
Crumble the tofu coarsely, add with the smoked paprika and nutritional yeast and fry for 3 minutes, stirring.
Fold in the baby spinach until it wilts, season with salt and pepper and serve on a plate sprinkled with chives.

title: Quick win: papaya lime soy skyr with pea protein and coconut flakes
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the pea protein, lime juice and lime zest until smooth and spoon into a shallow bowl.
Peel the papaya, remove the seeds and cut the flesh into cubes.
Arrange the papaya cubes on the skyr and sprinkle with the coconut flakes.

title: Quick win: cottage cheese bowl with pear, lingonberries and pecans
instructions: Spoon the cottage cheese into a shallow bowl.
Core the pear and cut it into thin wedges, roughly chop the pecans.
Arrange the pear wedges and lingonberries on the cottage cheese and sprinkle with the pecans and cinnamon.

title: Quick win: egg white omelette with courgette, cherry tomatoes and feta
instructions: Slice the courgette thinly, halve the cherry tomatoes and fry both in the olive oil for 2 minutes.
Whisk the egg whites and egg with oregano, salt and pepper, pour over the vegetables and let set over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Crumble the feta over the top, fold the omelette and slide it onto a plate.

title: Quick win: rye bread with sliced turkey, cottage cheese, tomato and cress
instructions: Spread the rye bread with the cottage cheese.
Slice the tomato and arrange on the bread with the sliced turkey breast.
Sprinkle with cress, salt and pepper and serve on a plate.

title: Quick win: tuna skyr spread on pumpernickel with cucumber and radishes
instructions: Stir the tuna with the skyr, lemon juice, chopped chives, salt and pepper into a spread.
Slice the cucumber and radishes thinly.
Spread the pumpernickel with the spread, top with the cucumber and radish slices and serve on a plate.

title: Black bean and pumpkin stew with soy mince and cumin
instructions: Deseed the pumpkin and cut into 2 cm cubes, dice the onion and garlic.
Sweat the onion and garlic in the oil in a pot for 2 minutes, add the soy mince, cumin and paprika and toast for 1 minute.
Add the pumpkin, strained tomatoes and vegetable stock, bring to the boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Add the rinsed black beans, simmer for another 5 minutes, season with chilli flakes, salt and pepper and serve in a bowl sprinkled with coriander.

title: Sauerkraut and potato stew with turkey sausages and caraway
instructions: Peel and dice the potatoes, dice the onion and slice the turkey sausages.
Fry the sausage slices in the oil in a pot for 3 minutes, add the onion and fry for another 2 minutes.
Add the potatoes, sauerkraut, caraway, bay leaf and vegetable stock and simmer covered for 20 minutes until the potatoes are soft.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper and serve in a bowl sprinkled with parsley.

title: Erwtensoep – Dutch split pea soup with smoked tofu, leek and celeriac
instructions: Rinse the split peas and bring to the boil with the vegetable stock and bay leaf, then simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Cut the leek into rings, dice the celeriac and carrot, add them and simmer for another 20 minutes until the peas break down.
Dice the smoked tofu and fry in a dry pan for 4 minutes on all sides.
Remove the bay leaf, season the soup with marjoram, salt and pepper, stir in the smoked tofu and serve in a bowl.

title: Venison and mushroom stew with chestnuts, savoy cabbage and potatoes
instructions: Cut the venison into 2 cm cubes and brown in the oil in a casserole for 5 minutes, dice the onion and fry for another 2 minutes.
Add the beef stock, crushed juniper berries, thyme and bay leaf and braise gently covered for 60 minutes.
Peel and dice the potatoes, quarter the mushrooms and cut the savoy cabbage into strips, add everything with the halved chestnuts and simmer for another 20 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper and serve in a deep bowl.

title: Ginger chicken soup with parsnips, leek and rice noodles
instructions: Bring the chicken stock to the boil with the sliced ginger, add the chicken breast and poach gently for 15 minutes until cooked through, then remove.
Slice the parsnip and carrot, cut the leek into rings, add to the stock and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the rice noodles and cook for 3 to 4 minutes according to the packet instructions. Shred the chicken and return it to the soup.
Season with salt and pepper and serve in a bowl sprinkled with parsley.

title: Pikeperch and root vegetable soup with horseradish and dill
instructions: Peel the potatoes, carrot and celeriac and cut into 1 cm cubes, cut the leek into rings.
Bring the vegetables to the boil in the vegetable stock and simmer for 12 minutes until soft.
Cut the pikeperch fillet into 3 cm pieces, add to the hot soup and poach for 5 minutes without letting the soup boil.
Stir the soured cream with the horseradish, season the soup with salt and pepper, serve in a bowl topped with a dollop of horseradish cream and sprinkled with dill.

title: Gong bao tofu – Sichuan tofu with peanuts, peppers and spring onions
instructions: Pat the tofu dry and cut into 2 cm cubes, dice the pepper, cut the spring onions into pieces and chop the ginger and garlic.
Stir the tamari, rice vinegar, cornflour and 40 ml water into a sauce.
Fry the tofu in the hot oil in a wok for 6 minutes until golden, add the dried chillies, Sichuan pepper, ginger and garlic and fry for 30 seconds.
Fry the pepper and spring onions for 2 minutes, pour in the sauce until glossy, fold in the peanuts and serve on a plate.

title: Tofu sisig – Filipino tofu skillet with onions, chilli and lime
instructions: Soak the soy mince in 40 ml hot water for 10 minutes. Cut the tofu into small cubes and finely chop the onion, garlic and chilli.
Fry the tofu in the oil in a cast-iron pan for 8 minutes until crisp, add the soy mince and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the onion, garlic and chilli and fry for 2 minutes, season with the tamari, lime juice and pepper.
Serve in the pan sprinkled with spring onion rings.

title: Tempeh bacem – Javanese braised tempeh with cucumber sambal and rice
instructions: Cut the tempeh into 6 slices. Pound the shallot and garlic with the coriander seeds and galangal in a mortar.
Bring the paste to the boil with the coconut sugar, 10 g tamari, bay leaf and 200 ml water, add the tempeh and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes until the liquid has almost evaporated.
Meanwhile cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Dice the cucumber and mix with the sambal oelek and remaining tamari.
Caramelise the tempeh slices in the oil for 2 minutes per side and serve with the rice and cucumber sambal.

title: Tantanmen with soy mince, shirataki, pak choi and sesame soy broth
instructions: Soak the soy mince in 60 ml hot water for 10 minutes. Rinse the shirataki and blanch in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Chop the garlic and ginger, fry with the soy mince in the sesame oil for 3 minutes and season with half the tamari and the chilli flakes.
Heat the vegetable stock and soy drink without boiling, stir in the tahini and remaining tamari. Quarter the pak choi lengthways and cook in the broth for 2 minutes.
Put the shirataki into a bowl, add the broth and pak choi and top with the soy mince and spring onion rings.

title: Panang curry with tofu, sugar snap peas and kaffir lime
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packet instructions. Cut the tofu into cubes and the pepper into strips and finely shred the kaffir lime leaves.
Toast the curry paste with 3 tbsp coconut milk in a pan for 1 minute, then stir in the remaining coconut milk, peanut butter and tamari.
Add the tofu, pepper, sugar snap peas and kaffir lime leaves and simmer for 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
Sprinkle with Thai basil and serve with the rice and a lime wedge.

title: Mole negro with tofu, black beans and cauliflower rice
instructions: Dice the onion and garlic, sweat in the oil for 2 minutes, add the ancho chilli powder, cinnamon and cumin and toast briefly.
Add the strained tomatoes, vegetable stock, cocoa and almond butter, simmer for 8 minutes and purée finely.
Cube the tofu and let it steep in the mole with the rinsed black beans for 5 minutes.
Finely grate the cauliflower, toast in a dry pan for 4 minutes, season with salt and serve with the mole, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

title: Savoury silken tofu chickpea flour crêpes with mushrooms and spinach
instructions: Blend the chickpea flour, silken tofu, 80 ml water and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Slice the mushrooms, crumble the tofu and fry both in half the oil for 6 minutes. Fold in the baby spinach until wilted and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining oil in a non-stick pan and cook 2 thin crêpes from the batter one after the other for 2 minutes per side.
Fill the crêpes with the mushroom and tofu filling, fold them over and serve warm.

title: Millet cocoa breakfast porridge with soy protein and plums
instructions: Bring the millet flakes and the soy drink to the boil in a small pan and simmer gently for 4 minutes, stirring.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the soy protein, cocoa and cinnamon until the porridge is smooth.
Halve and stone the plums and arrange on the porridge with the almond butter.

title: Wholegrain bagel with smoked tofu spread, cucumber and cress
instructions: Finely grate the smoked tofu and stir with the soy yoghurt, mustard, paprika, salt and pepper into a creamy spread.
Halve the bagel and toast it for 2 minutes until golden brown.
Cut the cucumber into thin slices.
Spread both bagel halves with the spread, top with the cucumber and sprinkle with cress.

title: Soy skyr bowl with pineapple, hemp seeds and soy protein
instructions: Stir the soy skyr with the soy protein until smooth and spoon into a bowl.
Peel the pineapple, remove the hard core and cut into small cubes.
Arrange the pineapple on the skyr and sprinkle with the hemp seeds.

title: Air fryer egg and halloumi nests with baby spinach
instructions: Wilt the baby spinach in a pan with half the oil for 1 minute and shape it into 3 nests in a small ovenproof dish.
Cut the halloumi into small cubes, halve the cherry tomatoes and scatter both between the nests.
Crack 1 egg into each nest, drizzle with the remaining oil and season with pepper.
Cook in the air fryer at 160 °C for 10 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft.

title: Keto omelette roll with smoked trout, cream cheese and rocket
instructions: Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan, pour in the eggs and let them set covered over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Slide the omelette onto a board, let it cool briefly and spread with the cream cheese.
Flake the smoked trout, slice the avocado and spread both over the omelette with the rocket.
Roll up the omelette tightly and cut into 4 pieces.

title: Buckwheat galette with fried egg, turkey breast and mushrooms
instructions: Whisk the buckwheat flour with 100 ml water and a pinch of salt into a smooth thin batter and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Slice the mushrooms, cut the turkey breast into fine strips and fry both in half the oil for 5 minutes until the turkey is cooked through. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining oil in a large non-stick pan, spread the batter thinly and cook for 2 minutes until the underside is set.
Crack the egg into the centre, scatter the mushrooms and turkey around it, fold the edges in to form a square and cook covered for 3 minutes until the egg white is set. Sprinkle with chives.

title: Low-fat quark bowl with physalis, mandarins and hazelnuts
instructions: Stir the quark with the cinnamon until creamy and spoon into a bowl.
Peel the mandarins and separate them into segments, remove the physalis from their husks.
Arrange the fruit on the quark, roughly chop the hazelnuts and sprinkle them over the top.

title: Pear ginger skyr with buckwheat crunch and flaxseed
instructions: Finely grate the ginger and stir it into the skyr.
Core the pear and cut it into small cubes.
Spoon the skyr into a bowl and top with the pear, buckwheat and flaxseed.

title: Air fryer breakfast potatoes with turkey sausages, fried egg and pepper
instructions: Wash the potatoes, cut into 2 cm cubes, toss with two thirds of the oil, paprika and salt and cook in the air fryer at 200 °C for 15 minutes, shaking once.
Cut the pepper into strips, slice the turkey sausages diagonally, add both to the potatoes and cook for another 8 minutes until the sausages are heated through.
Meanwhile fry the eggs sunny side up in the remaining oil in a pan for 3 minutes.
Put the potatoes, pepper and sausages on a plate, top with the fried eggs and season with pepper.

title: Red lentil pancakes with soy yoghurt herb dip
instructions: Soak the red lentils in plenty of cold water for at least 2 hours and drain.
Blend the lentils with 100 ml water, the soy protein and salt into a smooth batter. Finely slice the spring onion and stir it in.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan and cook 6 small pancakes from the batter for 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Stir the soy yoghurt with chives, parsley, salt and pepper and serve as a dollop next to the pancakes.

title: Air fryer tempeh breakfast plate with mushrooms and tomatoes
instructions: Cut the tempeh into 1 cm thick slices and marinate with the tamari, oil and smoked paprika.
Halve the mushrooms and halve the tomatoes.
Place the tempeh, mushrooms and tomatoes cut side up in the air fryer basket and cook at 190 °C for 12 minutes, turning the tempeh slices halfway.
Arrange on a plate with the rocket and season with salt and pepper.

title: Air fryer chicken thighs with paprika potato wedges and garlic yoghurt dip
instructions: Wash the potatoes, cut into wedges, toss with half the oil, half the paprika and salt and pre-cook in the air fryer at 200 °C for 10 minutes.
Rub the chicken thighs with the remaining oil, the remaining paprika, salt and pepper, add to the potatoes in the air fryer and cook for another 16 minutes until the meat is cooked through.
Stir the yoghurt with crushed garlic and salt.
Arrange the chicken thighs with the potato wedges and add the dip as a dollop.

title: Air fryer salmon fillet with sesame crust, sweet potato cubes and green beans
instructions: Peel the sweet potato, cut into 2 cm cubes, toss with the oil and salt and cook in the air fryer at 200 °C for 10 minutes.
Brush the salmon fillet with tamari and sprinkle the top with sesame seeds. Trim the green beans.
Add the salmon and beans to the sweet potatoes in the air fryer and cook at 180 °C for another 10 minutes until the salmon is cooked.
Arrange everything on a plate and season with pepper.

title: Air fryer turkey schnitzel in almond crust with cucumber dill salad
instructions: Cut the turkey breast horizontally into 2 thin schnitzels, pound them flat and season with salt and pepper.
Whisk the egg. Dip the schnitzels first in the egg, then in the almond flour and drizzle with the oil.
Cook in the air fryer at 190 °C for 12 minutes, turning halfway, until the turkey is cooked through.
Thinly slice the cucumber, mix with the skyr, dill and salt and serve with the schnitzels.

title: Air fryer tempeh cubes with sriracha ginger glaze, broccoli and rice
instructions: Cook the rice in plenty of salted water for 12 minutes and drain.
Cut the tempeh into 2 cm cubes and toss with the sriracha, tamari, maple syrup, grated ginger and sesame oil.
Cook the tempeh cubes and broccoli florets in the air fryer at 190 °C for 12 minutes, shaking halfway.
Serve the rice with the tempeh and broccoli and sprinkle with sliced spring onion.

title: Air fryer chickpea spinach patties with tahini sauce and cucumber salad
instructions: Drain the chickpeas and pulse with the baby spinach, chickpea flour, cumin, salt and pepper in a food processor to a coarse paste.
Shape the mixture into 6 patties, brush with the oil and cook in the air fryer at 190 °C for 14 minutes, turning halfway.
Stir the tahini with lemon juice, 30 ml water and salt until smooth.
Slice the cucumber, salt lightly and arrange with the patties. Drizzle the sauce over the patties.

title: Air fryer beef patties with Brussels sprouts, potato cubes and mustard skyr
instructions: Finely dice the onion, knead with the beef mince, paprika, salt and pepper and shape into 4 flat patties.
Halve the Brussels sprouts, cut the potatoes into 2 cm cubes and toss both with the oil and salt.
Pre-cook the vegetables in the air fryer at 200 °C for 8 minutes, then add the patties and cook for another 12 minutes until the meat is cooked through.
Stir the skyr with the mustard and serve with the patties and vegetables.

title: Air fryer chicken bites with sesame and sriracha skyr dip
instructions: Cut the chicken breast into 8 pieces, toss with the egg white, paprika and salt and roll in the sesame seeds.
Cook in the air fryer at 200 °C for 10 minutes, shaking halfway, until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir the skyr with the sriracha and serve as a dip with the bites.

title: Air fryer pumpkin wedges with chickpea flour crust and soy yoghurt dip
instructions: Deseed the pumpkin and cut it with the skin into 8 wedges.
Stir the chickpea flour with the paprika, salt, the oil and 30 ml water into a thick paste and coat the wedges with it.
Cook in the air fryer at 190 °C for 15 minutes until the crust is crisp and the pumpkin is tender.
Stir the soy yoghurt with chopped chives and salt and serve as a dip.

title: Air fryer shrimp tacos with corn cucumber salsa and lime skyr
instructions: Toss the shrimp with the oil, paprika and salt and cook in the air fryer at 200 °C for 6 minutes until pink and cooked through.
Finely dice the cucumber and mix with the corn, half the lime juice and salt into a salsa.
Stir the skyr with the remaining lime juice and a little lime zest.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side and fill with the salsa, shrimp and lime skyr.

title: Air fryer trout fillets with rosemary potato cubes and cucumber mustard dip
instructions: Cut the potatoes into 2 cm cubes, toss with the oil, chopped rosemary and salt and cook in the air fryer at 200 °C for 15 minutes.
Season the trout fillets with salt and pepper, place them skin side up next to the potatoes and cook at 180 °C for another 8 minutes.
Finely grate the cucumber and stir with the yoghurt, mustard, dill and salt.
Arrange the trout with the potato cubes and add the dip as a dollop.

title: Chicken fajita box with brown rice, peppers and black beans
instructions: Cook the rice in plenty of salted water for 30 minutes, drain and let cool.
Cut the chicken, pepper and onion into strips, toss with the oil, paprika, cumin and salt and fry in a hot pan for 7 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Drain the black beans and season lightly with salt.
Pack the rice, beans and fajita mix side by side into a container, let cool and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
To eat, reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot, stirring once.

title: Soy chunk chilli box with kidney beans, corn and millet
instructions: Soak the soy chunks in boiling water for 10 minutes, squeeze out well and chop roughly.
Cook the millet in plenty of salted water for 15 minutes and drain.
Dice the onion and pepper and fry in the oil for 4 minutes. Add the soy chunks, chilli powder and cumin and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the passata, kidney beans, corn and 150 ml water, season with salt and simmer for 15 minutes.
Pack the chilli and millet side by side into a container, let cool and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.
To eat, reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot, stirring once.

title: Pearl barley box with chicken, roasted beetroot and horseradish skyr
instructions: Cook the pearl barley in plenty of salted water for 30 minutes, drain and let cool.
Cut the beetroot into cubes, toss with half the oil and salt and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper, fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes per side until cooked through, let cool and slice.
Stir the skyr with the horseradish and salt.
Pack the barley, beetroot, rocket and chicken side by side into a container, add the horseradish skyr as a dollop and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
At the office eat cold.

title: Tuna potato box with green beans, egg and olives
instructions: Cook the potatoes in their skins in plenty of salted water for 20 minutes, adding the green beans for the last 6 minutes, drain and let cool.
Hard-boil the egg for 9 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and quarter.
Slice the potatoes and halve the cherry tomatoes. Whisk the oil, mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Pack the potatoes, beans, tomatoes, tuna, egg and olives side by side into a container, drizzle with the dressing and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
At the office eat cold.

title: Turkey meatball box with pepper tomato sauce, bulgur and courgette
instructions: Cover the bulgur with boiling salted water, let it soak for 15 minutes and fluff up.
Knead the turkey mince with oregano, paprika, salt and pepper and shape into 8 balls. Fry in half the oil all over for 8 minutes until cooked through.
Dice the onion, pepper and courgette and fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes. Add the passata, season with salt and simmer for 10 minutes, then place the meatballs in the sauce.
Pack the bulgur and the meatballs in sauce side by side into a container, let cool and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
To eat, reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot, stirring once.

title: Salmon soba box with cucumber, radish and wakame
instructions: Bake the salmon in the oven at 180 °C for 12 minutes, let cool and flake into large pieces.
Cook the soba noodles in plenty of boiling water for 5 minutes, adding the edamame for the last 2 minutes, drain and rinse under cold water.
Cut the cucumber and radish into fine matchsticks. Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar and sesame oil into a dressing.
Toss the noodles with the dressing and pack into a container with the cucumber, radish, wakame, edamame and salmon. Keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
At the office eat cold.

title: Wholewheat spaghetti box with red lentil bolognese and courgette
instructions: Finely dice the onion, carrot and courgette and fry in the oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and toast for 1 minute.
Add the red lentils, passata, 150 ml water and oregano, season with salt and simmer for 15 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Cook the spaghetti in plenty of salted water for 9 minutes until al dente and drain.
Pack the spaghetti and bolognese side by side into a container, sprinkle with basil, let cool and keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.
To eat, reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot, stirring once.

title: Bulgogi beef strip box with kimchi, cucumber and brown rice
instructions: Cook the rice in plenty of salted water for 30 minutes, drain and let cool.
Finely grate the pear and stir with the soy sauce and crushed garlic. Marinate the beef strips in it for 15 minutes.
Heat the sesame oil in a pan until very hot and sear the beef strips for 3 minutes until cooked through.
Slice the cucumber and grate the carrot. Pack the rice, beef, kimchi, cucumber and carrot side by side into a container, sprinkle with sesame and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days.
At the office eat cold or reheat covered in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes until piping hot.

title: Plum cinnamon protein shake with silken tofu
instructions: Wash, stone and quarter the plums.
Blend the plums with the silken tofu, soy drink, pea protein and cinnamon in a blender for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Apple cinnamon protein ice cream from the food processor with soy protein
instructions: Core the apple, cut into pieces and freeze for at least 4 hours.

Let the frozen apple pieces soften for 5 minutes and blend with the soy skyr, soy drink, soy protein, maple syrup and cinnamon in a food processor for 1 to 2 minutes until creamy, scraping down in between.
Spoon into a bowl straight away or freeze for another 30 minutes for a firmer texture.

title: Speculoos spice silken tofu cream with mandarins and pea protein
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, pea protein, maple syrup and speculoos spice in a blender for 30 seconds until smooth.
Spoon the cream into a dessert glass and chill for 30 minutes.
Peel the mandarins, separate into segments and arrange on the cream.

title: Sour cherry cocoa smoothie with soy protein and courgette
instructions: Wash the courgette and cut it into rough pieces.
Blend with the sour cherries, soy drink, soy protein and cocoa in a blender for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Edamame lupin hummus with carrot and cucumber sticks
instructions: Cook the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain.
Blend the edamame with the lupins, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt and 30 ml water in a food processor until creamy.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into sticks and arrange on a plate with the hummus.

title: Quark lemon ice lollies with blueberries
instructions: Stir the quark with the lemon zest, lemon juice and maple syrup until smooth.
Lightly crush the blueberries and fold them in.
Pour the mixture into 2 ice lolly moulds, insert the sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Briefly hold the moulds under warm water and release the lollies.

title: Chocolate peanut protein balls with dates and soy protein
instructions: Process the dates with the peanut butter, soy protein, cocoa and 20 ml water in a food processor into a mouldable mixture.
Roll the mixture into 6 equal balls and roll them in the desiccated coconut.
Chill in the fridge for at least 30 minutes until firm.

title: Pumpkin gingerbread spice protein ice cream with soy skyr and pecans
instructions: Deseed the pumpkin, cut into cubes, steam for 15 minutes, let cool and freeze for at least 4 hours.
Let the frozen pumpkin soften for 5 minutes and blend with the soy skyr, soy protein, maple syrup and gingerbread spice in a food processor for 1 to 2 minutes until creamy.
Spoon into a bowl and sprinkle with chopped pecans.

title: Oven-baked char with broccoli and almond butter sauce
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Season the char fillets with salt, brush with the olive oil and place on a baking tray with the broccoli florets.
Bake in the oven for 12 minutes until the fish is just cooked.
Foam the butter with the flaked almonds in a pan for 3 minutes until nutty brown and season with lemon juice.
Arrange the char and broccoli, drizzle with the almond butter and season with pepper.

title: Rump steak with herb butter, mushrooms and rocket
instructions: Let the butter soften and stir with chopped parsley, thyme, crushed garlic and a pinch of salt.
Pat the rump steak dry, sear in half the oil over high heat for 3 minutes per side, season with salt and pepper and let rest for 5 minutes.
Quarter the mushrooms and fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes until golden brown.
Slice the steak, arrange with the mushrooms and rocket and let the herb butter melt on top.

title: Lamb meatballs with feta, cucumber and mint oil
instructions: Finely grate the onion and knead with the lamb mince, cumin, salt and pepper. Shape the mixture into 8 balls.
Fry the meatballs in 1 tsp of the oil all over for 8 minutes until cooked through.
Finely chop the mint and stir with the remaining oil and a pinch of salt.
Slice the cucumber, arrange with the meatballs, crumble the feta over the top and drizzle with the mint oil.

title: Halloumi in spinach coconut sauce with turmeric
instructions: Cut the halloumi into 2 cm cubes and fry in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden brown all over. Remove.
Heat the coconut oil, finely chop the garlic and ginger and sweat with the turmeric and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the spinach and let it wilt, pour in the coconut milk and simmer for 4 minutes, then blend roughly and season with salt.
Add the halloumi to the sauce, warm briefly and serve with pepper.

title: Garlic butter shrimp with courgette noodles and parmesan
instructions: Spiralise the courgette into noodles and season lightly with salt.
Heat the butter and oil in a pan, finely chop the garlic and sweat for 1 minute. Add the shrimp and fry for 2 minutes per side until pink and cooked through.
Add the courgette noodles and baby spinach and toss in the garlic butter for 2 minutes until the spinach wilts. Season with lemon juice.
Season with chilli flakes, parsley and pepper and serve sprinkled with parmesan.

title: Chicken thighs with roasted pepper feta cream and broccoli
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210 °C. Rub the chicken thighs with half the oil, paprika, thyme, salt and pepper and roast skin side up for 25 minutes until the skin is crisp and the meat is cooked through.
Divide the broccoli into florets, toss with the remaining oil and salt and add to the tray for the last 12 minutes.
Drain the roasted pepper and blend with the feta in a food processor into a smooth cream.
Spread the pepper feta cream on the plate and arrange the chicken thighs and broccoli on top.

title: Winter salad with white beans, chicory, pear and hemp seeds
instructions: Drain the white beans. Cut the chicory into strips, core the pear and cut it into thin wedges.
Whisk the oil, mustard, cider vinegar, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Toss the beans, chicory, pear and lamb's lettuce with the dressing and sprinkle with the hemp seeds.

title: Freekeh bowl with kale, chickpeas and tahini
instructions: Cook the freekeh in plenty of salted water for 25 minutes and drain.
Strip the kale from the stalks, chop finely and massage with the oil and a pinch of salt for 1 minute until tender.
Stir the tahini with lemon juice, 30 ml water and salt until smooth.
Arrange the freekeh, kale and drained chickpeas side by side in a bowl, drizzle with the tahini sauce and sprinkle with the pomegranate seeds.

title: Kidney bean millet bowl with sweet potato, red cabbage and avocado
instructions: Peel the sweet potato, cut into cubes, toss with the oil, cumin and salt and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 25 minutes.
Cook the millet in plenty of salted water for 15 minutes and drain.
Finely shred the red cabbage and knead with half the lime juice and salt. Drain the kidney beans.
Arrange the millet, sweet potato, kidney beans, red cabbage and avocado slices side by side in a bowl, drizzle with the remaining lime juice and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Jerusalem artichoke lentil salad with rocket and goat cheese
instructions: Scrub the Jerusalem artichokes thoroughly, slice, toss with half the oil, thyme and salt and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 25 minutes until golden brown.
Cook the lentils in plenty of water for 25 minutes until al dente, drain and season with salt.
Whisk the remaining oil with the balsamic vinegar, salt and pepper and toss with the lentils, Jerusalem artichokes and rocket.
Crumble the goat cheese over the top and sprinkle with roughly chopped walnuts.

title: Chicken bulgur bowl with Brussels sprouts, pomegranate and chickpeas
instructions: Cover the bulgur with boiling salted water, let it soak for 15 minutes and fluff up.
Halve the Brussels sprouts, toss with half the oil and salt and roast in the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
Season the chicken with paprika and salt, fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes per side until cooked through and slice.
Mix the bulgur with lemon juice and parsley and arrange in a bowl with the Brussels sprouts, drained chickpeas, chicken and pomegranate seeds.

title: Buckwheat edamame bowl with shiitake, spinach and miso ginger dressing
instructions: Cook the buckwheat in plenty of salted water for 12 minutes, adding the edamame for the last 3 minutes, and drain.
Slice the shiitake and fry in the sesame oil for 4 minutes.
Stir the miso with grated ginger, rice vinegar and 20 ml water until smooth.
Arrange the buckwheat, edamame, shiitake and baby spinach side by side in a bowl, drizzle with the dressing and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Chirbuli – Georgian eggs in tomato walnut sauce with wholegrain bread
instructions: Finely dice the onion and sweat in the olive oil for 4 minutes until translucent. Chop the garlic, dice the tomatoes and add both.
Finely chop the walnuts, stir in with the fenugreek and chilli flakes and simmer the sauce for 6 minutes until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Make 4 hollows in the sauce with a spoon, crack the eggs into them and cook covered for 6 minutes until the whites are set.
Sprinkle with chopped coriander and serve with the wholegrain bread.

title: Chicken and sweet potato breakfast hash with fried eggs
instructions: Peel the sweet potato, cut into 1 cm cubes and fry covered in half the rapeseed oil for 8 minutes.
Dice the chicken breast, pepper and onion, add and fry uncovered for another 7 minutes until the chicken is cooked through. Season with smoked paprika, salt and pepper.
Fry the eggs sunny side up in the remaining oil for 3 minutes and place on top of the hash.

title: Breakfast burrito with beef mince, black beans and egg
instructions: Fry the beef mince in the rapeseed oil for 5 minutes until crumbly, add the black beans and cumin and fry for 2 more minutes. Season with salt and chilli flakes.
Whisk the eggs, pour into the pan and stir for 2 minutes until creamy scrambled.
Dice the tomatoes. Warm the wholegrain wrap in a dry pan for 30 seconds, spread the filling and tomatoes over it, roll up tightly and cut in half.

title: Turkey breast bagel with scrambled egg and baby spinach
instructions: Cut the turkey breast into thin strips, fry in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes until cooked through, season with salt and remove.
Whisk the eggs and cook in the same pan with the baby spinach for 2 minutes, stirring, until set, then season with pepper.
Halve and toast the bagel, spread both halves with the cream cheese and top with the scrambled egg and turkey strips.

title: Quark and oat pancakes with berries and peanut butter
instructions: Blend the oats, quark, eggs and cinnamon in a tall container until smooth and leave to swell for 5 minutes.
Brush a non-stick pan with the rapeseed oil and cook 3 pancakes from the batter for 2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Warm the berries in a small pan for 3 minutes until juicy and spread over the pancakes with the peanut butter.

title: Savoury buckwheat breakfast porridge with fried egg and cottage cheese
instructions: Rinse the buckwheat and cook covered with 200 ml water and a pinch of salt over low heat for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Slice the mushrooms and fry in half the olive oil for 5 minutes. Slice the spring onions into rings and fold in.
Fry the eggs sunny side up in the remaining oil for 3 minutes.
Put the buckwheat into a bowl, top with the mushrooms, cottage cheese and fried eggs and season with pepper.

title: Tempeh and potato breakfast pan with white beans and spinach
instructions: Wash the potatoes, cut into 1 cm cubes and fry covered in half the rapeseed oil for 10 minutes.
Dice the tempeh and onion, add with the remaining oil and fry for 6 minutes until golden brown. Deglaze with the tamari and smoked paprika.
Fold in the white beans and baby spinach and fry for 2 minutes until the spinach wilts. Season with salt and pepper.

title: Peanut soy protein porridge with banana and hemp seeds
instructions: Bring the oats and soy drink to the boil in a pan and simmer for 4 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Take off the heat and stir in the soy protein and cinnamon until smooth.
Slice the banana and arrange on the porridge with the peanut butter and hemp seeds.

title: Smoked salmon quesadilla with scrambled egg and spring onions
instructions: Whisk the eggs, season with pepper and cook in half the rapeseed oil for 2 minutes, stirring, until softly scrambled.
Slice the spring onions into rings. Top one half of the wrap with the cheese, scrambled egg, smoked salmon and spring onions and fold over.
Fry the quesadilla in the remaining oil for 2 minutes per side until crisp and the cheese melts, cut into triangles and serve with cucumber slices.

title: Halloumi and egg pitta with tomato and cucumber
instructions: Hard-boil the eggs in boiling water for 8 minutes, cool under cold water, peel and slice.
Slice the halloumi and fry in the olive oil for 2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Stir the skyr with chopped mint, salt and pepper. Slice the tomatoes and cucumber.
Briefly warm the pitta, slice open, spread with the mint skyr and fill with the halloumi, egg, tomato and cucumber. Sprinkle with sumac.

title: Cinnamon star protein shake with almond drink
instructions: Break the banana into pieces and put into the blender with the almond drink, pea protein, almond butter, cinnamon and orange zest.
Blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass, dust with a little cinnamon and drink straight away.

title: Baked apple nice cream with cinnamon and walnuts
instructions: Core the apple, cut into wedges, sprinkle with cinnamon and cook in the microwave for 4 minutes until soft. Let cool and freeze for at least 4 hours.
Let the frozen apple wedges and banana soften for 5 minutes and blend with the soy yoghurt and vanilla in a food processor for 2 minutes until creamy.
Roughly chop the walnuts and toast in a dry pan for 2 minutes. Spoon the nice cream into a bowl and sprinkle with the walnuts and a little cinnamon.

title: Almond cherry protein ice cream with silken tofu
instructions: Blend the silken tofu, soy protein, almond butter, almond drink and vanilla until smooth and blend in half the sour cherries.
Pour the mixture into a freezer-safe tub, fold in the remaining cherries and freeze for at least 12 hours.
Let the block soften for 10 minutes, break it into pieces and blend in a food processor until creamy. Serve straight away.

title: Sea buckthorn mango protein smoothie with soy yoghurt
instructions: Let the mango soften for 5 minutes.
Put the mango, sea buckthorn purée, soy yoghurt, pea protein and 100 ml water into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Poppy seed quark mousse with plum compote
instructions: Halve and stone the plums and simmer with 30 ml water, the maple syrup and cinnamon for 5 minutes into a compote. Let cool.
Whisk the quark, yoghurt, poppy seeds and vanilla for 2 minutes until airy.
Spoon the poppy seed mousse into a dessert glass and top with the plum compote.

title: Pomegranate frozen yoghurt bark with pistachios
instructions: Stir the skyr, protein powder and maple syrup until smooth and spread about 1 cm thick on a board lined with baking paper.
Chop the pistachios and scatter over with the pomegranate seeds, pressing in lightly.
Freeze for at least 3 hours, break into irregular pieces and enjoy straight away.

title: Matcha mango smoothie bowl with coconut
instructions: Let the mango and banana soften for 5 minutes.
Blend two thirds of the mango with the banana, soy skyr, pea protein and matcha in a blender for 1 minute until thick and creamy.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the remaining mango cubes, desiccated coconut and hemp seeds.

title: Orange semolina flummery with raspberry coulis
instructions: Bring the milk to the boil with the orange zest and vanilla, sprinkle in the semolina and let it thicken for 4 minutes, stirring. Take off the heat and let cool for 10 minutes.
Stir in the skyr and half the maple syrup, pour into a mould rinsed with cold water and leave to set in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Warm the raspberries with the remaining maple syrup, press through a sieve and let cool.
Turn the flummery out onto a plate and serve with the raspberry coulis.

title: Espresso chia protein pudding
instructions: Whisk the soy drink, espresso, soy protein and cocoa until smooth and stir in the chia seeds.
Stir again after 10 minutes and leave to swell in the fridge for at least 2 hours.
Spoon the pudding into a dessert glass and top with the raspberries.

title: Blueberry gingerbread spice smoothie with soy skyr
instructions: Let the blueberries soften for 5 minutes.
Put the blueberries, soy skyr, banana, almond butter, soy protein, soy drink and gingerbread spice into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Oven frittata with broccoli, goat cheese and walnuts
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Cut the broccoli into small florets and fry in the olive oil in an ovenproof pan for 4 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the thyme, salt and pepper and pour over the broccoli. Scatter the goat cheese over in pieces.
Roughly chop the walnuts, sprinkle over and bake the frittata in the oven for 12 minutes until set and golden brown.

title: Mushroom Gruyère scrambled eggs with avocado and chives
instructions: Slice the mushrooms and fry in half the butter for 5 minutes until golden brown. Season with salt and pepper.
Whisk the eggs, add to the pan with the remaining butter and cook over low heat for 3 minutes until creamy. Fold in the Gruyère.
Slice the avocado, arrange with the scrambled eggs and sprinkle with chives.

title: Stuffed mini peppers with herb cream cheese and walnuts
instructions: Halve the mini peppers lengthways and remove the seeds.
Stir the cream cheese with finely chopped parsley, chives, olive oil, salt and pepper until smooth.
Fill the herb cream cheese into the pepper halves, chop the walnuts and scatter over the top.

title: Cucumber and celery sticks with avocado tahini dip
instructions: Mash the avocado with the tahini, lemon juice, olive oil, cumin and salt with a fork into a creamy dip.
Cut the cucumber and celery into finger-length sticks.
Spoon the dip into a small dish, sprinkle with pepper and serve with the vegetable sticks.

title: Breakfast plate with eggs, avocado and smoked mackerel
instructions: Cook the eggs in boiling water for 7 minutes until jammy, cool under cold water, peel and halve.
Cut the avocado into wedges and the cucumber into slices and quarter the radishes. Remove the skin from the mackerel and flake into pieces.
Arrange everything on a plate, drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with dill, salt and pepper.

title: Smoked trout horseradish cream in chicory boats
instructions: Finely flake the smoked trout and stir with the cream cheese, horseradish, lemon juice, olive oil and dill into a cream. Season with salt and pepper.
Separate the chicory into individual leaves.
Fill the cream into the chicory boats, chop the walnuts and sprinkle over the top.

title: Coconut yoghurt bowl with pecans and cacao nibs
instructions: Stir the coconut yoghurt with the pea protein and cinnamon until smooth and spoon into a bowl.
Roughly chop the pecans.
Scatter the raspberries, pecans, cacao nibs and hemp seeds over the yoghurt.

title: Cauliflower halloumi fritters with almond flour and herb sour cream
instructions: Finely grate the cauliflower, coarsely grate the halloumi and mix both with the egg, almond flour and pepper into a firm mixture.
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan, shape 4 flat fritters from the mixture and fry for 4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Stir the sour cream with chopped parsley, chives and a pinch of salt and serve with the fritters.

title: Badrijani – Georgian aubergine rolls with walnut paste and beluga lentils
instructions: Bring the beluga lentils to the boil with 200 ml water and cook over low heat for 20 minutes until the water is absorbed. Season lightly with salt.
Cut the aubergine lengthways into 6 thin slices, brush with the olive oil and fry in a griddle pan for 3 minutes per side until soft.
Finely blend the walnuts with the garlic, vinegar, fenugreek, paprika, half the coriander and 2 tbsp of the lentils and season with salt.
Spread the aubergine slices with the walnut paste, roll up and arrange on the remaining lentils. Sprinkle with the pomegranate seeds and remaining coriander.

title: Picante de quinoa – Peruvian quinoa and potato stew with ají and feta
instructions: Rinse the quinoa thoroughly in a sieve. Finely dice the onion and garlic and sweat in the olive oil with the pepper paste and cumin for 4 minutes.
Peel the potatoes and cut into 1 cm cubes. Add with the quinoa and vegetable stock and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Stir in the milk and peas and simmer for 4 minutes until creamy. Season with oregano, salt and pepper.
Spoon into a deep plate and crumble the feta over the top.

title: Rajas con elote – pepper and sweetcorn pan with black beans and corn tortillas
instructions: Cut the peppers into thin strips and the onion into rings and fry in the rapeseed oil for 8 minutes until lightly browned. Chop the garlic and fry with the cumin for 1 more minute.
Add the sweetcorn and black beans and fry for 4 minutes. Take off the heat, stir in the soy yoghurt and lime juice and season with oregano, salt and pepper.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side and serve with the pan.

title: Fosolia – Ethiopian green bean and carrot stir-fry with red lentils and injera
instructions: Simmer the red lentils with 250 ml water, the turmeric and a pinch of salt for 15 minutes into a thick purée.
Cut the green beans into 4 cm pieces and the carrots into sticks. Finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger and sweat in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes.
Briefly toast the tomato purée and berbere, add the beans and carrots and cook covered for 10 minutes until al dente. Season with salt and pepper.
Lay the injera on a plate and arrange the vegetables and lentil purée side by side on top.

title: Japanese-style tofu steak with ginger tamari glaze, sesame spinach and rice
instructions: Wash the rice and cook according to the packet instructions. Cut the tofu into 2 thick slices, pat dry and coat all over in the cornflour.

Fry the tofu in the rapeseed oil for 4 minutes per side until crisp. Stir together the tamari, grated ginger, maple syrup and 30 ml water, add to the pan and reduce for 1 minute until the tofu is glossy.
Wilt the spinach in a pan for 2 minutes, squeeze out well, season with salt and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.
Arrange the rice, tofu steaks and sesame spinach side by side.

title: Kibbet laqteen – pumpkin bulgur kibbeh with spinach and chickpea filling
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Dice the pumpkin and steam in a pan for 12 minutes until soft, mash finely and knead while still hot with the bulgur, cinnamon, allspice and salt. Leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Dice the onion and fry in half the olive oil for 4 minutes. Add the spinach and let it wilt, then stir in the chickpeas, chopped walnuts and sumac.
Press half the pumpkin mixture into a small baking dish, spread the filling over it and cover with the remaining mixture. Score a diamond pattern and brush with the remaining oil.
Bake in the oven for 25 minutes until golden brown and serve cut into pieces.

title: Vegetable korma with chickpeas, cashews and basmati
instructions: Cook the basmati rice according to the packet instructions. Finely blend the cashews with the coconut milk and 80 ml water.
Finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger and soften in a pan with a little of the cashew sauce for 4 minutes. Toast the garam masala and turmeric for 1 minute.
Cut the cauliflower into small florets, add with the chickpeas and remaining cashew sauce and simmer covered for 10 minutes. Stir in the peas and cook for 3 more minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve the korma with the basmati rice.

title: Yachaejeon – Korean vegetable pancakes with tofu and tamari dip
instructions: Cut the courgette and carrots into thin strips and the spring onions into 4 cm pieces. Pat the tofu dry and crumble finely.
Whisk the flour with 90 ml water and a pinch of salt until smooth and fold in the vegetables and tofu.
Heat the rapeseed oil in a pan and fry 2 flat pancakes from the batter for 4 minutes per side until crisp.
Stir the tamari with the rice vinegar, sesame seeds and gochugaru and serve as a dip with the pancakes.

title: Swede soup with turkey breast, leek and marjoram
instructions: Peel the swede, potato and carrots and cut into 1 cm cubes; slice the leek into rings.
Sweat the leek in the rapeseed oil for 3 minutes, add the diced vegetables, pour in the vegetable stock and simmer covered for 15 minutes.
Cut the turkey breast into 1 cm cubes, add to the soup and let it cook gently for 8 minutes until done.
Season with marjoram, salt and pepper.

title: Warm Brussels sprout and lentil salad with apple
instructions: Bring the lentils to the boil with 150 ml water and cook over low heat for 20 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Trim and halve the Brussels sprouts and fry in a non-stick pan with the olive oil for 8 minutes until golden brown.
Stir together the mustard, cider vinegar, salt and pepper. Cut the apple into thin wedges and the red onion into fine rings.
Toss the warm lentils and Brussels sprouts with the apple, onion and dressing and serve lukewarm.

title: Warm kale and quinoa salad with roasted pumpkin and feta
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Cut the pumpkin into wedges, toss with half the olive oil and a little salt and roast for 25 minutes.
Rinse the quinoa, bring to the boil with 80 ml water and leave to swell covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Strip the kale from the stalks, chop small and massage firmly with the remaining oil, the lemon juice and a pinch of salt for 1 minute.
Fold the warm quinoa and roasted pumpkin into the kale, crumble the feta over the top and sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds and pepper.

title: Warm red cabbage salad with chicken breast and walnuts
instructions: Cut the red cabbage into thin strips, dice the onion and sauté both in half the rapeseed oil for 6 minutes until al dente. Season with the cider vinegar, cinnamon, clove, salt and pepper.
Season the chicken breast with salt, fry in the remaining oil for 5 minutes per side until cooked through and slice.
Cut the apple into thin wedges and mix with the warm red cabbage. Arrange on the lamb's lettuce, top with the chicken and sprinkle with the chopped walnuts.

title: Savoy cabbage and bean minestrone with rosemary
instructions: Finely dice the onion, carrots and celery, chop the garlic and sweat everything in the olive oil for 5 minutes.
Add the passata, vegetable stock and rosemary and simmer for 10 minutes.
Cut the Savoy cabbage into strips, add with the white beans and simmer for another 10 minutes. Season with thyme, salt and pepper.

title: Thai pumpkin coconut soup with prawns
instructions: Deseed and dice the pumpkin and chop the onion and ginger. Toast with the curry paste in a pan for 2 minutes.
Pour in the vegetable stock and coconut milk, simmer for 15 minutes and blend until smooth.
Add the prawns to the hot soup and cook gently for 3 minutes until pink. Season with lime juice and salt and sprinkle with coriander.

title: Warm parsnip and chickpea salad with lamb's lettuce and goat cheese
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Peel the parsnips, cut lengthways into batons and roast on a tray with the chickpeas, half the olive oil, the thyme and salt for 25 minutes.
Stir the remaining oil with the balsamic vinegar, salt and pepper.
Spread the lamb's lettuce on a plate, top with the warm parsnips and chickpeas, crumble the goat cheese over, sprinkle with chopped walnuts and drizzle with the dressing.

title: Pointed cabbage and lentil soup with cumin and lemon
instructions: Dice the onion and carrots, chop the garlic and sweat in the olive oil with the cumin and tomato purée for 4 minutes.
Rinse the red lentils, add with the vegetable stock and simmer for 10 minutes.
Cut the pointed cabbage into thin strips, add and simmer for another 8 minutes. Season with the lemon juice, paprika, salt and pepper.

title: Silken tofu berry cup with almonds and pea protein
instructions: Blend the silken tofu with the pea protein, maple syrup and vanilla in a tall container with a stick blender for 30 seconds until smooth.
Layer alternately with the thawed mixed berries in a glass.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 1 minute and sprinkle over the top.

title: Green protein smoothie with pear, lamb's lettuce and pea protein
instructions: Core the pear and dice roughly; wash the lamb's lettuce.
Put the pear, lamb's lettuce, banana, pea protein, soy drink and lemon juice into a blender and blend for about 45 seconds until creamy.
Pour into a large glass and drink straight away.

title: Tofu avocado sandwich with tomato and cress
instructions: Cut the tofu into 2 thin slices, fry in the rapeseed oil for 2 minutes per side and drizzle with the tamari.
Toast the wholegrain bread. Mash the avocado with a fork, season with salt and pepper and spread on one slice.
Slice the tomatoes and layer on the bread with the tofu and cress, cover with the second slice and cut in half.

title: Scrambled eggs with cherry tomatoes and rocket in a wholegrain flatbread
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the cottage cheese, salt and pepper and cook in the rapeseed oil for 2 minutes, stirring, until creamy scrambled.
Halve the cherry tomatoes. Warm the wholegrain flatbread in a dry pan for 30 seconds.
Put the scrambled eggs, cherry tomatoes and rocket on the flatbread, roll up and cut in half.

title: Cottage cheese with mandarins, kiwi and pumpkin seeds
instructions: Peel the mandarins and separate into segments; peel and slice the kiwi.
Put the cottage cheese into a bowl and arrange the fruit on top.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 1 minute, sprinkle over and dust with cinnamon.

title: Turkey and cucumber wrap with herb quark and pepper
instructions: Stir the quark with chopped chives, parsley, salt and pepper.
Cut the cucumber and pepper into thin strips.
Spread the wholegrain wrap with the herb quark, top with the turkey breast, cucumber and pepper, roll up tightly and cut in half.
